fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:

fields.name: CountryTag

read by CAIStrategy::GetCountryTag
BiceLib: tag (CCountryTag) - **Whose strategy this is** - four tag characters here, the country id at +0xC. The constructor seeds it with 0x2D2D2D, `"---"`, at 0x4A33DA, which is what identifies it. fields.name: command_level_state
fields.comment: **Not zero for the life of the object.** The constructor zeroes it and FINDINGS-aiunit.md notes that the luabind getter GetOwnerAI (0x4E90A0, `mov eax,[ecx+0x54]`) therefore answers null on a CAIUnit - but slot 82 (0x4C0600) *writes* it, at 0x4C0775, from 0x4DA340(this, unit->oob_level), gated on `this->+0x54 == 0` or its own bool argument being false plus 0xA56B0(unit->current_province, 0). So GetOwnerAI called on a CAIUnit answers null only until slot 82 has run once, and after that it hands back whatever 0x4DA340 returned. What that is was not established. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: owner_ai
fields.comment: The country's CEU3AI. Written by CAIUnit::CAIUnit (0x4AF530) from its first stack argument at 0x4AF578, and all four call sites pass the CEU3AI. **Not +0x54**, which CAIUnit's constructor zeroes even though that is where CAIAgent keeps the owner for the five ministers and where the luabind getter GetOwnerAI (0x4E90A0) reads. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: unit
fields.comment: The unit this agent commands. Zero at construction; written only by CAIUnit::SetUnit (slot 63, 0x4B9EB0), which refuses to overwrite it. Slot 54 reads `unit[+0x204]` (plan_active) through it, slot 82 asks it the `isLand` predicate, and slot 74 (0x4AF4D0) is a plain getter for it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: area_id_type
fields.comment: Type half of the object id of the agent's **area**, which in every path that fills it is a CTheatre. Written from the theatre's own `+0x8` in CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForTheatres (0x48AC4D) and CEU3AI::EnsureAgentForArea, and from FindTheatreForUnit's result in the two unit paths. GetArea (0x4BBAE0) resolves the pair through the game's id registry; a type above 0x1268 goes to the registry at 0x1A857F0 and anything lower to 0x1A857F4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: area_id
fields.comment: Serial half of the area's object id; see area_id_type. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: stance_set
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (slot 77, 0x4C36F0) at 0x4C3714, before anything else. The constructor seeds it 0. Slot 73 runs 0x4C3330 when the hour matches the country's stagger **or** this byte is clear, so it reads as 'a stance has been chosen at least once'. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: air_target_lists_built
fields.comment:
Set to 1 by CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists as its last act (0x4B4E18) and tested by CAIUnit::Tick at 0x4B0A45 immediately before calling it: `if (agent->unit (+0x64) == 0) skip; if (Tick's own replan flag) call; if (+0x83) skip; call`. So the four `air_target_provinces_*` lists are built once per agent and rebuilt only when Tick decides to replan. Nothing clears it in either body.

It sits between the already-recorded `+0x80 stance_set` and `+0x85 replan_naval`, i.e. in the same run of agent flags. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

fields.name: replan_naval
fields.comment: The naval sibling of +0x86 replan_subordinates. Slot 73 reads it at 0x4B0C9F as the second of the two things that make it pass `force` to CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits, and that body clears it at 0x4D08E8 as its first act when force is set. Seeded 1 by the constructor's `+0x84 = 0x10101`, so one naval pass runs at the start of a game. No other writer found in the bodies read. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorganise.md)

fields.name: replan_subordinates
fields.comment: Tested by slot 73 at 0x4B09F5 as one of the three things that make it call slot 78, and **cleared by slot 78 as its last act** (0x4B328C). So it is a request flag: whatever sets it asks for one subordinate-assignment pass. Nothing in slot 78 or 79 sets it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: area_dirty
fields.comment: Zero at construction (the constructor writes `+0x84 = 0x10101`, which leaves +0x84/+0x85/+0x86 at 1 and this byte at 0). CEU3AI::EnsureAgentForArea sets it to 1 on a freshly made agent; CAIUnit::Tick treats it as 'do the area work now' in place of waiting for the weekly slot, and CAIUnit::SetArea (0x4BA5A0) clears it as its first act. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: regroup_air_pending
fields.comment: 'This agent's air groups want regrouping.' Read, cleared and set by CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits only: it gates the split/merge phase at 0x4CE64F (`if (!this->+0x88 && !force) skip`), is cleared at 0x4CE67B before the phase runs, and is set back to 1 at 0x4CEA1D/0x4CEA30 whenever a wing was detached or merged. When it is still set after the phase the function returns 1 at 0x4CEE12 and assigns no missions at all that pass, so a pending regroup suppresses the whole mission half of the body. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorganise.md)

fields.name: ops_area_first
fields.comment: The agent's own copy of the operations area it last computed - a `std::vector<CMapProvince*>`, begin here, end at +0x94, capacity end at +0x98. Slot 76 erases it (std::vector_erase at 0x4DBEAC), fills it with the front provinces it has claimed (std::vector_pushBackByAddress at 0x4DC71F and the inlined push_back at 0x4DC2AB), tests whether it is non-empty to decide whether to post a command, and CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree (0x4DCA70) passes its address to three callees that read it as begin/end of 4-byte elements and dereference them as provinces. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: ops_area_last
fields.comment: End of the ops-area vector at +0x90. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: ops_area_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the ops-area vector at +0x90; read by the inlined push_back growth check at 0x4DC2F6. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: area_neighbours_first
fields.comment: Begin of a `vector<CMapProvince*>` (end at `+0xA4`, capacity end at `+0xA8`) that 0x4BC860 clears and refills on every replan from the provinces **adjacent to the operations area but not in it** that the country may enter - same side, or military access and not an enemy. The push_back is at 0x4BCD12. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: area_neighbours_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at `+0xA0`; 0x4BC860 resets it to begin at 0x4BC8AC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: order
fields.comment: 0x4AF4E0 asks it for its kind through slot 16 and compares against the save tokens 0x4E5 and 0x56C, which is the order-kind idiom the record already knows from CStrategicRedeploymentOrder's 0x5A4. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF5D5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: front_provinces_first
fields.comment: A second vector (end +0xC4, capacity end +0xC8) that 0x4BBB50 clears and rebuilds from the ops area at +0x90, as the first step of CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree. What it holds was not established - only that 0x4BBB50 empties it before walking the ops area's provinces. read (the clearing), inference (the contents) (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: front_provinces_last
fields.comment: End of the front-province vector whose begin the record already has at +0xC0. 0x4B630E..0x4B6316 takes (+0xC4 - +0xC0) / 4 as its element count and 0x4B634E does the same. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: amphibious_transport_tonnage
fields.comment: A tonnage floor on the transport-ship want: 0x4B7479 takes max(4 * enemy units counted in the objective areas * infantry transport_weight, this value) before dividing by a transport's capacity. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF604 and written in exactly one other place, 0x4C67CC, at the end of a loop in the unidentified CAIUnit helper 0x4C4370, from a tonnage accumulated on that function's frame. The use is read; the producer is not. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: submarine_want
fields.comment: Added straight onto the want vector's submarine entry - `want[nuclear_submarine or submarine] += this->+0xD8` at 0x4B7182, with no scaling at all. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF60A and accumulated by the unidentified CEU3AI helper 0x48C140 (`+= [esp+0x48]` at 0x48C750, and again at 0x48D52A). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: naval_units_first
fields.comment: Begin of a `std::vector<CNavy*>` (end +0xE0, capacity end +0xE4) that slot 78 erases at 0x4B1EDC and refills at 0x4B25A2-0x4B2614 with `unit->vf[11]()` for every **naval** unit in the agent's subtree. One of ten per-pass containers, not the seven the earlier survey counted. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: naval_units_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0xDC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: naval_units_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the vector at +0xDC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: naval_transports_first
fields.comment: Begin of a second `std::vector<CNavy*>` (end +0xF0, capacity +0xF4) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1F12. Filled at 0x4B2687 with the naval units whose aggregate definition has `transport_capacity` (`CUnit +0xC8 -> +0x144`) above zero **and** which either hold no objectives or fail 0x4B16F0 - the fleets available to lift troops. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: naval_transports_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0xEC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: naval_transports_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the vector at +0xEC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: air_units_first
fields.comment: **Head of the CList of CAir* that slot 78 rebuilds**, with the tail at +0x100 and the count at +0x104. Slot 78 walks and frees the chain from here at 0x4B1E76-0x4B1E92 and then zeroes all three words (0x4B1E94, 0x4B1E9A, 0x4B1EA0); it refills through 0x4DD3D0 at 0x4B26A8 with `unit->vf[13]()` for every **air** unit in the subtree. The record's existing `CAIUnit +0x100 subordinate_list_first` has the head one word too high. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: subordinate_list_first
fields.comment: A list (tail +0x104) that slot 78 frees node by node and re-heads at 0x4B1E86-0x4B1EA0, one of the seven subordinate-assignment containers it rebuilds every pass. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: air_units_count
fields.comment: Count of the CList headed at +0xFC. **0x4CD890's entry test**: `if (agent->+0x104 < 1) return false` at 0x4CD8BA, which is why that body only runs for an agent commanding aircraft. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: subordinate_vector_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x110) that slot 78 erases at 0x4B1EA6-0x4B1ED6. **Its emptiness is slot 78's entry test**: at 0x4B1D48 the function records `(+0x110 - +0x10C) > 0` into a local before clearing anything, so the pass knows whether it had subordinates assigned last time. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: subordinate_vector2_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x120) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1E45. One of its seven per-pass containers; what it holds was not established. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: subordinate_vector3_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x130) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1D81. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: subordinate_vector4_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x140) slot 78 erases first of all, at 0x4B1D42-0x4B1D7B. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: subordinate_vector5_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x150) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1DB2. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: subordinate_vector6_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x160) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1DE3. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: subordinate_vector7_first
fields.comment: A vector (end +0x170) slot 78 erases at 0x4B1E14. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: strategic_target_provinces_first
fields.comment: A std::vector<CMapProvince*> (end at +0x190) that both force planners walk to size the strategic-bomber want: they sum `province->modifiers[MODIFIER_LOCAL_IC] / 1000 + province->current_producing.crude_oil (+0x27C) / 1000` over it and divide by 300 (0x4B6E00..0x4B7014 in one arm, 0x4B5770 in the other). Only ever cleared through a plain displacement - by the constructor at 0x4AF6E2 and the destructor at 0x4B00C1 - so whatever fills it does so through `lea reg, [agent+0x18C]` and a vector helper, which a displacement scan cannot attribute. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: strategic_target_provinces_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x18C; the count is (+0x190 - +0x18C) / 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: enemy_sighting_provinces_first
fields.comment: A std::vector (end at +0x1A0) that 0x4B77CE..0x4B78A0 push_backs `unit->current_province_ptr (+0x130)` into, once per enemy unit taken off the sighting list at +0x25C. Named from that one producer; nothing was found that reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: enemy_sighting_provinces_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x19C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: invasion_target_provinces_first
fields.comment:
Begin of a `std::vector<CMapProvince*>` (end +0x1B0, capacity end +0x1B4) that slot 78 erases at 0x4B2000-0x4B2025.

**Retyped from `int*`.** CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 4 walks it at 0x4CF403-0x4CF489 and uses each element as a province object, not an id: `lea eax,[elem + 0x2B8]` into CountEnemyLandUnitsInList (the units list), `lea edi,[elem + 0x68]` into CWeather::AirCombatEffect (the embedded weather), and `[elem + 0xD0]` into CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces (the id). An int could not be used any of those three ways.

The first phase-4 arm of the ground-attack block scores exactly these provinces, so whatever the vector is for, the AI bombs enemy stacks standing in it in preference to the battles on its own front. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

fields.name: invasion_target_provinces_last
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x1AC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: invasion_target_provinces_capacity_end
fields.comment: Capacity end of the vector at +0x1AC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: hostile_route_provinces_first
fields.comment:
Head of a CList (last +0x1C0, count +0x1C4, nodes {data, prev, next, byte} with next at +8) holding **the provinces we do not control that lie on the routes from the operations area to the agent's selected target areas** - at war with us, rebel-held, ours-while-we-are-rebels, or covered by the pair's undeclared war. Cleared and refilled by CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches (clear 0x4BBFFB, fill 0x4BC72F-0x4BC791), the routes coming from CCountryTag::FindProvinceRoute out of the three ops-area provinces nearest each target area. CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces doubles a province's priority once per member of this list the province is adjacent to, but only when the plan stance is 3 or more (0x4BD9C8-0x4BDA3C). Four further readers: 0x4C9D25, 0x4C9E81, 0x4CA0F3 (all in 0x4C956B's body), 0x4CAA00 and 0x4D5FB3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)
+0x4 inside it: hostile_route_provinces_last (void*) - Tail of the CList at +0x1BC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)
+0x8 inside it: hostile_route_provinces_count (int) - Count of the CList at +0x1BC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: target_area_provinces_first
fields.comment:
Head of a CList (last +0x1D0, count +0x1D4) holding **every province of every owner area the agent has selected as a target**. Cleared and refilled by CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches at 0x4BC02B-0x4BC053 and 0x4BC3E5-0x4BC44A: an area qualifies when it is on `ourCountry->areas_first (+0xD30)` with its byte +0x68 set, is not our acting capital's area, passes 0x7FD90, and is reachable from one of our own ops-area owner areas in at most two hops under OwnerAreaCost_Accessible but not at all under OwnerAreaCost_NoEnemy. Three readers: 0x4C9D03, 0x4D5C73 and 0x4D6D4B / 0x4D6E63 / 0x4D7826. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)
+0x4 inside it: target_area_provinces_last (void*) - Tail of the CList at +0x1CC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)
+0x8 inside it: target_area_provinces_count (int) - Count of the CList at +0x1CC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: air_target_provinces_default
fields.comment:
Head of a CList (tail +0x200, count +0x204; nodes {payload, prev, next, byte} with the link at +8), kept **lowest-score-first** by CList_InsertByAscendingScore (0x4DD590). The payload is a 0x10-byte CPersistent record - vftable 0x15EB644, save id 0x18D at +4, a province id at +8 and a float at +0xC - built at 0x4B4C1B-0x4B4C45. It is *not* the 0x1C scored-province record used by +0x2C0.

**Writer: CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists (0x4B4740)**, called once per agent from CAIUnit::Tick at 0x4B0A4F and gated by `air_target_lists_built (+0x83)`. It clears this list at 0x4B47C2 and appends one record per candidate air-base province at 0x4B4C68.

**Reader: CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 2**, which picks one of the four by the wing's air role at 0x4CE253-0x4CE27B and scores it for a `rebase_air` destination. So these are **candidate air bases, ranked by proximity to the set each list is for** - this one's float is the mean distance to the agent's `ops_area (+0x90)` (or, when `manage_reserve (+0x364)` is clear, to the enemy's home air bases), blended 1:3 with the mean distance to `invasion_target_provinces (+0x1AC)` when that vector is non-empty. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

fields.name: air_target_provinces_strategic
fields.comment:
The +0x1FC list used for a wing carrying a strategic bomber, or whose definition's `strategic_attack (+0x17C)` exceeds 50000; selected at 0x4CE259-0x4CE26E. Same node and payload shape as +0x1FC.

**Written by CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists**: cleared at 0x4B47D1, appended at 0x4B4CC1, with the float being the mean map distance from the candidate base to `strategic_target_provinces (+0x18C)` (0x4B4C84). Lowest first. So a strategic bomber is rebased towards the provinces the force planner has already marked as strategic-bombing targets. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

fields.name: air_target_provinces_naval
fields.comment:
The +0x1FC list used for a wing carrying a naval bomber; selected at 0x4CE270-0x4CE27B. Same node and payload shape as +0x1FC.

**Written by CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists**: cleared at 0x4B47E0, appended at 0x4B4D1A, with the float being the mean map distance from the candidate base to `enemy_sighting_provinces (+0x19C)` (0x4B4CDD) - the provinces enemy units have been sighted in. Lowest first. So the naval-bomber list is 'bases near where we last saw the enemy', which is what makes it the naval one in practice rather than by any test on water. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

fields.name: air_target_provinces_transport
fields.comment:
The +0x1FC list used for a wing carrying a transport plane, and only when the vector at +0x16C/+0x170 is empty; selected at 0x4CE29F-0x4CE2A5. Same node and payload shape as +0x1FC.

**Written by CAIUnit::BuildAirTargetProvinceLists**: cleared at 0x4B47EF, appended at 0x4B4E00, with the float being the mean map distance from the candidate base to `invasion_target_provinces (+0x1AC)` (0x4B4DC9).

**But the writer's gate is the reader's gate inverted** (see AirTargetTransportListGate, 0x4B4D1F): nothing is appended here unless `(+0x170 - +0x16C)/4 > 0` and some unit in that vector sits in the candidate's area or an adjacent one, while phase 2 skips the wing outright when that vector is non-empty. Within one pass the two conditions are mutually exclusive, so whatever phase 2 reads out of this list was built on an earlier pass - the lists are rebuilt only on a replan, the vector every pass. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

fields.name: known_enemy_convoys
fields.comment:
Head of a CList of **convoy object id pairs** - each node holds the id type at +0, the serial at +4 and the next node at +0xC, the same shape as the +0x25C enemy_units_sighted list.

CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits' convoy-raid block is the only reader found: at 0x4D2526 it walks the list, resolves each pair through FindPersistentById against the persistent database at [0x1A857F0] (id type above 0x1268) or [0x1A857F4] (at or below), and scores the resolved object's `path` for a submarine raid target. That the resolved object is a CConvoy is not an inference - `CConvoy::GetDesiredTransports` is called on it twice (0x4D27F9, 0x4D288B) and `CConvoy +0xB0 path` / `+0xB8 path_count` are read as the record describes them.

Nothing writes it in either body, and what fills it was not looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

fields.name: enemy_units_sighted_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList of unit object id pairs - each node holds the id type at +0, the serial at +4 and the next node at +0xC - which both force planners resolve through the id registry (0x1A857F0 / 0x1A857F4) at 0x4B7550 and 0x4B5A00 and then count brigade by brigade to size the anti-ship wants. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF802, filled by the unidentified CEU3AI helper 0x48C140 (0x48CB21). The pair to +0x26C, which is walked the same way and **decrements** the same wants. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: enemy_units_lost_first
fields.comment: Head of a second CList of unit id pairs in the same form as +0x25C, walked by 0x4B78B3..0x4B7A0A. Every arithmetic step there is the mirror image of the +0x25C loop's: `dec want[...]` instead of `inc`, and the naval threat score has 0.07 / 0.15 / 0.02 subtracted instead of added. So the two lists are sightings gained and sightings lost. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4AF81A, filled by 0x48C140 (0x48D4E6). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: front_province_scores
fields.comment:
One of the AI's circular-sentinel ordered maps (comparator byte here, sentinel node at +0x298, size at +0x29C; nodes {next, prev, key, value}), keyed by a front province from +0xC0 and holding **a 0..100 nearness score, 100 on the front province closest to the unit's own plan objectives**. CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches builds it in two passes: the mean CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces from each plan objective in the same owner area (0x4BBF98, through AIOrderedMap_SubscriptFloat), then an in-place rescale to `(max - v) * 100 / (max - min)` at 0x4BC120-0x4BC1E8, skipped when every mean is equal. Nothing in 0x4AF000-0x4E0000 reads it besides the constructor, the destructor and that function; its subscript 0x4DCE40 has only two callers in the whole image, so **0x4D57F0 is the only possible consumer** and that function is unread.

**The name is doubtful - live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save.** Read live: **0xB6** on a freshly created agent and **0xB5** on the tick-0 agents, but **0x6F697412** on a live attached one and 0x532025CA on a detached one. No map size plausibly takes those values, so this is either not a size or not one field. What it *is* good for is a **state signature**: small means a fresh agent, large means one that has been attached, which is how the two kinds of unattached agent above were told apart. Treat the name as `inferred` and do not build on it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: front_province_scores_sentinel
fields.comment: The sentinel node of the ordered map at +0x294. CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches tears the map down by writing `[sentinel] = sentinel` and `[sentinel+4] = sentinel` at 0x4BBD66/0x4BBD6B, which is the family's circular-list reset, and uses it as `end()` when it walks the map at 0x4BC1DC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: front_province_scores_count
fields.comment: Size of the ordered map at +0x294; zeroed at 0x4BBD6E and incremented at 0x4BC1A2. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: unknown_2a4
fields.comment: Begin of a vector (end at +0x2A8) that CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches clears at 0x4BBD9E-0x4BBDBE with the usual zero-length-memmove-then-`end = begin` idiom and then never fills; its begin is handed to 0x10F4A0 at 0x4BBDCD with ecx = 0x10 and the map's sentinel as the second argument. What it holds is not established, and the windowed scan that found no other toucher covered only 0x4AF000-0x4E0000. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: unknown_2a8
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x2A4; see that field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: unknown_2b4
fields.comment: Written to the constant **7** by CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches at 0x4BBDD8 (as `[edi+0x20]` with edi = agent + 0x294) and by nothing else this pass found. Meaning not established. Beware when scanning for it: `[reg+0x2B4]` across the AI module is overwhelmingly CMapProvince::area, which is trap 12. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: unknown_2b8
fields.comment: Written to the constant **8** by CAIUnit::RebuildFrontAndApproaches at 0x4BBDDF, immediately after +0x2B4 gets 7. Meaning not established. The `movss [eax+0x2B8]` sites in CAIUnit::ClearUnit are CUnit +0x2B8, a different object. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: scored_provinces_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList (last +0x2C4, count +0x2C8) of the 0x1C scored-province records, kept in **descending score order** by CList_InsertByDescendingScore (0x4DD4B0) on the float at `record->+8`. CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces empties it through CListOfOwned_Clear at 0x4BD30A and appends one record per ops-area province. Its consumers pair it with the map at +0x2D0, or with (+0x2FC, +0x30C) instead when `unit->plan_stance` (CUnit +0x208) is 0 - which is the pair CAIUnit::RebuildOpsAreaProvinceRecords builds, and that function is called only at stance 0. Both switch sites: 0x4CC4B9-0x4CC4E9 and 0x4DCB20-0x4DCB2E, reached from CAIUnit::Tick at 0x4B0BC2 and 0x4B09F0. Record layout: +0 the province, +8 the score, +0xC the amount apportioned to it by 0x4C93B6, +0x18 a per-province cap. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: scored_provinces_last
fields.comment: Tail of the CList at +0x2C0; the insert walks backwards from here. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: scored_provinces_count
fields.comment: Count of the CList at +0x2C0, bumped by CList_InsertByDescendingScore at 0x4DD531 and tested for zero by 0x4DCB34 before the list is walked. **The `byte [reg+0x2C8]` reads and writes in CAIUnit slot 78, CAIUnit::ClearUnit and CAIUnit::SetPlanStance are CUnit +0x2C8, not this** - ClearUnit compares its base against `agent->unit` two instructions earlier and slot 78 reads `oob_level` off the same register. Trap 12. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: scored_province_map
fields.comment: An AI circular-sentinel ordered map, CMapProvince* -> the 0x1C scored-province record, with the same layout as +0x294 (comparator here, sentinel +0x2D4, size +0x2D8). CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces empties it through AIOrderedMap_Clear at 0x4BD305 and fills it through AIOrderedMap_Subscript at 0x4BDC6A, one entry per ops-area province, beside the list at +0x2C0. Read by 0x4CC450, which pairs the two and swaps both for (+0x2FC, +0x30C) at plan stance 0. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: focus_owner_areas_first
fields.comment: Head of a CList of `COwnerArea*` (0x10-byte nodes, payload at `+0`, next at `+8`), with the tail at `+0x33C` and the count at `+0x340`. **Rebuilt by CAIUnit::RebuildFocusOwnerAreas (0x4B0D20)**, which SetArea calls at 0x4BA679 before reading it: the entries come from the agent's theatre's `+0x84` list through 0x4B0F20. CAIUnit::SetArea then walks it at 0x4BA843-0x4BAA92 and, for each owner area 0x495140 approves, pulls in every front of every theatre of the country controlling that area - so this list is what lets a theatre agent claim ground on a front that is not its own theatre's. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: unknown348
fields.comment: Zeroed at the top of slot 78 (0x4B1F59), with the seven containers it rebuilds. Nothing else in the slot bodies read here touches it. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: apportion_a
fields.comment: One of two floats 0x4BD270 zeroes at the top of every replan (0x4BD2F5); `+0x350` is the other. Nothing read in this pass writes them again, because 0x4BD270's middle was not read. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: apportion_b
fields.comment: The second of the two floats 0x4BD270 zeroes at 0x4BD2FD. See `+0x34C`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: divisions_needed
fields.comment: What CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed last returned - the number of divisions the agent's theatre wants. Written only by CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower at 0x4B50AD. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: divisions_counted
fields.comment: What CAIUnit_SumOurPower last returned - how many `oob_level == 4` units it added up. Written only by CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower at 0x4B509C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: our_power
fields.comment: The agent's own copy of the figure it pushes into `CUnitPlan::our_power`. Zeroed and refilled by CAIUnit::UpdatePlanPower at 0x4B5088/0x4B508E, compared against the plan's value a thousandth at a time, and sent on through CSetPlanAttributesCommand's sixth argument. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: their_power
fields.comment: The agent's own copy of `CUnitPlan::their_power`; the out parameter CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed fills at 0x4B50A2/0x4B50A8, and the command's seventh argument. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: manage_reserve
fields.comment: Read into a local at the top of slot 78 (0x4B1FFC) and tested once, at 0x4B279F and again at 0x4B2A19: clear, every division is pushed straight onto the held-back vector at +0x15C and the whole reserve calculation is skipped with a surplus of -2. So this byte is what switches the commitment and reserve logic on. No writer was found in slot 78, 79 or 0x4B60F0. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: frontier_war_candidate
fields.comment: Set by CAIUnit::ClassifyOpsAreaFrontier (0x4BDF30) at 0x4BE14A when CAIStrategy::IsWarCandidate (0x4A9A30) accepts a neighbour of the operations area, and also implied by `+0x364`'s word write. So `+0x364` is "shooting war on my frontier" and `+0x365` is the weaker "war I might start". (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: frontier_controlled
fields.comment: Seeded 1 by the constructor; zeroed and recomputed by CAIUnit::ClassifyOpsAreaFrontier (0x4BDF30). Set to 1 for an operations area province unless all three of: `gamestate +0xD0C` is zero, the province's controller is not this agent's country, and the owner AI's `+0x2C` is set. Since `+0x2C` is set exactly for an AI-run country, the byte can only stay zero for a province an AI country does not control. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: invasion_transport_need
fields.comment: Extra transport ships an amphibious plan needs. CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion zeroes it at 0x492489 and adds `tonnageShort / transportCapacity + 1` at 0x4935DE; the force planner adds it straight onto the transport-ship want at 0x4B74F0. One writer and one reader, which is what makes the name safe. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: invasion_brigade_need
fields.comment: Extra brigades an amphibious plan needs. CEU3AI::PlanAmphibiousInvasion zeroes it at 0x492483 and adds a brigade shortfall at 0x493756. **It is the additive term in both force planners' brigade demand** - `+0x370 + round(need * shortage * 3)` at 0x4B626D and `+0x370 + need * 3` at 0x4B528B - so an invasion the AI is planning raises the land demand of the whole theatre. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_count

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: air_stance
fields.comment:
The air stance, 0..2, and the same field as `CUnit +0x20C plan_air_stance` (the plan is embedded at CUnit +0x1FC).

**1 is both the constructed and the reset value**: the constructor writes 1 at 0x4DE9EF and CUnitPlan::SetActive's deactivate arm writes 1 again at 0x4DEB78. 0 comes only from CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan's command (0x4DAD74) and switches the air body's phase 4 off entirely; 2 comes from CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances's command (0x4916AD) and from the interface, and is what phase 4's strategic and naval arm requires. 3 is not a value of this field at all - it is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "leave this one alone" sentinel, tested at 0x1E78C4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: Children
fields.comment:
read by CUnit::GetChildren. Reached only because the engine hands it in - no constructor and nothing returns one, but scripts use it (scripts/luacensus.py), inherited from CUnit
+0x8 inside it: children_count (int) - The count of the `children` CList at +0x1E4. Read as `> 0` meaning 'this unit has subordinates' by CAIUnit slot 76 (0x4DC026, 0x4DC5E2), slot 84 (0x4C17FE) and others, which is how those passes tell a leaf unit from an HQ. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md), inherited from CUnit

Also the guard on reading the first brigade in `AddRegimentToUnit` and `RemoveRegimentFromUnit`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md), inherited from CUnit

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: loaded_parent
fields.comment: The id half of the parent a save's `parent` key named (the type half at +0x58), read by CArmy::LoadKey; CUnit::CUnit zeroes both (0x5B5091). CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent (0x1CEDC0) resolves it as the game is entered and attaches the unit. Only a carried unit is saved with `parent`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_difference
fields.comment: Per CSubUnitDefinition::type_index: what the plan wants of that type minus what the unit's OOB actually has. Signed - a negative entry is a surplus. Written wholesale by CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (0x1BD240) and cleared by CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds for an HQ that has no plan. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_group_difference
fields.comment: The same differences summed onto one representative subunit type per group (0x1ADF70 does the folding: carrier air, capital ship, transport/submarine, and so on). Zeroed at the top of each pass and accumulated at 0x1BD544. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_needed
fields.comment: Per subunit type, the part of the deficit that the group as a whole is still short of - min(difference[i], whatever is left of that group's net difference), taken in index order. This is the list the plan machinery asks for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: shadowed_by_patrol
fields.comment: **Set on a fleet a patrol is shadowing**, and cleared when the patrol lets go: CPatrolOrder::UpdateShadow is its only writer in the naval order code (0x59CED5 clears, 0x59D17F sets). ShouldStartNavalCombat doubles the figure of every roll made against a fleet that has it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: is_reserve
fields.comment: The unit's own `is_reserve` key, token 0x57F, a plain ParseBool. **Its one use in the loader is to be copied onto each brigade read after it**: the `regiment` case of CUnit::LoadKey tests it either side of the brigade's own load and sets CSubUnit +0xA4. Nothing goes back over brigades already read, and the `wing` case does not test it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: was_paradropped
fields.comment: **Set on a land unit dropped by a paradrop into a province whose controller is at war with the dropper** (CAir::DropCarried, 0x5D0AF6 - the only writer but the constructor's zero), and saved as `was_paradropped` only where set. While it is set: CUnit::StartAttackDelay uses PARATROOP_MISSION_DELAY; CCombat::GetCombatWidth counts no paratrooper after the first; BM_PARATROOP_PENALTY applies (PARADROP_PENALTY + trait paradrop_mission, FINDINGS-combatmods.md); and BM_LACK_OF_SUPPLIES does not. CUnit::UpdateHourly clears it the first hour the unit is in no battle and multiplies every brigade's organisation by PARATROOP_DROP_ORG_MULT (military +0xA4, 0.66) / 1000. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: home_base_ptr
fields.comment: The object that knows the unit's base province - for an air unit, its airbase: its **slot 0 returns a `CMapProvince*`**, which `COrder::OrderReturnToBase` and `CAirInterceptOrder`'s slots 13 and 14 all compare against `CUnit + 0x130`. `CAir::UpdateDaily` (rva 0x1D0B60) opens by reading it, and every air order treats a null here as 'no mission possible' - `CAirInterceptOrder` slot 14 returns 'order finished' outright. `COrder::IsTargetInRange` also skips the range test when it is null. Its class has not been identified. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: no_bombing_hours
fields.comment: The twin of +0xA0 for a bombing: CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat writes 2 where the unit is in one (+0x110, at 0x5BA335) and takes one off at its end. Its readers were not looked for; the name is by the likeness. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: no_battle_hours
fields.comment: **The hours an air unit cannot be drawn into a battle.** CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat writes 2 at its start where the unit is an air unit in a battle (0x5BA350) and takes one off at its end; CCombatManager::StartCombat and JoinCombatInProvince refuse a unit with it above nothing. So an air unit out of a battle has one hour in which it may move and cannot be fought. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: upgrade_prio
fields.comment: **The unit's priority, for reinforcement as much as for upgrades**, saved as `is_prioritized`. CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute (0x51BC4F) and CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute (0x51CF96, 0x51D087) both read it for the same thing: a unit with it set joins the front of the list the share works through, the rest the back. The constructor clears it. The name is older than the second reader and is left as it is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: upgrade_active
fields.comment: Whether the unit's brigades are re-equipped, saved as `can_upgrade`. CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute leaves a unit with it clear out of its list (0x51CF82, 0x51D07A). **The constructor sets it**, so a unit upgrades unless told not to. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: reinforcements_active
fields.comment: Whether the unit's brigades are brought back to strength, saved as `can_reinforce`. CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute leaves a unit with it clear out of its list (0x51BC42, 0x51BD26). **The constructor sets it.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: disengage_to
fields.comment: The id of the province a fleet in a battle is to go to once it has counted its `disengage` (+0xA8) up: CMoveCommand::RouteUnit puts an ordered move here in place of a path, CUnit::RetreatFromCombat where a fleet beaten in one battle is still in another, and the tail of CNavalCombatant::Attack finds the path once WantsToDisengage. CUnit::ShowFighting zeroes it with the count. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: move_not_before
fields.comment: An hour before which the unit does not move at all: CUnit::AdvanceMovement returns while the game's hour is under it. Set to the null date by CMoveCommand::RouteUnit and CUnit::CancelMovement together with `end_date`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: hours_attacking
fields.comment: How many hours the unit has been attacking - in a battle, with a path and some progress. Counted up in CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat; once the battle is over and it is at most UNIT_ATTACK_DELAY_PERIOD the attack delay is cut to that share, and it is zeroed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment:
**The combat modifiers acting on this unit, on land only**, a CList: first here, last at +0xE0, count at +0xE4, all three cleared together by CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers (0x1C2FE0). One node per modifier; the node's record holds the id at +0 and the attack and defend values at +4 and +8, which the tooltip prints as `x%/y%` when they differ. 0x164060 turns the id into its BM_* key. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x4 inside it: combat_modifiers_last (LinkedListNode*) - The list's last node - the `last` of the CList at +0xDC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x8 inside it: combat_modifiers_count (int) - How many modifiers are on the list. **The one to watch** when looking for what adds to it: the head at +0xDC is only written by a push onto an empty list, while every addition has to touch this. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every modifier's attack side**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1C3040) multiplies each one in as it is added - `product = product * (delta + 1000) / 1000` - and CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers seeds it with 1000, an empty product. The battle tooltip prints `+0xEC * +0xF4 / 1000` as its Attack Modifier (0x32AE39). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every modifier's defend side**, the same shape as +0xEC and filled by the same function. The tooltip prints `+0xF0 * +0xF8 / 1000` as its Defend Modifier (0x32AE8A). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: landing_attack_scale
fields.comment: **The landing's attack scale**, thousandths: 1000 but for a land unit landing from the sea on enemy ground, for which CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (slot 19) sets AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_ATTACK_LOW + (HIGH - LOW) * CUnit::MovementProgressShare / 1000 every battle hour after CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers put it back to 1000. CLandCombatant::FireUnit multiplies the unit's shot count by +0xEC * +0xF4 / 1000 (0x16AED2); the battle tooltip prints it as AMPH_INVASION_ATTACK_SCALE where it is not 1000 and folds it into the Attack Modifier. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: landing_defend_scale
fields.comment: **The landing's defence scale**, thousandths: 1000 but for a land unit landing from the sea on enemy ground, for which slot 19 sets low + (AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_DEFEND_HIGH - low) * MovementProgressShare / 1000 with low = AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_DEFEND_LOW + the carrying fleet's summed amphibious_invasion_defence. CLandCombatant::FireUnit multiplies the unit's defence as a target by +0xF0 * +0xF8 / 1000 (0x16B0CB); the tooltip prints it as AMPH_INVASION_DEFEND_SCALE where it is not 1000. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: heading
fields.comment: Which way the unit faces: the angle from its province's unit point to the next province's, less pi/2, as CUnit::FaceNextProvince works it out. Its avatar's figure and the pointer beside its counter are turned by it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: heading_copy
fields.comment: Written with the same angle as `heading` (+0x104) by both of its writers, one instruction apart. What reads this one apart from that was not looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: avatar_stale
fields.comment: the avatar is to be made again: set when the intel level changes or the unit crosses between land and sea (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: current_combat
fields.comment: The combat the unit is in right now, distinct from the combats list at +0x114. Tested by GrantCombatExperience (0x1C433A, and at the call site 0x1BA54B) and cleared by CCombatant::DetachAllUnits when the combat ends (0x165D11). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaders.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: previous_province_ptr
fields.comment: The province the unit was in before the one it is in. CUnit::AdvanceMovement stores `current_province_ptr` here immediately before CUnit::EnterProvince, and the save key is `previous`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: movement_order_next_province_ptr
fields.comment: **The first node of the unit's path**, a CList of province ids - not a province pointer. The next province is `map->provinces[*node]`. With +0x13C and +0x140 it is the list's first, last and count; +0x144 is its no-unlink byte. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: movement_order_last_current_province_ptr
fields.comment: **The last node of the unit's path** (see +0x138). CMoveCommand::RouteUnit starts an appended route from `map->provinces[*this]`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: path_no_unlink
fields.comment: The `no_unlink` byte of the path's CList at +0x138: where set, a node reached is marked rather than freed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: arrow_percent
fields.comment: How far along the way to the next province the unit is, in whole per cent, capped at 100: `movement_progress * 100 / distance`. Written by CUnit::AdvanceMovement each hour. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: arrow_step_percent

fields.name: defences_used
fields.comment: **How many shots this unit has already defended against this tick.** CUnit::RollToHit compares it against the slots its defence value bought and increments it on each one spent; past that the unit falls back to CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF. Reset per tick somewhere not yet found. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CUnit

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_agent
fields.comment:
**The CAIUnit that commands this unit**, or null. Written by CAIUnit::SetUnit (slot 63, at 0x4B9F04) and only when both of the agent's flags +0x3D and +0x3E are clear; CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits skips any unit that already has one, and SetUnit calls the previous agent's slot 64 to detach it. CAIUnit::Tick and slots 76, 78, 83, 84 and 86 all read it.

**Retyped 2026-10-01 from `CAIUnit*`, and this one matters.** `CAIInvasion::AddUnit` (slot 63, at `0x8A16D7`) writes a **`CAIInvasion*`** here under the same two-flag guard, so the field holds either of two `CAIAgent` subclasses. Anything that reads it and assumes a `CAIUnit` can get a `CAIInvasion` and then read `+0x64` - the unit pointer on a `CAIUnit` - out of the middle of the invasion's transport list. Check the vftable, or slot 65/66 (`CAIUnit` has `mov al,1` at 65 and `xor al,al` at 66; `CAIInvasion` is the mirror), before treating it as a `CAIUnit`. See `FINDINGS-aitheatre.md`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: trespassing
fields.comment: **The unit stands where its owner may not enter** - CCountry::MayEnterProvince(owner, false, province) answers no (never set for REB). Recomputed every hour by CUnit::UpdateHourly (0x5B9D33-0x5B9D70, both ways) and at once by UnitList_MarkTrespassers on a diplomatic change (CCountry::OnDiplomacyChanged) and on entering a session; cleared by the constructor and by the AI (0x8E35A1, 0x8E3BBB). A trespasser cannot be the attacking unit of CUnit::CanEngage, takes no province in CheckForCombat, moves at full speed whatever its fuel, may stand in land owned by the owner of the province it is in (CArmy::MayStandIn), and is pulled home by the AI (CAIUnit_PullHeadquartersIn). Nothing moves it by itself. A declaration of war makes no trespassers among the belligerents, since war is itself leave to enter. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: subunit_group_present_begin
fields.comment: begin of a vector of one int per entry of `g_CSubUnitDataBase`'s definition vector, ending at +0x1D4. `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` zeroes it (0x1B5F80) and then writes 1 at each brigade definition's `unit_group` (+0x1B4) index (0x1B6123); afterwards it walks the vector from index 1 and totals the +0x28 of each marked definition into `base_ca_bonus` (+0x1CC). So this is **which combined arms groups the unit's composition covers**. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: subunit_group_present_end

fields.name: intel_level
fields.comment: **How well the screen's country knows this unit**: 9 for its own units and its friends' (the same real faction, or an alliance in the owner's status towards it), else the byte of `intel_by_country` for it in the province the unit is in (0 unseen, 3 partial, 9 own). Written by CUnit::EnterProvince and **every hour for every unit of every country by RunHourlyTick** (0x6822C8..0x6823D7), which sets the avatar's rebuild byte (+0x10C) where it changed. Under 2 its stack is not drawn, under 3 its counter shows the unknown picture, under 5 its name is `???`, under 7 its two figures are `?`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan
fields.comment:
The unit's battle plan, **held by value, not by pointer** - CUnit's constructor builds a CUnitPlan in place here at 0x1B5232 and its destructor destroys it in place at 0x1B5799. 0x90 bytes, so it runs to +0x28B and expeditionary_owner at +0x28C is the next field. Every plan field already recorded on CUnit is this object's offset plus 0x1FC: +0x204 plan_active = plan +0x8, +0x208 plan_stance = +0xC, +0x20C plan_air_stance = +0x10, +0x210 plan_naval_stance = +0x14, +0x26C plan_subunit_wanted = +0x70, +0x27C plan_our_power = +0x80, +0x280 plan_their_power = +0x84. The save writes it under `plan` by calling slot 1 on it, which works because +0x1FC is the embedded object's own vftable pointer. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x8 inside it: plan_active (unsigned char) - CUnitPlan +0x8. Whether the unit's battle plan is switched on; CUnitPlan::SetActive (0x4DEB10) resets the whole plan when it goes to zero. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0xC inside it: plan_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0xC, the `stance` key. Defaults to 2 when the plan is switched off. The one plan attribute whose change makes CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute call CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds; 5 is the command's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x10 inside it: plan_air_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0x10, the `air_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it.

**Every writer in the image, and who reaches it:**

| writer | value | path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute, store at 0x1E7907 | the command's `+0x6C`, skipped when it is 3 | the only store by this displacement; everything below goes through it |
| CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan, 0x4DE9EF | 1 | construction, so 1 is every unit's starting value |
| CUnitPlan::SetActive(plan, 0), 0x4DEB78 | 1 | deactivating a plan resets it; reached from CActivateUnitPlanCommand::Execute and CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit, both interface commands |
| CUnitPlan::LoadKey, 0x4DF93B | whatever the save holds | load |

And the seven places that post that command, by what they pass for air_stance: **2 from CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4916AD), for every unit agent, every ProcessAI pass**; 0 from CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan (0x4DAD74) when it builds a plan; 3 (leave alone) from CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (0x4C375E) and from the two power-estimate sites 0x4B5152 and 0x4B7E87; and the interface's own control at 0x35244E, which passes the value the player chose (0x351C8E is its naval twin and passes 3 here).

**So the AI drives this field to 2 by itself and the strategic air war is not player-only.** The sentinel-3 AI sites mean the ground-stance machinery never disturbs it.

**Live distribution (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save)**, unchanged and still worth reading with the above: 1 on 1,125 of 1,126 `CAir` formations and on 737 of 738 `CNavy`, and **2 on all 101 of the armies attached to a CAIUnit agent**. The air formations are not the objects phase 4's gate reads; the 101 armies are. And `+0x20C` and `+0x210` holding the identical value on all 4,864 objects read is explained: the AI's one writer sets both to 2 in the same command, and CUnitPlan's constructor and reset set both to 1. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x14 inside it: plan_naval_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0x14, the `naval_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x20 inside it: plan_ops_area_count (int) - CUnitPlan +0x18 is the plan's operations-area province CList; this is its count (first at CUnit +0x214, last +0x218). CAIUnit slot 76 tests it twice on its fallback path, at 0x4DBCDA and 0x4DBEB4, to decide whether a CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand is worth posting. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x38 inside it: plan_objectives (CList) - CUnitPlan +0x38 projected onto the unit (`plan` is held by value at CUnit +0x1FC), so this is the `objectives` block of the unit's battle plan: a list of CObjective, each 0x24 bytes, linked through its own +0x18/+0x1C. CAIUnit::Tick copies it into CArmy +0x2EC once a week through CopyObjectiveList (0x4DD350). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x40 inside it: plan_objectives_count (int) - Count of the plan's objective CList whose head is `plan_objectives` at +0x234 (CUnitPlan +0x38/+0x3C/+0x40). CAIUnit slot 84 compares it against the objective list it has just computed, and against how many of the two lists' provinces match, to decide whether a CSetPlanObjectivesCommand is needed (0x4C1B08-0x4C1B61). CTogglePlanObjectiveCommand::Execute increments it at 0x1E7036. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x48 inside it: plan_path_first (void*) - CUnitPlan +0x48 - the plan's `path`, a CList whose nodes carry a province id at +0x0 and chain through +0x8. **This is the list CAIUnit slot 76 walks first**: it follows the drawn path and stops at the last province whose successor the agent may not enter (CCountry::CanOperateIn), which is how the AI turns a drawn arrow into a frontier province to build a front around (0x4DAE8B-0x4DB0C3). read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x5C inside it: plan_path2_first (void*) - CUnitPlan +0x5C projected onto the unit (`plan` is held by value at CUnit +0x1FC, and 0x1FC + 0x5C = 0x258), so this is the `path2` block of the battle plan: a CList whose nodes carry a province id at +0x0 and chain through +0x8, exactly like plan_path_first at +0x244. CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits walks both at 0x4D5DCA and 0x4D5E9A and adds 90.0 to a front province's attack priority for being on either path and 45.0 for merely touching it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x70 inside it: plan_subunit_wanted (std::vector<int>) - The composition the plan asks for, per subunit type - the array 0x4E1D00 fills from the plan and the owner's available subunit types. Sits inside CUnit::plan at plan+0x70. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x74 inside it: plan_subunit_wanted_end (int*) - End of the std::vector<int> whose begin the record already has at +0x26C. 0x4B7D1C/0x4B7D25 takes (+0x270 - +0x26C) and compares it against the subunit database's own count before comparing the vectors element by element; CUnitPlan::SetMinForces replaces the pair. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x80 inside it: plan_our_power (int) - CUnitPlan +0x80, the `our_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the owner's strength for it. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x84 inside it: plan_their_power (int) - CUnitPlan +0x84, the `their_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the opposition's strength. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

Filled by CUnit_GrantIntel, whose caller is `local_intel_boost` (level 8, SPY_MILITARY_INTEL_LOCAL_TIME_BASE). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectrun.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_attack_fitness
fields.comment: **Per-pass scratch, written only by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits (0x4D714A) and read only by its own insertion sort (0x4D716F).** The fitness of this unit as a contributor to an attack on one particular target province: `enemyNeighboursOfItsOwnProvince * 10 - agent->slot89(target, unit, 1) * 10`, plus 100.0 when agent->slot88(unit) exceeds 95.0f, then divided by 10 when the unit answers to another agent and by 5 when UnitHasBlockingOrder accepts it. It is recomputed for every target province of every pass, so a value read out of a live game is only meaningful during that pass. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_uncovered_enemy_neighbours
fields.comment: **Per-pass scratch, written only by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits (0x4D715A).** The count, as a float, of enemy provinces adjacent to this unit's own province that are garrisoned (or whose owner is reinforcing them) and that nothing of ours is already ordered against. It is the single input to the stay-or-go decision: a unit with a non-zero value, sitting in a province with a supply depot and with no stand-in garrison available, is given a `support_attack` order instead of being marched into the target (0x4D7651, 0x4D7876). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_leader_fit
fields.comment: What AI_ReassignLeaders makes of how well the unit's leader suits it: 0 with no leader, else 0x499500's answer. Read for its shape only. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 8. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_held_back
fields.comment: **The AI's hysteresis bit on a division.** Slot 78 sets it (0x4B298B) when the division is pushed onto the held-back vector at CAIUnit +0x15C, and clears it (0x4B2CAC) when the division is recalled from it, at 0x4B2714/0x4B2746/0x4B2798 when the division is disqualified for other reasons, and sets it again at 0x4B3243 when a division is taken back out of the committed vector. While set, the strength bar the division has to clear to be committed rises from the commitment factor to halfway between it and 1.0, and the organisation bar from 0.300 to 0.650 (0x4B2835-0x4B2876); it is also worth +0.2 in the detachment score (0x4B30D4). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: unknown_2c9
fields.comment: One reader found, CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits at 0x4D6CE0: a non-zero value disqualifies a land unit from being considered as an attacker for the rest of the pass. No writer was looked for. It sits one byte before the recorded +0x2CA ai_pass_scratch, which slot 78 zeroes at the top of every unit iteration and never reads - worth checking whether the two are the same field and the earlier attribution was off by one. Named unknown deliberately. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_pass_scratch
fields.comment: Zeroed by slot 78 at the top of every unit iteration (0x4B2104) and not read anywhere in slot 78, 79, 0x4B60F0 or 0x4B82F0. Either a flag a later slot consumes or dead. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: movement_destination_province_id
fields.comment: The id of the province the unit is moving to, resolved against the game state's province array by CUnit::GetMovementDestinationProvince (0x49AF00); zero when it is not moving. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_defence
fields.comment: The cached half of AICombatEstimateDefenceValue (rva 0x4D8590), written at 0x4D8A88 with the dirty byte +0x2D8 cleared one instruction earlier and returned unchanged when that byte is zero. It holds a **sum of combat-modifier fractions** - 1.0 means +100% - covering the modifiers that depend on the unit alone: the fort_defence trait, combined arms, experience, the leader bonus, dig-in, the terrain defence adjuster, dissent, lack of supplies, the difficulty modifier and the encirclement penalty. The stacking and envelopment penalties are **not** in it, because they depend on the attackers; the helper subtracts those on every call. 'Defence' is now from the body, not just from which side uses it. CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (slot 31, rva 0x1BA2F0) sets this byte and the attack pair's at 0x1BA313/0x1BA31A and is still the only invalidation found, so how often the value is refreshed is how often slot 31 runs - which that entry records as not established. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aihelpers.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_defence_dirty
fields.comment: The dirty byte for +0x2D4. Non-zero means the AI's defensive combat-value helper (rva 0x4D8590) recomputes; the helper writes zero here at 0x4D8A81 as it stores the new value. Set to 1, together with +0x2E0, at the top of CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (rva 0x1BA313). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attackodds.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_attack
fields.comment: The cached half of AICombatEstimateAttackValue (rva 0x4D8C50), written at 0x4D8FC2 with the dirty byte +0x2E0 cleared at 0x4D8FBB and returned unchanged when that byte is zero. A **sum of combat-modifier fractions** - 1.0 means +100% - over the modifiers that depend on the unit alone: combined arms, experience, the leader bonus, dissent, lack of supplies and the difficulty modifier. The stacking penalty, the weather, the river or amphibious crossing penalty, the terrain attack adjuster and the fort penalty are **not** in it, because they depend on the target province and the two counts, and are recomputed on every call. 'Attack' is now from the body. Set dirty with +0x2D8 at the top of CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (rva 0x1BA31A), still the only invalidation found. fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_attack_dirty

fields.name: value
fields.comment:
**The operand, as a plain integer - not thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CIntTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D1400) as `atoi(text)`, which truncates, so the decimal a mod writes is lost before anything compares it. Zeroed instead when the argument was the keyword `this` (SaveToken 0x377) or `from` (0x34F), which set `CTrigger +0x18`/`+0x19`; only 3 of the 37 leaves read those flags back, so for the other 34 `keyword = this` degenerates to `field >= 0`.

Four leaves multiply this by 1000 inside their own Evaluate because the field they compare it against is thousandths - `revolt_risk`, `pure_revolt_risk`, `nationalism`, `province_temperature` - which is the one place the script number is the natural unit and still cannot carry a fraction. **`CValueTrigger::value` is the same offset with the opposite convention.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

Also the guard on reading the first brigade in `AddRegimentToUnit` and `RemoveRegimentFromUnit`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_difference
fields.comment: Per CSubUnitDefinition::type_index: what the plan wants of that type minus what the unit's OOB actually has. Signed - a negative entry is a surplus. Written wholesale by CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (0x1BD240) and cleared by CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds for an HQ that has no plan. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_group_difference
fields.comment: The same differences summed onto one representative subunit type per group (0x1ADF70 does the folding: carrier air, capital ship, transport/submarine, and so on). Zeroed at the top of each pass and accumulated at 0x1BD544. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan_subunit_needed
fields.comment: Per subunit type, the part of the deficit that the group as a whole is still short of - min(difference[i], whatever is left of that group's net difference), taken in index order. This is the list the plan machinery asks for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: shadowed_by_patrol
fields.comment: **Set on a fleet a patrol is shadowing**, and cleared when the patrol lets go: CPatrolOrder::UpdateShadow is its only writer in the naval order code (0x59CED5 clears, 0x59D17F sets). ShouldStartNavalCombat doubles the figure of every roll made against a fleet that has it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: is_reserve
fields.comment: The unit's own `is_reserve` key, token 0x57F, a plain ParseBool. **Its one use in the loader is to be copied onto each brigade read after it**: the `regiment` case of CUnit::LoadKey tests it either side of the brigade's own load and sets CSubUnit +0xA4. Nothing goes back over brigades already read, and the `wing` case does not test it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: was_paradropped
fields.comment: **Set on a land unit dropped by a paradrop into a province whose controller is at war with the dropper** (CAir::DropCarried, 0x5D0AF6 - the only writer but the constructor's zero), and saved as `was_paradropped` only where set. While it is set: CUnit::StartAttackDelay uses PARATROOP_MISSION_DELAY; CCombat::GetCombatWidth counts no paratrooper after the first; BM_PARATROOP_PENALTY applies (PARADROP_PENALTY + trait paradrop_mission, FINDINGS-combatmods.md); and BM_LACK_OF_SUPPLIES does not.
