fields.name: ai_agent
fields.comment:
**The CAIUnit that commands this unit**, or null. Written by CAIUnit::SetUnit (slot 63, at 0x4B9F04) and only when both of the agent's flags +0x3D and +0x3E are clear; CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits skips any unit that already has one, and SetUnit calls the previous agent's slot 64 to detach it. CAIUnit::Tick and slots 76, 78, 83, 84 and 86 all read it.

**Retyped 2026-10-01 from `CAIUnit*`, and this one matters.** `CAIInvasion::AddUnit` (slot 63, at `0x8A16D7`) writes a **`CAIInvasion*`** here under the same two-flag guard, so the field holds either of two `CAIAgent` subclasses. Anything that reads it and assumes a `CAIUnit` can get a `CAIInvasion` and then read `+0x64` - the unit pointer on a `CAIUnit` - out of the middle of the invasion's transport list. Check the vftable, or slot 65/66 (`CAIUnit` has `mov al,1` at 65 and `xor al,al` at 66; `CAIInvasion` is the mirror), before treating it as a `CAIUnit`. See `FINDINGS-aitheatre.md`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: trespassing
fields.comment: **The unit stands where its owner may not enter** - CCountry::MayEnterProvince(owner, false, province) answers no (never set for REB). A trespasser cannot be the attacking unit of CUnit::CanEngage, takes no province in CheckForCombat, moves at full speed whatever its fuel, may stand in land owned by the owner of the province it is in (CArmy::MayStandIn), and is pulled home by the AI (CAIUnit_PullHeadquartersIn). Nothing moves it by itself. A declaration of war makes no trespassers among the belligerents, since war is itself leave to enter. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md), inherited from CUnit

Written by CUnit::EnterProvince and **every hour for every unit of every country by RunHourlyTick** (0x6822C8..0x6823D7), which sets the avatar's rebuild byte (+0x10C) where it changed. Under 2 its stack is not drawn, under 3 its counter shows the unknown picture, under 5 its name is `???`, under 7 its two figures are `?`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: plan
fields.comment:
The unit's battle plan, **held by value, not by pointer** - CUnit's constructor builds a CUnitPlan in place here at 0x1B5232 and its destructor destroys it in place at 0x1B5799. 0x90 bytes, so it runs to +0x28B and expeditionary_owner at +0x28C is the next field. Every plan field already recorded on CUnit is this object's offset plus 0x1FC: +0x204 plan_active = plan +0x8, +0x208 plan_stance = +0xC, +0x20C plan_air_stance = +0x10, +0x210 plan_naval_stance = +0x14, +0x26C plan_subunit_wanted = +0x70, +0x27C plan_our_power = +0x80, +0x280 plan_their_power = +0x84. The save writes it under `plan` by calling slot 1 on it, which works because +0x1FC is the embedded object's own vftable pointer. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x8 inside it: plan_active (unsigned char) - CUnitPlan +0x8. Whether the unit's battle plan is switched on; CUnitPlan::SetActive (0x4DEB10) resets the whole plan when it goes to zero. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0xC inside it: plan_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0xC, the `stance` key. Defaults to 2 when the plan is switched off. The one plan attribute whose change makes CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute call CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds; 5 is the command's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x10 inside it: plan_air_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0x10, the `air_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it.

**Every writer in the image, and who reaches it:**

| writer | value | path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute, store at 0x1E7907 | the command's `+0x6C`, skipped when it is 3 | the only store by this displacement; everything below goes through it |
| CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan, 0x4DE9EF | 1 | construction, so 1 is every unit's starting value |
| CUnitPlan::SetActive(plan, 0), 0x4DEB78 | 1 | deactivating a plan resets it; reached from CActivateUnitPlanCommand::Execute and CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit, both interface commands |
| CUnitPlan::LoadKey, 0x4DF93B | whatever the save holds | load |

And the seven places that post that command, by what they pass for air_stance: **2 from CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4916AD), for every unit agent, every ProcessAI pass**; 0 from CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan (0x4DAD74) when it builds a plan; 3 (leave alone) from CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (0x4C375E) and from the two power-estimate sites 0x4B5152 and 0x4B7E87; and the interface's own control at 0x35244E, which passes the value the player chose (0x351C8E is its naval twin and passes 3 here).

**So the AI drives this field to 2 by itself and the strategic air war is not player-only.** The sentinel-3 AI sites mean the ground-stance machinery never disturbs it.

**Live distribution (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save)**, unchanged and still worth reading with the above: 1 on 1,125 of 1,126 `CAir` formations and on 737 of 738 `CNavy`, and **2 on all 101 of the armies attached to a CAIUnit agent**. The air formations are not the objects phase 4's gate reads; the 101 armies are. And `+0x20C` and `+0x210` holding the identical value on all 4,864 objects read is explained: the AI's one writer sets both to 2 in the same command, and CUnitPlan's constructor and reset set both to 1. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x14 inside it: plan_naval_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0x14, the `naval_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x20 inside it: plan_ops_area_count (int) - CUnitPlan +0x18 is the plan's operations-area province CList; this is its count (first at CUnit +0x214, last +0x218). CAIUnit slot 76 tests it twice on its fallback path, at 0x4DBCDA and 0x4DBEB4, to decide whether a CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand is worth posting. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x38 inside it: plan_objectives (CList) - CUnitPlan +0x38 projected onto the unit (`plan` is held by value at CUnit +0x1FC), so this is the `objectives` block of the unit's battle plan: a list of CObjective, each 0x24 bytes, linked through its own +0x18/+0x1C. CAIUnit::Tick copies it into CArmy +0x2EC once a week through CopyObjectiveList (0x4DD350). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x40 inside it: plan_objectives_count (int) - Count of the plan's objective CList whose head is `plan_objectives` at +0x234 (CUnitPlan +0x38/+0x3C/+0x40). CAIUnit slot 84 compares it against the objective list it has just computed, and against how many of the two lists' provinces match, to decide whether a CSetPlanObjectivesCommand is needed (0x4C1B08-0x4C1B61). CTogglePlanObjectiveCommand::Execute increments it at 0x1E7036. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x48 inside it: plan_path_first (void*) - CUnitPlan +0x48 - the plan's `path`, a CList whose nodes carry a province id at +0x0 and chain through +0x8. **This is the list CAIUnit slot 76 walks first**: it follows the drawn path and stops at the last province whose successor the agent may not enter (CCountry::CanOperateIn), which is how the AI turns a drawn arrow into a frontier province to build a front around (0x4DAE8B-0x4DB0C3). read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x5C inside it: plan_path2_first (void*) - CUnitPlan +0x5C projected onto the unit (`plan` is held by value at CUnit +0x1FC, and 0x1FC + 0x5C = 0x258), so this is the `path2` block of the battle plan: a CList whose nodes carry a province id at +0x0 and chain through +0x8, exactly like plan_path_first at +0x244. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x70 inside it: plan_subunit_wanted (std::vector<int>) - The composition the plan asks for, per subunit type - the array 0x4E1D00 fills from the plan and the owner's available subunit types. Sits inside CUnit::plan at plan+0x70. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x74 inside it: plan_subunit_wanted_end (int*) - End of the std::vector<int> whose begin the record already has at +0x26C. 0x4B7D1C/0x4B7D25 takes (+0x270 - +0x26C) and compares it against the subunit database's own count before comparing the vectors element by element; CUnitPlan::SetMinForces replaces the pair. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x80 inside it: plan_our_power (int) - CUnitPlan +0x80, the `our_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the owner's strength for it. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x84 inside it: plan_their_power (int) - CUnitPlan +0x84, the `their_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the opposition's strength. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: intel_grants

fields.name: ai_attack_fitness
fields.comment: **Per-pass scratch, written only by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits (0x4D714A) and read only by its own insertion sort (0x4D716F).** The fitness of this unit as a contributor to an attack on one particular target province: `enemyNeighboursOfItsOwnProvince * 10 - agent->slot89(target, unit, 1) * 10`, plus 100.0 when agent->slot88(unit) exceeds 95.0f, then divided by 10 when the unit answers to another agent and by 5 when UnitHasBlockingOrder accepts it. It is recomputed for every target province of every pass, so a value read out of a live game is only meaningful during that pass. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_uncovered_enemy_neighbours
fields.comment: **Per-pass scratch, written only by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits (0x4D715A).** The count, as a float, of enemy provinces adjacent to this unit's own province that are garrisoned (or whose owner is reinforcing them) and that nothing of ours is already ordered against. It is the single input to the stay-or-go decision: a unit with a non-zero value, sitting in a province with a supply depot and with no stand-in garrison available, is given a `support_attack` order instead of being marched into the target (0x4D7651, 0x4D7876). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: ai_held_back
fields.comment: **The AI's hysteresis bit on a division.** Slot 78 sets it (0x4B298B) when the division is pushed onto the held-back vector at CAIUnit +0x15C, and clears it (0x4B2CAC) when the division is recalled from it, at 0x4B2714/0x4B2746/0x4B2798 when the division is disqualified for other reasons, and sets it again at 0x4B3243 when a division is taken back out of the committed vector. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: unknown_2c9

No writer was looked for. fields.name: ai_pass_scratch

fields.name: movement_destination_province_id

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_defence

fields.name: ai_objectives

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: combat_status_billboard
fields.comment:
**CORRECTION - this field is not a GUI window.** It is a live **billboard** object (the 0xB48-byte class with vftable 0x16010D0, constructor rva 0x6B68F0), built from the `combat_status` **billboardType** declared in `interface/mapitems.gfx` inside an `objectTypes = { }` block. CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow (rva 0x17BD70) finds the type in the object-type registry at `CGraphics +0x6BCF0` (rva 0x17BE56) and calls its slot 18, CBillboardType::CreateInstance (rva 0x707340), caching the result here at 0x17BE7F. Slot 24 is `C3dVisibleObject::SetFrame` (rva 0x660460), a `short` at `+0x4E`, and it takes 0, 1 or 2 because the .gfx entry says `noOfFrames = 3`. The percentage text goes into the billboard's own caption `std::string` at `+0xB2C`. **Freed with the combat**, by CCombat::DestroyInterface (rva 0x16DF80), which zeroes this field - so it must be re-read, never cached across a combat ending. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md; the old wording called this a GUI window with an unidentified class.

**Renamed from `combat_status_window` 2026-10-02.** The old name was left in place when the comment above was corrected, which is the same mistake that once kept the word 'loss' in CSubUnit +0x54 after the owning function had been corrected - the comment said one thing and the name went on saying another. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md)

fields.name: combat_status_close_billboard
fields.comment:
**CORRECTION - this field is not a GUI element, and its slot 24 does take an argument.** It is a second live billboard of the same class as `+0x2C`, built from the `combat_status_close` billboardType in `interface/mapitems.gfx` (`scale = 1.7` against the other's 2.6, also three frames), cached at 0x17BF02. It gets the **same** frame index as `+0x2C`: slot 24 is `ret 4`, and the `push` that feeds the call at 0x57C29E was hoisted above the call at 0x57C292 by the compiler - the four arms at 0x57C208, 0x57C262, 0x57C26A, 0x57C278 and 0x57C290 each push the value twice. It gets the same SetPosition, UpdateTransform, SetRotation and caption treatment too. Freed beside `+0x2C` in CCombat::DestroyInterface (rva 0x16DF80). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md.

**Renamed from `combat_status_close_button` 2026-10-02.** The old name was left in place when the comment above was corrected, which is the same mistake that once kept the word 'loss' in CSubUnit +0x54 after the owning function had been corrected - the comment said one thing and the name went on saying another. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md)

fields.name: value
fields.comment:
**The operand, as a plain integer - not thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CIntTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D1400) as `atoi(text)`, which truncates, so the decimal a mod writes is lost before anything compares it. Zeroed instead when the argument was the keyword `this` (SaveToken 0x377) or `from` (0x34F), which set `CTrigger +0x18`/`+0x19`; only 3 of the 37 leaves read those flags back, so for the other 34 `keyword = this` degenerates to `field >= 0`.

Four leaves multiply this by 1000 inside their own Evaluate because the field they compare it against is thousandths - `revolt_risk`, `pure_revolt_risk`, `nationalism`, `province_temperature` - which is the one place the script number is the natural unit and still cannot carry a fraction. **`CValueTrigger::value` is the same offset with the opposite convention.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: modifier_used
fields.comment: **One bool per combat modifier id, at 8 + id** - +0x08 BM_DISSENT (0) through +0x25 BM_SURPRISE_BONUS (0x1D). CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590) zeroes exactly these 30 bytes at the top of every tick (three movq, a dword and a word, the same run CCombatant::CCombatant zeroes and which FINDINGS-combat.md records as 'all unnamed'), and every one of the 69 AddCombatModifier call sites writes `this->[8 + id] = 1` immediately after its call. Checked on all 24 distinct ids that have a site, with no exception; the two ids with no site, BM_ARMOR_ADVANTAGE (+0x1B) and BM_SURPRISE_PENALTY (+0x24), are never written. So this is the per-side 'which modifiers were in play this tick' set, and it is almost certainly what the battle UI reads to choose which rows to print. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)

fields.name: front_line
fields.comment:
**The units that actually fight this tick**, and the CList's own `count` at +0xB8 is how many. Distinct from `units` at +0x40, which is everyone on this side: CLandCombatant::Attack walks this one to decide who shoots, and CCombatant::PickTarget draws from the enemy's to decide who is shot at. **What puts a unit on it has not been read** - combat width is the obvious candidate and is not yet evidence.

**This is the land family's layout, not the base's (2026-10-05, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md).** The CList reading is right for CLandCombatant - its Attack does `lea esi, [ebx+0xB0]` and walks nodes at +8 from 0x16B3B0, and CCombatant::PickTarget takes the count from +0xB8 - and both of those are land. The air and bombing combatants use those bytes for a target array instead, and **the two layouts are the opposite way round** (corrected 2026-10-05, later the same day): CBomberCombatant keeps `target_count` at +0xB0 and `targets[1024]` at +0xB4 (0x160BD3, 0x160BDE), while CAirCombatant keeps `targets[1024]` at +0xB0 and the count at +0x10B0 (0x16D4C3, 0x16D4D0, 0x16D529). Both arrays are *derived* fields over the same 0xB0-byte base - RTTI gives CBomberCombatant : CCombatant and CGroundTargetCombatant : CBombTargetCombatant : CCombatant - so neither order constrains the other, and the first version of this note generalised the bomber's order onto the family wrongly. The 1024 bound is confirmed off `cmp eax, 0x400` at 0x16D4C9. Both classes now have struct records. The allocation sizes settle it: CLandCombatant is **0xE4** (0x17B4EB), CAirCombatant and the CBombTargetCombatant family **0x10B4**, CBomberCombatant **0x10E8** - and 0x10B4 - 0xB4 is exactly 0x1000, 1024 pointers. So sizeof(CCombatant) is 0xB0 and this field belongs on CLandCombatant, which has no struct record to move it to (mergeFindings cannot create one). Note the granularity difference it exposes: the land front line holds CUnit*, the air and bombing target arrays hold CSubUnit*. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: amount
fields.comment: Saved as `amount`: how many of the building; a new line's size, or what is added to a line already queued in the province (capped at the room left under max_allowed_level). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md)

fields.name: country
fields.comment: Saved as `country`: whose queue the line goes on and whose IsBuildingAllowed IsValid asks. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-buildingqueue.md)

fields.name: class_id
fields.comment: 0x18D for CHourlyTickCommand. Distinct from the type id at +0x2C/+0x30. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCommand

fields.name: name
fields.comment: Empty at construction in CHourlyTickCommand. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCommand

fields.name: type_id
fields.comment: The value virtual slot 7 returns; CHourlyTickCommand's constructor writes 0x28D here and at +0x30. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCommand

fields.name: type_id_2
fields.comment: Written with the same value as +0x2C by the constructor. Why there are two has not been established. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCommand

fields.name: issued_turn
fields.comment: WORD, not a byte. 0xFFFF until posted; the post writes the session's turn counter (session+0x54, zeroed if above 0x7FFF) here. Session::PumpCommands reads it at rva 0x689CD7 and can reject the command with 'Atempted to execute invalid order with stamp '. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCommand

fields.name: targeted_async
fields.comment: WORD, 0 for an ordinary command. When non-zero the post skips the serial and takes the 'Sending targeted asynchronous command: ' path instead of the queue. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCommand

fields.name: serial
fields.comment: A per-channel monotonic serial, taken with lock xadd on channel+0x88 (loopback) or channel+0xA8 (server) at post time, carried across the pump's clone by hand, and appended after Execute to the 100-entry history at session+0x220 that 'Command double! Skipping.' is decided against. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCommand

fields.name: country
fields.comment: Saved as `country`: whose queue the line goes on. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoylines.md)

fields.name: line_id_type
fields.comment: Type half of the id the new line takes (Execute hands &+0x44 to the line's SetId): 0x1268 + word[0x1A857EC], 4713 in the maintainer's saves. Saved as `id`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoylines.md)

fields.name: line_id
fields.comment: Serial half of that id, minted from the counter at 0x1A857F8, which then moves on by 1 + 2 * amount. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoylines.md)

fields.name: escorts
fields.comment: Saved as `status`, yes or no: escorts where set, transports where clear. The confirm dialog passes 1 in its mode 2 and 0 in mode 1; Lua passes its second argument. Copied to the line's +0x58. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoylines.md)

fields.name: amount
fields.comment: Saved as `amount`: how many in series - the new line's size, each item CONVOY_CONSTRUCTION_SIZE ships. The confirm dialog's serial count; the AI's 1 to 5. Not checked anywhere. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoylines.md)

fields.name: Cost
fields.comment:
read by CConstruction::GetCost. Reached only because the engine hands it in - no constructor and nothing returns one, but scripts use it (scripts/luacensus.py)
BiceLib: cost (int) - what it costs in IC, a CFixedPoint: the game's GetCost (0x837C0), which CCountry::GetUsedIC sums over the country's constructions (reversing/CLASSES.md:502)

fields.name: Size
fields.comment: read by CConstruction::GetSize. Reached only because the engine hands it in - no constructor and nothing returns one, but scripts use it (scripts/luacensus.py)

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the `id` pair, written after the id (BiceLib/GameClasses/CConstruction.hpp:29)

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the queue item's id (BiceLib/GameClasses/CConstruction.hpp:30)

fields.name: duration
fields.comment: x1000, saved as `duration` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CConstruction.hpp:33)

fields.name: progress
fields.comment: x1000, saved as `progress` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CConstruction.hpp:34)

fields.name: status
fields.comment: thousandths, saved as `status`: **the share of a full day's work the item received the last time the queue advanced** - 1000 for a full day, the part-paid amount for part, 0 for none. Written in one place, CConstruction::AddProgress, and initialised to 1000 by each constructor. **It has two readers**, both for the production screen: CBuildQueueEntry::Update shows a line green where it is above 990, orange above 0 and red at 0, and prints it as the line's speed; and CConstruction::GetEtaText divides the days left by it. On a convoy construction the key `status = yes` is taken by the derived loader before this field sees it. (BiceLib/GameClasses/CConstruction.hpp:39)

fields.name: location
fields.comment: where it is being built, saved as `location`. **Read live**: a CMapProvince on all 89 building items and null on the military and convoy ones, which are not placed (BiceLib/GameClasses/CConstruction.hpp:46)

fields.name: country
fields.comment: who it is for, saved as `country` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CConstruction.hpp:49)

fields.name: builder
fields.comment: who is building it, saved as `builder`. **Read live**: the same as `country` on every military item and the no-country tag `---` on every building and convoy one (BiceLib/GameClasses/CConstruction.hpp:54)

fields.name: items
fields.comment: Head of the list of what a military construction builds, one item per brigade: +0x18 its name, +0x34 its type, +0x38 the type it upgrades from, +0x40 the experience it inherits. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-productiontooltip.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-productiontooltip.md)

fields.name: item_count
fields.comment: How many items the list at +0x7C holds. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-productiontooltip.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-productiontooltip.md)

fields.name: accumulated_experience
fields.comment: Thousandths: what the queue line's BRIGADE_MIL_CON_CUMULATED_EXP shows to two places. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-productiontooltip.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-productiontooltip.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: the keyword, as a save token. The ten MakeScope switches on - `owner` 0x1EC, `controller` 0x1ED, `from` 0x34F, `ally` 0x359, `this` 0x377, `capital_scope` 0x3B4, `sea_zone` 0x3E8, `local_enemy` 0x621, `overlord` 0x631 - plus 0xC for a bare number and 0xF for an identifier, neither of which is in the compiled token table because both are the lexer's own classes (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: text
fields.comment: the keyword's text, copied verbatim; the 0x104 bytes from +0 are copied as one block (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: literal_province
fields.comment: `atoi(text)` when the text is a number - the `1234 = { ... }` form, which MakeScope answers with the province directly (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: literal_country_tag
fields.comment: `CCountryDataBase::GetTag(text)`, set only when `token` is 0xF - the `GER = { ... }` form (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: literal_country_id
fields.comment: the id half of the tag at +0x108. **MakeScope tests this against zero before its switch**, so a literal country tag wins over any keyword reading (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: spec
fields.comment: **What the script wrote on the left of `= { ... }`**, as a by-value `CEventScopeSpec` - the same 0x110-byte specification `CContextTrigger` keeps at +0x40. Built by `EventScopeSpec_Construct` (rva 0x5C1B30) from the constructor and resolved by `CEventScope::MakeScope` (rva 0x5C1C10) each time the effect runs. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CAndTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CAndTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CAndTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CAndTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CAndTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CAndTrigger

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: values
fields.comment: the values, one entry per ModifierType and indexed by it; CModifier::GetValue reads [this+0x18][type*8]. Typed as a structure of named entries so a read is a field rather than an index. **The index is the definition's registration order, which is CModifier::id only up to 101.** The global initialiser builds 108 definitions in array order but stamps ids that are not in that order at the end: entries 102..107 are LAND_INTEL_BOOST (id 103), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST (id 104), LOCAL_UNDERGROUND (id 102), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST a second time (id 104 again), STRATEGIC_RESOURCE_EFFICIENCY (id 105) and LOCAL_UNIT_SPEED (id 106). So an index below 102 can be read straight off reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py, and one at or above 102 has to be read off this structure instead - while a comparison against CModifier +0x24 `id` is the other way round. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: id
fields.comment: Which modifier this is. The constructor at rva 0x56D50 takes it in edx and writes it here, and it is what everything that asks about a modifier compares - CBuildingDataBase's role ladder at rva 0xB78AB is five of these in a row, deciding which building is the naval base, the air base, the anti-air, the underground and the industry. Typed as the ModifierId enum so those read as names; the enum is built by reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py out of the global initialiser, which is the only place the 107 names exist. (reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py)

fields.name: icon

The Strategic Effects window shows a triggered modifier's as the frame of `modifier_strip` (BuildTriggeredModifierEntry). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md, section 3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent

fields.name: values
fields.comment: Thousandths, one per ideology, indexed by CIdeology +0x4C. CIdeologyData::GetValue (Lua, 0x128480) is `[ecx+8][ideology->+0x4C]`; CalculateTotalSum sums it from index 1 to +0xC. CCountry +0x10C4 (organisation_by_ideology) and +0x10FC (popularity_by_ideology) are this field of the two embedded copies. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectrun.md)

fields.name: values_end
fields.comment: End of the `values` array; CalculateTotalSum's bound. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectrun.md)

fields.name: tallies
fields.comment: Begin of a vector of 16-byte per-party entries, each itself a vector<int> of **five** tally slots (the constructor sizes them to 5): **the month's account of what set each figure, by source** - slot 0 the election's scratch copy, 1 the effects (`organisation`, `popularity`, an ideology's block), 2 the history (C*Change::Apply through CIdeologyData_SetValue), 3 the espionage missions BOOST_RULING_PARTY and BOOST_OUR_PARTY, 4 the monthly drift. Every writer adds the **new figure**, not the change. Cleared once a month (CIdeologyData_ClearTallies) just after the drift; read only by CIdeologyData_BuildChangeTooltip, which shows slots 1 and 3. Not saved. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: tallies_end
fields.comment: End of the tallies vector; ClearTallies' bound. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: last_change
fields.comment: One int per party: **the total change the last monthly drift made** (drift + ruling-party support + the draw + the ministers' dissent penalty), written by CCountry_UpdatePartyPopularity for popularity only - organisation's is never written - and shown by CIdeologyData_BuildChangeTooltip as POL_PARTY_POP_FACTORS. Written even when the change was not applied because the result was negative. Not cleared and not saved. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: last_change_end
fields.comment: End of last_change. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: The country the object belongs to (CCountry +0x1198 = the country itself). StrategicWarfare_GetICScale reads its TotalIC; CStrategicWarfare::AddBombingImpact its sw_national_unity_effect. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: convoy_entries
fields.comment: The convoy list: nodes of 0x10 bytes holding an 8-byte {date (hours), value (thousandths)}; last at +0x1C, count at +0x20, flag byte at +0x24. Appended by CStrategicWarfare::AddConvoyImpact, pruned to a week by StrategicWarfare_PruneList, summed into ConvoyImpact (+0x8). Saved under `convoy`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: alliance_entries
fields.comment: The alliance list, the same shape (last +0x2C, count +0x30). Appended by CStrategicWarfare::AddAlliesImpact once a day per land battle; summed into AlliesImpact (+0xC). Saved under `alliance`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: bombing_entries
fields.comment: The ground-bombing list, the same shape (last +0x3C, count +0x40). Appended by CStrategicWarfare::AddBombingImpact; summed into BombingImpact (+0x10). Saved under `ground_bombing`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: random_state
fields.comment: **The scope's own random number state**, advanced in place. CEventScope's constructor (rva 0x5C1610) sets it from its EDX argument - the same value it puts in `seed` at +0x2C - and CEventScope::MakeScope passes `&scope->+8` to the LCG at rva 0x6A2E90, which reads the state, runs two steps of the MSVC `rand` recurrence (0x343FD / 0x269EC3) and writes the new state back before returning a 30-bit value. That is what picks the country for an `ally = { ... }` or `local_enemy = { ... }` context, so **those two contexts are deterministic given the scope's seed and advance it as a side effect**. The copy constructor copies it, so a rebound scope starts from wherever the parent had got to and advances its own copy. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: country_tag
fields.comment:
The three letters and a NUL of the `country` CCountryTag whose id half the record already has at +0x14. CEventScope::SaveContents (rva 0x5C1690) writes it as the `country` key by taking `strlen` of this address and making a string of it; CEventScope::LoadKey writes it and +0x14 together from CCountryDataBase::GetTag. The constructor sets it to `0x2D2D2D`, `"---"`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)
BiceLib: _Country (CCountryTag) - declared to Lua, by value - luabind's def_readwrite getter returns `CCountryTag&`, and the reference is the accessor's, not the member's. **No script can reach this**: CEventScope has no Lua constructor, nothing returns one, and nothing in the 300-file Lua corpus names it or any of its members - so the registration is abandoned and its name and type are unverified by use (scripts/luacensus.py)

fields.name: country_id
fields.comment: **the country the scope is about**, and what every effect indexes the country database with. The Lua API declares `_Country` at +0x10 as a `CCountryTag&` - that is its getter's return type, not the layout: the tag sits there **by value**, three letters at +0x10 and this id at +0x14, which is why CCountryTag::GetCountry is passed `scope + 0x10` (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

fields.name: from_country_tag
fields.comment: The letters of the **FROM** country, saved and loaded under the key `from_country` (token 0x61B); the id half is at +0x1C. The constructor sets it to `"---"`. CEventScope::MakeScope's `from` arm (token 0x34F) copies this pair into the new scope's `country`, which is what `FROM = { ... }` resolves to. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: from_country_id
fields.comment: Id half of the tag at +0x18, and the field SaveContents guards the `from_country` key on - a zero here means FROM has no country and the key is not written at all. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: rebel_faction_type
fields.comment: First half of the `{ type = N id = N }` object reference saved under the key `rebel_faction` (token 0x644). CEventScope::LoadKey reads it with **ParseObjectId** (rva 0x67B250) given `scope + 0x20`, which is the same call CReferenceObject::LoadKey makes with `this + 8` and the reason CMinister keeps `id_type` at 0x8 and `id` at 0xC; SaveContents writes the pair back through rva 0x6789F0. So a scope can be about a rebel faction as well as a country and a province, and nothing in the evaluation half read here ever looks at it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: rebel_faction_id
fields.comment: Second half of the object reference at +0x20 - the id ParseObjectId writes into `pair[1]`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: province
fields.comment:
**The province the scope is about**, saved and loaded under the key `province` (token 0x1EE). Everything that resolves a scope indexes a province array with it: CEventScope::MakeScope uses `g_CMap (0x1A8557C) + 0x2200` for the `owner`, `controller`, `sea_zone` and `local_enemy` contexts, and EventScope_GetCountryTag uses `g_CCurrentGameState (0x1A89790) + 0xB8C` to fall back on the province's owner when the scope names no country. Zero means the scope is not about a province; the constructor leaves it so, and every context that sets a country clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)
BiceLib: _nProvince (int) - declared to Lua. **No script can reach this**: CEventScope has no Lua constructor, nothing returns one, and nothing in the 300-file Lua corpus names it or any of its members - so the registration is abandoned and its name and type are unverified by use (scripts/luacensus.py)

fields.name: seed
fields.comment: The random seed the scope was built with, saved under the key `seed` (token 0x356) - the only one of the six keys SaveContents writes **unconditionally**. The constructor puts its EDX argument here and in the live state at +8 and +0xC, and at two of the call sites inspected that argument comes straight out of the generator at rva 0x6A2F80. So this is the seed as recorded and +8 is the state as it stands. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: from_province
fields.comment: The **FROM** province, saved and loaded under the key `from_province` (token 0x61C). CEventScope::MakeScope's `from` arm copies it into the new scope's `province`, beside the `from_country` pair. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: days_in_month
fields.comment:
The one field the two CEventScope builders disagree about. RebuildCountryEventCandidates sets it to the current month's length, recomputed at 0x5C0273-0x5C02E4 from state+0xBDC with the same 0x29C55C0 epoch and 365.0 constant (0x120A550) RunHourlyTick uses and then indexed into MonthLengthTable (0x1313294); RunDailyEventPass leaves it zero (0x5C0AAD). CMeanTimeToHappen::GetChance never reads the scope, only forwards it, so this can only matter to a trigger. **The name is inference from how the value is derived, not from a use.** CEventScope is 0x48 bytes, vftable 0x11B8AEC, base CPersistent; +0x10 and +0x18 are two CCountryTags, both 0x2D2D2D ("---") at construction and only +0x10 ever filled in with the country being scoped.

**Its reader is CDateTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D3100)**, which tests `tick + this * 24 >= date`: so in RebuildCountryEventCandidates' scope `date` is already true up to a month early, and in RunDailyEventPass' scope it is exact. That makes the field a look-ahead in days rather than a calendar fact; the name is kept because it says what the value is. `year` (0x5D2510) and `month` (0x5D2B30) do not read it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md)

fields.name: this_scope
fields.comment: **The scope the event was raised with - what `this = { ... }` means.** The constructor sets it to `this`, so it is never null and for an unrebound scope points at the scope itself; CEventScope::CopyConstruct copies the pointer verbatim, so every scope a context rebinds **still points at the original**. Two readers: CEventScope::MakeScope's `this` arm (token 0x377) takes the country and province off it, and EventScope_GetCountryTag (rva 0x5C1A40) resolves "which country is this scope about" through it rather than off the scope directly. Not saved. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: resolved
fields.comment: **Did this scope resolve to anything.** 1 at construction (`mov word ptr [eax+0x3c], 1`, which sets this byte and clears +0x3D) and cleared in exactly one place, 0x5C1F34 in CEventScope::MakeScope, when the candidate list for an `ally` or `local_enemy` context came up empty or the key was not a context at all. CContextTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D154D) and CContextTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D248D) test it and do nothing when it is 0 - so **an unresolvable scope makes the block false rather than raising anything** - and so do two of the three effect-side callers of MakeScope, at 0x59E2CD and 0x59E33C. CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation and CContextTrigger::GetBlockText do **not** test it, which is a real asymmetry between the tooltip's tally and the answer. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: unknown_context
fields.comment: **Was the key not a scope keyword at all.** 0 at construction, set to 1 only by the default arm of CEventScope::MakeScope's token switch (0x5C1F01), and read in exactly one place in the image: CTrigger::LoadKey at 0x5CAE9B, which makes a CContextTrigger for an otherwise unknown trigger key only while this is still 0. So the flag is the whole of how the grammar decides whether something like `owner`, `GER` or `64` is a scope rather than a parse error - and the ten tokens CEventScope::MakeScope knows, plus any country tag and any number, are the complete list of CContextTrigger's keys. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: combatant
fields.comment:
**The combat side the scope is about, or null.** This is the constructor's one stack argument, which FINDINGS-triggereval.md left unnamed ("0 at 28 of the 29 call sites inspected" - the exception, 0x74501, being the one place a combat raises an event).

**The record already knew what it is and never wrote it down as a field.** CCombatModifierTrigger::Evaluate (0x607E80), CCombatIsConvoyTrigger::Evaluate (0x607F70) and CCombatIsWinnerTrigger::Evaluate (0x607F90) each say so in their own comments, the last two calling themselves the "second" and "third independent witness that a combat trigger's scope holds the CCombatant at +0x40". This entry is the fourth and fifth, and the first time the field itself is recorded: CEnemyScopeTrigger::Evaluate (0x607980) reads `is_attacker (+0x38)`, `combat (+0x3C)` and `countries (+0x54)` off it, and CCombatHasArmourUnitTrigger::Evaluate (0x607FD0) walks `front_line (+0xB0)`. CCombatTemperature (0x607E50), CCombatTerrain (0x607DC0) and CHasCombinedArmsBonus (0x607D60) are the rest of the family and were not decoded.

**A scope with this null makes every one of them false**, which is why combat conditions silently fail in an ordinary event. CEventScope::MakeScope never writes it and CopyConstruct copies it, so it survives every context rebinding; `enemy = { ... }` is the only thing in the language that changes it, swapping it for the other side. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

fields.name: isMobilized
fields.comment:
read by CCountry::IsMobilized
BiceLib: mobilised (bool) - Set by CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies at 0x4E6D49, immediately after it adds the static modifier `initial_mobilization` to the country, and only on the transition from clear to `at_war` set. Cleared at 0x4E6EBD on the reverse transition, but only for a country the played-countries array (`CGameState +0xBCC`) says is not played - the second demobilisation path at 0x4E6DCB removes the modifier without clearing the byte, which was not explained. The third reader agrees with the name: CSubUnit slot 12 skips the RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE penalty when the owner's `+0x94` is set, which is what mobilisation would do. `inferred` would understate it and `confirmed` would overstate it; the demobilisation asymmetry is the reason. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aifields.md)

fields.name: isGovernmentInExile
fields.comment:
read by CCountry::IsGovernmentInExile
BiceLib: government_in_exile (bool) - **The country is a government in exile.** Saved by CCountry::SaveContents as `government_in_exile=yes` in the country's block and only when set (0x4CFED0, token 0x583 'government_in_exile'); loaded by CCountry::LoadKey's government_in_exile case through ParseBool. Written only by SetGovernmentInExile (rva 0x102BC0), whose seven callers are the po_annex exile, the effect form_government_in_exile, the history key government_in_exile (CExileStatusChange), a liberation (CLiberateCountryCommand), the daily puppet swap (CCountry_ReplaceExileWithPuppet) and the daily return of an exile that leads its faction. Read at about 170 sites in 85 functions - the stockpile becomes pool_in_exile (+0x9F8), surrender progress is 0, the AI and the diplomatic actions refuse or skip an exile; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md section C lists them. The game's Lua reads it as CCountry::IsGovernmentInExile (0xB4EAE0, `mov al,[ecx+0x95]; ret`). Renamed from `use_own_pool` long ago: 0x50AFF5 emits WE_NOT_GOVERNMENT_IN_EXILE when it is clear. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

fields.name: Strategy
fields.comment:
read by CCountry::GetStrategy
+0x15 inside it: fixed_ai_strategy (bool) - **Written by the `fixed_ai_strategy` effect and read by nothing.** CFixedAIStrategyEffect::Execute (0x5B0E90) stores `value == yes` here, and a byte-level sweep of .text finds no other access to the offset at all - so the effect is inert. A byte. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)
+0x1C inside it: ai_objective_bonus_list_first (void*) - A list whose nodes carry a province id at payload +0x8 and a value at payload +0xC. CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives (0x4980E0) searches it by province id at 0x498470-0x49847C and **adds the matched entry's +0xC to the objective's priority** (0x4984A0, 0x498480). What fills it was not traced; naming it would complete the priority formula. read (the use), unnamed (the list) (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)
+0xE4 inside it: oob_theatres_first (CTheatre*) - Head of the order of battle's theatre CList (last at +0x574, count at +0x578; nodes 0x10 bytes {data, prev, next, byte}). **Only two writers in the image**: CCreateHigherCommand::Execute (0x5DFE20) and CAddTheatreCommand::Execute (0x550600); CRemoveTheatreCommand::Execute unlinks. **Neither saved nor loaded** - neither CCountry::SaveContents (0x4CFF20) nor CCountry::LoadKey (0x4CCDA0) is among the 32 sites that touch +0x570 - so it is rebuilt by commands during play. This is a *different set* from CAIStrategy +0xE4: no code writes both. The AI reads it in CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForTheatres (0x88AAAC) and in ProcessAI's readiness gate (0x8897F7); the interface reads it from the CInGameIdler family (0x64D850) and the map-mode band (0x66A3D0). (agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion)
+0xE8 inside it: oob_theatres_last (CTheatre*) - Tail of the order of battle's theatre CList at +0x570. (agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion)
+0xEC inside it: oob_theatres_count (int) - Count of the order of battle's theatre CList at +0x570. Expected to be zero immediately after loading a save, since nothing loads the list - the cheapest live falsification of that claim. (agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion)
+0xF4 inside it: theatres_dirty (unsigned char) - The flag that asks for a full theatre rebuild. RunCountryHourlyPass tests it at 0x4D9079: set, it calls CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres(&country->strategy, 0) at 0x4D9093; clear, it calls the cheaper CAIStrategy::MaintainTheatres with `hour == country->id % 24` at 0x4D90C6. Set at 0x4A3517, 0x4B8268, 0x4E3E63 and 0x4E7152; cleared at 0x661952; also read by ProcessAI at 0x88951C. **Inferred from its one consumer**; what each setter is reacting to was not traced. (agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion)
+0x104 inside it: unknown_590 (int) - Thousandths. **Exactly one reader in the whole image**, 0x4B6141 in 0x4B60F0, where it becomes a shortage factor: `f = 1.0` and, when `+0x590 / 1000 < 0.2`, `f = 1.0 + (0.2 - value) * 2.5`, so f runs from 1.0 down at 0.2 to 1.5 at 0. That factor multiplies the brigade demand twice (0x4B6230, 0x4B6477). A complete byte scan of `.text` for the displacement finds no writer at all - the only `[reg+0x590]` write in the image, 0x249C6C, is on a CInGameIdler. The control for that scan is the same scan on `CUnit +0x2C8`, which does find writers. So this field is **probably never written and therefore always 0**, making the factor a constant 1.5 - but "probably" is the right word, because a writer holding a pointer to a sub-object of CCountry would use a different displacement and the scan cannot see it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)
+0x108 inside it: unknown_594 (int) - Thousandths. **One reader and no writer anywhere**: read at 0x4B61A7 into a float and multiplied into the brigade demand at 0x4B645D. Same scan and same control as +0x590. If it really is always 0 then that one term of 0x4B60F0's demand is always 0; the demand has other terms, so this is not by itself proof the function is inert. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

read by CCountry::GetMaxIC

RunSupplyAndConvoyIterations gives a country with no transports half of this, and the start-date savegame has exactly half the unscaled figure free for 19 of 19 countries. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md)

BiceLib: convoyed_in (CGoodsPool) - The third of the 23 pools, base +0x79C. fields.comment:
read by CCountry::GetConvoyedOut
BiceLib: convoyed_out (CGoodsPool) - The pool the ledger labels **RES_CONVOYED_OUT**, loaded at 0x4F43FE. Named by `BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip` (0x4F3000), which pushes the localisation key within four instructions of loading this pool's supplies member and comparing it to zero. Positive control: the same pattern in the same function names the already-known home_produced (+0x778) and convoyed_in (+0x79C). The asymmetry the expense side could not offer is on the display side instead: the tooltip labels each pool by name. **Credit where it is due, corrected 2026-10-02:** this name was *not* first established here. `BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp` has carried it all along, named from the game's own accessors, while this record said `unknown`/`unused` - the two halves of the fact base had drifted and this half was the stale one. What the goods-ledger tooltip adds is an **independent derivation from a different source**, the display side rather than the accessors, agreeing name for name. It also corroborates two header details nothing else had: the tooltip's displacement list skips 0x808 and 0x898, which are the header's `traded_away_sans_allied_supply` and `traded_for_sans_allied_supply`, and it suppresses `convoyed_in` for goods 0 and 1, which is the header's note that convoyed_in counts only for goods other than supplies and fuel.

The record's account of GetDailyExpense names its added terms 'traded_away, convoyed_out and the three pools at +0x8D8, +0x98C and +0x9B0', so this and +0x7DC are those two - **which is which was not established**, because the expense side skips nothing and so offers no asymmetry to fit on. BiceLib: traded_for (CGoodsPool) - The pool the ledger labels **RES_TRADED_FOR**, loaded at 0x4F3750. Positive control: the same pattern in the same function names the already-known home_produced (+0x778) and convoyed_in (+0x79C). Consistent with the record's existing note that CCountry::GetDailyIncome adds this pool unconditionally at 0xF1869: goods received by trade are income.

Previously recorded as `unknown_pool_86c`: The ninth of the 23 pools (base +0x874), added unconditionally by CCountry::GetDailyIncome at 0xF1869 and so one of the ones the record lists as unnamed. Read here only as its fuel member +0x878, inside the force planner's inlined GetDailyIncome.

**Credit where it is due, corrected 2026-10-02:** this name was *not* first established here. `BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp` has carried it all along, named from the game's own accessors, while this record said `unknown`/`unused` - the two halves of the fact base had drifted and this half was the stale one. What the goods-ledger tooltip adds is an **independent derivation from a different source**, the display side rather than the accessors, agreeing name for name. It also corroborates two header details nothing else had: the tooltip's displacement list skips 0x808 and 0x898, which are the header's `traded_away_sans_allied_supply` and `traded_for_sans_allied_supply`, and it suppresses `convoyed_in` for goods 0 and 1, which is the header's note that convoyed_in counts only for goods other than supplies and fuel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers.md; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: isAtWar
fields.comment:
read by CCountry::IsAtWar
BiceLib: at_war (bool) - **Whether the country is at war with anybody.** Its only writer is CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies (0x4E6A70): cleared at 0x4E6A91, then set to 1 at 0x4E6BCC for the first country in the whole country database whose shared `CDiplomacyStatus +0x20` (war) is non-null. Every reader in the image tests it as a byte against zero. This agrees with the name `isAtWar` the BiceLib header already carried in a comment on `last_surrender` (+0xAC8) - two readings converging, trap 14 - and it is what makes `+0xAC8 last_surrender` / `+0xAD0 war_exhaustion` sit either side of it. Among the consequences already in the record: a convoy wants no escorts while it is clear, consumer-goods demand switches between MODIFIER_WAR_ and MODIFIER_PEACE_CONSUMER_GOODS_DEMAND on it, reserve brigades take the RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE when it is clear, and `CEU3AI::RebuildPriorityProvinces` abandons its whole pass at 0x89773C unless the AI's own country has it set. fields.name: Dissent
fields.comment:
read by CCountry::GetDissent
BiceLib: dissent (int) - **Dissent, thousandths, at least 0 and with no upper bound.** Every writer (a displacement scan of .text, the CCountry sites read): the constructor and CCountry_Reset (0); CCountry::LoadKey (the save's `dissent`, raw); **the consumer goods share each day** (CDistributeConsumerGoods::Distribute: `+= GetConsumerGoodsNeeded - share + MODIFIER_DISSENT`, floored at 0 - laws and ministers act only through MODIFIER_DISSENT here, and there is no decay of any other kind); RunCountryDailyPass zeroing it for REB; the `dissent` effect (CDissentEffect::Execute, floored at 0); a history `dissent` entry through CCountry::SetDissent; and CMakePrideCommand::Execute (GetPrideRedesignationDissent, never negative). Nothing on war, occupation, a law or a minister change, or a pride sunk. Read by: the static `dissent` modifier scaled by it in RebuildStaticModifiers (base game: global_ic -0.01 a point); CCountry::GetSpareICIn (no spare consumer goods IC while there is any); every combatant's ApplyCombatModifiers and the AI's two estimates (COMBAT_DISSENT_IMPACT x dissent / 100); the monthly party drift 0xF6D00 (ELECTION_MINISTER_DISSENT_PENALTY x dissent x the party's posts where it holds two or more); the `dissent` trigger, the top bar, its tooltip, the intelligence screen (VA 0x625E68) and the AI's production Lua (GetDissent). **Not read by revolt risk or the revolt roll.** See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md, section C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: NationalUnity
fields.comment:
read by CCountry::GetNationalUnity
BiceLib: national_unity (int) - **National unity, thousandths, held between 1000 and 100000** - 1.0 to 100.0. Written by: CCountry::CCountry (0); CCountry::LoadKey (the save's `national_unity`, raw); CCountry::SetNationalUnity (clamped, unscaled - a history `national_unity` entry, which is where a new game's figure comes from, and the `setnationalunity` console command); and CCountry::ChangeNationalUnity (scaled by national_unity_effect, clamped) from exactly three places - the daily drift (RunCountryDailyPass_NationalUnityDrift: a thirtieth of the month's MODIFIER_NATIONAL_UNITY and strategic-warfare impacts a day, slowed by the square root of the distance from 50 when moving away from it), the nuclear bomb (NUKE_UNITY_IMPACT) and the `national_unity` effect. CCountry_Reset does not touch it. Nothing writes it on war, occupation, a lost capital or surrender. Read by CCountry::GetSurrenderProgress (the surrender level is reached when the occupied share of the owned cores' victory points reaches unity), the coup chance (0xF7AD0: `x (1 - unity / 100)`), the `national_unity` trigger (the laws' `allow` blocks among others), the top bar, its tooltip, the surrender tooltip, the intelligence screen (VA 0x625FC9) and the AI's intelligence Lua. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)
