fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - saved under the key "usage"; GetDailyExpense counts it. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:219)

fields.name: sent_to
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - saved under the key "to"; GetDailyExpense counts it. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:220)

fields.name: sent_back
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - saved under the key "back"; GetDailyIncome counts it. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:221)

fields.name: pool_in_exile
fields.comment: a CGoodsPool - the stockpile a government in exile holds itself. The good is pool + 8 + category * 4 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:229)

fields.name: diplo_influence
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `diplo_influence`. Neutrality sits at +0xA8C and EffectiveNeutrality at +0xA90, both of which the Lua API had already named the same way (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:291)

fields.name: reinforcement_cost
fields.comment: what reinforcement currently costs; the spare IC calculation subtracts it from what the reinforcement slider allocates (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:81)

fields.name: upgrade_cost
fields.comment: what upgrading currently costs; the spare IC calculation subtracts it from what the upgrade slider allocates (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:82)

fields.name: last_election_at_start
fields.comment: CCountry::LoadKey copies last_election here, but only while CCurrentGameState +0xD9C is clear, which is what tells a history file from a save. Nothing that reads it has been traced, and it is not saved (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:295)

fields.name: last_election
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `last_election`; a date, written through the same formatter as the other three (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:292)

fields.name: remove_fow
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `remove_fow`. The head of a linked list, with the tail at +0xABC and the count at +0xAC0; the loader appends a node per entry (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:294)

fields.name: remove_fow_end
fields.comment: the tail of the remove_fow list (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:295)

fields.name: remove_fow_count
fields.comment: how many are in the remove_fow list (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:296)

fields.name: last_surrender
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `last_surrender`; a date. isAtWar is the byte at +0xACC (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:297)

fields.name: war_exhaustion
fields.comment:
named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `war_exhaustion`

**What it does, 2026-10-12.** Each month (CCountry::UpdateMonthly) it gains the WAR_EXHAUSTION modifier (values +0x40; 0.041 from the `war` static modifier in Their Finest Hour), floored at 0 and capped at MAX_WAR_EXHAUSTION (+0x48; 100); at peace a positive balance is added to neutrality whole through CCountry::ChangeNeutrality and the field zeroed. REB is zeroed every month. Thousandths. (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:298)

fields.name: color
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `color`, which it loads by calling slot 3 on the object here and then copies to +0xC50 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:299)

fields.name: has_color
fields.comment: set the moment the `color` key has been read (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:300)

fields.name: history
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `history`, loaded by calling slot 3 on the object here (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:301)

fields.name: leaders
fields.comment: the country's leaders (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:83)

fields.name: capital_province_id
fields.comment: the capital, as a province id - index it into the game state's province vector. CCountry::GetCapitalLocation (0x17AF0) reads it and is otherwise identical to GetActingCapitalLocation, which reads +0xE24 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:173)

fields.name: active_mission
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `active_mission`, loaded by calling slot 3 on the object here (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:305)

fields.name: graphical_culture
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::LoadKey reads it from, `graphical_culture`. CCountry::AfterLoad (0xD2500) puts the Generic one here when a country was loaded without it (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:306)

fields.name: neighbours
fields.comment: which countries are in the Neighbours list at +0xFD8: a byte per country, indexed by its id. RebuildNeighbours (0xE21E0) walks the provinces this country **owns** and marks the owner of each adjacent province whose owner and controller are the same - so not one somebody is occupying - and which is neither unowned nor this country. CCountry::IsNeighbour is this indexed by the tag's id (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:354)

fields.name: neighbours_end
fields.comment: one past the last of neighbours (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:355)

fields.name: neighbours_capacity
fields.comment: the end of the room neighbours has (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:356)

fields.name: controller_neighbours
fields.comment: which countries are in the ControllerNeighbours list at +0xFE8, the same shape as neighbours. RebuildNeighbours walks the provinces this country **controls** and marks the controller of each adjacent province that is owned by somebody and neither owned nor controlled by this country. So occupation moves a country from one set to the other: Sweden has Denmark in neither, and Germany here, because Germany holds Denmark. CCountry::IsNonExileNeighbour reads this and then checks the other country is not a government in exile, which this list does not do for itself (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:357)

fields.name: controller_neighbours_end
fields.comment: one past the last of controller_neighbours (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:358)

fields.name: controller_neighbours_capacity
fields.comment: the end of the room controller_neighbours has (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:359)

fields.name: land_battles_fought
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `land_battles_fought`; the three counters are written one after another and sit next to each other (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:310)

fields.name: air_battles_fought
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `air_battles_fought` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:311)

fields.name: naval_battles_fought
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `naval_battles_fought` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:312)

fields.name: historical_friends
fields.comment:
The CCountryList of this country's historical friends, named from the key `CCountry::LoadKey` reads it from - `historical_friends`, which reads tags and looks each one up in the country database. `last` at +0x10A8, `count` at +0x10AC, 0x14-byte nodes holding a CCountryTag by value. Filled at 0x4CE920-0x4CE9DB, one node per tag, the tag coming out of the lookup at 0x518480; the same block clears `neutrality` (+0xA8C) a few instructions later, which is what identifies the receiver as a CCountry. (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:313)
+0x4 inside it: historical_friends_end (void*) - one past the last of historical_friends (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:314)
+0x8 inside it: historical_friends_capacity (void*) - the end of the room historical_friends has (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:315)

fields.name: espionage
fields.comment: the first of an array of 0xF8 byte entries, one per country, ending at +0x1164. **Entry +0 is what the save writes as `spy_allocation`** - CCountry::LoadKey's case for that key (0xCE3C1) walks the array 0xF8 at a time writing entry+0 - and entry+4 is `spy_priority` (0xCE34B writes `[edx + esi + 4]`), entry+0xF4 `covert_ops_points`; `spy_mission` walks nine values an entry. The country's `spies` key is **not** in here: it is a single field elsewhere on the country. Entry+0 is thousandths - an accessor at 0x49F3B0 answers `< 1000`, i.e. under one spy, and everything that writes it clamps to the 10000 at rva 0x130D164. CModifySpiesEffect::Execute adds to entry+0, which is what that effect is for: the spies this country has on mission in the target. The country's `spies` field at +0x1170 is a separate figure. The assigner at 0xD59D0, reached from CInGameIdler::Enter, recomputes entry+0 from relations and faction when a game is entered, so a value written mid-game does not survive a reload. (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:317)

fields.name: espionage_end
fields.comment: one past the last of espionage (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:318)

fields.name: spiescaught
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `spiescaught`. HighestThreat, which the Lua API names, is the next field at +0x11D8 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:319)

fields.name: daily_event_candidates_first
fields.comment: Head of the CList of CEvent* this country is a candidate for. Nodes are 0x10 bytes, {data, prev, next, byte}. **Written only by RebuildCountryEventCandidates (0x9C0050), which the tick reaches only on a month change**, and read by RunDailyEventPass (0x9C0A40) at 0x9C0B52, which skips the country entirely when it is null. It is not in CCountry's save grammar (fieldmap over CCountry::LoadKey 0x4CCDA0 has no key landing at +0x8, +0xC or +0x10) and CCountry::AfterLoad (0x4D2500-0x4D273D) never writes it, so after a load it is empty. That is the reported no-events-until-the-1st bug. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-events.md)

fields.name: daily_event_candidates_last
fields.comment: Tail of the candidate event CList at +0x8. Appended to at 0x9C03DE. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-events.md)

fields.name: daily_event_candidates_count
fields.comment: Count of the candidate event CList at +0x8. **The single cheapest live test of the loaded-save event bug**: zero right after a load, non-zero after the next month change. Incremented at 0x9C03E1 and zeroed at 0x9C017C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-events.md)

fields.name: walk_mark
fields.comment: Scratch: SpreadThreat's per-country visited mark. Cleared on every country, set to 1 on the feared country, tested and set on each controller as the walk charges it, so a country feels one spread once. Whether anything else in the image uses this dword was not surveyed, so the name is deliberately general. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplostate.md)

fields.name: officers_ratio
fields.comment: **Taken to be the history key `officers_ratio`**, thousandths: 1500 for Germany. Read once, as a new game starts: CInGameIdler::Enter adds each unit's officers to the country's, times this over 1000 where it is not zero. The name rests on the arithmetic and not on the loader, whose case for the key was not found: with the history's ratio the sum reproduces the officers 95 countries of 100 hold in a save two days in, less their two days of training. It is not the ratio the game shows - that is OfficerRatio at +0xD4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md)

fields.name: history_threat
fields.comment: The threat a country's history file gives it, thousandths: set by CThreatChange::Apply (0x1F1B20) from a dated `threat = N` in history/countries, and spread once as a new game starts by CInGameIdler::Enter (SpreadThreat at 0x65B64C, origin the country's own acting capital) where it is not zero. No other reader was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplostate.md)

fields.name: ai_trade_routes
fields.comment: Begin of a std::vector<CTradeRoute*> that CCountry::AIGetTradeRoutes (rva 0x1080C0) empties and refills on every call with every route on every one of the country's CDiplomacyStatus objects, in id order, and hands to Lua as `CArray<CTradeRoute*>&`. Scratch: nothing else is known to read it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: ai_trade_routes_end
fields.comment: End of the ai_trade_routes vector (+0x34). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: ai_trade_routes_capacity
fields.comment: Capacity of the ai_trade_routes vector (+0x34); compared against the end before the grow through 0x4C0700. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: in_scenario
fields.comment: **Whether the country takes part in the session.** Set to 1 by CCountry::CCountry (0x4C8A9B) and by CCountry_Reset (0x4D4B78); cleared only by CInGameIdler::Enter (0x65B1B9), for each country whose id is not on the list at the scenario's +0x88 when a scenario is set (CCurrentGameState +0xD0C). So in a campaign every country holds it, REB among them. Read by the loops that skip a country without it: RunDailyPass's country pass (0x682D65), RunHourlyPass's RunCountryHourlyPass (0x682833), ProcessCountryFunctor's CCountry::RecountUnitTotals and with it the officer ratio (0x68EDC1), RunIntelRefresh, RebuildNeighbours's caller and 0x68F059, 0x683EA9. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section D.10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: oob_file
fields.comment: **the order of battle to read**, relative to `history/units`. CLoadOOBEffect::Execute writes the effect's own string here through CCountry::SetOobFile and then calls CCountry::LoadOobFile, which reads it back. Nothing else uses it, so it is an argument passed on the object rather than a property of the country (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

fields.name: nukes
fields.comment:
The country's stock of nuclear bombs, x1000. The `nukes` key, save token 0x577, per findings/FINDINGS-fieldmap.md's map of CCountry::LoadKey - **that is where it was settled; this is corroboration from the consumer side, not a first reading.**

CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 4 reads it twice, both `>= 1000` i.e. 'at least one bomb': at 0x4CFE07 it adds a filter to the strategic-target survey so that only a province its own controller cores is kept, and at 0x4CFF8E it swaps the order token from `strategic_bomb (0x6F9)` to `nuke_mission (0x579)`. The second is per country and per pass, so one bomb in stock turns the whole strategic bomber force onto nuke missions. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

fields.name: subunit_total
fields.comment: The total number of regiments, ships and wings the country commands, x1000. CCountry::RecountUnitTotals (0x1004F0) zeroes it and adds `unit->regiments_count (CUnit +0x40) * 1000` per unit across its three passes - the country's own units, units on loan from faction members (CUnit +0x290 == our id), and finished deployments (+0x688). Hourly, on a TBB worker. This closes one of the four offsets FINDINGS-schedule.md left open on that function. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: army_combat_value
fields.comment: **The country's total brigade combat value, thousandths** - the sum of GetSubUnitDefinitionCombatValue (0x1A8690) over every brigade, ship and wing it commands, including units on loan from faction members and finished-but-unplaced deployments. The one writer is CCountry::RecountUnitTotals (0x1004F0, at 0x1005A3 / 0x1006CD / 0x10078A), hourly, on a **TBB worker**, so a hook must not assume the main thread. CCountry::LoadKey never writes it and CCountry::SaveContents never emits it, which is why the savegame is not an oracle for it. Three readers across both country-access idioms: CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces averages it over the hostile countries across one ops-area province's borders and compares mean/ours against 0.150, scaling that province's priority down to between 5% and 100% when the neighbours are that feeble (0x4BD78F, 0x4BD7D2); and CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances sums `+0xCC / 1000` over a side's members at 0x4918C3 and 0x491994, which is the arithmetic that function's own entry records as unread. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: officers_required
fields.comment: The officers the country's brigades require: the sum of each commanded brigade's definition `officers` (CSubUnitDefinition +0x118), written by CCountry::RecountUnitTotals at 0x1005B6 / 0x1006B9 beside +0xCC and +0xC8. It sits beside the officers pool at +0xC4, which CCountry::LoadKey reads from the save key `officers`, so the pair is have/need. The name is from the summand; nothing was watched running. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: next_alignment_update
fields.comment: A tick, **not saved and not loaded** (neither CCountry::LoadKey nor SaveContents touches it), set to the null date [0x170C2B8] = 43800000 (year 0) by the constructor and CCountry_Reset. The daily pass runs CAlignment::UpdateDaily only when today > this, then sets it to today + (ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL / 1000) x 24. So the first daily pass after a new game **or a load** drifts every unaligned country at once, and because the test is strict and the day's tick is its hour 0, **a step comes every ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL + 1 days** - 25 in Their Finest Hour and BlackICE, which both set 24. A new game's first step is its first day, before the first hour (Jan 1, then Jan 26, Feb 20, Mar 17, Apr 11). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-alignment.md)

fields.name: taken_decisions_first
fields.comment: **Head of the country's taken-decisions list**: 0x28-byte nodes, the name (Hoi3CString) at +0, previous at +0x1C, next at +0x20. Filled only by the history - CCountryDecisionChange / CCountryRemoveDecisionChange Apply, through CCountry_AddTakenDecision (which refuses a name already there) and CCountry::RemoveTakenDecision. **Read by SetUpCountryForNewGame**, which runs each listed decision's effect on a new game. Taking a decision in play does not add to it, and nothing that offers a decision reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: taken_decisions_last
fields.comment: Tail of the taken-decisions list at +0x128. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: taken_decisions_count
fields.comment: Count of the taken-decisions list at +0x128. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: templates
fields.comment: Begin of a vector of the country's division templates, end at +0x14C; from `default_templates` in its file under common/countries. A template has its name - a localisation key - as a string at +0x08 and a CList of unit types at +0x24. CDivisionDesigner's constructor names one `divdesign_button` for each. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md)

fields.name: ai
fields.comment: the country's CEU3AI, on two independent lines of evidence: GetDiploScoreFromLua (0x60DC70) reads it and hands it to Lua, where every DiploScore_* function's first parameter is `voAI`; and 0x26196F passes the same field to the AI agent update loop at 0x4894E0. No luabind accessor exposes it, so the name is ours (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacy.md)

fields.name: lend_lease_ic
fields.comment: **The whole IC of lend-lease received, which costs no domestic resources**, in whole IC. Zeroed at the head of CCountry::UpdateIC (0xF0DE4); with applyDailyEffects set to lend_lease_income (+0x6E8) / 1000, truncated, and added to TotalIC (+0x604) from the same register at 0xF14C1/0xF14D0 - **after** TotalIC has been capped at what the stockpile supports (0xF14A6), so it is IC on top of the cap (UpdateIC_ResourceCapAndLendLease, 0xF146E). Read in exactly five places, one per IC distributor - consumer goods 0x118D67, production 0x119D5E, supply 0x11AB4A, reinforcement 0x11BB96, upgrade 0x11CEE9 - and by nothing else; the lend-lease distributor does not read it. Each takes its own slider's share of it as a free budget: production spends it first on each line with no resource check; consumer goods, supply and upgrade subtract it from their one resource charge; reinforcement takes it off brigade by brigade. The lend-lease slider's share of it is used by nobody. Not written on a day UpdateIC does not run, which is every day for a country that holds no province and is not in exile. Two readings of this field were merged here: `lend_lease_ic` (from the writer) and `resource_free_ic` (from the five readers). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

fields.name: core_home_area_ic
fields.comment: in thousandths. CCountry::UpdateIC adds a province's contribution here when all three hold: the province's owner id (+0x330) is this country, its COwnerArea (+0x2B4) is the acting capital's, and this country is in its `core` list (+0x344). Read at 0xF1C9E and 0x11AC33, neither named. **The game's own name is not established** - this one describes the three tests. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ic.md)

fields.name: ic_lost_to_shortage
fields.comment: in thousandths and **negative**: (resource-limited IC - total IC) x 1000, written by CCountry::UpdateIC at 0xF14A0 only when the metal and energy stockpiles cannot support +0x604. Written in exactly two places in the image, here and the CCountry constructor (0xC8D25), and **read nowhere in .text** - it is not cleared on a day with no shortage either. Name inferred from the arithmetic. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ic.md)

fields.name: ministers_end
fields.comment: End of the `ministers` vector at +0x618 (capacity at +0x620). The array is resized at 0x4CA0A0-0x4CA0AA to the number of entries in the government-position database's vector (`[0x1A87990] +0x10 - +0xC` over 4) and every slot is then filled with the `CNullMinister` singleton at 0x1A855C8, so its length is exactly the number of cabinet posts and an unfilled post is the null minister rather than a null pointer. CCountry::SaveContents walks it at 0x4D0F96-0x4D109B, calls slot 8 on each element - CMinister's last of nine - and on true writes `position->+0x2C` as the key and the minister's `id` (+0xC) through `%d` as the value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aifields.md)

fields.name: ministers_capacity
fields.comment: Allocation end of the `ministers` vector at +0x618. All three are zeroed together in the constructor at 0x4C8D2B and freed together at 0x4CB179-0x4CB198. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aifields.md)

fields.name: laws
fields.comment: **The laws, not the ministers** - correcting CLASSES.md. One CLaw* per law group, indexed by the CLawGroup's own index at +0x50. Three readings agree: CChangeLawCommand::Execute (0x54EF60) stores the value its loader reads from the key `law` (+0x44) at the index of the object from the key `position` (+0x48); CCountry::LoadKey's loop over this array calls slot 16 on each element and CLaw's vftable has exactly seventeen slots; and the parallel +0x618 loop calls slot 8, CMinister's last. The three accessors are 0xF0510, 0xF0530 and 0xF0550. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-politics.md)

fields.name: laws_end
fields.comment: End of the `laws` vector at +0x628 (capacity at +0x630), and the independent proof that +0x628 is the laws: the array is resized at 0x4CA1D0-0x4CA1E0 to the number of **law groups** (`GetLawDataBase() +0x2C - +0x28` over 4) and filled with the `CNullLaw` singleton at 0x1A855B8, exactly as +0x618 is sized to the government positions and filled with `CNullMinister`. CCountry::SaveContents walks it at 0x4D10C1-0x4D11BE, calls slot 16 on each element - CLaw's last of seventeen - and on true writes the law group's own token (`CLawGroup +0x54`) as the key and the law's own token (`CLaw +0x2C`) as the value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aifields.md)

fields.name: laws_capacity
fields.comment: Allocation end of the `laws` vector at +0x628; zeroed in the constructor at 0x4C8D3D-0x4C8D49 and freed at 0x4CB154-0x4CB173. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aifields.md)

fields.name: active_modifiers
fields.comment: **The event modifiers on the country**, a list: what `add_country_modifier` gives and the save writes as `modifier = { modifier = ... date = ... }`. Each entry has the modifier at +8 and a date at +0xC. CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers adds every entry's modifier, and first removes one whose date is before today - unless the date is in year 1 or earlier, which is how one with no end is written (`1.1.1`). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: triggered_modifiers
fields.comment: Head of the list (tail +0x65C, count +0x660) of the CTriggeredModifier* that currently apply to the country. UpdateTriggeredModifiers is its only writer; CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers adds each one. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: strategic_resource_modifiers
fields.comment: Head of a list (tail +0x66C, count +0x670) of the scaled CStrategicResource copies the last CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers made. The country owns them: each rebuild destroys the old ones first. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: strategic_resource_levels
fields.comment: **How much of each strategic resource the country has the use of**, thousandths, one int for each entry of the strategic-resource database, by index; end at +0x67C, capacity at +0x680. 1000 is a whole resource. UpdateStrategicResources raises an entry to the best efficiency any qualifying province gives and nothing lowers it; CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers scales the resource's modifier by it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: strategic_resource_levels_end
fields.comment: End of the vector whose begin is strategic_resource_levels at +0x678. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: lendlease_distributions
fields.comment: **The countries this one gives lend-lease to**: a vector of 16-byte entries {CCountryTag receiver; int weight (+8); int effectiveness (+0xC)}, end at +0x6BC. Save keys `lendlease_targets` (the tags, loaded with weight 0 and effectiveness 1000), `lendlease_distributions` (the weights) and `lendlease_effectiveness`. weight: the receiver's share is weight / the sum (CCountry::GetLendLeaseShare); a new entry gets 500, CChangeLendLeaseDistributionCommand sets them. effectiveness: thousandths, 1000 over land and the lend-lease convoy's efficiency over sea, set hourly by CCountry::UpdateLendLeaseRoutes; 0 until then. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: lend_lease_from_values
fields.comment: **The countries this one receives lend-lease from**: a vector of 12-byte entries {CCountryTag giver; int amount}, end at +0x6CC; save keys `lend_lease_from` (the tags) and `lend_lease_from_values`. amount: thousandths of IC credited by the giver's CDistributeLendLease and not yet turned into IC; CCountry::UpdateIC takes the whole IC out of the entries in order and leaves the fraction. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: lend_lease_from_yesterday_values
fields.comment: A copy of lend_lease_from_values (+0x6C8) taken by the daily CCountry::UpdateIC before it spends them (LendLeaseReceipts_Clear, then LendLeaseReceipts_AppendAll): per giver, what that giver had credited and not yet turned into IC - today's deliveries since the last UpdateIC plus the fraction carried from before. The top bar's tooltip shows it (0x508A20). 12-byte entries {CCountryTag giver; int amount}, end at +0x6DC; save keys `lend_lease_from_yesterday` and `_values`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

fields.name: lend_lease_income
fields.comment: Lend-lease received and not yet turned into IC, thousandths of IC: the sum of lend_lease_from_values. CCountry::UpdateIC adds its whole part (/ 1000, truncated) to TotalIC (+0x604) after the resource cap and stores it in lend_lease_ic (+0x608), then subtracts what it used, keeping the fraction for the next day. Save key `lend_lease_income`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: lend_lease_income_yesterday
fields.comment: The lend-lease IC a day's CCountry::UpdateIC turned into IC, thousandths (a whole number of IC times 1000), or 0 with no giver. Save key `lend_lease_income_yesterday`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: tech_sharing_given
fields.comment: Begin of a vector of twelve-byte entries, { CCountryTag receiver; int category }, end at +0x6F4. CCountry::UpdateTotalLeadership charges SHARE_TECH_LEADERSHIP_COST leadership for each entry and cancels the newest while the country cannot pay; CCountry::StopSharingTechWith erases the entries naming one country. **That it is the technology categories this country shares is inference** from those two readers; its writer was not read. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leadership.md)

fields.name: tech_sharing_given_end
fields.comment: End of the vector whose begin is tech_sharing_given at +0x6F0; the count is the difference over twelve. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leadership.md)

fields.name: unfilled_modifier
fields.comment: A CModifier embedded in the country that CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers adds whole, between the neutrality modifier and the event modifiers. **Nothing was found that fills it**: a scan for `lea reg,[reg+0x700]` and `add reg,0x700` gives the constructor, the destructor and that one add. Likely always empty. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: auto_maintain_convoy
fields.comment: Guards CCountry::DistributeConvoyShips in RunCountryDailyPass. Named for the save key written first of the three; the loader was not read, so the pairing is by order and by what each byte guards. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md)

fields.name: auto_supply_convoy
fields.comment: Guards CCountry::MaintainSupplyConvoys in RunCountryDailyPass. Named for the save key; inferred as for +0x748. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md)

fields.name: auto_resource_convoy
fields.comment: Guards CCountry::MaintainResourceConvoys in RunCountryDailyPass. Named for the save key; inferred as for +0x748. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md)

fields.name: auto_assign_leaders
fields.comment: Whether a unit placed, joined or made a headquarters is given CUnit::AssignBestLeader. CCountry::SaveContents writes this byte under the key auto_assign_leaders (`movzx eax, byte [edi+0x74B]; mov ecx, 0x5A5; call SaveWriteBool` at 0xD12B6), so the name is read, not inferred. The start's own assignment does not ask it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 8. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md)

fields.name: repaid_away
fields.comment: The pool the ledger labels **RES_REPAID_AWAY** (BuildGoodsLedgerTooltip, 0x4F42AF). **Corrected 2026-10-13: it is written** - its money (+0x834) gets each day's debt repayment the country pays, in the repayment loop at the end of CCountry::CollectDailyProduction (0x4F2589); no other good is ever written. The earlier comment's 'no writer outside construction and the daily reset' missed that site; the live zeros it recorded (0 of 108 countries in a 1936 and a 1942 game) fit, because no debt arrangement was in force. Not saved (CCountry::SaveContents writes ten pools, not this one). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: income_from_debt
fields.comment: The pool the ledger labels **RES_INC_DEBT** (0x4F396C), and part of CCountry::GetDailyIncome. **Corrected 2026-10-13: it is written** - its money (+0x858) gets each day's debt repayment the country receives, in CCountry::CollectDailyProduction (0x4F258F); no other good. The live zeros recorded earlier fit, because no debt arrangement was in force. Not saved. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: ic_resources_reserved
fields.comment: One of the thirteen unnamed goods pools. CLASSES.md records it as never used in this build; it is **read** - CCountry::GetResourceLimitedIC (0xF15C0) subtracts its metal (+0x95C), energy (+0x960) and rare materials (+0x964) from the national stockpile before working out how much more IC the resources will support. Nothing writes it outside the constructor and the daily resets, which is consistent with it reading zero in all 108 countries of two games, so the reservation is real machinery that this build never uses. The name is ours. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-production.md)

fields.name: unknown_a1c
fields.comment: an embedded CGoodsPool of which only supplies (+0xA24) and fuel (+0xA28) are ever touched - a daily accumulator, added to by CSupply::DailySupplyPass at 0x287671 and 0x287993 with the part of a province's need met by its own current_producing, and by 0x1BBFBA in the unit consumption code; reset along with +0x994..+0x9AC by 0x4F28B0. Deliberately left unnamed: the pass writes production met locally into it and the unit code adds to it as well, and which of the two the field is for was not settled. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: unit_demand
fields.comment: What the units drawing on this country asked for today, before any shortfall - supplies accumulate at +0xA48 and fuel at +0xA4C on every path through CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel, including the one where the pool cannot pay. Distinct from CCountry::usage (+0x98C), which only gets what was actually handed over. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: received_from_exiles
fields.comment: **What governments in exile hand this country each day**: RunCountryDailyPass (0x4DB46F, 0x4DB48D) adds an exile's pool_in_exile supplies and fuel here, for the controller of the exile's acting capital province, as it moves them into that province's pool. Only supplies (+0xA6C) and fuel (+0xA70) are ever written. GetDailyIncome counts it as income, so the top bar's ledger shows it (the game's text key for the line is likely LEDGER_FROM_EXILES 'From Exiles', near 'Into Network' at 0x7A1002 - not traced). Good g at +0xA64 + 8 + g*4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

fields.name: reinforcement_manpower_needed
fields.comment: manpower to bring every subunit back to strength, rebuilt daily by CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute; the tooltip's $NEED$ (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: reinforcement_manpower_used
fields.comment: manpower spent reinforcing today, rebuilt daily beside the one above; the tooltip's $USED$ (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: last_rebel_acceptance
fields.comment: named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `last_rebel_acceptance`; a date. **Written only by CCountry_StampRebelAcceptance (rva 0xEFED0), from CExecuteRebelAcceptanceCommand::Execute, which nothing posts**, besides the constructor, CCountry_Reset and the loader; **read by nothing but the save writer** (0x4D0682, which writes it only when it is past year 1). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: in_undeclared_war
fields.comment: **Whether the country is in an undeclared war with anybody** - the exact twin of +0xACC at_war, and the sibling it is tested beside at five places across CAIUnit slot 73 and both AI bodies. Its only two writers are CCountry::UpdateUndeclaredWars (0xE6EE0): cleared at 0xE6EFC, then set to 1 at 0xE7025 for the first country in the database whose CDiplomacyStatus::undeclared_war (+0x24) against this one is set. Thirteen readers, all `cmp ... , 0`: four in CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits, six in CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits, two in slot 73 and one at 0x4CF0C4. The scan that found this has a positive control - the same displacement scan over .text finds 101 operands for +0xACC, including UpdateAtWarAndEnemies's own two writes. Live at the 1936 scenario start it is 0 on all 108 countries while +0xACC is 1 on 5, which is what a start with declared wars and no undeclared ones should look like. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)

fields.name: war_exhaustion_modifier
fields.comment: The country's own copy of static_modifiers.txt's `war_exhaustion`, every value scaled by war_exhaustion (+0xAD0) / 1000 on each rebuild. 0x48 bytes. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: dissent_modifier
fields.comment: The country's own copy of static_modifiers.txt's `dissent`, every value scaled by dissent (+0x10B4) / 1000 on each rebuild - so the file's figures are for one point of dissent. 0x48 bytes. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: neutrality_modifier
fields.comment: The country's own copy of static_modifiers.txt's `neutrality`, every value scaled by effective neutrality / 100 on each rebuild. 0x48 bytes; the units list at +0xBAC follows it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: expeditionary_units_lent
fields.comment: **The units this country has lent out as expeditionary forces** - its second unit list, right after units (+0xBAC). CUnit::ReturnFromExpedition unlinks a returning unit from its expeditionary_owner's list here (0x502120-0x502143); AnnexCountry walks the annexed country's (0x4E86AF) recalling each; the reinforcement and upgrade shares walk it after units, skipping units with an expeditionary owner in +0xBAC - so a lender reinforces and upgrades what it lent. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

fields.name: max_manpower
fields.comment: **So many years of the manpower the country gets, in thousandths, and not a ceiling.** Written by UpdateMaxManpower: the year's manpower times MAX_MANPOWER, at least 1000. A new game starts the pool at it; nothing holds the pool to it afterwards. The field `max_manpower = N` reads, and the denominator of `manpower_percentage`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpowergain.md)

fields.name: blockade
fields.comment: Thousandths. **Likely** the blockade level the `blockade = N` keyword tests, and likely only because the single reader found is `CBlockadeTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D4100), whose class name is the whole of the evidence for the name. It sits immediately after `manpower` and `max_manpower`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: core_victory_points_owned
fields.comment: **Victory points in thousandths, summed over the country's core provinces (CoreProvinces +0xD10) that it owns.** Written only by CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (0xE21E0): zeroed with its counter block at 0x4E2305, then `prov->victory_points (+0x34) * 1000` added at 0x4E3059 for each core whose `owner.id (+0x330)` is the country's id. The denominator of CCountry::GetOccupiedVictoryPointShare, the surrender measure; CAIUnit::EstimateTheatreNeed takes `+0xBE0 - +0xBE4` at 0x4B99FF and tests it against 2 victory points. CGameState and CInGameIdler also have a +0xBE0 - trap 12. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: core_victory_points_held
fields.comment: **Victory points in thousandths, summed over the country's core provinces that it both owns and controls.** The other half of +0xBE0, in the same loop of CCountry::RebuildNeighbours: zeroed at 0x4E2311 and added at 0x4E3076 on `prov->controller_id (+0x338) == country->id`, a test reached **only after the owner test passed** - so a core held by another country and liberated by this one counts in neither, and this never exceeds +0xBE0. `1000 - 1000 * held / owned` is the occupied share surrender_progress is built from. CGameState writes a float at +0xBE4 - trap 12. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: unit_names
fields.comment: Begin of a vector indexed by a unit type's index (CSubUnitDefinition +0x24), 0x10 bytes an entry, each holding a vector of 0x1C-byte strings: the names `unit_names` in the country's file gives that type. A division is named from its first brigade's list; a ship or a wing from its own. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md)

fields.name: unit_name_cursors
fields.comment: One int for each unit type: where the country has got to in that type's list of names. Left on the name last taken, so the next search starts there again and passes it as in use. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md)

fields.name: areas_first
fields.comment: Head of the country's COwnerArea list, nodes with data at +0x0 and next at +0x8. It is the outer loop of CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres (0x8A9CAD) - one pass per area, which is what produces one or more CTheatre per area - and the middle loop of CAIInvasion::PickEmbarkationPort (0x89FD88, 0x8A00EB). Which areas it holds (owned, controlled or merely present-in) was not traced. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatre2.md)

fields.name: supply_groups
fields.comment: The country's supply groups. AnnexCountry calls CSupplyGroup::PickDepot on each of the annexer's at its end (0x4E8E3D-0x4E8E54); DeleteSupplyGroups collects the distinct groups of this list, frees it and zeroes it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

fields.name: underground_provinces
fields.comment: Head of the list of province ids holding the country's undergrounds (tail +0xD64, count +0xD68); nodes {id, prev, next, deleted}. **Rebuilt whole** by CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (0x4E3086) from every province, in id order, whose underground has level_max above 0 and whose underground_owner id is the country - which is how it comes back after a load, since the province loader sets only the owner tag. Added to by CCountry_AddUnderground (rva 0x10A030) and the inlined push in SpawnUndergroundFromProvince; taken from by RunDailyUndergroundPass's removal, CCountry_RemoveUnderground (Province_SetController) and CCgmSetUndergroundCommand; freed by 0x50A0C0. Walked by the underground pass, both predicates, the revolt button and its tooltip, CCountry_MobilizeAllUndergrounds and the AI. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: rule_none
fields.comment: Rules (+0xDBC) +0x18, the CRule bool of rule definition 0, NONE. Cleared by CCountry_Reset and CCountry::RebuildRules and ORed in by CRule::Merge like the other three, but no file rule names it in Their Finest Hour, and **nothing reads it**: a disp32 scan of 0xDD4 over .text finds only the reset's clear and esp-based frame slots. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: rule_limited_war
fields.comment: **The faction rule limited_war, as the country holds it**: Rules (+0xDBC) +0x20, CRule bool 1 (RULE_LIMITED_WAR "Limited war"). Cleared and set again by CCountry::RebuildRules from the faction's `rule` through CRule::Merge - a disp8 store off the Rules base - so it is 1 for every member of a real faction whose rule has `limited_war = yes`: the Axis in Their Finest Hour and BlackICE. Two readers: the diplomacy screen's action list offers 'Declare Limited War' only where it is set (0x4E40D5), and the AI's war plans declare a limited war where it is set (0x89D9A1, AIForeignMinister_LimitedWarByFactionRule). The four bytes +0xDD4/+0xDDC/+0xDE4/+0xDEC are the four rule definitions NONE, LIMITED_WAR, ALLIANCE_GUARANTEE, FREE_RESOURCE_GIFTS. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: rule_alliance_guarantee
fields.comment: **The faction rule allience_wide_guarantee (so spelled in the file), as the country holds it**: Rules (+0xDBC) +0x28, CRule bool 2 (RULE_ALLIANCE_GUARANTEE "Alliance-wide guarantees"). Set by CCountry::RebuildRules through CRule::Merge for every member of a real faction whose rule has it - the Allies in Their Finest Hour and BlackICE. Three readers: CGuaranteeAction::Apply (0xA1BDF4) - the guarantor's guarantee is made by every other member of its faction too; CGuaranteeAction::GetDialogText (0xA1DE77) - ALLIES_GUARANT 'Should we need to come to their aid, all members of our faction will follow us.'; CCallAllyAction::Apply (0xA28CA0) - a member answering a call to arms brings in every member of its faction not already defending. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: can_trade_free_resources
fields.comment: **The faction rule free_resource_gifts, as the country holds it**: the fourth bool of `Rules (+0xDBC)` (CRule +0x18 + 3 x 8, rule definition 3 RULE_FREE_RESOURCE_GIFTS "Free resources gifts"). Cleared and rebuilt by CCountry::RebuildRules, which ORs in the rule of the country's faction where that faction is real (CRule::Merge) - in the base game the Comintern's (common/ideologies.txt, `rule = { free_resource_gifts = yes }`). Three readers, all requiring it on **both** countries of a trade: CEU3AI::CanTradeFreeResources; CTradeRoute::IsValid, which then accepts any route; and CTradeAction::SetTrading, which then leaves the money column alone - so **two members of such a faction trade goods for goods, or for nothing**. NO_TRADE_RULE names the same rule definition. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: active_leaders
fields.comment:
**The country's leaders in service, a CList** (first +0xE00, last +0xE04, count +0xE08), node `{leader +0, next +8}` - not a vector. Named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under. Filled at a new game's start and by leader activation (FINDINGS-leaderassign.md); walked by `has_leader`, the leader choice and the leader window. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md)
+0x4 inside it: active_leaders_last (void*) - The last node of the active_leaders CList at +0xE00. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md and FINDINGS-leaderassign.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md)
+0x8 inside it: active_leaders_count (int) - How many leaders the active_leaders CList at +0xE00 holds. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md and FINDINGS-leaderassign.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md)

fields.name: mission
fields.comment: **The country's current mission definition**, or null. `CActiveMissionTrigger::Evaluate` (rva 0x5F16D0, the whole of it) is `return scopeCountry->mission == this->+0x40`, so this is the pointer a `mission = X` condition compares against; the saved instance is the separate `active_mission` at +0xE38. ApplyCountryAIStrategies uses it as the **first of trigger slot 10's two roots**: when the mission's own slot 6 answers true it walks the `CAndTrigger` embedded at `CMission +0xC4` with weight 600 and the scope at +0xE44. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: mission_scope
fields.comment: **The event scope the current mission was started with**, embedded by value - 0x48 bytes, +0xE44 to +0xE8B. It is what ApplyCountryAIStrategies passes as trigger slot 10's `scope` argument when it walks the mission's trigger block, so the mission's conditions are evaluated against the scope the mission was created in rather than against a fresh one. A second scope of the same size follows at +0xE8C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: last_mission_cancel
fields.comment: The hour the country's last mission ended, saved as `last_mission_cancel` (token 0x68D). Stamped with CGameState::tick by CCountry_CancelMission (rva 0xEE700). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md)

fields.name: last_mission
fields.comment: **The name of the country's last ended mission**, saved as `last_mission` (token 0x6A8) unless empty or `no_mission`. Set from the outgoing mission's name by CCountry_CancelMission (rva 0xEE700); compared by `last_mission` (CLastMissionTrigger::Evaluate, through Trigger_CopyLastMission). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md)

fields.name: interface_host
fields.comment: The object a country's interface goes through: slot 14 the gui, slot 16 a window's parent, slot 18 the session whose +0x38 channel commands are posted on - the shape of CInGameIdler, which is what it is inferred to be. The event window builds through it; FINDINGS-diploaction.md and FINDINGS-ai.md post commands through it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: pending_diplomatic_actions
fields.comment: Head of the country's list of **pending CDiplomaticActions** - offers made to it and replies made to its own offers, of every kind. Node is 0x10 bytes: +0x0 the action, +0x4 the previous node, +0x8 the next, +0xC a byte. Tail at +0xF28, count at +0xF2C. Appended by CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction (rva 0xE61C0) and by CCountry::LoadKey, whose nineteen action-token cases reach three entry points (0x4CD393 for declarewar, 0x4CD5FB for sixteen more, 0x4CDAE1 for influence and request_lendlease) that all call CDiplomaticAction::Create (rva 0xE5800) with the token, run CPersistent::Load and append to this one list. Read by CCountry::HasPendingTradeProposal (rva 0xE6360), by CAIForeignMinister::DoWork (0x89E05A) and by the hourly AI pass (0x682B83), and emptied wholesale by CCountry::ClearPendingDiplomaticActions (rva 0xE63A0). In a save it appears as one `<action_token>={...}` key per entry inside the country's block, not under a `declarewar` wrapper. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: pending_diplomatic_actions_end
fields.comment: the tail of the pending_diplomatic_actions list (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: pending_diplomatic_actions_count
fields.comment: how many are in the pending_diplomatic_actions list (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: pending_diplomatic_actions_no_unlink
fields.comment: The fourth member of the pending list's CList (head +0xF24, tail +0xF28, count +0xF2C): while set, a removal marks the node's +0xC byte instead of unlinking it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: provinces_in_revolt
fields.comment: **How many provinces the country owns that rebels hold**: CCountry::RebuildNeighbours zeroes it and adds one for each province of OwnedProvinces (+0xCF0) whose controller tag is REB (0x4E2A05), recounting it daily and at every change of hands. Read by `num_of_revolts` (CNumOfRevoltsTrigger::Evaluate, 0x5D73D0, `>=` a raw count) and as the numerator of `revolt_percentage` over NumberOfOwnedProvinces (+0xCF8) (CNumOfRevoltsFractionTrigger, 0x5D7950); FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md's AI slot 73 tests it `> 0`. +0xF54 is counted identically and never read. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: provinces_in_revolt_unread
fields.comment: Counted exactly like provinces_in_revolt (+0xF50) - the same REB-controller test over OwnedProvinces, in CCountry::RebuildNeighbours (0x4E2A26) - and zeroed with it (0x4E231D, CCountry_Reset 0x4D42AA). **No reader anywhere in .text**: a dead duplicate. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: non_hostile_countries
fields.comment:
The CCountryList of countries this one is not hostile to. Membership, read off 0x4E32E9-0x4E338E in CCountry::RebuildNeighbours: the pair's CDiplomacyStatus +0x58 (`co_belligerent`) must be non-zero, and then **the owner itself is added unconditionally** - in fact before the database loop, at 0x4E234F-0x4E23A0, where the node is built from our own +0xCA4/+0xCA8 - while anybody else is rejected if `war` (+0x20) is set or either side is REB. Seven readers, all in the AI layer: 0x88D14F, 0x895A62, 0x897826, 0x89FD52, 0x8AC3A9, 0x8CC823, 0x8D9F76; plus the clear in 0x4D2B60. **It is not `enemies`** - CAIInvasion's 0x89FBC0 iterates it to find a friendly port to load troops in, which is why countries we are at war with are excluded and why we are always in it ourselves. The name is from the membership rule rather than from that single use (trap 14).

`last` is at +0xF9C and `count` at +0xFA0; reach them as `non_hostile_countries.last` and `.count`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatre2.md)
+0x4 inside it: non_hostile_countries_last (void*) - Tail of the list at +0xF98; read at 0x4E3341 before each append. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatre2.md)
+0x8 inside it: non_hostile_countries_count (int) - Count of the list at +0xF98; incremented at 0x4E337F. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-theatre2.md)

fields.name: allied_or_faction_countries
fields.comment: One of the nine CCountryLists CCountry::RebuildNeighbours fills: the other country is appended when the pair's CDiplomacyStatus +0x14 (`alliance`) or +0x18 (`dependency`) is non-null, or both are in the same real faction (+0xD8, slot 7). The else-arm of the same test elects `highest_threat` (+0x11D8/+0x11DC). **Read by the intelligence passes**: every 9 a controller, an underground's owner or a radar's country gets on a province goes to every country on its list too, and a controller's 3 on adjacent land likewise - so allies, puppets and masters, and faction members share what each other's ground and radar show. `last` at +0xFAC, `count` at +0xFB0; append at 0x4E3506-0x4E3553. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: strong_allies_at_war
fields.comment: One of the nine CCountryLists CCountry::RebuildNeighbours fills, and the only one built from another of them: a second pass over `Allies (+0xF88)` at 0x4E3616-0x4E370D appends every ally that clears four tests - not a government in exile (`+0x95` zero), its acting capital on the same continent as ours (`CCountry::GetActingCapitalLocation` at 0x42F100 on each, then `CProvince +0x368`), `max_ic (+0x60C)` at least half ours, and itself at war (`at_war +0xACC`). **Type confirmed, name inferred from those four tests**; no reader was traced. `last` at +0xFBC, `count` at +0xFC0; append at 0x4E36AE-0x4E36FF. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: guarantors
fields.comment: The CCountryList of countries that **guarantee** this one. One of the nine CCountry::RebuildNeighbours fills; the gate at 0x4E3394-0x4E33B7 requires the pair's `CDiplomacyStatus +0x1C` (`guarantee`) to be non-null and then `guarantee->+0xC == status->+0xC`. That comparison is **byte-identical to the game's own `CDiplomacyStatus::IsGuaranteed` (rva 0x648760)**, whose twin `IsGuaranting` (0x648730) differs only in `setne` for `sete` - so the direction is the game's name and not ours. It agrees with the sibling test ten instructions earlier, which appends to `Vassals (+0xF78)` when the other country is the **second** party of the `dependency`, i.e. the subordinate: `first` is the senior party in these relation objects, and here the other country is `first`. `last` at +0xFCC, `count` at +0xFD0; append at 0x4E33B9-0x4E3406. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: unknown_list_ff8
fields.comment: **A CCountryList whose contents are not identified.** It is the one list in CCountry's run of thirteen that CCountry::RebuildNeighbours clears (`lea edi,[ebx+0xFF8]; call 0xA77750` at 0x4E23CE) without appending to, so whatever fills it is elsewhere. `last` at +0xFFC, `count` at +0x1000. Recorded for the type alone, so that the apply lays a typed list here and the next function to touch it decompiles as a list walk instead of raw offsets - which is how the filler is most cheaply found. **The negative with its control:** `fieldchain.py --field 0xFFC` returns three sites, of which two are stores - 0x4C9951 in CCountry::CCountry (the four-member initialisation) and 0x4D41D8 in 0xD2B60, which the record already identifies as a clear of these lists - and one is an unrelated `lea esi,[esp+0xFFC]`. The same scan over +0xFAC, the `last` of the list two slots below, finds its genuine writer in RebuildNeighbours, so the method can see a writer when there is one. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: undeclared_war_opponents
fields.comment:
The CCountryList of countries this one is in an **undeclared** war with - the twin of `enemies` at +0x1008, `last` at +0x101C, `count` at +0x1020, same 0x14-byte nodes. Rebuilt from nothing by CCountry::UpdateUndeclaredWars (0xE6EE0): freed and zeroed at 0xE6F03-0xE6F2E, one node appended per country whose `CDiplomacyStatus::undeclared_war` (+0x24) is set, at 0xE7032-0xE7078. Live at the scenario start the count is 0 for all 108 countries. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)
+0x4 inside it: undeclared_war_opponents_last (void*) - Tail of the list at +0x1018; read at 0xE702C before each append and written at 0xE7063. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)
+0x8 inside it: undeclared_war_opponents_count (int) - Count of the list at +0x1018; read at 0xE705A and incremented at 0xE7060-0xE7069. Zeroed with the head and tail at 0xE6F2E. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)

fields.name: total_num_of_ports
fields.comment: A plain count. **Likely** ports including those of subjects or faction partners - the `total_num_of_ports` keyword's field, read by `CTotalNumOfPortsTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D8A50). Which of the two counts is 'total' is not established; only that the keyword reads this one and `num_of_ports` reads +0x105C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: num_of_vassals
fields.comment: A plain count. **Likely** the `num_of_vassals` keyword's field, read by `CNumOfVassalsTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5D9550). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: total_sea_battles
fields.comment: A plain count - the operand is divided by 1000 before the comparison, so the field is a whole number. **Likely** the `total_sea_battles` keyword's field, read by `CTotalSeaBattlesTrigger::Evaluate` (0x600060). The four fields +0x1070..+0x107C are read by four consecutive `CValueTrigger` leaves and sit immediately below the three `*_battles_fought` counters at +0x1080..+0x1088 that the savegame already names, so they are one war-statistics block. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: total_offensives
fields.comment: A plain count, the operand divided by 1000 before comparison. **Likely** the `total_offensives` keyword's field, read by `CTotalOffensivesTrigger::Evaluate` (0x600610). BlackICE's two uses are `total_offensives = 5` and `= 10`, which read as counts. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: total_defensives
fields.comment: A plain count, the operand divided by 1000 before comparison. **Likely** the `total_defensives` keyword's field, read by `CTotalDefensivesTrigger::Evaluate` (0x601170). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: total_we_bomb

fields.name: land_brigades_in_service
fields.comment: Counted by CCountry::RecountUnitTotals once per subunit of a unit the land predicate (unit slot 15, `[vftable+0x3C]`) accepts, and only when the country is mobilised (CCountry +0x94) or the subunit is not a reserve (CSubUnit +0xA4). So: land brigades in service, with reserves counted only once mobilisation has happened. The fourth of the four offsets FINDINGS-schedule.md left open on that function. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md)

fields.name: distribution_locked
fields.comment: Begin of a vector of ints (end at +0x1094), one for each slider in the order the production screen makes them: positive means the slider is held where it is. CProductionView::BuildSliders disables such a slider's button, and Update writes each slider's state back. The name is ours and what else reads it was not looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md)

fields.name: cabinet
fields.comment: **Cabinet seats per party**, a vector<int> indexed by CIdeology +0x4C, whole seats (not thousandths), written only by CCountry_AllotCabinetSeats. Saved as `cabinet = { ... }` (token 0x7C3); CCountry_Reset empties it and sizes it to the ideology count, and the `cabinet` key in LoadKey (0x4CEB73, through 0x45F450) appears to append, which is why a game loaded from a save writes 22 figures where a new one writes 11 (inferred). Read by CCountry_HasFracturedGovernment, CoupCabinetSeats, RunCountryDailyPass (0x4DBCBB: no seat for the ruling party runs AllotCabinetSeats), CEspionageView's tooltip (0x6200F2) and the politics view (0x6C0444). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: election
fields.comment: Named from the key CCountry::SaveContents writes it under, `election`. LoadKey stores the **negation** of the parsed yes/no (0x4CE6EC `cmp byte [esi],0; sete dl; mov [esi],dl`), the constructor zeroes it, and **nothing else in the image reads or writes it**: it is not the has-elections flag, which is the government's (CGovernment +0x7C). Every country in the start save says `election = yes` whatever its government. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: being_influenced
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CInfluence::Activate on the influenced country and to 0 by CInfluence::Deactivate and the constructor. **No reader in .text** at a disp32 encoding (a scan of all four displacement bytes finds those three stores and a stack `lea`); a byte this deep cannot be reached by a disp8, so only a read through a pointer already inside the object would be missed. Its use, if any, was not found. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: radar_provinces
fields.comment: Head of the list of province ids where the country has radar (tail +0x114C, count +0x1150), 0x10-byte nodes {id, prev, next, deleted}. Kept by CCountry::AddRadarProvince (rva 0xDD250) and CCountry_RemoveRadarProvince (rva 0xDD370), both gated on MODIFIER_RADAR_LEVEL; every change asks for the hourly intelligence refresh. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

fields.name: lost_ic
fields.comment: Thousandths - **unlike `total_ic`, which is whole IC**. The `lost_IC` keyword's field, read by `CLostICTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F86D0), which is the canonical direct-compare `CValueTrigger` body with no divide in it. **Likely** in name; the scale is read off the body. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: lost_national_provinces
fields.comment: Thousandths, compared directly against the operand. **Likely** the `lost_national` keyword's field, read by `CNationalProvinceTigger::Evaluate` (0x5F7D30). A thousandths field for what sounds like a count is the same oddity as `lost_ic` beside it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: espionage_capacity
fields.comment: The capacity pointer of the `std::vector<CSpyPresence>` whose begin is `espionage` (+0x1160) and end `espionage_end` (+0x1164). Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4C9ACB and again by the teardown at 0x4CA9A8. The vector is sized once per game, from the country count (`countryDatabase[+0x168]`), by 0x50EB70 at 0x4D4FC9, and then filled with one record per country - which is why the index into it is the country id. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: spy_pool
fields.comment: Spies the espionage leadership slider has bought and not yet placed, x1000; the save key is `spies` (token 0x272). CDistributeEspionage::Distribute adds `basePercentage * factor * available * 1000 * LEADERSHIP_TO_SPIES / 1000` to it at 0x51EDC6 and takes whole spies off it at 0x51F112 as it hands them to presences, highest priority band first. **There is no ceiling**: a country whose presences are all at band 0 or full keeps adding - Germany's is 13.723 in the 20 April 1936 save. Zeroed by the constructor and CCountry_Reset (0x4D2EBA); Lua's GetNumberOfFreeSpies (0x5187E0) answers it in whole spies. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: tech_decay_modifier
fields.comment: **not the tech ability array** - that is +0x698. Ints in thousandths indexed by CTechnologyCategory +0x5C, and the image's one use is at 0x420652, where the decay step is `BASE_TECH_DECAY x (this[cat] + 1000) / 1000`. So this is a per-category multiplier on the decay, and BiceLib's fixMinisterTechDecay (rva 0xDE3ED, a `mov` turned into an `add`) is a decay patch, not an ability one (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-research.md)

fields.name: tech_decay_modifier_end

fields.name: controlled_victory_points
fields.comment: The victory points of the provinces this country controls, thousandths - the country's own share of what its faction's Progress sums. Zeroed at the end of RunCountryHourlyPass and added to by RunHourlyProvincePass, which runs after it in RunHourlyPass, so between hours it holds the last hour's sum. Its readers were not sought. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: possible_vassals

fields.name: children_spare

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation. (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process; BiceLib/GameClasses/CCurrentGameState.hpp:47)

fields.name: strategic_warfare

fields.name: tutorial_active
fields.comment: set while a tutorial is running. **Renamed from `autosave_blocked`**, which was named after one reader - the autosave gate at 0x661DC9 - out of twelve. The only two writers in the image are CTutorialScreen button handlers: 0x71D6BA sets it when one of tutorial_button_1..6 is pressed, 0x71D365 clears it on back_button, and every constructed game state zeroes it through the word store that clears +0xD9C with it. Three readers say what it is for: while it is set RunHourlyPass never clears the AI latch +0xC68 (0x682B14), RunDailyPass skips the daily event pass (0x682F7B) and RunMonthlyPass skips the event-candidate rebuild (0x683C69) - so a tutorial runs with the event system off and the parallel AI pass latched off, declaring war through the command queue instead. It is zero in every ordinary game including a loaded one, so it cannot be the cause of an AI-stopped report. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-schedule.md. (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCurrentGameState.hpp:115)

fields.name: invasion_warnings_head
fields.comment: **The list of invasion warnings** is a std::map from +0x8 (head here, count at +0x10): one entry per country whose units are landing on the player's coast, keyed by country id, its value a vector of 0x28-byte unit references and a byte `new` at +0x10. Filled by InvasionWarnings_Add from SetUnitPath, read and pruned by InvasionWarnings_Hourly, which raises INVADEDUS from it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

fields.name: invasion_warnings_count
fields.comment: How many countries the list of invasion warnings holds (the map's size). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

fields.name: invasion_warnings_player
fields.comment: **The tag of the player the list of invasion warnings (+0x8) was kept for**, with its id at +0x1C. InvasionWarnings_Hourly compares the id with the player's (+0xC34) every hour and, where they differ, empties the list and copies +0xC30/+0xC34 here. That settles both readings this field had: the null tag `---` before the first hour of a session, the player's own tag (`IRE`) after it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

fields.name: invasion_warnings_player_id
fields.comment: The id half of +0x18: the player the invasion warnings were kept for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

fields.name: last_battle_winner_losses
fields.comment: The last land battle's winner losses, for the whole world - one figure, overwritten by CCombat::Conclude (0x174580) each time a battle of that kind ends, anywhere. Read only by the `last_battle_winner_losses` trigger. A plain number: the side's CCombatant losses (+0x84) / 1000, plus a term for the side's remaining units when the side's unnamed byte +0xA8 is set (land: total strength x 100; naval: ships; air: wings - read in the decompile, not the listing).
