fields.name: last_pride_sunk
fields.comment: The last pride of the fleet to be sunk; CGameState's field, carried here as the other base fields are. Written by CNavalCombatant::Attack, read for `$PRIDE_SUNK$`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-onactions.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-onactions.md)

fields.name: last_pride_sinker
fields.comment: The ship that sank the last pride of the fleet; CGameState's field, carried here as the other base fields are. Read for `$PRIDE_SINKER$`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-onactions.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-onactions.md)

fields.name: supply_network_dirty
fields.comment: set to 1 whenever CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot changes a province's supply depot label, and cleared by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork; the two rebuild sites are both `cmp byte [state+0x50], 0; je` around the call, one in the tick's hourly pass (0x282630, at 0x2826E8) and one in its daily pass (RunDailyPass 0x282C20, at 0x282CEF) (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: provinces_by_supply_order
fields.comment: every province sorted by supply depot distance, farthest first. Storage is one new[] of provinceCount*4 bytes at 0x27E52A; CSupply::ResetSupplyOrder (0x289AD0) refills it in province-id order and the qsort at 0x282D18 reorders it with CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending. The length is never stored here - every walker recomputes it from provinces_end - provinces_begin. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: max_supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: the largest supply_depot_distance on the map, taken from element 0 of provinces_by_supply_order right after the sort and clamped to 500. It is not the end pointer of the +0x54 vector - +0x54's storage is a plain new[] at 0x27E52A and its length is recomputed from the province vector everywhere it is walked. Where the raw value exceeded 500 the game also re-runs CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot on that farthest province, which is how a province cut off at 100000 gets a fresh depot label. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: flags
fields.comment: The global flags; CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's. See CGameState +0xC4. **The `CPersistent` second base is 0x24 into it**, and it is the sub-object `SaveContents` calls slot 1 on to write the `flags` block - which is why that offset once looked like a field of this class and was recorded as one (`flags_persistent` at +0xE8, deleted 2026-10-05). It is not declared here any more: `CFlags` is 0x28 bytes and Ghidra's own RTTI pass already names the second base's vftable at `CFlags+0x24`, so a `CPersistent` declared at +0xE8 collided with the `CFlags` held here and the two replaced each other on every apply - the period-2 cycle described in ghidra/README.md. The tree itself is this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md)

fields.name: strategic_resource_provinces
fields.comment: Begin of a vector (end +0xF8) of 16-byte elements, one for each strategic resource by index, each a vector of the provinces that have that resource (begin at +0, end at +4). RebuildStrategicResourceProvinces fills it; UpdateStrategicResources walks it from index 1. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset; both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: player_strategic_resource_provinces
fields.comment: Head of a list (tail +0x108, count +0x10C) of the provinces whose strategic resource the player's country has the use of. UpdateStrategicResources clears and refills it. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset; both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: ai_agents
fields.comment: Vector of every country's CEU3AI, begin. CGameState::StartAI (0x283140) pushes one per country here as it constructs them, and CGameState::RunAIPass hands this range to the ProcessAI tbb::parallel_for - so this vector is the AI's work list. A get-or-create at 0x683629 also searches it, matching an entry's `+0x20` and `+0x24` against a tag and a country id. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ai.md)

fields.name: ai_agents_end
fields.comment: Vector of every country's CEU3AI, end. `(+0x118 - +0x114) / 4` is the country count CGameState::RunAIPass divides into TBB grains at 0x6830C0. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ai.md)

fields.name: ai_agents_capacity
fields.comment: Vector of every country's CEU3AI, capacity; CGameState::StartAI compares end against it at 0x683325 before growing through 0xAB9B90. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ai.md)

fields.name: ai_generator
fields.comment: The same field as CGameState +0x124 - the AI's MT19937 - repeated because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

fields.name: relations
fields.comment:
**Head of the single polymorphic list of every CRelation in the game** - it is the list inside the embedded CDiplomacy at +0xB24, whose own fields sit at +8 (head), +0xC (tail) and +0x10 (count), which is why one helper is passed +0xB24 and the other +0xB2C. Every `type == ACCEPT` arm of the diplomatic actions' slot 7 appends its freshly made agreement here through 0x493E10 with the owner in ESI (five call sites: 0xA195DF alliance, 0xA1BDCA guarantee, 0xA21155 align, 0xA2BAC8 nap, 0xA2EFB9 embargo, 0xA35ED3 trade), and a cancellation finds its object here and takes it out with CList_RemoveNode before deleting it. This is what the savegame writes as the one top-level `diplomacy=` block: in Ireland1939_01_03_02.hoi3 it holds 1,248 `trade`, 38 `guarantee`, 21 `alliance`, 21 `influence`, 8 `align`, 8 `nap` and 7 `vassal` entries - seven of CRelation's ten subclasses, with CCasusBelli, CEmbargo and CWarning simply absent from that game. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)
+0x4 inside it: relations_end (void*) - Tail of the relation list at +0xB2C - the CDiplomacy's own +0xC. Written by 0x493E10 on every append. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)
+0x8 inside it: relations_count (int) - How many CRelation objects exist - the CDiplomacy's own +0x10. Incremented by 0x493E10 on every append and used there to tell the first append from the rest. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: unknown_b3c
fields.comment: start of an embedded object with vftable 0x11C9BEC (reversing/CLASSES.md:46)

fields.name: tick
fields.comment: current tick: **hours**, counted from an epoch 43800000 hours earlier. RunHourlyTick subtracts 0x29C55C0 from it and divides by 24 to get days, then uses MonthLengthTable and the 365.0 at 0x160A550 for month and year. 43800000 is 5000 x 365 x 24, so the epoch is 5000 years of 365 days before year zero (the factorisation is the evidence; that the designers thought of it as 5000 BC is inference). The image advances it in exactly one place, `inc dword [edi+0xBDC]` at 0x28155F inside RunHourlyTick. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tick.md)

fields.name: frame_time_accumulator
fields.comment: real time waiting to be turned into game hours: CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock adds each frame's delta to it and zeroes it when it posts a CHourlyTickCommand. The add happens before the in-flight test at +0xBF0, so time that passes during a long tick is caught up afterwards rather than lost (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tick.md)

fields.name: game_speed
fields.comment: the speed setting, used as an index into five float thresholds that CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock loads onto the stack from 0x160A2EC, 0x1718064, 0x171DBAC, 0x15AB304 and 0x160A740 - so speed is a table lookup, not arithmetic on one constant. Which index is pause, and the five values, have not been read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tick.md)

fields.name: tick_in_flight
fields.comment: set to 1 by RunHourlyTick in its third instruction (0x281425) and tested by CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock at 0x28114F, which posts nothing while it is set. It is the interlock that stops a second hour being queued inside the first (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tick.md)

fields.name: pending_unit_removals
fields.comment: A `tbb::strict_ppl::concurrent_queue` of `{id_type, id}` pairs - units a TBB worker has decided should die. `CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval` pushes with a `lock xadd`; `RunHourlyTick` drains it at `0x682230`-`0x6822B7` and calls `CGameState::RemoveUnit` per entry, **on the tick thread**. The queue object is two dwords: the representation pointer is `+0xBF8`, and the counters live in the representation - head at `rep+0`, tail at `rep+0x80`, eight micro-queues from `rep+0x180`. `CheckTransportOverload`'s comment already called this "the game state's message ring at +0xBF8"; it is a work queue, not a message ring. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-schedule.md)

fields.name: pending_unit_removals_rep
fields.comment: The representation of the queue at `+0xBF4`. `RunHourlyTick`'s emptiness test reads it directly at `0x682230`: the queue is empty when `rep[0x80] == rep[0]` and `rep[0] == rep[0] + rep[0x108]`, which is the TBB base's `empty()`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-schedule.md)

fields.name: fired_once_events
fields.comment: **The fire_only_once registry starts here**: this word is its element count, +0xC3C the bucket count and +0xC40 the buckets; &+0xC38 is what FiredEventRegistry_Find takes. Keyed by the event's id pair alone, not by country. Inserted into by FireEvent when a fire_only_once event fires (before it is answered), and by ResolveSavedFiredEvents on entering a loaded game. RebuildCountryEventCandidates and FireEvent both refuse an event found here. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: fired_once_bucket_count
fields.comment: The fired_once_events registry's bucket count; a key goes to bucket ((id_type << 16) + id) % this. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: fired_once_buckets
fields.comment: The fired_once_events registry's bucket array; each bucket heads a chain of 8-byte nodes {CEvent*, next}, new nodes pushed at the head. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: fired_events_loaded
fields.comment: Begin of a vector of 8-byte persistent id pairs read from the save - inferred to be the `fired_events` key - waiting to be resolved into the fired_once registry. ResolveSavedFiredEvents erases each entry it resolves. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: fired_events_loaded_end
fields.comment: End of the fired_events_loaded vector; ResolveSavedFiredEvents moves it down 8 for each id it resolves. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md)

fields.name: random_snapshot
fields.comment: a vector that SnapshotRandomState (0x282440) clears and refills every hour with g_random_draws and the dword at 0x174DA94. A pointer to this field is the second argument to CHourlyTickCommand::Construct, so the hourly tick command carries it (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tick.md)

fields.name: ai_pass_done
fields.comment: **The latch that makes the AI hourly.** CGameState::RunAIPass (0x283080) returns at once while this is set and sets it after launching the ProcessAI parallel_for (0x68309F, 0x683116); **RunHourlyPass clears it at its very end** (0x682B1D, guarded by `+0xD9D == 0`). A byte-exact sweep of .text finds only seven instructions touching this offset - those four plus two zeroing writes in the CGameState constructor region and nothing else - so the AI runs exactly once per game hour. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ai.md)

fields.name: year_change_count
fields.comment: Incremented once per year change, by RunYearlyPass at 0x283E67 as its last act, and zeroed in CGameState::CGameState at 0x27D487 immediately after the +0xC68 zero. A displacement-exact sweep of .text for `[reg + 0xC78]` finds those two sites and no other on the game state: **nothing reads it and nothing saves it**. So it counts year changes since this game-state object was built, which - because a load constructs a fresh one - is not the number of years since 1936. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aisched.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aisched.md)

fields.name: difficulty
fields.comment: The campaign's difficulty, 0..4 (`VERY_EASY`, `EASY`, `NORMAL`, `HARD`, `VERY_HARD` in the localisation). Element 0 of the save's `setgameplayoptions` vector, written only by `CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute` (0x2D5D20) and so fixed for the game. CCurrentGameState's constructor defaults it to 2, Normal, and every save read here carries `setgameplayoptions = { 2 0 }`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: arcade_mode
fields.comment:
The lobby's **Game Mode**: 0 Normal, 1 Arcade. Element 1 of the save's `setgameplayoptions` vector, written only by `CSetGamePlayOptions::Execute` (0x2D5D20), so it is set once when the game is started or loaded. CCurrentGameState's constructor defaults it to 0.

**This is the switch between the two supply models.** `CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel` tests it at 0x1BBA3A: above zero the unit draws straight from the owner's capital pool (`CProvince +0x15C`), at or below zero it walks the supply network. Twenty-odd other sites read it the same way. Measured live it reads 0, and every save in `BlackICE GitHub/save games` writes `{ 2 0 }`, so the network path is the one that runs in an ordinary campaign. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: intel_refresh_requests_first
fields.comment: Head of a `CList` of 0x10-byte nodes each holding an int: provinces whose intelligence is to be raised this hour, appended by GameState_RequestIntelRefresh (CUnit::EnterProvince, CLocalIntelBoost::Execute), and **-1 pushed to the front** to ask for the whole rebuild (a change of owner or controller, a radar, an alliance or military access made or ended, a faction joined, a change of who controls a country, and the rest RunIntelRefreshIfRequested lists). RunIntelRefreshIfRequested reads it at the end of every hour - the whole rebuild where the head is -1, else each named province - and RunHourlyTick then frees every node and zeroes head, tail and count (0x6823DD..0x682407). So a request lives one hour. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: intel_refresh_requests_last
fields.comment: Tail of the list at `+0xCF8`. The position is inference from the `{first, last, count}` shape plus `+0xD00` being read as the count; this dword was not read directly. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-schedule.md)

fields.name: intel_refresh_requests_count
fields.comment: Count of the list at `+0xCF8`. `RunIntelRefreshIfRequested` tests it with `cmp dword [eax+8], 1; jl` at `0x689319` and returns without doing anything when it is zero. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-schedule.md)

fields.name: victory_conditions
fields.comment: The victory conditions (CVictoryConditionManager). Saved as `victory_conditions` by CGameState::SaveContents, and the loader puts it back here. CCurrentGameState derives from CGameState and adds nothing at this offset. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: leader_trait_filters
fields.comment: The leader window's trait filter, one std::vector<CTrait*> of the traits that are on per leader type at 0x10 each - land, naval, air (a fourth, for type 3, would reach +0xD9C). Read by CCurrentGameState::LoadLeaderTraitFilters, written by SaveLeaderTraitFilters. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderwindow.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderwindow.md)

fields.name: loaded_from_save
fields.comment:
**Nonzero when this session was loaded from a savegame rather than started from history** - the new-game/load switch, and the field CInGameIdler::Enter uses to tell the two apart.

One instruction in the image writes it a one: 0x27CEB9, inside CGameState::LoadFromSave (0x27CE30), set after the session reset has cleared it and immediately before CPersistent::Load parses the save, so it stays set for the life of the session. The three clears are the session reset 0x27BB26 (which the loader calls first), the startup reset 0x27B599, and 0x23A60E in the unread 0x23A460; every construction of the game state zeroes it as part of the word store that clears tutorial_active +0xD9D with it.

**23 readers, and thirteen of them are inside CInGameIdler::Enter** (0x25A89B, 0x25ACA2, 0x25B06B, 0x25B26D, 0x25B37F, 0x25B4D4, 0x25B8B7, 0x25BF47, 0x25C7F0, 0x25D22D, 0x25D4C9, 0x261935, 0x261A85) - i.e. thirteen places where entering a game does something different for a load than for a new game. The rest: CCountry::LoadKey (0x4CE6B1), CUnit::LoadKey (0x1B70C7), SupplyNeed (0x9E0D7), ProcessAI twice (0x4896B3, 0x4897CB), two inside CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler (0x248CD2, 0x248EFD), 0x24C317, and four in gamesetup.cpp (0x30E744, 0x31545A, 0x315D31, 0x3160F9).

Read live as 0 in a freshly started 1936 campaign - one session, so that is one data point, but with this writer list a zero reading is what says the session was not loaded. The record previously treated this byte as nothing but the other half of tutorial_active's word store. `likely` for the name, `confirmed` for the writers and the reader count. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-session.md section 7.

**Confirmed live live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save: reads 1 in a loaded save.** The scenario-start reading was 0 in a freshly started campaign, so both arms of the flag are now observed and the name is no longer resting on the writer list alone.

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation. (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-session.md)

fields.name: tutorial_id
fields.comment:
The dword between +0xD9C and in_game, zeroed by every construction of the game state and by the startup reset (0x27B599's neighbour at 0x27B59F), by CFrontEnd::Enter (0x2EFEF5) and by CTutorialScreen (0x31D3E2).

**Set to 1..6 by CTutorialScreen::OnTutorialButtonPressed at 0x31D73C**, one arm per tutorial button, 0x82 bytes after the same function sets tutorial_active (+0xD9D) = 1 - and **read in exactly one place in the whole image**, 0x24FE97, which hands it to CInGameIdler slot 90 as the tutorial runner's value.

Method: of 2441 instructions in .text whose own displacement is 0xDA0, 2434 are copies of the inlined get-or-create accessor, identified by the CCurrentGameState vftable constant 0x15CF674 within the preceding 0x18 bytes - the same discriminator FINDINGS-session.md section 1 used for +0xDA4. Of the remaining seven, one (0x4CACC5) is a different class, five are the construction zeroes above and the tutorial-screen write, and one is the single read. Trap 14 checked both halves: neither project.json nor BiceLib/GameClasses/CCurrentGameState.hpp names this offset. `likely` rather than `confirmed` only because the name reads the one writer and the one reader rather than any string. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

fields.name: in_game
fields.comment:
Nonzero while the in-game screen is the live one: set to 1 at `0x25D126`, the end of `CInGameIdler::Enter`'s session build, and cleared by `CInGameIdler::Leave` (`0x262337`), by `CFrontEnd`'s enter (`0x2EFE58`) and at `0x2ED9AF`. Zeroed by every construction of the game state.

**This is the attrition gate.** `CUnit::UpdateDaily` tests it at `DailyTickEndGate` (`0x1BB3E8`) and skips both `ApplyAttrition` and `CheckTransportOverload` when it is zero - so it is not a development-era "enable attrition" switch, and attrition does run. About twenty other places test it before touching live game data (`0x255AB7` reaches `strategic_warfare`, `0x4349B2` reaches the player tag), which is the sense the name is taken from: a game is running.

One byte. The last field of the class: the object is allocated `0xDA8` bytes and the constructor tail writes a word at `+0xD9C`, a dword at `+0xDA0` and this byte, so `+0xDA5..+0xDA7` are padding.

Not saved: no access to it lives in the save or load code, and no key in a `.hoi3` save corresponds to it.

**Confirmed in a running game**, not only traced: sampled every frame it read 0 at the main menu with the pointer already live, 1 once a campaign was up - while the clock was still not reporting in play, which is the write landing before the in-game GUI is built - and 0 again on returning to the menu. See `Reversing/Watch.hpp`.

**The writer census completed 2026-10-02, and re-derived by a second method before anything was changed on its strength** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-session.md section 1). Of 2,822 occurrences of the displacement 0xDA4 in .text, 2,820 are instructions whose own displacement it is, 2,778 of those are writes on a register other than esp/ebp, and **2,772 of those are one inlined get-or-create accessor**, identified by the CCurrentGameState vftable constant 0x15CF674 within 0x18 bytes before the write. That leaves **exactly six real writes**, and **only one of them writes a one**: 0x25D126 in CInGameIdler::Enter. The clears are 0x262337 (CInGameIdler::Leave), 0x2ED9AF (CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd), 0x2EFE58 (CFrontEnd::Enter) and two that were **not previously in this list**: 0x27B146, the out-of-line constructor CCurrentGameState::CCurrentGameState, and 0x27B599, the startup reset 0x27B240.

**It is NOT set during a load.** The savegame loader 0x27CE30 and its caller 0x27CAE0 contain none of the six, and 0x27CAE0's only three callers are the pre-game lobby (twice) and CTutorialScreen - screens that are not the in-game screen. So in_game is 0 for the whole of a load. What GameClock::movedInPlay() actually excludes is a different window: the write at 0x25D126 sits 0x4A92 bytes from the end of CInGameIdler::Enter, and everything after it builds the in-game interface, so there is a stretch in which in_game is 1 and the in-game GUI does not exist yet.

**Measured across a menu trip (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process).** Returning to the main menu in the same process, the game-state pointer read **0x37BBD818 before and after, byte-identical** - so the object is reset and never replaced, which promotes FINDINGS-session.md section 5 from `likely` to observed. In the same action: `in_game` 1 -> 0, `loaded_from_save` 1 -> 0, `in_game_screen` from a `CInGameIdler` to a **`CFrontEnd`**, `player` from `GER` to the null tag `---`, and the tick reset to **60759360**, which is the 1936-01-01 00:00 epoch. Five separate static claims and one prediction, all confirmed by one observation. (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 save, in-game then main menu, same process; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-session.md; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: Type
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetType, inherited from CDiplomaticAction
BiceLib: type (int) - The action's `CDiplomaticAction::EType`, and the **stage** an offer is at rather than what kind of offer it is: the kind is the C++ subclass, and its name is slot 15's save token. `CDiplomaticAction::GetType` is registered to Lua and resolves to a two-instruction `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret` at 0x416000. The enum has **three** values, all registered in one luabind chain ending at 0x8ED397: ('PROPOSE', ebx) at 0x8ED38D with ebx zeroed at 0x8EAE68 and never rewritten, ('DECLINE', 1) at 0x8ED37F, and **('ACCEPT', 2) at 0x8ED3BB**, appended to the same value vector at 0x8ED3C9 and registered by the loop at 0x8ED3CE. So 0 = PROPOSE, 1 = DECLINE, 2 = ACCEPT. What acts on it: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute enqueues a PROPOSE on the recipient and anything else on the actor; the hourly AI pass at 0x682BA8 only touches entries still at PROPOSE and writes 2 into the field at 0x682BB3 to accept them. The body at 0x416000 has two references and so is **not** recorded under a class name (trap 4); the field is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: Value
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetValue, inherited from CDiplomaticAction
BiceLib: value (unsigned char) - A bool, exposed to Lua as GetValue/SetValue: CDiplomaticAction::SetValue (0xA0E980, one reference, no vftable) is `this->+0x24 = [ebp+8]` and the getter is the folded `mov al,[ecx+0x24]` at 0xA0E990. **CTradeAction::IsValid (slot 13, 0xA38770) branches on it at 0xA387DA**: set, and it validates a fresh trade offer; clear, and it instead requires that an identical route already exist on the pair. So `value` is the proposal/cancellation polarity a script controls. **Units: none - it is a bool, not thousandths.** In the save it is written `value=yes` / `value=no`, 39 yes and 6 no over the 45 saves on this machine, which is also how the `value` loader case reads it: ParseBool (rva 0x67B410) at 0xA0E6E6, not a number. Seven of the family also use it as their slot-18 answer, through the folded `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x24], 0; setne al; ret` at 0xA0FE10 and the recorded ReturnByteAt24 at 0xA0E990. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: persistent_id
fields.comment: Always 0x18D. Written by CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor (0xA0EB30), by each of the eleven Lua `Create` factories (e.g. 0x8E84A9) and copied by every slot-16 clone, so every action in the family carries it. **It is not a per-class discriminator**: CCommand +0x4 is recorded as "a class id" and holds the same 0x18D, and the kind of action is carried by slot 15's save token instead. What reads it was not traced; token 0x18D resolves to `none`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: actor
fields.comment: The country making the offer, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the four-character tag at +0x8 and the country id at +0xC. Loaded from the save key `actor` (token 0x2E9) at 0xA0E7B5/0xA0E7BB, where CCountryDataBase::GetTag's result is copied as two dwords. CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor fills it with "---" and id 0. Every reader that wants the CCountry indexes `g_CCountryDataBase::countries_first` with +0xC: CTradeAction::IsValid, CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute and the base's slot 14 all do. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: recipient
fields.comment: The country being offered to, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the tag at +0x10 and the id at +0x14. Loaded from the save key `recipient` (token 0x2EA) at 0xA0E86A/0xA0E874. The base's slot 14, `IsSelectable` (0xA0EAE0), is three instructions: `return actor_id != recipient_id` - so the family's default selectability test is just "these are two different countries". (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: date
fields.comment: When the offer was made, in **hours** on the same scale as g_CCurrentGameState's tick (+0xBDC), counted from the 43,800,000-hour epoch. Loaded from the save key `date` (token 0x1F8) through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E70A, written by every Lua `Create` factory from the current tick, and set to the epoch itself - the engine's null date, [0x170C2B8] - by the null action's constructor. CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's only use of it is `date + 0xA8`, seven days, handed to CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: last_command_date
fields.comment: When the action was last put on the wire, in hours on the tick scale - the save's own key name (token 0x3EC), loaded through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E806. **Two independent writers, both setting it to the current tick**: CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand stamps it just before wrapping the action in a command (0xA0E92D) and CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction stamps it again as the action is enqueued (0x4E62EB). That is what makes it later than `date` for an offer that has travelled: in the save corpus it differs from `date` in 34 of 56 blocks and is never earlier. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: war_goal
fields.comment: The goal the declaration is made over, embedded by value (0x2C bytes, vftable 0x15BDB34). The war effect copies its first attacker goal here; Apply hands it to CWarGoal::AddToWar and RunCasusBelliOnAdd and spends a matching casus belli; slot 13 tests it with CWarGoal::IsValidForWar. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: joined_attackers
fields.comment: Scratch list filled by Apply: the countries it put on the attacker side or called for it (puppets). Freed and zeroed at the start of each Apply; CallAllies skips the countries on it when the caller is the actor. Nodes 0x14 bytes {tag, id, prev, next, byte}. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: joined_defenders
fields.comment: The same for the defender side: puppets, guarantors whose accepted call was executed, the recipient's overlord whose call was made. CallAllies skips them when the caller is the recipient; the overlord's call is skipped where the overlord is already here. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.comment: defines.lua's top-level `base_militia` ('militia_brigade' in Their Finest Hour), a string by value (buffer at +0x80, length +0x90, capacity +0x94, zeroed by the constructor at 0x445365). Read by name into the subunit database: the regiment type a government in exile's partisans (supply_consumption 0 or less) become when it comes back (SetGovernmentInExile, 0x503315). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

fields.comment: the economy block of defines.lua. the entries are not read in file order - they are read by key, and the offsets are compiled into CDefines::Load. This block happens to agree with the file, which is exactly why the file-order reading looked confirmed. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

The entries are read by key, so their offsets do not move when the mod's defines.lua changes. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.comment: the diplomacy block of defines.lua. CDefines::Load loads this pointer into a register and stores each entry of the block through it at a compiled-in offset, keyed by name. 67 entries, WARDEC_BELIGERENCY at +0x0 to LEND_LEASE_MAX_IC_HIGH at +0x108. No struct is recorded for it yet; `python scripts/definesMap.py --block diplomacy` prints the map. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.comment: the country block of defines.lua. the entries are not read in file order but by key, into offsets compiled into CDefines::Load, and for this block the two disagree: NO_MISSION_SPY_DETECTION_MULTIPLIER is at +0x3C, not +0x60. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.comment: the alignment block of defines.lua. CDefines::Load loads this pointer into a register and stores each entry of the block through it at a compiled-in offset, keyed by name. 13 entries, ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL at +0x0 to REPULSION_IC_FACTOR at +0x30. No struct is recorded for it yet; `python scripts/definesMap.py --block alignment` prints the map. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

CDefines::Load loads this pointer into a register and stores each entry of the block through it at a compiled-in offset, keyed by name. 56 entries, PRESSUREMIN at +0x0 to INITIAL_SIMULATION_HOURS_AHEAD at +0xDC. No struct is recorded for it yet; `python scripts/definesMap.py --block weather` prints the map. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: map
fields.comment: the map block of defines.lua. CDefines::Load loads this pointer into a register and stores each entry of the block through it at a compiled-in offset, keyed by name. 10 entries, SUEZ at +0x0 to GIBRALTAR_BLOCKER at +0x24, and these are read by rva 0x460D0 as plain ints, not scaled - they are province ids. The mod's WHITESEA and WHITESEA_BLOCKER are not among them and are never read. No struct is recorded for it yet; `python scripts/definesMap.py --block map` prints the map. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CRelation

fields.name: first
fields.comment: **The first party to the agreement** (save key `first`). Resolved from the three letters in the save through CCountryDataBase::GetTag, so the tag characters land at +0x8 and the index at +0xC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: second
fields.comment: **The second party to the agreement** (save key `second`). The same resolution as `first`, into the tag at +0x10 and the index at +0x14. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement began**, as a tick (save key `start_date`). Parsed from `year.month.day.hour` text by Date_SetFromString, which is the same representation every other date in the simulation uses. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement ends**, as a tick (save key `end_date`); **the null date 43,800,000 (`[0x170C2B8]`) where it has none** - every constructor sets it so, not zero. A real date is told by `(end_date - 43,800,000) / 24 / 365.0 > 1`. Read only by CCasusBelli (Activate, which will not attach an expired one, and IsOver) and by CRelation::SaveContents (written only when real). **No other relation's IsOver reads it**: a guarantee ends twenty years after `start_date`, a NAP NAP_EXPIRY_MONTHS after it, and the history files' end dates take effect only while history is replayed before play. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: cancel
fields.comment: **Whether the agreement is cancelled** (save key `cancel`), the last of CRelation's own bytes - a subclass's data starts at +0x24. Loaded as a plain comparison against the token `yes`, so any other value, including `no`, leaves it 0. **CDiplomacy::SaveContents skips every relation with it set**, and CRelation::SaveContents, given one, writes `cancel = yes` instead of `start_date`. No writer in play was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: Value
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomacyStatus::GetValue
BiceLib: relation (int) - The pair's relation, **thousandths on a -200.000..+200.000 scale**. CCountry::ChangeRelation (rva 0xE65C0) adds a delta to the forward side, clamps against [0x1710C38] = -200000 and [0x1710C34] = 200000, and writes the single clamped result to **both** directions. 24 call sites: diplomatic actions' slot 7, effects, faction joins' war sweep and a combat conclude. **But it is not the only writer, and the two sides are not equal by construction** (corrected 2026-10-12, FINDINGS-diplostate.md). One direction only: CDiplomacyStatus::SetValue (rva 0x648160, a loaded save's `value`), CRelationChange::Apply (rva 0x1F2CA0, history/diplomacy/relation.txt) and SetUpCountryForNewGame (rva 0xD6230, the store at VA 0x4D7316: the starting relation from the Lua global AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation, written only where this is still 0). Both directions from one side's value: CCountry::UpdateMonthly (rva 0xDC840, stores at VA 0x4DCCF0 and 0x4DCD27: the month's drift from MonthlyRelationDrift, rva 0xE78D0), MakeVassal (rva 0xD94A0) and CCreateVassalCommand::Execute (rva 0x14BD00). Zeroed by the constructor (rva 0x647DF0) and CDiplomacyStatus::Reset (rva 0x647F20). So at a new game's start the matrix is asymmetric wherever history set one side, and is made symmetric by the month pass that runs before the first hour - from the side of whichever country comes first in the country order. The savegame writes it as whole points truncated toward zero (`value=75`, `value=-125` for -125.100) while writing `threat` beside it with three decimals, so the save is not the evidence for the scale; BlackICE's common/defines.lua:299 EMBARGO_RELATION_CHANGE = -200.0, i.e. -200000 stored, exactly the clamp floor, is. The alignment relation term averages this field over a faction's members and scales it by RELATION_WEIGHT. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-politics.md)

read by CDiplomacyStatus::IsFightingWarTogether
BiceLib: co_belligerent (unsigned char) - Set to 1 between two countries when either joins the side of a war the other is already on, and cleared when either leaves. The writers are SetWarSideCoBelligerentFlags (0xA51CB0) and ClearWarSideCoBelligerentFlags (0xA51C40), each of which writes **both** directions of the pair; their four callers are CWar::AddAttacker (0x64F220, already named), CWar::AddDefender (0x6506B0, already named) and the two Remove siblings 0x650440/0x651710, passing `war->attackers` (+0x2C) or `war->defenders` (+0x3C). Found by scanning every function that mentions the disp32 0xE28 for a byte store to [reg+0x58] - 177 candidates, of which only these two write both halves of a pair. Not a save key (FINDINGS-theatre2.md) and not military_access (+0x4C). This is the byte CCountry::RebuildNeighbours tests at 0x4E32E9 to decide membership of CCountry +0xF98, so that list is **us plus our co-belligerents, minus anyone we are also at war with** - the rule the record had to name from the walk alone.

**Two readers in the AI confirm the sense from the other side**, found independently (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-subdivide.md): AreaMayWidenFrontSearch (0x495140, at 0x4951DD) and CAIUnit::RebuildAreaNeighbourProvinces (0x4BC860) both require this byte on exactly the branch where CCountry::IsSameSide has already answered no - i.e. "not on our side, but co-belligerent, so this area may widen the front search". That survey proposed the name `military_access` for it from that role alone; the writers settle it the other way, and military_access is +0x4C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-trade2.md)

fields.name: Threat
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomacyStatus::GetThreat
BiceLib: threat (int) - How much threat the array's owner feels from the other country, thousandths, never below 0 and never capped. **Every writer**: SpreadThreat (0xF50A0) and SpreadThreatToAll (0xF4E80), the two spreaders every game event goes through; CThreatEffect::Execute with a tag (a direct add, no modifiers); AnnexCountry (0xE7B00), which takes 9999.000 off both directions between the annexed country and every other and then resets the other's status (to 0); CDiplomacyStatus::Reset (0x647F20) and the constructor (0x647DF0), 0; CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey, the save's `threat`. **Nothing decays it**: no daily or monthly pass writes it, and nothing but a negative effect, demobilisation, an embargo lifted or an annexation lowers it. Readers: the alignment threat term (max over a faction's members), CCountry::RebuildNeighbours electing highest_threat (+0x11D8), EffectiveNeutrality through that, CIsThreatendTrigger::Evaluate over the neighbours, and CDiplomacyStatus::GetThreat for Lua. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplostate.md)

fields.name: TradeRoutes
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomacyStatus::GetTradeRoutes
BiceLib: trade_routes (CList<CTradeRoute*>) - The pair's trade routes - head at +0x60, count at +0x68. It is what the game's own Lua `CDiplomacyStatus:GetTradeRoutes()` hands out (the luabind registration is for `const CList<CTradeRoute*>&`). CCountry::RunDailyTradeRoutes (0xFEE70) skips a pair whose count is zero and otherwise walks this list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoys.md)
+0x4 inside it: trade_routes_end (void*) - Tail of the `trade_routes` list at +0x60, between it and `trade_routes_count` at +0x68. Read as the previous node and overwritten with the new one by CTradeRoute::Activate (0xA4D2F3 and 0xA4D31E), which appends the route to both directions' lists when a trade offer is accepted. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)
+0x8 inside it: trade_routes_count (int) - How many trade routes the pair has; the count of the list at +0x60, tested at 0x4FEF66 before the list is touched. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoys.md)

fields.name: allowDebts
fields.comment: read by CDiplomacyStatus::AllowDebts

fields.name: occupation_policy
fields.comment: The occupation policy the array's owner applies to provinces of the other country it controls. **Never null**: CDiplomacyStatus::Reset stores the shared `no_occupation` (g_null_occupation_policy). Written by Province_SetController on a capture (Province_SetController_InitOccupationPolicy - keyed new controller -> old controller: `civil_war` where its allow holds, else the file's first policy, only while it is still no_occupation), by CChangeOccupationPolicyCommand::Execute (the player, from the politics screen), by COccupationChange::Apply (history), by the save loader, and back to no_occupation by Reset (new country, session reset, AnnexCountry for every country's status toward the annexed). Nothing at peace or on a change of hands resets it. Read by RebuildProvinceModifierValues (controller -> owner), the politics screen's rows, and the save writer (written only when slot 14 holds, so a new game's save has none). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section A. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: alliance
fields.comment:
The pair's alliance object, or null - the first of the relation pointers that run +0x14 `alliance`, +0x18 (a relation tested for token `vassal`), +0x1C `guarantee`, +0x20 `war`, +0x24 `undeclared_war`, +0x28 `nap`. Named by the game's own Lua predicate `CDiplomacyStatus::HasAlliance` (rva 0x94660), which is `cmp dword [ecx+0x14], 0; setne al; ret` and nothing else.

This is the field the event language's `alliance_with` trigger evaluates (CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate, rva 0x5EF5A0, at 0x5EF605) and the gate on the append to `CCountry +0xF88` (Allies) in CCountry::RebuildNeighbours at 0x4E328E. It is **not** what faction membership sets - that is `CCountry +0xD8 -> CFaction +0x28` - which is why the allies list has a second, faction-walking source and `alliance_with` does not. FINDINGS-faction.md section 4 measures how far the two diverge: in the 1945 save the world holds 7 of these against 674 intra-faction country pairs.

Written in **both** directions by CAlliance::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA46A40), which is reached from CAllianceAction::Apply (slot 7) when an alliance offer is accepted; the same object is appended to the one CDiplomacy relation list at CCurrentGameState +0xB24 and is saved as an `alliance=` block there. Independent agreement: project.json's own account of 0x8A9390 reads +0x14 as 'they are our ally'.

**Merged 2026-10-06** from two records on this offset - a `void*` one and a `CAlliance*` one. merge_fields keeps whichever comes first, so the decompilation had been getting `void*`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

fields.name: dependency
fields.comment: The pair's overlord/puppet relationship, or null - a CDependency or its subclass CVassal. Written in **both** directions by CDependency::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA47760, inherited by CVassal), which also calls 0x4EDD80 on each country. Saved as a `vassal=` block in the one `diplomacy=` list at CCurrentGameState +0xB24; the save corpus has 7. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: guarantee
fields.comment:
The pair's guarantee object, or null. Named by the game's own Lua predicates `CDiplomacyStatus::IsGuaranting` (rva 0x648730) and `CDiplomacyStatus::IsGuaranteed` (rva 0x648760), which are the same body twice over: both read `+0x1C`, answer false when it is null, and otherwise compare the relation's `+0xC` with the status's own `+0xC` - `setne` for one direction and `sete` for the other. So the one pointer carries both directions and the `+0xC` comparison is what tells them apart; **no token test is involved**, unlike the relation at +0x18.

CCountry::RebuildNeighbours appends to the list at `CCountry +0xFC8` on this field plus the same direction test (0x4E3398-0x4E3406), so `+0xFC8` is one of the two guarantee directions - which one was not settled.

Written in **both** directions by CGuarantee::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA46DB0), a 17-instruction function that does nothing else. Reached from CGuaranteeAction::Apply (slot 7), which - alone in the family - builds and attaches its object on the `value` test without ever looking at `type`, so a guarantee takes effect when it is offered. Saved as a `guarantee=` block with `first`, `second`, `start_date` and `end_date` in the one `diplomacy=` list; the save corpus has 38.

**Merged 2026-10-06** from a `void*` record and a `CGuarantee*` one; the `void*` came first and was what reached the decompilation. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

fields.name: undeclared_war
fields.comment: The pair's undeclared war, or null - the field that sits between +0x20 `war` and +0x28 `nap`. Read in exactly one shape: CCountry::IsEnemy (0x42F25D) and the dozen places that inline it take it, give up when it is null, and otherwise hand it to UndeclaredWarCoversProvince (0x4763A0) together with the province, which walks its +0x28/+0x2C region vector against the province's own region list. CUndeclaredWar::LoadKey (0x475A60) has a `region` key (token 0x414), which is what makes the vector the war's regions. Likely rather than confirmed because nothing seen here writes the field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-invasion.md)

fields.name: nap
fields.comment: The pair's non-aggression pact, or null - one CNap for both directions. Written by CNap::Activate (both directions) and cleared by CNap::Deactivate (both). CCountry::CanBreakNap reads its `second` (+0x10/+0x14), `start_date` (+0x18) and `balance` (+0x24); CNap_UpdateForceBalance measures it weekly from the first party's daily pass; CDiplomacyStatus_ExpireRelations ends it NAP_EXPIRY_MONTHS after its start; CDeclareWarAction::Apply ends it between belligerents (0xA122C8). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: influence_running
fields.comment: **The `CInfluence*` itself**, not a flag - non-null exactly while a diplomatic influence is running between the pair, and carried **only on the influenced country's side**, `influenced->diplomacy[influencer]`. Writer CInfluence::Activate (rva 0x64AAD0); cleared by CInfluence::Deactivate. Readers: CCountry::PayDailyInfluenceUpkeep charges INFLUENCE_UPKEEP once a day for each country whose status toward the payer has it set, CCountry::GetInfluencedCountryCount counts the same, CInfluenceNation::Apply refuses a second influence from the same faction on it, and CDiplomacyStatus_ExpireRelations and SetPairWar end it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: align
fields.comment: The alignment drift the array's owner is running against the other country, or null - **one direction only**, written by CAlign::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA4B110) as `countries[first_id]->diplomacy[second_id]->+0x30 = this`, and it is the one slot 10 that does not set `+0x59`. Reached from CInfluenceAllianceLeader::Apply (slot 7), which reads ALIGN_INFLUENCE_COST and DAYS_OF_ALIGN_RELATION_CHANGE. Saved as an `align=` block in the one `diplomacy=` list; the save corpus has 8. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: embargo
fields.comment: The pair's embargo, or null. Written in **both** directions by CEmbargo::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA4B530), which sets `+0x59` on neither side. Reached from CEmbargoAction::Apply (slot 7), which reads EMBARGO_RELATION_CHANGE and EMBARGO_INFLUENCE_COST and has no accept/decline pair in its message keys: an embargo is imposed, not agreed. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: casus_belli
fields.comment:
The casus belli the array's owner holds against the other country - **one direction only**, `countries[first_id]->diplomacy[second_id]`. Head at +0x3C, tail at +0x40, count at +0x44, nodes 0x10 bytes `{payload, prev@+4, next@+8, byte@+0xC}`. Written by CCasusBelli::Activate (CRelation slot 10, 0xA47BB0), which refuses to attach one whose end date (CRelation +0x1C) is in the past or within two of whatever `[0x160A550]` divides by. **This is the list CWarGoalBaseAction::Apply (slot 7 of CAddWarGoalAction and CJoinFactionGoalAction) searches**, matching a list entry's +0x24 against the action's own war goal's `casusBelli->+8`, and then removes that CCasusBelli from the CDiplomacy relation list and deletes it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)
+0x4 inside it: casus_belli_end (void*) - Tail of the casus-belli list at +0x3C. Read as the previous node and overwritten with the new one by CCasusBelli::Activate at 0xA47CB7 and 0xA47CE2. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)
+0x8 inside it: casus_belli_count (int) - How many casus belli the array's owner holds against the other country; the count of the list at +0x3C, incremented by CCasusBelli::Activate at 0xA47CDC and used there to tell the first append from the rest. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: next_offer_allowed
fields.comment:
A tick (hours), set to the proposal's `date + 0xA8` - **exactly seven days** - by CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed (0xA4A550), whose one caller is CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute on the PROPOSE path, for every kind of action except `callaction` (0x309), on the proposer's status toward the recipient. **Read by CCountry::HasDiplomatEnroute (rva 0xE3ED0), `tick <= this`**: while it holds the proposer has "a diplomat enroute" to that country - the diplomacy screen greys the row and shows ENROUTE with this date, and the AI scripts skip that country. Execute does not test it, so an offer posted regardless (Lua's PostAction with no check) is not refused. The setter's own comparison against `tick + 0xA8` is dead - both arms store the same value.

**The game's own name for the field is `last_send_diplomat`**: CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey (rva 0x648190) stores that key, token 0x306, here at 0xA482C1 through Date_SetFromString. The code is on the record's side about tense: what is stored is the date the diplomat arrives, seven days in the future. So the key is noted and the behavioural name kept. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: war_seen_tick
fields.comment: Save key `last_war` (CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey, token 0x305, at VA 0xA4823E). **Written by CCountry::UpdateAtWarAndEnemies (0x4E6C32) with the current tick, for every pair still at war when it runs - and it runs only as a session is entered and when a war's membership changes, not hourly** (corrected 2026-10-13: this said 'on every diplomatic action and once an hour'). So it is the tick of the last such moment while the pair were at war, and CDiplomacyStatus::HasTruce counts the 2400-hour truce from it; a long war with no change of membership since the last load leaves no truce. Other writers: SetUpCountryForNewGame puts a value later than now back to the null date, and ReleaseProvinces stamps a released country's pair with its former owner. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: changed
fields.comment:
Set to 1 by everything that changes the pair's standing, and **read by nothing in the image**. The whole universe of `[reg+0x59]` instructions in `.text` is 60 sites - 52 stores, 7 loads and one `lea` - and every one of the eight non-stores belongs to another class: three to CCreateUnitCommand (vftable 0x11C36D4), three to the CSetRandomSeed/CPauseGame command family (vftable 0x11D3434), one to a refcounted SEH object at 0x8364B0, and the `lea` to a hash-padding buffer at 0xAF8D40. **Thirty-seven of the 52 stores are on a CDiplomacyStatus**, all reached as `country->diplomacy_status_array (+0xE28)[id]` or through one of two setter helpers whose first act is this write - 0xA4A400 (which also writes +0x4C and then, if `g_CCurrentGameState->in_game` is set, ORs 0x100 into something reached through the state's +0xBE8, i.e. refreshes the interface) and 0xA4A3B0 (which also frees the casus-belli list). So the interface refresh is done by the **writer**, not by a reader of this flag.

The writers are CCountry::ChangeRelation (both directions, 0x4E65D8 and 0x4E660B) and **six** of the nine CRelation::Activate bodies - CAlliance, CGuarantee, CNap and CDependency twice each, one side apiece for CCasusBelli and CInfluence - plus CCountry::UpdateUndeclaredWars, CCountry::AfterLoad, CCountryEventEffect::Execute, CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey's neighbourhood and several of the command LoadKeys.

Nothing reads it, so `changed` describes its writers and cannot be falsified beyond that; it is kept rather than renamed because no better name is available from a body that has no consumer. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

fields.name: debt
fields.comment: **What the array's owner owes the other country**, thousandths of money - corrected 2026-10-13, this said the other way round. Save key `debt`, token 0x727 (CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey at 0xA4836E). Grows only while the owner is at war and has allowDebts (+0x78) towards the other: by a licence fee (CLicenceTechnologyAction::Apply, 0xA3C5A1 - the buyer's status towards the seller) and by a trade route's money (CCountry::RunDailyTradeRoutes, 0x4FF442 and 0x4FF485). **Nothing reduces it**: the daily repayment (CCountry::CollectDailyProduction) pays out of it without subtracting, so a debt is repaid for ever. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: daily_repay
fields.comment: How much the owner repays the other a day, thousandths of money. Save key `dailyrepay`, token 0x728. Fixed by CDiplomacyStatus::GetDailyRepay as debt / (YEARS_TO_REPAY_DEBT * 365 days) the first time it is asked with a debt and nothing here; set back to 0 by CCountry::CollectDailyProduction on a day the owner is at war or cannot pay, so it is worked out again from the debt as it then stands. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: next_wargoal_date
fields.comment: A tick (hours): the earliest the array's owner may add another war goal against the other country. Named from the loader: CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey (rva 0x648190) stores the key `next_wargoal_date`, token 0x7A7, here at 0xA4832A through Date_SetFromString (rva 0x4CDA0). **Its one writer is CWarGoal::AddToWar (rva 0x651FB0)** at 0xA520D2, which sets it to the current tick advanced by `WARGOAL_ADD_COOLDOWN / 1000` **months** through AddMonths (rva 0xB8C90). The status written is `countries[actorId]->diplomacy[goal->receiver.index]`, so the cooldown is per aggressor-and-victim pair. No reader was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: mode_left_observer
fields.comment: Embedded button glue on `mode_arrow_left`, handler 0x2EC4C0 (slot 12). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md), inherited from CCountryView

fields.name: mode_right_observer
fields.comment: Embedded button glue on `mode_arrow_right`, handler a call of slot 13. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md), inherited from CCountryView

fields.comment: Which of the local player's automation settings is this view's: `[player + 0x38][view_index]`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md), inherited from CCountryView

fields.name: idler

fields.name: next_alignment_refresh
fields.comment: Clock hour after which Update rebuilds the alignment markers; then set to now + ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL * 24. The null date at construction. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md)

fields.name: alignment_markers
fields.comment: The faction triangle's markers: head +0xC0, tail +0xC4, count +0xC8, each a 0xC-byte {CCountryTag, element}. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md)

fields.name: countries
fields.comment: **The country list the left half shows**: head +0xD0, tail +0xD4, count +0xD8, lock byte +0xDC; 0x14-byte nodes {tag, id, prev +8, next +0xC, removed +0x10}. Refilled by each tab, faction and continent button; the sort buttons do not reorder it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md)

fields.name: trade_automate_observer
fields.comment: An embedded checkbox observer glue (CCheckBoxObserverGlue<CDiplomacyView>, 0x20 bytes) on `trade_automate_checkbox`, handler 0x38E290. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md)

fields.name: relation_sort_descending
fields.comment: The relation list's by-relation direction, 1 = best relation first. Set 1 by the constructor (as the low byte of `mov word [esi+0x318], 1`), flipped by sortby_relation_button before each sort. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md)

fields.name: relation_list_by_relation
fields.comment: 1 after a by-relation fill of the relation list, 0 after a by-name one or from the constructor. Read by nothing in 0x77A000..0x790000. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md)

fields.name: faction_boxes

fields.name: Type
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetType
BiceLib: type (int) - The action's `CDiplomaticAction::EType`, and the **stage** an offer is at rather than what kind of offer it is: the kind is the C++ subclass, and its name is slot 15's save token. `CDiplomaticAction::GetType` is registered to Lua and resolves to a two-instruction `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret` at 0x416000. The enum has **three** values, all registered in one luabind chain ending at 0x8ED397: ('PROPOSE', ebx) at 0x8ED38D with ebx zeroed at 0x8EAE68 and never rewritten, ('DECLINE', 1) at 0x8ED37F, and **('ACCEPT', 2) at 0x8ED3BB**, appended to the same value vector at 0x8ED3C9 and registered by the loop at 0x8ED3CE. So 0 = PROPOSE, 1 = DECLINE, 2 = ACCEPT. What acts on it: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute enqueues a PROPOSE on the recipient and anything else on the actor; the hourly AI pass at 0x682BA8 only touches entries still at PROPOSE and writes 2 into the field at 0x682BB3 to accept them. The body at 0x416000 has two references and so is **not** recorded under a class name (trap 4); the field is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: Value
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetValue
BiceLib: value (unsigned char) - A bool, exposed to Lua as GetValue/SetValue: CDiplomaticAction::SetValue (0xA0E980, one reference, no vftable) is `this->+0x24 = [ebp+8]` and the getter is the folded `mov al,[ecx+0x24]` at 0xA0E990. **CTradeAction::IsValid (slot 13, 0xA38770) branches on it at 0xA387DA**: set, and it validates a fresh trade offer; clear, and it instead requires that an identical route already exist on the pair. So `value` is the proposal/cancellation polarity a script controls. **Units: none - it is a bool, not thousandths.** In the save it is written `value=yes` / `value=no`, 39 yes and 6 no over the 45 saves on this machine, which is also how the `value` loader case reads it: ParseBool (rva 0x67B410) at 0xA0E6E6, not a number. Seven of the family also use it as their slot-18 answer, through the folded `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x24], 0; setne al; ret` at 0xA0FE10 and the recorded ReturnByteAt24 at 0xA0E990. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: persistent_id
fields.comment: Always 0x18D. Written by CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor (0xA0EB30), by each of the eleven Lua `Create` factories (e.g. 0x8E84A9) and copied by every slot-16 clone, so every action in the family carries it. **It is not a per-class discriminator**: CCommand +0x4 is recorded as "a class id" and holds the same 0x18D, and the kind of action is carried by slot 15's save token instead. What reads it was not traced; token 0x18D resolves to `none`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: actor
fields.comment: The country making the offer, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the four-character tag at +0x8 and the country id at +0xC. Loaded from the save key `actor` (token 0x2E9) at 0xA0E7B5/0xA0E7BB, where CCountryDataBase::GetTag's result is copied as two dwords. CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor fills it with "---" and id 0. Every reader that wants the CCountry indexes `g_CCountryDataBase::countries_first` with +0xC: CTradeAction::IsValid, CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute and the base's slot 14 all do. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: recipient
fields.comment: The country being offered to, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the tag at +0x10 and the id at +0x14. Loaded from the save key `recipient` (token 0x2EA) at 0xA0E86A/0xA0E874. The base's slot 14, `IsSelectable` (0xA0EAE0), is three instructions: `return actor_id != recipient_id` - so the family's default selectability test is just "these are two different countries". (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: date
fields.comment: When the offer was made, in **hours** on the same scale as g_CCurrentGameState's tick (+0xBDC), counted from the 43,800,000-hour epoch. Loaded from the save key `date` (token 0x1F8) through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E70A, written by every Lua `Create` factory from the current tick, and set to the epoch itself - the engine's null date, [0x170C2B8] - by the null action's constructor. CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's only use of it is `date + 0xA8`, seven days, handed to CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: last_command_date
fields.comment: When the action was last put on the wire, in hours on the tick scale - the save's own key name (token 0x3EC), loaded through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E806. **Two independent writers, both setting it to the current tick**: CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand stamps it just before wrapping the action in a command (0xA0E92D) and CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction stamps it again as the action is enqueued (0x4E62EB). That is what makes it later than `date` for an offer that has travelled: in the save corpus it differs from `date` in 34 of 56 blocks and is never earlier. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: window
fields.comment: The row's `diploactionentry` window; `button_diploaction` is looked up in it (slot 13). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: idler
fields.comment: The in-game screen (the view's +0xB0), the constructor's ECX. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: action
fields.comment: The row's own clone of the action (slot 16 of the one GetDiplomaticActionsToward made). Its slot 10 is the button text, slot 11 the tooltip, slots 14 and 21 the greying; a click opens a dialog for it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: view

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: target
fields.comment: The tag the keyword names, `---`/0 when unknown, unless use_this/use_from is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: date

The constructor (0x1F4550) initialises it from [0x170C2B8], the engine's null date. It is what CHistoryContainer::AddEntry (0x1F4660) sorts the list by and what ApplyRange (0x1F47C0) compares against its two bounds. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CHistoryEntry, inherited from CCountryHistoryEntry

fields.name: country
fields.comment: The country the change applies to, taken from the constructor's one argument (0x1EEA40, the store at 0x1EEA5E). Every derived Apply starts from it: the flag changes hand it to CCountry::GetFlags (0xCCD30) to reach CCountry +0x180. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCountryHistoryEntry

fields.name: value

fields.name: previous_value

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred key. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred keys' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values
fields.comment: First element of the second std::vector<std::string>: the value written beside each deferred key, index for index. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred values' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: value
fields.comment: **The operand, in thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CValueTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D13E0) as `TokenToFixedPoint(text)`, so `war_exhaustion = 7.5` is stored as 7500 - the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `national_unity=81.752`). A leaf's own Evaluate then either compares it straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3 says which does which. **This is the opposite convention from `CIntTrigger::value` at the same offset**, and nothing in the script files distinguishes them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: band0_cursor
fields.comment: Initialised to 1 with the other three by CCountry::CCountry (0x4C9F93) and **never read or written again**: it is the cursor priority band 0 would have, and Distribute's band loop stops at 1. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: band1_cursor
fields.comment: Where priority band 1's scan of the country list starts, 1 to begin with (CCountry::CCountry, 0x4C9F96..0x4C9F9C) and not saved. Each placement sets it to the next country; a day's scan runs from it to the end of the list and **does not wrap**, and it goes back to 1 when that scan places nothing or the cursor has reached the end - so a presence before the cursor waits a day. A home presence that is a country's only one in the band therefore gets a spy every second day at most. The whole cursor rule is in CDistributeEspionage::Distribute's entry. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: band2_cursor
fields.comment: Where priority band 2's scan of the country list starts, 1 to begin with (CCountry::CCountry, 0x4C9F96..0x4C9F9C) and not saved. Each placement sets it to the next country; a day's scan runs from it to the end of the list and **does not wrap**, and it goes back to 1 when that scan places nothing or the cursor has reached the end - so a presence before the cursor waits a day. A home presence that is a country's only one in the band therefore gets a spy every second day at most. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

A home presence that is a country's only one in the band therefore gets a spy every second day at most. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: needed
fields.comment: An fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>: the total daily IC the production queue wants, the sum of every construction's cost divided by 1000. Zeroed by the constructor at 0x4C9DB1, rebuilt by 0x11A290 at the end of every Distribute, and returned verbatim by slot 3 GetNeeded (0x11A2E0). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-production.md)

fields.name: spent_beyond_free
fields.comment: An fpml::fixed_point<__int64,48,15>, zeroed at the start of every Distribute (0x519D23). It accumulates the IC the pass asked for **beyond the resource-free part** - the two adds, 0x51A03B and 0x51A137, both happen before the resource check, so it counts what was wanted rather than what was got. Nothing in the ten distributors reads it back; only the constructor, the two adds and the reset touch it. The name is ours. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-production.md)
