fields.name: country_tag
fields.comment:
The AI's own country tag, eight bytes with the id at +0x24. Two independent readers in the trade predicates: CEU3AI::IsTradeingAwayNeededResource does `lea ecx, [this+0x20]` at 0x89B4B2 and 0x89B4FC followed by CCountryTag::GetCountry (0x402610), and CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingResourceOtherWay does `lea edi, [this+0x20]` at 0x89B322, reads the id half as [edi+4] at 0x89B329 and calls GetCountry on edi at 0x89B343 - both comparing it against a CTradeRoute's from_id and to_id to work out which side of a route the AI is on. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md)
+0x4 inside it: country_id (int) - The country id half of the tag at +0x20. Compared against CTradeRoute +0x28 (from_id) at 0x89B4A2 and 0x89B32E, and against +0x30 (to_id) at 0x89B4EC. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md)

fields.name: runs_units
fields.comment: **1 for an AI-run country, 0 for the human's own country.** The constructor (0x488020, vftable 0x11EB660) seeds it 1 at 0x4880BA, and ProcessAI (0x4894E0) clears it at 0x4895BA the first time it runs for the country whose id equals `gamestate->player` (`+0xC34`) - once only, because the write is guarded on the byte still being set. Four consumers in the unit AI, and they are the whole of what the flag does: CAIUnit::UpdatePlanAxis (0x4C3330) returns at once unless it is set, so the AI never redraws a human's attack arrows; slot 82 posts CSetCommandLevel only when it is set; CAIUnit::SetArea *skips* its objective-owner-area pass when it is set, so objectives constrain the human's delegated AI and not the AI's own; and ClassifyOpsAreaFrontier reads it in the `+0x366` test. The same split appears a second way in slot 73, which chooses 0x4B5210 or 0x4B60F0 on `gamestate->played_countries_array[countryId]`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-setarea.md)

fields.name: unit_agents_first
fields.comment: **The country's CAIUnit agents**, a CList of `{agent, prev, next, byte}` nodes. All four creation paths push_back onto it, and ProcessAI walks it at 0x48986D calling each agent's slot 9 once per game hour. Distinct from the minister list at +0x74 and the invasion list at +0x50. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: unit_agents_last
fields.comment: Last node of the unit-agent list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: unit_agents_count
fields.comment: How many unit agents. ProcessAI tests it at 0x4897C6 and only runs CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits when it is zero, so that path builds the player's agents once. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: invasion_agents_first
fields.comment: **The country's CAIInvasion agents**, the same node shape. Filled at 0x493B34-0x493B5D right after CAIInvasion's constructor (0x49F920), and walked by ProcessAI at 0x489887 immediately after the unit agents. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: invasion_agents_last
fields.comment: Last node of the invasion-agent list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: invasion_agents_count
fields.comment: How many invasion agents. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: flag_a5
fields.comment: A second ProcessAI gate beside +0xA6: set at 0x889B94, read at 0x88961B, 0x889A82 and 0x899CF2. What it means was not established - recorded only so the next reader does not mistake it for +0xA6. (agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion)

fields.name: theatres_changed
fields.comment: Set to 1 by the AI's theatre layer whenever it makes or re-points a theatre - 0x8ABAA4 and 0x8ABB77 in CAIStrategy::BuildTheatres, 0x8ABF22 in CAIStrategy::RefreshTheatreProvinces, each as `mov byte [GetCountry(tag)->+0x1D8 + 0xA6], 1`. Cleared only by ProcessAI, at 0x8896BC and 0x889852, and only once every theatre in CCountry +0x570 has a resolvable HQ unit; until then ProcessAI leaves it set and retries next hour. Written on the **tick** thread and cleared on a **worker** - an unsynchronised byte either way. (agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion)

fields.name: update_stances_pending
fields.comment: CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4912D0) returns immediately when its `force` argument is false and this byte is clear (0x4912F3-0x491301). ProcessAI's one call site is at 0x489B8F. read (the gate), inference (the name) (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: priority_province_list_first
fields.comment: A list of province ids. CEU3AI::GenerateUnitObjectives (0x4980E0) adds **100 flat** to a candidate objective's priority when the province is in it (0x49848F-0x4984A8). What fills it was not traced. read (the use) (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: priority_province_list_last
fields.comment: Tail of the province-id CList whose head project.json already records at +0x118. Zeroed with the head at 0x49772B and written on every append at 0x4979D5 by CEU3AI::RebuildPriorityProvinces. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

fields.name: priority_province_list_count
fields.comment: Count of the province-id CList at +0x118. Zeroed at 0x497731 and incremented at 0x4979DB. The list is freed and rebuilt in full once per AI pass, so this is never persistent state. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

fields.name: settings
fields.comment: A live CSettings, named by RTTI. Noted in passing while verifying the gui route; not read. (live 2026-10-02, verified against the process's only CEU3Gui)

fields.name: graphics
fields.comment: The one live CEU3Graphics, named by RTTI on the live object. Sits immediately before `gui`, which is consistent with FINDINGS-gui.md having found `CGui +0x30` pointing at the same object from the other side. (live 2026-10-02, verified against the process's only CEU3Gui)

fields.name: gui
fields.comment:
The one live CEU3Gui. **The route the DLL uses to reach the GUI, verified live 2026-10-02**: `CCurrentGameState +0xBE8` (in_game_screen) -> `CInGameIdler` -> `+0x1790` -> `CEU3Application` -> `+0x120` -> the one live `CEU3Gui`, compared for pointer equality against the process's only instance. Three reads, and RTTI names every step.

**There is no global holding the gui pointer** - a scan of the whole 16 MB exe image for the live address found **zero** hits - so an owner walk is the only cheap way in. It needs a session, because at the main menu `+0xBE8` holds a `CFrontEnd` instead of the idler; BiceLib's WidgetStats falls back to a cached vftable scan there.

Written by the construction at 0x231C41, which sets CEU3Gui's three vftables (0x11CD754 TGui, 0x11CD7D8 CPersistent, 0x11CD7F4 CFactory) and then installs the object here at 0x231C5D with the usual release-the-old-one guard. (live 2026-10-02, verified against the process's only CEU3Gui)

fields.name: session
fields.comment: The CSession. CEU3Application::CEU3Application (0x22F080) builds the startup session with mode 2 at 0x22F30F and stores it here; CInGameIdler::GetSession (virtual slot 18, 0x24D800) is three instructions returning [this+0x1790]->[0x12C], and CCurrentGameState::AdvanceClock tests +0x34 on the result and posts through +0x38. The class is `CSession` from the session.cpp strings its constructor 0x6887A0 carries ('NoAdress', 'InitialSession'); the field's own type is left void* because nothing here read the object's layout. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-session2.md)

fields.name: font_name
fields.comment: the `fontName` key, which is the stem of both gfx/fonts/<name>.tga and the .fnt beside it. CEU3BitmapFont::LoadKey takes the key straight onto this+0x78 and both loaders read it from there; 0x78 + 0x18 leaves it ending at 0x90, four bytes short of the glyph table (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: glyphs
fields.comment: one pointer per character code, null where the font has no such glyph. Indexed by the raw byte in GetStringWidth, so 256 entries exactly - and 0x94 + 256 * 4 is 0x494, which is the next field LoadGlyphs writes (0x6FA26D), so the length is measured rather than assumed (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: second
fields.comment: the character code that has to follow for this pair to apply (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: amount
fields.comment: pixels added to the advance, almost always negative (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: x
fields.comment: left edge in the font texture (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: y
fields.comment: top edge in the font texture (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: width
fields.comment: how wide the glyph is in the texture, which is not what the pen moves by (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: height
fields.comment: how tall it is; forced to 0 for the space (id 0x20) at 0x6FA3BD whatever the file says, and GetStringWidth reads a zero height as a glyph that draws no ink (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: xoffset
fields.comment: where the glyph is drawn relative to the pen (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: yoffset
fields.comment: the same vertically (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: xadvance
fields.comment: **what the pen moves by** - the number that decides how wide text draws. The .fnt's value reaches here unchanged, since the parse is positional and nothing scales it (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: kerning
fields.comment: pairs in the order the .fnt listed them, only the first kerning_count of them meaning anything (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: kerning_count
fields.comment: how many of the pairs are filled; zeroed as the glyph is made and incremented by each kerning line naming this glyph first (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-text.md)

fields.name: window
fields.comment: The dialog's window, made by the constructor; the CAsk* constructors look `AgreeButton`, `DeclineButton`, `Title` and `Description` up in it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: closed
fields.comment: Set by a button that has done its work; slot 1 then answers false and the idler deletes the dialog. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: window
fields.comment: The slider's window - `domesticpanel_slider` or `tech_slider` - renamed to the slider's index. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md)

fields.name: setting
fields.comment: The share this slider shows. Its slots 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 and 11 are what the slider asks. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md)

fields.name: value
fields.comment: The value last set by SetValue. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md)

fields.name: moved
fields.comment: The scrollbar's +0x252 as LatchMoved found it: the player moved the slider since the last look. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md)

fields.name: is_ic
fields.comment: 1 for one of the six IC sliders, 0 for one of the four leadership ones. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md)

fields.name: pinned
fields.comment: Set by OnNeedButton when it disables the slider at its need. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CRelation

fields.name: first
fields.comment: **The first party to the agreement** (save key `first`). Resolved from the three letters in the save through CCountryDataBase::GetTag, so the tag characters land at +0x8 and the index at +0xC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: second
fields.comment: **The second party to the agreement** (save key `second`). The same resolution as `first`, into the tag at +0x10 and the index at +0x14. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement began**, as a tick (save key `start_date`). Parsed from `year.month.day.hour` text by Date_SetFromString, which is the same representation every other date in the simulation uses. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement ends**, as a tick (save key `end_date`); **the null date 43,800,000 (`[0x170C2B8]`) where it has none** - every constructor sets it so, not zero. A real date is told by `(end_date - 43,800,000) / 24 / 365.0 > 1`. Read only by CCasusBelli (Activate, which will not attach an expired one, and IsOver) and by CRelation::SaveContents (written only when real). **No other relation's IsOver reads it**: a guarantee ends twenty years after `start_date`, a NAP NAP_EXPIRY_MONTHS after it, and the history files' end dates take effect only while history is replayed before play. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: cancel
fields.comment: **Whether the agreement is cancelled** (save key `cancel`), the last of CRelation's own bytes - a subclass's data starts at +0x24. Loaded as a plain comparison against the token `yes`, so any other value, including `no`, leaves it 0. **CDiplomacy::SaveContents skips every relation with it set**, and CRelation::SaveContents, given one, writes `cancel = yes` instead of `start_date`. No writer in play was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CCountryTargetEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_last

fields.name: deferred_values_end

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: value
fields.comment: **The operand, in thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CValueTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D13E0) as `TokenToFixedPoint(text)`, so `war_exhaustion = 7.5` is stored as 7500 - the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `national_unity=81.752`). A leaf's own Evaluate then either compares it straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3 says which does which. **This is the opposite convention from `CIntTrigger::value` at the same offset**, and nothing in the script files distinguishes them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_last

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

FINDINGS-guilive.md section 5 measured that vector live and found 46 buttons, 20 child windows and 1 icon, i.e. game code attaches non-windows through the same slot, which is why project.json's child_windows_begin on +0x2FC is a slight misnomer and why this list is not called child_windows either. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md)

Look up with slot 1 of the container's vftable (a std::string) or slot 2, GuiTypeTree_Find (rva 0x67DEE0), with a plain const char*; the walk lowercases the query so any case works. Paired with the name list at complete+0x424. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guilive.md)

fields.name: subwindows_begin
fields.comment:
**Begin of the window's subwindow map - the container that really holds the child windows the .gui file declares, and not +0x2FC.** A std::vector of 0x20-byte entries, {Hoi3CString name at +0; CFixedWindow* window at +0x1C}, used as a name-keyed map: SubWindowMap_Contains (0x6C4580) tests a key, SubWindowMap_FindOrAdd (0x6C4640) returns the value slot, SubWindowMap_Add (0x6C44F0) appends. Complete-object offset; the pointer CGui +0x5C hands you is complete+0x18, so this is +0x3FC from it.

Filled only by the CFixedWindow constructor's build loop at 0xAC0C33..0xAC0C90, which walks the name list the constructor was handed in its 11th argument - that argument is `&CWindowType +0x214`, the `windowType` keyword's declared-name list - and for each name calls CWindowType::CreateWindow (0x6C76D0) on the window's own type at +0x88 and adds the result here under that name.

The value is a **complete** CFixedWindow pointer: CFixedWindow::FindChild adds 0x18 to it to get a CGuiObject, the show and hide walks read `[entry+0x1C]` and then call CGuiObject slot 13 with `this = value + 0x18`, and CGuiObject slot 37's recursion does the same. 'Subwindow' is the engine's own word, from the warning CFixedWindow::GetSubWindow logs at fixedwindow.cpp line 1042.

+0x418 is the end and +0x41C the capacity end. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: subwindows_end
fields.comment: End of the subwindow map at +0x414. Every walk of the map compares its cursor against this. (end - begin) / 0x20 is the subwindow count. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: subwindows_capacity_end
fields.comment:
Capacity end of the subwindow map at +0x414 - the third pointer of the vector. Read only by the insert helper 0x542FC0, which compares the end against it to decide whether to grow.

**Do not confuse it with the CGuiObject-relative +0x41C**, which is complete +0x434, `three_d_button_names`. CFixedWindow::Show and CFixedWindow::Hide both read `[esi+0x41C]` with esi as the CGuiObject subobject and that is the name list, not this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: text_box_names
fields.comment: Complete-object offset; +0x40C from the CGuiObject pointer. Head of a linked list of 0x24-byte nodes, each holding a child's name as a std::string at +0 with the next at +0x20. CFixedWindow::Show and ::Hide walk it and look each name up in the text-box registry at complete+0x33C, which is what pairs the six lists (stride 0x10 from here) with the six registries (stride 0x24 from +0x33C). 101 nodes across the 206 live windows, matching the registry exactly. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guilive.md)

fields.name: three_d_button_names
fields.comment: Head of the linked list of declared child names whose widgets the registry at +0x360 indexes - the second of six (name list, registry) pairs at 0x10 and 0x24 strides respectively. Nodes are the same 0x24-byte shape as +0x424's, with the next pointer at +0x20. The kind is 3dButtonType: the constructor iterates THIS list, calls the factory 0xAC6C80 for each name and inserts the result into the registry at +0x360. **Empty on all 206 live windows because neither the mod's nor the game's own interface/ folder uses the keyword at all** - 0 occurrences of 3dButtonType against 996/392 for positionType in the same grep. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md)

The kind is threeDguiType: unlike the other five this one is not built by a 0xAC6xxx/0xAC7xxx factory at all. For each name the constructor looks the name up in the gui-type tree embedded at CWindowType +0x150, hands the result to the EXTERNAL factory 0xB45670, and inserts what comes back. **Empty on all 206 live windows because the keyword appears 0 times in both interface/ folders.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guistatic.md)

Not read beyond that. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

The constructor adds the parent's size to +0x240 by it once; CFixedWindow::SetPosition does not consult it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect, inherited from CBoolEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CBoolEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CBoolEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CBoolEffect

fields.name: value
fields.comment: True only for the bare token `yes`. Written by CBoolEffect::TakeScalarValue; read as a byte by CBoolEffect::FormatValueText. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md), inherited from CBoolEffect

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md)

fields.name: deferred_values_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md)

fields.name: deferred_values_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred values' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md)

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md)

fields.name: flags
fields.comment: **The global flags** - the tree `set_global_flag` and `clr_global_flag` write and `has_global_flag` reads, held by value. CGameState::CGameState writes CFlags' own vftable (0x15BB468, a virtual address) here and CFlags' CPersistent vftable at +0xE8, which is the +0x24 second base CFlags.hpp documents - so the field project.json has been calling `flags` at +0xE8 is that sub-object and the flags themselves start here. CSetGlobalFlagEffect::Execute dispatches slot 2 on this address. **The `CPersistent` second base is 0x24 into it**, and it is the sub-object `SaveContents` calls slot 1 on to write the `flags` block - which is why that offset once looked like a field of this class and was recorded as one (`flags_persistent` at +0xE8, deleted 2026-10-05). It is not declared here any more: `CFlags` is 0x28 bytes and Ghidra's own RTTI pass already names the second base's vftable at `CFlags+0x24`, so a `CPersistent` declared at +0xE8 collided with the `CFlags` held here and the two replaced each other on every apply - the period-2 cycle described in ghidra/README.md. The tree itself is this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md)

fields.name: allied_objectives
fields.comment: **The allied objectives, indexed by the country the objective is set for**, and the half that is saved. A `std::vector` of 0x10-byte elements (end +0xBA0, capacity +0xBA4) resized to the country count by 0x67E320; element `i` is itself a vector (begin +0, end +4, capacity +8) of 0x14-byte records `{ province id, int* requesters_begin, int* requesters_end, int* requesters_capacity, ? }`. So country `i` has a set of provinces, and each province carries the set of countries that asked `i` to take it. Written only by CGameState_AddAlliedObjective / CGameState_RemoveAlliedObjective / CGameState_ClearAlliedObjectivesForCountry. `CGameState::SaveContents` flattens it at 0x67F97E-0x67FA73 into one int list under the key `allied_objectives` (token 0x758), three ints per (record, requester) pair in the order **province, requester, country**, and the key is skipped when the list is empty - which is why no savegame in this repository carries it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aifields.md)

fields.name: allied_objectives_by_requester
fields.comment: **The same allied objectives, inverted: indexed by the country that asked.** Identical shape to +0xB9C - a vector of 0x10-byte per-country elements (end +0xBB0, capacity +0xBB4), each a vector of 0x14-byte `{ province id, vector<int> countries }` records - but here the int vector holds the countries the objective was set *for*. Not saved; CGameState::LoadKey rebuilds it by feeding every saved triple through CGameState_AddAlliedObjective, which writes both halves. **This is the field `CEU3AI::RebuildPriorityProvinces` (0x8976E0) walks**: for each candidate ally `Y` it takes `state->allied_objectives_by_requester[Y]` and appends `record->province` to `CEU3AI +0x118` for every record whose int vector contains our own country id, which is worth a flat +100 on that province's AI objective priority. fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

Typed as a structure of named entries so a read is a field rather than an index. **The index is the definition's registration order, which is CModifier::id only up to 101.** The global initialiser builds 108 definitions in array order but stamps ids that are not in that order at the end: entries 102..107 are LAND_INTEL_BOOST (id 103), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST (id 104), LOCAL_UNDERGROUND (id 102), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST a second time (id 104 again), STRATEGIC_RESOURCE_EFFICIENCY (id 105) and LOCAL_UNIT_SPEED (id 106). So an index below 102 can be read straight off reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py, and one at or above 102 has to be read off this structure instead - while a comparison against CModifier +0x24 `id` is the other way round. fields.name: gui_objects_begin
fields.comment:
**Begin of the vector of every live gui object in the process** - the answer to FINDINGS-gui.md's open item 1. 2305 objects in a paused 1936 game, across 13 classes. Thirteen TGui slots push into it (slots 16 and 23 are the bare push_back 0xA7DC60; the other eleven look a name up in the +0x34 tree, build a widget from the type and then push); slots 19 and 30 iterate it. **It holds CGuiObject subobject pointers, not complete objects** - complete+0x18 for a CFixedWindow, complete+4 for a list box, complete+0 for an icon or button. No code that removes an element was found, and front-end widgets are still in it after CFrontEnd has been destroyed, so a held pointer should be revalidated rather than trusted.

**Open item 1 of FINDINGS-guilive.md is closed, live (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save): yes, elements are removed, and by erase-and-compact with no holes.** Measured by snapshotting the vector either side of opening and closing the production window in a running game.

Opening it took the vector from **2,415 to 4,124** entries while `widget_nulls` stayed at **0**, and **six names disappeared entirely** - `info_text`, `outliner_standard`, `outliner_combat_entry`, `outliner_unit_entry_bg`, `movment`, `outliner_top_unit_entry` (the outliner, which a full-screen window hides). `widget_end` moved by exactly 0x1AB4, i.e. 1,709 entries, matching the count delta, and `widget_begin` never moved - so the backing buffer did not reallocate but elements inside it shift when one is erased.

**The rule for the DLL, and it is a hard one: never cache a widget pointer or an index across anything that can open or close a panel.** A cached pointer to a removed widget dangles; a cached *index* is worse, because after a compaction it addresses some other live widget and returns plausible garbage instead of crashing.

**Removal is not symmetric.** Closing the window did not undo the opening: all 47 names it added were still present afterwards and the count rose again to 4,279. So some panels are torn down on hide and others are built once and kept, and the vector grows monotonically as a session visits panels - which is what the 64,000-slot preallocation is budgeted for (4,339 in use after three cycles). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guilive.md; live 2026-10-02, GER 1942 war save; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guilive.md)

fields.name: values
fields.comment: the values, one entry per ModifierType and indexed by it; CModifier::GetValue reads [this+0x18][type*8]. Typed as a structure of named entries so a read is a field rather than an index. **The index is the definition's registration order, which is CModifier::id only up to 101.** The global initialiser builds 108 definitions in array order but stamps ids that are not in that order at the end: entries 102..107 are LAND_INTEL_BOOST (id 103), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST (id 104), LOCAL_UNDERGROUND (id 102), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST a second time (id 104 again), STRATEGIC_RESOURCE_EFFICIENCY (id 105) and LOCAL_UNIT_SPEED (id 106). So an index below 102 can be read straight off reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py, and one at or above 102 has to be read off this structure instead - while a comparison against CModifier +0x24 `id` is the other way round. Typed as the ModifierId enum so those read as names; the enum is built by reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py out of the global initialiser, which is the only place the 107 names exist. What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: graphics
fields.comment: The CEU3Graphics. Constructor argument 2, = CFrontEnd +0x20C = CBackEndIdler +0xB4. Returned by virtual slot 17. Statically: LoadEverything passes **CEU3Application +0x11C**, which project.json already names `graphics`, as CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd's arg2 at 0x2329D4/0x2329DC; CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd stores arg2 at +0x20C; CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler copies [frontEnd+0x20C] to +0x178C at 0x248412. MakeBackEndIdler writes the same object to CBackEndIdler +0xB4 beside +0xB8 = the application, and ProcessSessionEndRequests hands (+0x178C, +0x60, +0x1790) back to CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd as (graphics, gui, app). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-session2.md)

fields.name: application
fields.comment: The CEU3Application. Constructor argument 4, written at 0x248418 - the **only** write to this displacement in the image (a per-displacement scan over .text finds 32 accesses to +0x1790, 31 reads and that one write). The chain, every link in the bytes: CEU3Application::LoadEverything constructs the first CFrontEnd at 0x2329DE with `mov ecx,[edi+0x120]; mov edx,[edi+0x11c]; push edi; push ecx; push edx; push eax; call 0x6ed660`, where edi is the application - its +0x11C and +0x120 are the already-named `graphics` and `gui` - so **arg4 is the application's own `this`**; CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd stores arg4 at CFrontEnd +0x210 (already recorded); CInGameIdler::CInGameIdler is called once, from CFrontEnd::LaunchGame at 0x2F1144, with [frontEnd+0x20C], [frontEnd+0x60], [frontEnd+0x210] as args 1-3 after `this`, and copies the third to +0x1790. Live RTTI on the object agrees (2026-10-02), as does the DLL: BiceLib/Gui/WidgetStats.cpp already spells this offset `IDLER_APPLICATION`. Its +0x12C is the session, which virtual slot 18 (CInGameIdler::GetSession, 0x24D800) returns and which every CCommand is posted to - that field is where the name `session_manager` came from. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-session2.md)

Slot 82 (GetProvinceView) answers it; slots 11/12 show and hide it; the per-frame update (0x650700, from CInGameIdler::Update) runs ProvinceView_Update on it while its window is shown. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-provinceview.md)

fields.name: quit_requested
fields.comment: One byte, set to 1 by virtual slot 73 (rva 0x24C000) and never cleared; zeroed as part of a dword at 0x24846D in the constructor. Its one reader is ProcessSessionEndRequests at 0x2547D2, which on seeing it replaces the session, sets the global byte [0x1A857EF] and calls PostQuitMessage(0) through the IAT at 0xD2B2BC. A deferred request, so that a button handler never destroys the screen it is running under. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

fields.name: game_over_requested
fields.comment:
One byte with two writers: virtual slot 74 (rva 0x24C010) and ProcessSessionEndRequests itself at 0x25432E, which sets it when the played tag's CCountry has NumberOfOwnedProvinces (+0xCF8) below 1 and the tag is not "REB" - the elimination detector, evaluated every frame. Its one reader is 0x254335, which builds a CBackEndIdler through SessionManager::MakeBackEndIdler and makes it the pending screen.

**It does not reset the game state and it does not clear in_game** - but MakeBackEndIdler calls CGameState::SetInGameScreen, so for the remainder of that frame state->in_game_screen is a CBackEndIdler while in_game is still 1. in_game is cleared by CInGameIdler::Leave at 0x2913BC, four instructions after Update's slot-1 call returns. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 7. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

fields.name: exit_to_menu_requested
fields.comment:
One byte, zeroed in the constructor at 0x248473 and set to 1 at exactly one instruction in the image, 0x24FF10 in UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows, when the tutorial runner at +0x1D54 reports itself finished. Its one reader is ProcessSessionEndRequests at 0x254573.

**This is the only route from CInGameIdler::Update to the full game-state reset**: the branch calls ResetGameStateToStartDate(1) at 0x25472C and then, 0x49 bytes later, constructs a CFrontEnd at 0x254775, which clears in_game at 0x2ED9AF. The one branch in between (0x254760, the operator-new failure arm) skips that clear, but CInGameIdler::Leave still clears the byte at 0x262337 from the run loop's swap at 0x2913BC, which runs four instructions after Update's slot returns and before the swap reads the incoming pointer. So there is no frame in which in_game is 1 over a reset game state - which is what FINDINGS-session.md section 11 item 1 asked. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md, section 3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

fields.name: tutorial_runner
fields.comment:
A 0x40-byte object, created and destroyed only through virtual slot 90 (rva 0x274FE0) and tested by slot 91 (rva 0x275080). Three accessors in the image and no other reader. **It exists only during a tutorial**: the one `create` call, at 0x24FEAA, is gated on state->tutorial_active (+0xD9D) and is handed state->tutorial_id (+0xDA0) as its value. Its +0x3C byte means finished - when it is set, UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows destroys the object and sets exit_to_menu_requested, which resets the game state and returns to the main menu.

The class is unidentified (its constructor is 0x8E7370; 0x8E7950, 0x833F40 and 0x8E72B0 are consulted on it and were not read), so the name rests on the creation gate rather than on the object. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CRelation

fields.name: first
fields.comment: **The first party to the agreement** (save key `first`). Resolved from the three letters in the save through CCountryDataBase::GetTag, so the tag characters land at +0x8 and the index at +0xC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: second
fields.comment: **The second party to the agreement** (save key `second`). The same resolution as `first`, into the tag at +0x10 and the index at +0x14. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement began**, as a tick (save key `start_date`). Parsed from `year.month.day.hour` text by Date_SetFromString, which is the same representation every other date in the simulation uses. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement ends**, as a tick (save key `end_date`); **the null date 43,800,000 (`[0x170C2B8]`) where it has none** - every constructor sets it so, not zero. A real date is told by `(end_date - 43,800,000) / 24 / 365.0 > 1`. Read only by CCasusBelli (Activate, which will not attach an expired one, and IsOver) and by CRelation::SaveContents (written only when real). **No other relation's IsOver reads it**: a guarantee ends twenty years after `start_date`, a NAP NAP_EXPIRY_MONTHS after it, and the history files' end dates take effect only while history is replayed before play. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: cancel
fields.comment: **Whether the agreement is cancelled** (save key `cancel`), the last of CRelation's own bytes - a subclass's data starts at +0x24. Loaded as a plain comparison against the token `yes`, so any other value, including `no`, leaves it 0. **CDiplomacy::SaveContents skips every relation with it set**, and CRelation::SaveContents, given one, writes `cancel = yes` instead of `start_date`. No writer in play was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: faction_name
fields.comment: The influencer's faction's name (`CFaction +0xC`), copied by CInfluence::Activate and used by CInfluence::Deactivate to find the faction and remove `align_towards_<name>` from the influenced country. **Not saved** (CRelation::SaveContents); CDiplomacy::LoadKey's Activate re-derives it from the influencer's faction at load. The object is 0x40 bytes (CDiplomacy::LoadKey and CInfluenceNation::Apply allocate 0x40), so the string fills +0x24..+0x3F. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: Type
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetType, inherited from CDiplomaticAction
BiceLib: type (int) - The action's `CDiplomaticAction::EType`, and the **stage** an offer is at rather than what kind of offer it is: the kind is the C++ subclass, and its name is slot 15's save token. `CDiplomaticAction::GetType` is registered to Lua and resolves to a two-instruction `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret` at 0x416000. The enum has **three** values, all registered in one luabind chain ending at 0x8ED397: ('PROPOSE', ebx) at 0x8ED38D with ebx zeroed at 0x8EAE68 and never rewritten, ('DECLINE', 1) at 0x8ED37F, and **('ACCEPT', 2) at 0x8ED3BB**, appended to the same value vector at 0x8ED3C9 and registered by the loop at 0x8ED3CE. So 0 = PROPOSE, 1 = DECLINE, 2 = ACCEPT. What acts on it: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute enqueues a PROPOSE on the recipient and anything else on the actor; the hourly AI pass at 0x682BA8 only touches entries still at PROPOSE and writes 2 into the field at 0x682BB3 to accept them. The body at 0x416000 has two references and so is **not** recorded under a class name (trap 4); the field is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: Value
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetValue, inherited from CDiplomaticAction
BiceLib: value (unsigned char) - A bool, exposed to Lua as GetValue/SetValue: CDiplomaticAction::SetValue (0xA0E980, one reference, no vftable) is `this->+0x24 = [ebp+8]` and the getter is the folded `mov al,[ecx+0x24]` at 0xA0E990. **CTradeAction::IsValid (slot 13, 0xA38770) branches on it at 0xA387DA**: set, and it validates a fresh trade offer; clear, and it instead requires that an identical route already exist on the pair. So `value` is the proposal/cancellation polarity a script controls. **Units: none - it is a bool, not thousandths.** In the save it is written `value=yes` / `value=no`, 39 yes and 6 no over the 45 saves on this machine, which is also how the `value` loader case reads it: ParseBool (rva 0x67B410) at 0xA0E6E6, not a number. Seven of the family also use it as their slot-18 answer, through the folded `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x24], 0; setne al; ret` at 0xA0FE10 and the recorded ReturnByteAt24 at 0xA0E990. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: persistent_id
fields.comment: Always 0x18D. Written by CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor (0xA0EB30), by each of the eleven Lua `Create` factories (e.g. 0x8E84A9) and copied by every slot-16 clone, so every action in the family carries it. **It is not a per-class discriminator**: CCommand +0x4 is recorded as "a class id" and holds the same 0x18D, and the kind of action is carried by slot 15's save token instead. What reads it was not traced; token 0x18D resolves to `none`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: actor
fields.comment: The country making the offer, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the four-character tag at +0x8 and the country id at +0xC. Loaded from the save key `actor` (token 0x2E9) at 0xA0E7B5/0xA0E7BB, where CCountryDataBase::GetTag's result is copied as two dwords. CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor fills it with "---" and id 0. Every reader that wants the CCountry indexes `g_CCountryDataBase::countries_first` with +0xC: CTradeAction::IsValid, CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute and the base's slot 14 all do. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: recipient
fields.comment: The country being offered to, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the tag at +0x10 and the id at +0x14. Loaded from the save key `recipient` (token 0x2EA) at 0xA0E86A/0xA0E874. The base's slot 14, `IsSelectable` (0xA0EAE0), is three instructions: `return actor_id != recipient_id` - so the family's default selectability test is just "these are two different countries". (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: date
fields.comment: When the offer was made, in **hours** on the same scale as g_CCurrentGameState's tick (+0xBDC), counted from the 43,800,000-hour epoch. Loaded from the save key `date` (token 0x1F8) through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E70A, written by every Lua `Create` factory from the current tick, and set to the epoch itself - the engine's null date, [0x170C2B8] - by the null action's constructor. CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's only use of it is `date + 0xA8`, seven days, handed to CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: last_command_date
fields.comment: When the action was last put on the wire, in hours on the tick scale - the save's own key name (token 0x3EC), loaded through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E806. **Two independent writers, both setting it to the current tick**: CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand stamps it just before wrapping the action in a command (0xA0E92D) and CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction stamps it again as the action is enqueued (0x4E62EB). That is what makes it later than `date` for an offer that has travelled: in the save corpus it differs from `date` in 34 of 56 blocks and is never earlier. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: influence_modifier
fields.comment: The static modifier the **actor's** faction's `influence` names (align_towards_axis and the like), looked up once when the action is made; slot 14 tests whether the recipient has it, slot 12 shows its ALIGN_TOWARDS value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. fields.name: value
fields.comment:
**The operand, as a plain integer - not thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CIntTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D1400) as `atoi(text)`, which truncates, so the decimal a mod writes is lost before anything compares it. Zeroed instead when the argument was the keyword `this` (SaveToken 0x377) or `from` (0x34F), which set `CTrigger +0x18`/`+0x19`; only 3 of the 37 leaves read those flags back, so for the other 34 `keyword = this` degenerates to `field >= 0`.

Four leaves multiply this by 1000 inside their own Evaluate because the field they compare it against is thousandths - `revolt_risk`, `pure_revolt_risk`, `nationalism`, `province_temperature` - which is the one place the script number is the natural unit and still cannot carry a fraction. **`CValueTrigger::value` is the same offset with the opposite convention.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md)

fields.name: arg_is_this

fields.name: arg_is_from

fields.name: value
fields.comment: **The operand, in thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CValueTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D13E0) as `TokenToFixedPoint(text)`, so `war_exhaustion = 7.5` is stored as 7500 - the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `national_unity=81.752`). A leaf's own Evaluate then either compares it straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3 says which does which. **This is the opposite convention from `CIntTrigger::value` at the same offset**, and nothing in the script files distinguishes them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: faction
fields.comment: The faction the scripted `join_faction` effect names - the whole payload of the effect. `CJoinFactionEffect::Execute` reads it at 0x9A1C66, walks its `Members (+0x28)` to see whether the scoped country is already in, and otherwise hands it to `CFaction::AddCountry` as the receiver. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-faction.md)

fields.name: Type
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetType, inherited from CDiplomaticAction
BiceLib: type (int) - The action's `CDiplomaticAction::EType`, and the **stage** an offer is at rather than what kind of offer it is: the kind is the C++ subclass, and its name is slot 15's save token. `CDiplomaticAction::GetType` is registered to Lua and resolves to a two-instruction `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret` at 0x416000. The enum has **three** values, all registered in one luabind chain ending at 0x8ED397: ('PROPOSE', ebx) at 0x8ED38D with ebx zeroed at 0x8EAE68 and never rewritten, ('DECLINE', 1) at 0x8ED37F, and **('ACCEPT', 2) at 0x8ED3BB**, appended to the same value vector at 0x8ED3C9 and registered by the loop at 0x8ED3CE. So 0 = PROPOSE, 1 = DECLINE, 2 = ACCEPT. What acts on it: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute enqueues a PROPOSE on the recipient and anything else on the actor; the hourly AI pass at 0x682BA8 only touches entries still at PROPOSE and writes 2 into the field at 0x682BB3 to accept them. The body at 0x416000 has two references and so is **not** recorded under a class name (trap 4); the field is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: Value
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetValue, inherited from CDiplomaticAction
BiceLib: value (unsigned char) - A bool, exposed to Lua as GetValue/SetValue: CDiplomaticAction::SetValue (0xA0E980, one reference, no vftable) is `this->+0x24 = [ebp+8]` and the getter is the folded `mov al,[ecx+0x24]` at 0xA0E990. **CTradeAction::IsValid (slot 13, 0xA38770) branches on it at 0xA387DA**: set, and it validates a fresh trade offer; clear, and it instead requires that an identical route already exist on the pair. So `value` is the proposal/cancellation polarity a script controls. **Units: none - it is a bool, not thousandths.** In the save it is written `value=yes` / `value=no`, 39 yes and 6 no over the 45 saves on this machine, which is also how the `value` loader case reads it: ParseBool (rva 0x67B410) at 0xA0E6E6, not a number. Seven of the family also use it as their slot-18 answer, through the folded `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x24], 0; setne al; ret` at 0xA0FE10 and the recorded ReturnByteAt24 at 0xA0E990. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: persistent_id
fields.comment: Always 0x18D. Written by CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor (0xA0EB30), by each of the eleven Lua `Create` factories (e.g. 0x8E84A9) and copied by every slot-16 clone, so every action in the family carries it. **It is not a per-class discriminator**: CCommand +0x4 is recorded as "a class id" and holds the same 0x18D, and the kind of action is carried by slot 15's save token instead. What reads it was not traced; token 0x18D resolves to `none`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: actor
fields.comment: The country making the offer, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the four-character tag at +0x8 and the country id at +0xC. Loaded from the save key `actor` (token 0x2E9) at 0xA0E7B5/0xA0E7BB, where CCountryDataBase::GetTag's result is copied as two dwords. CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor fills it with "---" and id 0. Every reader that wants the CCountry indexes `g_CCountryDataBase::countries_first` with +0xC: CTradeAction::IsValid, CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute and the base's slot 14 all do. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: recipient
fields.comment: The country being offered to, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the tag at +0x10 and the id at +0x14. Loaded from the save key `recipient` (token 0x2EA) at 0xA0E86A/0xA0E874. The base's slot 14, `IsSelectable` (0xA0EAE0), is three instructions: `return actor_id != recipient_id` - so the family's default selectability test is just "these are two different countries". (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: date
fields.comment: When the offer was made, in **hours** on the same scale as g_CCurrentGameState's tick (+0xBDC), counted from the 43,800,000-hour epoch. Loaded from the save key `date` (token 0x1F8) through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E70A, written by every Lua `Create` factory from the current tick, and set to the epoch itself - the engine's null date, [0x170C2B8] - by the null action's constructor. CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's only use of it is `date + 0xA8`, seven days, handed to CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: last_command_date
fields.comment: When the action was last put on the wire, in hours on the tick scale - the save's own key name (token 0x3EC), loaded through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E806. **Two independent writers, both setting it to the current tick**: CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand stamps it just before wrapping the action in a command (0xA0E92D) and CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction stamps it again as the action is enqueued (0x4E62EB). That is what makes it later than `date` for an offer that has travelled: in the save corpus it differs from `date` in 34 of 56 blocks and is never earlier. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: front_line
fields.comment:
**The units that actually fight this tick**, and the CList's own `count` at +0xB8 is how many. Distinct from `units` at +0x40, which is everyone on this side: CLandCombatant::Attack walks this one to decide who shoots, and CCombatant::PickTarget draws from the enemy's to decide who is shot at. **What puts a unit on it has not been read** - combat width is the obvious candidate and is not yet evidence.

**This is the land family's layout, not the base's (2026-10-05, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md).** The CList reading is right for CLandCombatant - its Attack does `lea esi, [ebx+0xB0]` and walks nodes at +8 from 0x16B3B0, and CCombatant::PickTarget takes the count from +0xB8 - and both of those are land. The air and bombing combatants use those bytes for a target array instead, and **the two layouts are the opposite way round** (corrected 2026-10-05, later the same day): CBomberCombatant keeps `target_count` at +0xB0 and `targets[1024]` at +0xB4 (0x160BD3, 0x160BDE), while CAirCombatant keeps `targets[1024]` at +0xB0 and the count at +0x10B0 (0x16D4C3, 0x16D4D0, 0x16D529). The 1024 bound is confirmed off `cmp eax, 0x400` at 0x16D4C9. Both classes now have struct records. The allocation sizes settle it: CLandCombatant is **0xE4** (0x17B4EB), CAirCombatant and the CBombTargetCombatant family **0x10B4**, CBomberCombatant **0x10E8** - and 0x10B4 - 0xB4 is exactly 0x1000, 1024 pointers. So sizeof(CCombatant) is 0xB0 and this field belongs on CLandCombatant, which has no struct record to move it to (mergeFindings cannot create one). Note the granularity difference it exposes: the land front line holds CUnit*, the air and bombing target arrays hold CSubUnit*. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CCombatant

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: no_unlink
fields.comment:
**The list's fourth member: a deferred-deletion lock.** While it is set, code that would remove a node from this list instead **marks the node and leaves it linked**, so nothing is unlinked while something is walking it; the node carries the matching mark at its own +0xC. Read with those semantics by CWeatherManager::Tick at 0x4B5CD7 - `cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` on a list at +0x8, i.e. this member - which on the set branch does `mov byte ptr [eax+0xc], 1` on the spent node and skips the unlink, and on the clear branch relinks prev/next and fixes `first` and `last`. That same unlink confirms the head layout from the other side.

**The head really is 0x10 and this really is part of it.** CEffect's inlined base constructor writes `+8 = +0xC = +0x10 = 0` and then `byte +0x14 = 0` - three dwords and a byte, which is this head being zeroed rather than a triple followed by a holder's own field. CCountry's thirteen CCountryLists sit at a 0x10 stride, each with its byte; CFaction's head at +0x28 ends here at +0x34 with `members_changed` a separate field at +0x38; and CWeatherFront's hand-decomposed `provinces` triple put its byte at +0x18, which is this offset exactly.

**Three field records were each describing this one member from their holder's side, and all three were folded away** - a field inside a larger typed one never reaches the apply - so they disagreed in silence and none of them was visible in Ghidra. Deleted 2026-10-07 and preserved here: `CEffect +0x14 unused`, "a byte every effect carries, zeroed when it is built and touched by nothing else in the image"; `CWeatherFront +0x18 provinces_flag`, "the byte that follows the game's CList triple; zeroed by the constructor and never read in this class"; and `CWeatherManager +0x14 freeze_fronts`, "while set, CWeatherManager::Tick marks a spent front's node at +0xC instead of unlinking it, so no front is ever removed" - which is the one that had the semantics right and only mistook them for weather. Each is consistent with this reading: an effect never iterates-and-deletes its children, so its copy stays clear.

**One record still does not fit.** `CNavy +0x2F0 at_sea` is written as a *dword* by CNavy::LoadKey's save-token-0x3FC handler, at what is this offset inside `CUnit +0x2E4 carrying`. Both offsets are instruction-anchored, so either a fleet loaded at sea leaves its carrying list permanently locked, or one of the two is misread - see CANDIDATES.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factbase.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect, inherited from CStringEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CStringEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CStringEffect
