fields.name: definition_file
fields.comment: `default.map` - the name of the map definition file, the first thing the constructor puts in the +8 sub-object. The full path built from it goes to the global Hoi3CString at VA 0x170C750. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: cache_stale
fields.comment: The one gate on every map cache. Written once, at 0x489C49, from IsCacheStale(this); non-zero means every cache must be rebuilt. Six readers, all byte-sized: three in CMap::LoadMapFiles (0x48A6A0 the adjacency cache, 0x48A777 the CALC_PATHS block, 0x48AE73 whether to write adjacencies.bin back) plus 0x48B808 provincecache.bin, 0x48BE3C climate.bin and 0x48DA46 navaldist.bin. Read 0 live, which the session's own time.log corroborates: 'It takes <0> seconds to calculate paths'. Because one flag covers all of them and the stamp behind it ignores climate.bmp, a climate edit alone can never invalidate cache/climate.bin. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: cache_stamp
fields.comment: The sum of ChecksumFile over seven map files - default.map, positions.txt, terrain.txt, provinces.bmp, terrain.bmp, definition.csv, adjacencies.csv - computed by 0x492100 and stored at 0x489C3B. Compared against the four bytes of map/cache/time to decide staleness, and written back there by 0x4922D0. Read 0x856CAC69 live, which equals both the recomputed sum over the mod's own map folder and the contents of the mod's cache/time file. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: lists
fields.comment: **512 CLists, 0x2000 bytes, from +0x50 to +0x2050** - the largest single thing the map holds and the one nothing has identified. The constructor runs the CRT vector-constructor iterator over them; the element destructor (rva 0x4A30D0) walks the chain from `first` freeing each node through node+8, so they are used, not vestigial. What indexes them - 512 of what - is **not settled here**; nothing in the constructor says. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: adjacencies_file

fields.name: province_raster
fields.comment: The province-id raster: a 16-bit image whose pixel is a province id. Read live, the object holds width 5616 at +0x04, height 2160 at +0x08, bytes per pixel 2 at +0x0C, bits per pixel 16 at +0x10, stride 11232 at +0x18 and +0x1C, and the pixel data at +0x20. The engine addresses it as base + x*bpp + y*stride and takes p[0] | p[1]<<8 (0x48FE7A and 0x4900BC). Row index is the engine's y directly, so the raster is already flipped relative to the BMP on disk. Looking 2000 provinces up at their own (+0x64,+0x68) returns the province itself 1984 times, with the same 16 misses and the same wrong ids that reading provinces.bmp gives - so this and the bitmap are the same function. Closes one of the three dwords project.json records as unidentified here. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: climate_file
fields.comment: default.map's `climate`. Three dwords at +0x20E0, +0x20E4 and +0x20E8 sit between this and the string before it, zeroed by the constructor and unidentified. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: unknown_210c

(reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: provinces_capacity
fields.comment: End of the province vector's storage. The constructor reserves **14500** entries here before anything is loaded, against the 14190 max_provinces the recorded +0x21FC holds - so the vector never grows during a game and the province pointers never move. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: terrains_capacity

fields.name: terrain_by_palette_index
fields.comment: **256 pointers, one per palette index of the terrain bitmap**, each to the entry terrain.txt declares for that index; the entry's +0xC is its CTerrain. CProvinceTemplate::MeasureEdges and the terrain pass of CMap::LoadMapFiles read a pixel's terrain as `[[map+0x2220+index*4]+0xc]`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: unknown_2620
fields.comment: A 0x400-byte table the constructor fills with 0xFF - the 'nothing here yet' fill, beside the zero-filled one at +0x2220. It ends at +0x2A20, where the next run of zeroed words begins. Unidentified. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: regions_begin

fields.name: regions_end

fields.name: by_name
fields.comment: The engine's own string hash table, `{int count; unsigned bucketCount; void** buckets;}` at +0x2A50/+0x2A54/+0x2A58 - the same shape StringHashFind (rva 0x5C7D60) walks. The constructor sets 0x1FF buckets and allocates and zeroes them; **what it indexes is not established here**, but every other instance of this table in the image is a by-name index for a loader, and CMap loads the terrains, continents and regions. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: province_templates
fields.comment: An array of CProvinceTemplate* indexed by province id, with the count beside it at +0x2A64. Already described in CProvinceTemplate +0x7C's comment but not carried as a field. Indexed at 0x48E0C5 (ReadAdjacencyCache), 0x48FEAC and 0x4900C5 (the positions.txt loader), 0x48AD30 and 0x48ADAA (LoadMapFiles) and 0x4913E4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: selection_listener
fields.comment: The screen every province's +0xCC was last set to (CMap_SetSelectionListener). Readers not looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-provinceview.md)

fields.name: sea_index_count
fields.comment: How many provinces have a sea index: the side of the table of distances by sea. Zeroed at the top of CMap::LoadPositionsFile (0x48FBE2) and raised once for each index given. 5,936 in Their Finest Hour. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

fields.name: naval_distances
fields.comment: **The table of distances by sea**: the upper triangle, diagonal included, of an N by N table of 16-bit numbers, row by row - the cell of indices i <= j is `(N - 1) * i - (i - 1) * i / 2 + j`. A cell is the shortest way between the two places in quarters of a pixel, or 0 where there is none. Allocated and filled by CMap::BuildNavalDistances; `map/cache/navaldist.bin` is exactly this. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

fields.name: map_width
fields.comment: 5616 live. Already cited in CProvinceTemplate +0x2C's comment as the value MapDistance (0x492030) wraps dx by, but not carried as a field. Equals provinces.bmp's and climate.bmp's pixel width, which is how the pixel formula in FINDINGS-mapbuild.md checks out. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: map_height
fields.comment: 2160 live. Read through the CMap global at 0x48FEC7 and 0x4900A3, where half of it is compared against CProvinceTemplate +0x68 to set the hemisphere byte +0xA2. Engine y runs 0..2159 with 0 in the far south, and a bitmap row is (height - 1 - y). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: unknown_2a80
fields.comment: An int the constructor defaults to **400**. FINDINGS-fieldmap.md puts default.map's `tree` key here, which would make it a list rather than an int, so the two do not agree and the field is left unnamed rather than named off the weaker of them. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: player

fields.name: map_mode
fields.comment: A copy of the map mode on screen: the supply setter writes 4 here beside CInGameIdler::current_map_mode. Readers were not looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md, section 9. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplyconvoys.md)

fields.name: x
fields.comment: The point's x in map pixels. Save key `x`, token 0x1F: CMapPoint::SaveContents writes it from here (rva 0x5D1E3) and CMapPoint::LoadKey sscanfs into here (rva 0x5D2D6). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md)

fields.name: y
fields.comment: The point's y in map pixels. Save key `y`, token 0x20: written from here at rva 0x5D239, parsed into here at rva 0x5D2C1. Last four bytes of a 0x10-byte object. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md)

fields.name: humidity
fields.comment: save key `humidity`, thousandths. Each hour CWeather::Update adds ((1000 - pNorm) x t / 1000) x cap / 1000 - more under low pressure, more when warm, slower once above 1.000, cap = 5 x the terrain's `humidity` on land (negative for a desert, which dries it) and 5.000 at sea, where t is also 10 degrees warmer - and, with no front, takes 10 x the hour's precipitation away. A front's SpreadWeather adds 0.98 of the source's to each province it reaches and takes a fifth of that from the source. CWeather::Clamp holds it in [MINHUMIDITY, MAXHUMIDITY]. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section B. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: pressure
fields.comment: save key `pressure`; a new province starts at PRESSUREDEFAULT (CProvince::CProvince at 0x9479E) and the high pressure zones push it up by PRESSUREPROPAGATION a step in CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: windspeed
fields.comment: save key `windspeed`; read by the air, bomb and naval weather terms and by WINDATTRITIONTHRESHOLD, and decayed by a compiled-in 0.750 an hour where no front is over the province **Corrected 2026-10-01: the factor is 0.750, not 0.980.** `CWeather::Update` reads `[0x1A86F3C]` = floor(750.5) = 750, which has exactly two references in the image - that read and its CRT initialiser. 0.980 is `[0x1A8703C]`, a different global: the humidity and pressure transfer factor in SpreadWeather. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: temperature
fields.comment: save key `temperature`, thousandths of a degree; the threshold tested by every LAND/AIR/BOMB temperature define, by the two attrition thresholds, and by the cold movement penalty (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: precipitation
fields.comment: save key `precipitation`; drives the land rain penalty, the air and bomb rain terms, the naval rain term, naval spotting, firing range and whether the ground freezes (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: muddyness
fields.comment: save key `muddyness`, 0..1000; the only thing that slows land movement (MUDDYNESSMOVEMENTMODIFIER) and the only weather term in supply losses (MUDDYNESSSUPPLYTAXMODIFIER). It rises while it rains, dries by max(the province's infrastructure effect, 2) an hour, and is zeroed below -5C - where `frozen` takes over (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: frozen
fields.comment: save key `frozen`, 0..1000; non-zero suppresses the mud movement penalty and the mud supply tax entirely. Rises by HOURLYFROZENINCREASE in the cold, falls by HOURLYTHAW above 0C (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: cloud_coverage
fields.comment: save key `cloud_coverage`; the air and bomb cloud terms, naval spotting, and - at or above ALLOWEDTOFLYTHRESHOLD - the flat refusal in CAir::CanMoveTo (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: front
fields.comment: the weather front over this province, copied from CProvince+0x14 at the top of CWeather::Update (0xB25D1) and zeroed there when there is none. Not saved (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: province

the units in the province, what CProvince::GetUnits answers (BiceLib/GameClasses/CMapProvince.hpp:214)

(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)

the controller (BiceLib/GameClasses/CMapProvince.hpp:211)
+0x4 inside it: controller_id (int) - The id half of the `controller` CCountryTag at +0x334 (letters at +0x334, id here). Slot 76 compares it directly in the inlined IsEnemy tests at 0x4DB3EA and 0x4DB46F and uses it to index CCountry +0xE28. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: weather_pressure_distance
fields.comment: scratch for CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure (0xB6050): the cost-so-far of the breadth-first walk out from a high pressure zone. Set to 99999 on every province at the start of each propagation and lowered as the walk reaches the province. Nothing outside that function reads it (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: weather_front
fields.comment: the CWeatherFront currently over this province, or 0. CWeatherManager::Tick clears it on every province each hour (0xB5C7C) and then every live front re-stamps itself onto the provinces on its own list (CWeatherFront::Tick, 0xB4657). CWeather::Update reads it and caches it in CWeather+0x28 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: nationalism
fields.comment: Years of nationalism left, thousandths: YEARS_OF_NATIONALISM on a change of owner, 83 off a month, scales static `nationalism` in the rebuild. See CProvince +0x24 and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section A. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: suppression
fields.comment: How much suppression stands in and around this province, thousandths. Recomputed every day by the daily province pass (0x49EE04) from SuppressionNearProvince (rva 0x9F360): the province's own figure plus that of every land province within two edges under the same controller - and the province's own a second time, since it is in its own two-edge list. A province's figure is the sum over its friendly units of strength/max_strength times the division's suppression (the sum of its brigades'), divided by 10 - so a full-strength brigade with suppression 1.00 contributes 0.100, and 1.000 here (ten such brigades' worth) stops the daily climb. Two readers on a tick: the daily revolt-risk step subtracts min(this x 0.1, 0.2) from its plus-or-minus 0.1, and GetProvinceEffectiveRevoltRisk subtracts this outright, a full point per 1.000. Checked against a save to the thousandth (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section B.2). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: is_night
fields.comment: a byte: whether it is night here, written once an hour by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange (0x27B204) from IsNight (0xA7390). Read by CWeather::BaseTemperature for a night temperature drop and by CNavalCombat::Tick (0x17BA27) for the break-off chance. NOTE: CLASSES.md's account of the command-reach maths calls CProvince +0x2C and +0x30 a pair of province coordinates; a byte store into +0x2C and a 1..5 climate id in +0x30 cannot both be true of that, and 0xA7390 takes its x position from CProvinceTemplate+0x64 instead. **It is also the largest single term in the naval disengage chance**: CNavalCombat::Tick uses a base constant of 11000 where this byte is set against 1000 where it is clear, so a naval battle is around eleven times more likely to break off at night. The naval survey found that lever and could not identify the byte; this is it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: climate
fields.comment: The season band 1..5 - not a climate zone - worked out by ComputeProvinceClimate (0xA81A0) from the day of the year, the latitude (+0x388) and the hemisphere byte (template +0xA2): north of 0.250 latitude, northern provinces run 5 (winter, L days about 1 January), 1, 2, 3 (summer, 183 - L days), 4, 4; southern ones 3, 4, 4, 5, 1, 2; at 0.250 or below, which is the whole southern hemisphere, it is always 3. Recomputed every game day by RunDailyProvincePass and on game entry; the lazy computes where it is 0 (BaseTemperature, CWeather::Update, CreateFront) are only a first-hour net. Read by BaseTemperature's switch, by CWeather::Update's two step multipliers and by CreateFront's zone mask (1 << climate). Not saved. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section B. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: convoys_begin
fields.comment: begin of a vector of the convoy routes touching this province; the daily supply pass walks it at a depot to work out how much surplus can be shipped home, counting only entries whose end_province_id is this province and whose start_province_id lies in the acting capital's area (BiceLib/GameState/CustomMapMode.cpp)

fields.name: convoys_end
fields.comment: end of the convoy vector at +0x38 (BiceLib/GameState/CustomMapMode.cpp)

fields.name: supply_depot_id
fields.comment: province id of the depot it draws from, and the supply network's label: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot only relaxes a neighbour that already carries the same value, and CSupply::DailySupplyPass only moves goods between provinces that do. Written only by CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0). A province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id is a depot, and is where the distance relaxation starts. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: not a hop count - the infrastructure-weighted cost of the cheapest path to the depot, 0 at the depot itself and 100000 while cut off. Each step adds max(4000 - 4*infrastructure, 1000)/1000 - an integer 1, 2 or 3, worst where infrastructure is lowest: 1 above half infrastructure, 2 over a quarter, 3 at a quarter and under - times the entered province's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. The cost belongs to the province entered and not to the edge, so a route's distance is the sum of its provinces' entry costs, and a neighbour u on the same network is a predecessor of v on a least-cost route exactly when d(u) == d(v) - cost(v). Written only by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x289B20, the reset) and CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0, the relaxation). The plain hop count is +0x50. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: supply_depot_hops
fields.comment: the plain hop count to the depot, as against the weighted cost at +0x4C. Zeroed by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork and set to the parent's value plus one by each relaxation in CSupply::SpreadFromDepot. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: home_base_ptr
fields.comment: The province's base object - the same object a unit's home-base pointer CUnit +0x98 holds. CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits compares the two for identity at 0x4CE47D (`if (wing->+0x98 != prov->+0x54) ...`), and walks prov->+0x54 -> +4 as a CList of the units stationed there, summing their regiments_count into the airfield occupancy figure at 0x4CE449-0x4CE49C. So +0x54 carries a unit list at its own +4. Read only by the air body of the two; it has **not** been shown that a naval base is a different field, so the name deliberately says 'home base' rather than 'air base'. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorganise.md)

fields.name: naval_base_station
fields.comment:
The province's **naval** base object - the naval sibling of `+0x54 home_base_ptr`, which is the object an air unit's `CUnit +0x98` holds.

CAIUnit_ManageNavalUnits' rebase block hands `candidate->+0x58 + 4` to the same ship counter (0x5D5CC0) that it hands `fleet->home_base_ptr (+0x98) + 4` eight instructions earlier (0x4D2EC2 against 0x4D2FB4), so the two are the same kind of object and `+0x58` is where a province keeps the one a fleet bases at. `+4` is the CList of units stationed there, exactly as `+0x54 + 4` is for an airfield.

**Inferred, not confirmed**: what makes it the *naval* one is that only fleets reach it and only wings reach +0x54, which is a reading of the two callers rather than of the object. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

fields.name: MaxInfrastructure
fields.comment:
An int in thousandths that the unit AI uses as "is this province worth holding a front over". `CAIUnit::EstimateAreaNeed` requires a neighbour's value to be at least 200 before the province counts as a front (0x4B8830), and gives the province itself the floor weight 500 instead of 1000 when its own value is at or below 300 (0x4B8BF4). Eight more readers across the unit AI and the map code. **Written in exactly one place**: `CProvince::LoadKey`'s default arm, which treats an unknown key as a building name and, when the loaded building's definition `+0x24` is 12, sets `province->+0x5C = building->level(+0x20) * definition->+0x8 / 1000` (0x96132-0x96152). Which building type index 12 is was **not** established - the mod reorders `common/buildings.txt`, so it is not safe to count. The cheapest live check is `dumpStruct.py` on a province and a comparison against the province panel.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02, and renamed from `ai_front_value`.** Read on every province with an `infra` key in `history/provinces/`, and compared: **10,642 of 10,642 agree** with `infra * 100`, where `infra` is the file's 0-10 value. (A first pass scored 98.43% against the *first* `infra` key in each file; all 167 misses were files that repeat the key, and the engine is **last-wins** - the residual was the test, not the field.) This does not contradict 'an int in thousandths': `infra * 100` and a fraction in thousandths are the same number, since the file's 0-10 is 0-100%. Paris (2613) reads 1000 = infra 10.0 = 100%.

**The old name named a use, not the field.** The unit AI reads infrastructure when deciding whether a province is worth holding a front over, which is why it looked like an AI value. The gain from the rename is that the thresholds become readable in the units a modder sees: the 200 at 0x4B8830 is **infrastructure 2.0** and the 300 at 0x4B8BF4 is **3.0**. A province under 2.0 does not count as a front; under 3.0 it gets the floor weight 500 instead of 1000.

`+0x24 == 12` is untouched by this and is still not a building index - `infra` is building no.21 in the mod's `common/buildings.txt`, so 12 is an id of something else, as the record already says.

**Renamed from `infrastructure` and retyped 2026-10-05, in step with CProvince +0x5C**, which is the same field: RTTI has CMapProvince deriving from CProvince at offset 0, and both structures carry it only because Ghidra has no inheritance. The game's own name is `MaxInfrastructure`, from `CProvince::GetMaxInfrastructure` (rva 0x6C360); the effective infrastructure is a different quantity computed by `CProvince::GetInfrastructure` (rva 0x94570) out of the modifier array at +0x114. The unit AI's use of this field - a neighbour needing at least 200 before a province counts as a front, the floor weight dropping to 500 at or below 300 - is unchanged by the rename and now reads as thresholds on 20% and 30% of full infrastructure, which is what the 1000 clamp in GetInfrastructure says the scale is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: rebel_type_ptr
fields.comment: The rebel type of a province history's `revolt = { type ... }`, or null. Written only by SetProvinceRevolt (rva 0xA6E40), from CRevoltChange::Apply when the history is replayed (and zeroed by 0x496AB1, 0x40DE92). Read by SpawnFullRevoltInProvince (rva 0xA6C30) when a new game is entered, which does nothing more for a province where it is null. **Not saved**. No province file of Their Finest Hour or BlackICE has a `revolt`, so it is null in both. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: rebel_brigades_per_manpower
fields.comment: The `size` of a province history's `revolt`: SpawnFullRevoltInProvince (rva 0xA6C30) makes this times max(1, manpower(+0x320)/1000) rebel brigades. Written by SetProvinceRevolt (rva 0xA6E40) from CRevoltChange::Apply; not saved, and zeroed by the same two writers as +0x60. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: weather_graphic
fields.comment: the std::string CWeather::GraphicName last answered for this province - a pointer to one of its seven globals (g_WeatherGraphic_*), so never owned; written hourly by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange. ProvinceGraphics_UpdateWeatherPicture reads its length (+0x10) to tell a picture from the clear sky. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section C.3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: weather_graphic_changed
fields.comment: set by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange (0x27B21D) when the weather picture's name changed in the hour; read and cleared by ProvinceGraphics_UpdateWeatherPicture, which then rebuilds the picture - only while the weather map mode is on, so outside it the flag stays set. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section C.3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: flags
fields.comment: The province's flags, held by value; CMapProvince derives from CProvince, whose constructor places it. See CProvince +0xA0. **The `CPersistent` second base is 0x24 into it**, and it is the sub-object `SaveContents` calls slot 1 on to write the `flags` block - which is why that offset once looked like a field of this class and was recorded as one (`flags_persistent` at +0xC4, deleted 2026-10-05). It is not declared here any more: `CFlags` is 0x28 bytes and Ghidra's own RTTI pass already names the second base's vftable at `CFlags+0x24`, so a `CPersistent` declared at +0xC4 collided with the `CFlags` held here and the two replaced each other on every apply - the period-2 cycle described in ghidra/README.md. The tree itself is this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md)

fields.name: selection_listener
fields.comment: Who a selection of this province is told to: CProvince::OnSelected calls its slot 11 (CInGameIdler::ShowProvinceView) and OnDeselected its slot 13. Written for every province by CMap_SetSelectionListener (the in-game screen's constructor hands it the idler); the province constructor zeroes it. The field is the base's, CProvince +0xCC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-provinceview.md)

fields.name: scaled_modifiers
fields.comment: See CProvince +0x12C: the rebuild's scaled copies, tail +0x130, count +0x134. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: near_provinces_begin
fields.comment: Begin of a vector of **every province within two edges**, each once, in the order met - and so the province itself, once it has a neighbour; sea provinces too. Filled by the province's reset at 0x496480 from its template's edges and each neighbour's. CSupplyGroup::PickDepot scores a province over it and SuppressionNearProvince sums over it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md)

fields.name: near_provinces_end
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x14C; +0x154 is its end of storage. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md)

fields.name: last_pool
fields.comment: **The pool as the daily supply pass left it when it came to this province** - after the province's own takes, before anything further in the day. A province further from the depot is offered no more than this, and since it is visited first, what it reads is yesterday's: goods move one province a day. A province nothing was asked of does not have it brought up to date. Not saved. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md, section 3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md)

fields.name: need
fields.comment: **What the units drawing on the province ask for in a day, as phase 2 of the daily supply pass set it**: SupplyNeed's figure, raised to 1.000 where it is between nothing and that and the pool holds under 5.000. Zeroed in phase 1 and not set for a capital, so there it is nothing. CUnit::ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel shares a short pool out by it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md, section 3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md)

fields.name: capital
fields.comment: **The province is its controller's acting capital or touches it.** RunDailyProvincePass rewrites it every day at 0x49ED9D and 0x49EDEC: 1 where the controller's acting capital is this province or the province across one of its template's edges, 0 otherwise. The game saves it as `capital` - 402 provinces on the first day, all of them a capital or beside one - and the loader sets it from a `yes`. While it is set SupplyCapacity answers 99999. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 7. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md)

fields.name: area
fields.comment: the area the province is in: **read live**, the object's own RTTI says COwnerArea, or CNullOwnerArea where nothing owns it, and 4999 provinces share 50 of them in blocks of neighbouring ids. CCountry::NeedConvoyToTradeWith wants both acting capitals to have one, and asks AreaIsConnectedTo about the two when the capitals are on different continents (reversing/CLASSES.md:1)

fields.name: combats
fields.comment: Every ordinary combat going on in this province - first at +0x2EC, last at +0x2F0, count at +0x2F4, 0x10-byte nodes. CMapProvince::AddCombat appends to it and CMapProvince::HasCombatOfKind walks it. Bombings do not go here: CCombatManager::CreateCombat puts a combat on this list only when the combat's slot 8 is false, and in the same `else` writes +0x2FC when it is true, so +0x2FC is the province's *bombing* slot and this is the list of the rest. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: naval_base
fields.comment: the province's naval base; NavalBaseCapacity (0xA75D0) multiplies its level_current by a supply define and by the NAVAL_BASE_EFFICIENCY modifier (BiceLib/GameState/CustomMapMode.cpp)

fields.name: air_base
fields.comment: **The province's air base**, the sibling of the naval base at +0x300. The crowding of an air unit's base reads `base->slot0()->+0x304->level_current (+0x24)` as the room it has - in CUnit::RegainOrganisation (0x5C6D65) and in CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute (0x51BF00) - on the arm an air unit takes, where a fleet's arm calls NavalBaseCapacity. Earlier reader, which is what the old name came from: CAIUnit slot 78 reads `provinces[army->ai_param_b]->+0x304->+0x20 / 1000` at 0x4B245F-0x4B2482 and, when that is below 1, clears `CArmy +0x2E4` and posts `CSetAIParamCommand` - +0x20 is the building's level_max, so that test is "the air base this AI parameter was set for is gone". (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-organisation.md)

fields.name: anti_air
fields.comment: The province's anti-aircraft building, as CProvince +0x308. UpdateAirMapIcons sizes the large anti-aircraft picture by its built level (+0x20). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airmap.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airmap.md)

fields.name: owner
fields.comment:
the owner. Eight bytes: the tag at +0x32C and **the id at +0x330**, which is what code asking whether a province is owned at all compares against zero - `---` with id 0 is what CCountryDataBase::GetTag hands back where there is none. Two such tests are the sea-hop gate at rva 0x1CEEA4 and the naval-base check at rva 0xA7EE3. (reversing/CLASSES.md)
+0x4 inside it: owner_id (int) - Id half of the `owner` CCountryTag at +0x32C, and the half every comparison actually uses. CEventScope::MakeScope's `owner` arm (0x5C1CE2) reads +0x32C and +0x330 as one pair into the rebound scope's `country_tag`/`country_id`, and its `local_enemy` arm (0x5C1ED4) compares each unit's `owner_id (CUnit +0x128)` against this field to decide which units in the province count as enemies. Symmetric with `controller_id` at +0x338 beside `controller` at +0x334. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

fields.name: peace_new_owner
fields.comment: Scratch: who the province would go to at a peace. Written only by CCountry_ListPeaceTransfers (VA 0x503AC4, 0x503B6B) and read by CollectPeaceTransfers, CPeaceAction::Apply (the ChangeOwner owner, 0xA3FE74) and CPeaceAction_BuildResultText; set to '---' with id 0 by the province's constructor (0x494AD4). Never saved. So a tooltip or dialog that builds the result text rewrites it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: port
fields.comment: **The province's port, or null**: a 0x1C-byte CPort made by CMap::LoadBuildingPositions for a land province whose naval_base position lies on a pixel of a sea province that is not landlocked water. Its +0x18 is that sea province's id and its list (+8, +0xC, +0x10) the fleets lying in the province now. CNavy::MayStandIn requires it of a land province. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

fields.name: regions_first
fields.comment: The first node of the province's list of regions, in the map's order (CMap::AssignRegions); its first region is the one an air window's region shape uses. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md)

fields.name: regions_last
fields.comment: The last node of that list. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md)

fields.name: regions_count
fields.comment: How many regions list the province. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md)

fields.name: continent
fields.comment: The continent continent.txt lists the province under, set by CMap::AssignContinents the first time the province is met; a second listing is logged and ignored. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

fields.name: blockaded
fields.comment: **Whether the port is blockaded**: set by UpdateProvinceBlockaded (rva 0xA65E0) when enemy, unretreating, not-fighting units with at least one ship stand in the port's sea province, cleared otherwise and on a province with no owner, port or working naval base. Its only caller is the controller setter, so it is as of the last change of controller. Read by `is_blockaded`, UpdateBlockadeLevel (the country's share at CCountry +0xBD4), RebuildProvinceModifierValues (rva 0x9FD51), COwnerArea::FindOpenPort (0x7E552) and a read at 0xDEB60. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md)

fields.name: intel_by_country_ptr
fields.comment: One byte per country index: how well that country knows the province, **0 to 9**. Rebuilt from nothing once a game day (RunIntelRefresh) and raised for single provinces in the hour a unit enters or leaves them (RunIntelRefreshIfRequested): 9 for the controller and every country on its allied_or_faction_countries (alliance, dependency, the same faction), for the underground's owner and its list, and for a foreign unit's owner on land (at sea where in a battle or patrolling after a target, else 2); 3 on every adjacent land province for the controller and its list; 2 to 9 on every adjacent land province for a foreign unit's owner, by its decryption against that province's controller's encryption; up to 8 from radar; a spy's or local_intel_boost's grant on a unit. All 0 to 9 can be written. Not saved. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md, section C. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset; both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: area_seen
fields.comment: Marked by CAirOrder::FillArea as it reaches a province, and cleared afterwards from the order's +0x58 list. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md)

fields.name: theatre_id_type
fields.comment: The province's theatre, held as an object id pair in the same form as CAIUnit +0x68/+0x6C: type half here, serial half at +0x384. CAIUnit slot 76 compares the pair against a CTheatre's own id (+0x8 type, +0xC serial) at 0x4DB5B8-0x4DB5C2 to give a front in the unit's own theatre a tenfold scoring bonus. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: theatre_id
fields.comment: Serial half of the theatre object id whose type half is at +0x380; compared against CTheatre +0xC. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: latitude_north
fields.comment: Same field as CProvince +0x388 - CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset. Normalised distance north of the equator in thousandths of half the map height, written by ComputeProvinceLatitude (0x963F0) and zero across the whole southern hemisphere. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.comment: End of the deferred keys' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: token

CModifier::LoadKey matches a key against it, first match by position in the definition vector. Renamed 2026-10-14 from order_token, which described the 32 alone. fields.name: id
fields.comment: The modifier's own id - its index in the definition vector at 0x1686194 - which is what a CModifier block indexes at id * 8. InitMissionEfficiencyModifiers writes it at 0x583994 from the vector's length taken immediately before the push_back, which is what makes the engine's 32 `*_eff` modifier ids consecutive and dependent on how many modifiers were registered before startup reached that function. fields.name: percent

fields.name: ESPIONAGE_BONUS
fields.comment: modifier 42, script key `espionage_bonus` (token 0x4C4), percent and more-is-better, displayed 'Espionage bonus' (TFH interface.csv; BlackICE relabels it 'Domestic Counterespionage Difficulty'). Its one reader in the image is CSpyPresence::CatchSpies at 0x52E6C3, off the country the spies are in: every catch there is multiplied by (1000 - this)/1000, so a positive value makes spies in the holder's own country harder to catch, by anyone, and does nothing for the holder's spies abroad. Named in BiceLib/GameClasses/CModifier.hpp. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section F. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: COUNTER_ESPIONAGE
fields.comment: modifier 55, script key `counter_espionage` (token 0x4EB), percent and more-is-better, displayed 'Counterespionage'. Its one reader in the image is CSpyPresence::CatchSpies at 0x52E484, in the home arm only (actor == target): added to SPY_DETECTION_CHANCE before everything else, so a total of +0.1 doubles the base 0.1, and a total of -0.1 (free_press alone) brings it to nought and lower makes it negative - either way no roll then passes, except for a friend's hostile spies, whose +1000000 still does. It does nothing to spies abroad, the holder's or anyone's. The espionage screen lists its sources under `value_spies_caught` (0x620498). Named in BiceLib/GameClasses/CModifier.hpp. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section F. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_last

fields.name: children_count

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: is_script_block

While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. fields.name: value
fields.comment: **The operand, in thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CValueTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D13E0) as `TokenToFixedPoint(text)`, so `war_exhaustion = 7.5` is stored as 7500 - the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `national_unity=81.752`). A leaf's own Evaluate then either compares it straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3 says which does which. **This is the opposite convention from `CIntTrigger::value` at the same offset**, and nothing in the script files distinguishes them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: value
fields.comment:
**The operand, as a plain integer - not thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CIntTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D1400) as `atoi(text)`, which truncates, so the decimal a mod writes is lost before anything compares it. Zeroed instead when the argument was the keyword `this` (SaveToken 0x377) or `from` (0x34F), which set `CTrigger +0x18`/`+0x19`; only 3 of the 37 leaves read those flags back, so for the other 34 `keyword = this` degenerates to `field >= 0`.

Four leaves multiply this by 1000 inside their own Evaluate because the field they compare it against is thousandths - `revolt_risk`, `pure_revolt_risk`, `nationalism`, `province_temperature` - which is the one place the script number is the natural unit and still cannot carry a fraction. **`CValueTrigger::value` is the same offset with the opposite convention.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: mode_68
fields.comment: **`clear`**: whether the order replaces the path the unit has. It is the key the command is saved under, and CUnit::OrderToProvince passes `!append`. fields.name: death_date

Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement began**, as a tick (save key `start_date`). Parsed from `year.month.day.hour` text by Date_SetFromString, which is the same representation every other date in the simulation uses. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement ends**, as a tick (save key `end_date`); **the null date 43,800,000 (`[0x170C2B8]`) where it has none** - every constructor sets it so, not zero. A real date is told by `(end_date - 43,800,000) / 24 / 365.0 > 1`. Read only by CCasusBelli (Activate, which will not attach an expired one, and IsOver) and by CRelation::SaveContents (written only when real). **No other relation's IsOver reads it**: a guarantee ends twenty years after `start_date`, a NAP NAP_EXPIRY_MONTHS after it, and the history files' end dates take effect only while history is replayed before play. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: cancel
fields.comment: **Whether the agreement is cancelled** (save key `cancel`), the last of CRelation's own bytes - a subclass's data starts at +0x24. No writer in play was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

CCountry::CanBreakNap compares it with NAP_BREAK_FORCE_BALANCE_1..3, inverting it (1,000,000 / balance) for the second party. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: positioning
fields.comment: Naval positioning, thousandths, save key `positioning` (0x39B). Rolled once at combat start by CNavalCombat slot 13 (0x17B910) and then written by CNavalCombatant::UpdatePositioning (0x166E70) as `clamp0(+0x10B8 + 400 + leaderSkill*100 - stackPenalty)`; CNavalCombatant::Attack (slot 15) adds 20 a tick while it is below `max(100, 400 + leaderSkill*100 - stackPenalty)`. leaderSkill is CLeader.skill (+0x70) of the highest-ranked real leader on the side; stackPenalty is NavalStackingPositionPenalty (0x1D5B80). **The base 400, the per-tick 20 and the skill weight 100 are all hardcoded literals, not defines** - only the three NAVAL_STACK_POS_* defines are mod-facing. Because the die can be up to 190, a side can start above its own cap and then never move. What positioning is multiplied into is not established. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navaldetection.md)

fields.name: positioning_roll

Every plan field already recorded on CUnit is this object's offset plus 0x1FC: +0x204 plan_active = plan +0x8, +0x208 plan_stance = +0xC, +0x20C plan_air_stance = +0x10, +0x210 plan_naval_stance = +0x14, +0x26C plan_subunit_wanted = +0x70, +0x27C plan_our_power = +0x80, +0x280 plan_their_power = +0x84. The save writes it under `plan` by calling slot 1 on it, which works because +0x1FC is the embedded object's own vftable pointer. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit

+0xC inside it: plan_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0xC, the `stance` key. Defaults to 2 when the plan is switched off. The one plan attribute whose change makes CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute call CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds; 5 is the command's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md), inherited from CUnit
+0x10 inside it: plan_air_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0x10, the `air_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it.

**Every writer in the image, and who reaches it:**

| writer | value | path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute, store at 0x1E7907 | the command's `+0x6C`, skipped when it is 3 | the only store by this displacement; everything below goes through it |
| CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan, 0x4DE9EF | 1 | construction, so 1 is every unit's starting value |
| CUnitPlan::SetActive(plan, 0), 0x4DEB78 | 1 | deactivating a plan resets it; reached from CActivateUnitPlanCommand::Execute and CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit, both interface commands |
| CUnitPlan::LoadKey, 0x4DF93B | whatever the save holds | load |

And the seven places that post that command, by what they pass for air_stance: **2 from CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4916AD), for every unit agent, every ProcessAI pass**; 0 from CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan (0x4DAD74) when it builds a plan; 3 (leave alone) from CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (0x4C375E) and from the two power-estimate sites 0x4B5152 and 0x4B7E87; and the interface's own control at 0x35244E, which passes the value the player chose (0x351C8E is its naval twin and passes 3 here).

**So the AI drives this field to 2 by itself and the strategic air war is not player-only.** The sentinel-3 AI sites mean the ground-stance machinery never disturbs it.

**Live distribution (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save)**, unchanged and still worth reading with the above: 1 on 1,125 of 1,126 `CAir` formations and on 737 of 738 `CNavy`, and **2 on all 101 of the armies attached to a CAIUnit agent**. The air formations are not the objects phase 4's gate reads; the 101 armies are. And `+0x20C` and `+0x210` holding the identical value on all 4,864 objects read is explained: the AI's one writer sets both to 2 in the same command, and CUnitPlan's constructor and reset set both to 1. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md), inherited from CUnit

fields.name: value

**The operand, as a plain integer - not thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CIntTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D1400) as `atoi(text)`, which truncates, so the decimal a mod writes is lost before anything compares it. fields.comment: the area the province is in: **read live**, the object's own RTTI says COwnerArea, or CNullOwnerArea where nothing owns it, and 4999 provinces share 50 of them in blocks of neighbouring ids. CCountry::NeedConvoyToTradeWith wants both acting capitals to have one, and asks AreaIsConnectedTo about the two when the capitals are on different continents (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCountry.hpp:390)

fields.comment: the combat being fought here, or null. CCombat::AfterLoad puts the combat here when the province has none yet; **read live**, 4 of 4999 provinces had one and every one of them was a CCombat subclass by its own RTTI (BiceLib/GameClasses/CCombat.hpp:102)

CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. fields.comment: leadership. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures (BiceLib/GameClasses/CMapProvince.hpp:188)
