fields.comment: the head of the list of countries holding a core here; the writer emits one `core` key per node, out of the tag at the node itself (BiceLib/GameClasses/CMapProvince.hpp:51)

fields.name: intel_country_count
fields.comment: number of entries in the intel array. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures (BiceLib/GameClasses/CMapProvince.hpp:55)

fields.name: underground_owner
fields.comment: who owns the underground here, saved as `underground_owner`: four characters and the id at +0x390, the shape of a CCountryTag (BiceLib/GameClasses/CMapProvince.hpp:54)

fields.name: weather_pressure_distance
fields.comment: scratch for CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure (0xB6050): the cost-so-far of the breadth-first walk out from a high pressure zone. Set to 99999 on every province at the start of each propagation and lowered as the walk reaches the province. Nothing outside that function reads it (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: weather_front
fields.comment: the CWeatherFront currently over this province, or 0. CWeatherManager::Tick clears it on every province each hour (0xB5C7C) and then every live front re-stamps itself onto the provinces on its own list (CWeatherFront::Tick, 0xB4657). CWeather::Update reads it and caches it in CWeather+0x28 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: strategic_resource
fields.comment: The strategic resource here, as a **pointer to the entry in the strategic-resource CNameDataBase**, not a number. Null when the province has none. The entry carries its key as an Hoi3CString at +0x30 and answers a bool from virtual slot 14, which is what decides whether the key is written at all. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: nationalism
fields.comment: Years of nationalism left, thousandths: set to YEARS_OF_NATIONALISM (20000 in Their Finest Hour) by CMapProvince::ChangeOwner when the old owner is a real country, 83 off a month in RunMonthlyPass after that month's rebuild, floored at 0. The rebuild adds static `nationalism` times it / 1000 where the controller (also the owner) has no core here. Saved as `nationalism` only when not 0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md, section A. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: is_night
fields.comment: a byte: whether it is night here, written once an hour by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange (0x27B204) from IsNight (0xA7390). Read by CWeather::BaseTemperature for a night temperature drop and by CNavalCombat::Tick (0x17BA27) for the break-off chance. NOTE: CLASSES.md's account of the command-reach maths calls CProvince +0x2C and +0x30 a pair of province coordinates; a byte store into +0x2C and a 1..5 climate id in +0x30 cannot both be true of that, and 0xA7390 takes its x position from CProvinceTemplate+0x64 instead (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: climate
fields.comment: The season band 1..5 - not a climate zone - worked out by ComputeProvinceClimate (0xA81A0) from the day of the year, the latitude (+0x388) and the hemisphere byte (template +0xA2): north of 0.250 latitude, northern provinces run 5 (winter, L days about 1 January), 1, 2, 3 (summer, 183 - L days), 4, 4; southern ones 3, 4, 4, 5, 1, 2; at 0.250 or below, which is the whole southern hemisphere, it is always 3. Recomputed every game day by RunDailyProvincePass and on game entry; the lazy computes where it is 0 (BaseTemperature, CWeather::Update, CreateFront) are only a first-hour net. Read by BaseTemperature's switch, by CWeather::Update's two step multipliers and by CreateFront's zone mask (1 << climate). Not saved. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section B. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: supply_depot_id
fields.comment: province id of the depot it draws from, and the supply network's label: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot only relaxes a neighbour that already carries the same value, and CSupply::DailySupplyPass only moves goods between provinces that do. Written only by CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0), from the province's area or, failing that, from CCountry::FindSupplyDepot on the controller - which answers the supplying country's acting capital. A province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id is a depot, and is where the distance relaxation starts. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: supply_depot_distance
fields.comment: not a hop count - the infrastructure-weighted cost of the cheapest path to the depot, 0 at the depot itself and 100000 while cut off. Each step adds max(4000 - 4*infrastructure, 1000)/1000 - an integer 1, 2 or 3, worst where infrastructure is lowest: 1 above half infrastructure, 2 over a quarter, 3 at a quarter and under - times the entered province's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. The cost belongs to the province entered and not to the edge, so a route's distance is the sum of its provinces' entry costs, and a neighbour u on the same network is a predecessor of v on a least-cost route exactly when d(u) == d(v) - cost(v). Written only by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x289B20, the reset) and CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0, the relaxation). The plain hop count is +0x50. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: supply_depot_hops
fields.comment: the plain hop count to the depot, as against the weighted cost at +0x4C. Zeroed for every province by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork and set to the parent's value plus one each time CSupply::SpreadFromDepot relaxes a neighbour. CSupply::DailySupplyPass never reads it; the only other reader found is 0xDB3CC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

fields.name: weather_graphic
fields.comment: the std::string CWeather::GraphicName last answered for this province - a pointer to one of its seven globals (g_WeatherGraphic_*), so never owned; written hourly by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange. ProvinceGraphics_UpdateWeatherPicture reads its length (+0x10) to tell a picture from the clear sky. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section C.3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: weather_graphic_changed
fields.comment: set by UpdateProvinceWeatherRange (0x27B21D) when the weather picture's name changed in the hour; read and cleared by ProvinceGraphics_UpdateWeatherPicture, which then rebuilds the picture - only while the weather map mode is on, so outside it the flag stays set. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section C.3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: flags
fields.comment: **The province's flags** - what `set_province_flag`, `clr_province_flag` and `has_province_flag` work on, held by value. CProvince::CProvince writes CFlags' vftable here and its CPersistent vftable at +0xC4, 0x24 later; the field project.json has been calling `flags` at +0xC4 is that sub-object. **The `CPersistent` second base is 0x24 into it**, and it is the sub-object `SaveContents` calls slot 1 on to write the `flags` block - which is why that offset once looked like a field of this class and was recorded as one (`flags_persistent` at +0xC4, deleted 2026-10-05). It is not declared here any more: `CFlags` is 0x28 bytes and Ghidra's own RTTI pass already names the second base's vftable at `CFlags+0x24`, so a `CPersistent` declared at +0xC4 collided with the `CFlags` held here and the two replaced each other on every apply - the period-2 cycle described in ghidra/README.md. The tree itself is this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md)

fields.name: selection_listener
fields.comment: See CMapProvince +0xCC: the screen a selection of the province is told to, set by CMap_SetSelectionListener, zeroed by the constructor. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-provinceview.md)

fields.name: scaled_modifiers
fields.comment: Head of the list of CStaticModifier copies the province rebuild made and scaled (manpower, nationalism, revolt_risk), tail +0x130, count +0x134; nodes {copy, prev, next, byte}. Emptied at the top of the next rebuild. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: near_provinces_begin
fields.comment: Begin of a vector of **every province within two edges**, each once, in the order met - and so the province itself, once it has a neighbour; sea provinces too. Filled by the province's reset at 0x496480 from its template's edges and each neighbour's. CSupplyGroup::PickDepot scores a province over it and SuppressionNearProvince sums over it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md)

fields.name: near_provinces_end
fields.comment: End of the vector at +0x14C; +0x154 is its end of storage. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md)

fields.name: combats
fields.comment: The same field as CMapProvince +0x2EC; project.json carries both structures with the same offsets because Ghidra has no inheritance between them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: naval_base
fields.comment: buildings[naval_base.index]: the province's naval base, cached at rva 0x969D7 out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x20. Never null once the province has been reset - the array holds one CProvinceBuilding per defined building - so readers test its level at +0x20, not the pointer. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-definitions.md)

fields.name: air_base
fields.comment: buildings[air_base.index]: the province's air base, cached at rva 0x9694F out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x1C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-definitions.md)

fields.name: anti_air
fields.comment: buildings[anti_air.index]: the province's anti-air, cached at rva 0x968C7 out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x24. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-definitions.md)

fields.name: underground
fields.comment: buildings[underground.index]: the province's underground, cached at rva 0x96A5F out of g_CBuildingDataBase +0x28. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-definitions.md)

fields.name: revolt_risk
fields.comment: Revolt risk, thousandths, saved as `revolt_risk` and only when positive. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the same in both. (reversing/CLASSES.md)

fields.name: peace_new_owner
fields.comment: Scratch: who the province would go to at a peace - see CMapProvince +0x33C. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: port
fields.comment: the province's map port - the link to the sea province beside it - or null where it has none. Built at map load from the land/sea adjacency, not from buildings.txt; the naval base building is the separate thing at +0x300, and the sea hop tests both. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-definitions.md)

fields.name: regions_first
fields.comment:
Head of the list of regions the province belongs to, nodes with the region at +0 and next at +0x8; count at +0x360. UndeclaredWarCoversProvince (0x4763A0) walks it against an undeclared war's region vector, and the canal tests at 0x4A7EE0/0x4A7F80 compare `count ? *head : 0` against the cached g_mediterranean_region / g_black_sea_region / g_baltic_sea_region pointers - which is also what identifies the member type, since those three are looked up by the names of map/region.txt's first three entries.

**The element class is `CRegion`, named live 2026-10-02.** Reached as `*(*(province + 0x358))`; `classNameForVftable` answers `CRegion` on 8 of 8 provinces tried, so +0x358 is the begin pointer of a `vector<CRegion*>` rather than an inline list. This settles `FINDINGS-opsarea.md`'s open item 1 - `ScoreOpsAreaProvinces` adds +100 per region whose byte at `CRegion +0x6D` is set, and the owning class of that byte was open. `CAreaBorder` had already been eliminated statically and that elimination was right. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md; live 2026-10-02; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-invasion.md)

fields.name: regions_count
fields.comment: How many regions the province is in; the count of the list at +0x358. Tested for zero at 0x4A7F21, 0x4A7F86, 0x4A7FA1 and 0x4A8013 before the head is dereferenced, which is the usual CList shape here. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-invasion.md)

fields.name: intel_by_country_ptr
fields.comment: One byte per country index: how well that country knows the province, **0 to 9**. 9 for whoever holds it and their friends and for a country with a unit on its ground, 2 for a country with a unit in its water, up to 8 from radar; worked out afresh by UpdateIntelFunctor_SerialBody. An air mission picks its targets only where this is 2 or better. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 7. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md)

fields.name: radar_level_applied
fields.comment: The last value of provinceValues[MODIFIER_RADAR_LEVEL] (modifier id 0x30, so +0x180 in the 8-byte-per-entry values array) that RebuildProvinceModifierValues acted on. At 0x4A03EB..0x4A047F it compares the new value against this one and, on a crossing of 1000 (1.0) in either direction, calls 0x4DD250 or 0x4DD370 on the controller country with province->id (+0xD0), then stores the new value here. Nothing else in the image reads it. The name is from the modifier id, which is certain; what 0x4DD250 and 0x4DD370 do was not read. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-revolt.md, section 3)

fields.name: latitude_north
fields.comment: The province's distance north of the equator, normalised to thousandths of half the map height, written once per game entry by ComputeProvinceLatitude (0x963F0) as clamp(template->centre_y - height/2, 0) x 1000 / (height/2). **Zero everywhere south of the equator**, because of the clamp at 0x96412; the abs() at 0x9646D is dead. Two readers: ComputeProvinceClimate (0x9821C, which leaves climate at 3 when it is 250 or less) and CWeather::BaseTemperature (0xB23A1, 0xB23ED, 0xB247E, 0xB24CA, the four latitude thresholds 950/650 on climates 1 and 5). IsNight (0xA73DE) reads it as well, scaling the per-month day-length table at rva 0x130C8B0. Not saved; CProvince::CProvince zeroes it at 0x94B44. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: Max
fields.comment:
read by CProvinceBuilding::GetMax
BiceLib: level_max (int) - maximum level x1000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CProvinceBuilding.hpp:25)

fields.name: Current
fields.comment:
read by CProvinceBuilding::GetCurrent
BiceLib: level_current (int) - current level x1000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CProvinceBuilding.hpp:26)

fields.name: effect
fields.comment: effect (BiceLib/GameClasses/CProvinceBuilding.hpp:23)

fields.name: definition_ptr
fields.comment: building definition (BiceLib/GameClasses/CProvinceBuilding.hpp:24)

fields.name: effect_kind
fields.comment: The modifier kind the building's effect (+0x10) is added at - its +0x24 is the id. With +0x10 it reads like one values entry {value, kind}. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: province_ptr
fields.comment: back to the province (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmode.md:60)

fields.name: changed
fields.comment: Set where a bombing, a fallen-back defender's damage or the day's repair moved the current level, and cleared where it did not. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CHistoryEntry

fields.name: date
fields.comment: When the change happens, in hours on g_CCurrentGameState's tick scale (+0xBDC) - the same scale and the same 43,800,000-hour epoch as CDiplomaticAction::date. The constructor (0x1F4550) initialises it from [0x170C2B8], the engine's null date. It is what CHistoryContainer::AddEntry (0x1F4660) sorts the list by and what ApplyRange (0x1F47C0) compares against its two bounds. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CHistoryEntry

fields.name: province
fields.comment: The province whose history holds the entry; every Apply acts on it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred key. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred keys' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values
fields.comment: First element of the second std::vector<std::string>: the value written beside each deferred key, index for index. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred values' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: value
fields.comment:
**The operand, as a plain integer - not thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CIntTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D1400) as `atoi(text)`, which truncates, so the decimal a mod writes is lost before anything compares it. Zeroed instead when the argument was the keyword `this` (SaveToken 0x377) or `from` (0x34F), which set `CTrigger +0x18`/`+0x19`; only 3 of the 37 leaves read those flags back, so for the other 34 `keyword = this` degenerates to `field >= 0`.

Four leaves multiply this by 1000 inside their own Evaluate because the field they compare it against is thousandths - `revolt_risk`, `pure_revolt_risk`, `nationalism`, `province_temperature` - which is the one place the script number is the natural unit and still cannot carry a fraction. **`CValueTrigger::value` is the same offset with the opposite convention.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: terrain
fields.comment: the province's terrain (BiceLib/GameClasses/CMapProvince.hpp:7)

fields.name: edges_begin
fields.comment: vector of edges to neighbours, begin (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPathFind.hpp:91)

fields.name: edges_end
fields.comment: vector of edges to neighbours, end (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPathFind.hpp:92)

fields.name: base_temperature
fields.comment: The province's base temperature in thousandths of a degree, and the single largest term in CWeather::BaseTemperature. Zeroed by CProvinceTemplate::CProvinceTemplate (0xA92E4) and written in exactly one place, LoadProvinceClimate at 0x8C0DD: (map/climate.bmp byte at the province's position - 100) x 150 + terrain->temperature (CTerrain +0x58). Exactly one reader in the image, 0xB22F6. In BlackICE the bitmap's 84 distinct indices run 26..255, so the bitmap contributes -11.100 to +23.250 C and terrain.txt's temperature another -22.000 to +12.000. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: is_lake
fields.comment: **Set on a province continent.txt lists under the continent `lake`**, by CMap::AssignContinents at 0x48F4A3. MapProvinceIsLandlockedWater (0x4A9B70) answers true at once for a sea province with it set; such a province gets no sea index and a port cannot open onto it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

fields.name: is_crossed
fields.comment: Set to 1 on a province a row of adjacencies.csv names as what a crossing goes through. No reader was looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: is_land
fields.comment: Non-zero on a land province, zero on a sea zone. 245 places in the image read it through a province's `path_node_ptr` (+0xD4), which is why it looked fundamental and unnameable; three of them fix which way round it is. `CPathFind::MayStep` refuses a **naval** step between two provinces that both have it set, and where exactly one has it, that template's `sea_province_id` (+0xA4) must name the other province. `CProvince::IsFrontProvince` (0xA56B0) skips any neighbour that does not have it. `CSafeNavalPathFind::StepCost` only looks for hostile buildings around the destination when the destination does **not** have it - i.e. only when a fleet is entering open sea. `CheckTransportOverload` puts a carried unit ashore only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

fields.name: size_class
fields.comment: **How big the province counts as, 1 to 4**: set by CMap::ComputeProvinceGeometry at 0x49183E..0x491860 from bbox_width + bbox_height - under 30 pixels 1, under 60 2, under 90 3, else 4. CSupply::SpreadFromDepot multiplies it by 1, 2 or 3 for the province's infrastructure to get the step it adds to supply_depot_distance, and CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure uses it as its step. Not a distance: an edge carries its own at +0xC. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplynetwork.md)

fields.name: source_object
fields.comment: Whatever CMap +0x2198 held for this province id, stored by the constructor at 0xA92E7; the id itself goes to +0x7C at 0xA933B. Named from the constructor only - what the object is was not established. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: centre_x
fields.comment: The province's bounding-box centre x in map pixels, written at 0x917FB as bbox_x (+0x80) + bbox_width (+0x88)/2. This is the pair MapDistance (0x92030) uses, wrapping dx by the map width at CMap +0x2A74. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: centre_y
fields.comment: The province's bounding-box centre y in map pixels, written at 0x91815 as bbox_y (+0x84) + bbox_height (+0x8C)/2. y grows northward: province 1, Porsangerhalvoya at 71 N, sits at y 2106 of a 2160-pixel map. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: text_position_vftable
fields.comment: A **CMapPoint held by value** occupies +0x34..+0x43, and this is its vftable word (VA 0x15BC65C, written at rva 0xA930A); `text_position_token` at +0x38 is CPersistent's token, and the object's own `x` and `y` are the already-named `text_position_x`/`text_position_y` at +0x3C/+0x40. Recorded because the two words before those floats otherwise read as a hole, and because these two embedded points plus the 60-element vector at +0x258 are the whole of the 879,780 live CMapPoints in a running game: 14,190 templates x (60 + 2). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md)

fields.name: text_position_token
fields.comment: CPersistent's `token` word of the CMapPoint embedded at +0x34, set to `none` (0x18D) at rva 0xA9302 like all 714 inlined CPersistent constructors. Nothing reads it; see BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp on why every instance in the image carries the same value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md)

fields.name: text_position_x
fields.comment: positions.txt's `text_position` x, as a float, written at 0x48FE70. Paris reads 2786.300048828125 against the file's x=2786.300049. On a sea zone the same handler also truncates this pair into +0x64/+0x68; on a land province it does not. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: text_position_y
fields.comment: The y beside +0x3C, written at 0x48FE75. Paris reads 1657.5 against the file's y=1657.500000. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: city_vftable
fields.comment: The second **CMapPoint held by value**, occupying +0x44..+0x53: vftable word here (written at rva 0xA931A), token at +0x48, and its `x`/`y` are the already-named `city_x`/`city_y` at +0x4C/+0x50. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md)

fields.name: city_token
fields.comment: CPersistent's `token` word of the CMapPoint embedded at +0x44, set to `none` (0x18D) at rva 0xA9317. Nothing reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md)

fields.name: city_x
fields.comment: positions.txt's `city` x, as a float, written at 0x490070 (save token 0x2A2). Where the province declares no `city` it holds the bounding-box centre as a float: Paris, which has no `city` key, reads 2786.0 against its centre_x of 2786. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: city_y
fields.comment: The y beside +0x4C, written at 0x49007B. Province 14000 reads 1214.0 / 984.0 for the pair, which is its bounding-box centre, not its `unit` position - so this pair keeps the centre where +0x64/+0x68 has moved. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: label_x
fields.comment: A second copy of the centre, x half, initialised at 0x91822 from +0x2C in the same pass. The code after it in 0x917A0 goes on to refine this pair, so treat it as the province's display/representative point rather than a plain duplicate; whatever it ends up as, it stays a map pixel coordinate. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: label_y
fields.comment: The y half of the pair at +0x5C, initialised at 0x91827 from +0x30. **This is the y ComputeProvinceLatitude (0x963F0) reads** to build CProvince +0x388, so it is what decides a province's season. Only reader in the map/weather code is 0x96407. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: position_x
fields.comment: A map-pixel x written by the map loader at 0x8FEC4 and 0x900A0. Read by IsNight (0xA7399) as the longitude that offsets local time, and by LoadProvinceClimate (0x8BF79) as the x at which climate.bmp is sampled. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: position_y
fields.comment: The y beside +0x64, written at 0x8FEBB and 0x9009D. Compared against half the map height at 0x8FED2 to set the hemisphere byte at +0xA2, and used by LoadProvinceClimate (0x8BF72) as the row at which climate.bmp is sampled. y grows northward, so the comparison at 0x8FED2 is true in the **northern** hemisphere. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: pixels_begin
fields.comment: Begin of the province's own pixels, pairs of x and y, ending at +0x70. CMap::BuildAdjacencyFromRaster walks it to find the province's neighbours, which is what orders its edges; the order agreeing with adjacencies.bin for every province shows it runs from the south row by row, west to east. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: pixels_end
fields.comment: One past the last of the province's pixels (see +0x6C). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: province_id
fields.comment: The province id, passed to CProvinceTemplate::CProvinceTemplate in EDX and stored at 0xA933B. The templates live one per id in CMap +0x2A60, 0x27C bytes each, allocated at 0x8A153. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: bbox_x
fields.comment: Left edge of the province's pixel bounding box; 0x917F2 adds half of +0x88 to it to make centre_x at +0x2C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: bbox_y
fields.comment: Bottom edge of the province's pixel bounding box; 0x91809 adds half of +0x8C to it to make centre_y at +0x30. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: bbox_width
fields.comment: Width of the province's pixel bounding box, halved into centre_x at 0x917E7. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: bbox_height
fields.comment: Height of the province's pixel bounding box, halved into centre_y at 0x917FE. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-temperature.md)

fields.name: coastal
fields.comment: Set to 1 at 0x48AD67 on a LAND province that has at least one neighbour of the other kind - the branch at 0x48AD4E compares the two templates' is_land (+0x22) and 0x48AD58 picks the field by this province's own. Checked live against the edge lists: +0xA0 is non-zero on exactly the land provinces that have a sea neighbour, 10642 of 10642. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: touches_land
fields.comment: The sea-side counterpart of +0xA0, set to 1 at 0x48AD5E on a SEA province that has a land neighbour. Checked live: non-zero on exactly the sea provinces with a land neighbour, 3547 of 3547. The pair is written in one pass of CMap::LoadMapFiles over every province's edges, so it is available from the end of the map build onward. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapbuild.md)

fields.name: northern_hemisphere
fields.comment: Set where the province's unit point y (+0x68) is at or past half the map height (CMap +0x2A78): **the northern hemisphere**, since y grows northward (province 1, at 71 N, has y 2106 of 2160; Murmansk, Reykjavik and Paris have it set, Cape Town, Hobart and Ushuaia clear - FINDINGS-mapbuild.md section 7). Written with the unit point by CMap::ComputeProvinceGeometry (0x4918DF, a setge), and again where positions.txt moves it (0x48FED8 for a sea zone's text_position, 0x4900B6 for unit). Two consumers: ComputeProvinceClimate (0xA81A0), set: bands A..F = 1 2 3 4 4 5, clear: 4 4 5 1 2 3; and CWeatherManager::CreateFront (0xB5EF4), which negates a new front's rotation where it is set. IsNight shifts the month by six where it is clear. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: sea_province_id
fields.comment:
On a land province (`is_land` set), the id of the one sea province it connects to, as an index into `CMap::provinces` (`+0x2200`); 0 where there is none. Meaningless where `is_land` is clear, and nothing reads it there.

It is the single gate on a fleet crossing the coast. `CPathFind::MayStep` (0x1A2700) and `CPlannedPathFind::MayStep` (0x1A2D30) let a naval unit step out of a land province only to the province this names, and into a land province only from it; a step between two land provinces is refused outright. The helper at `0xA7D70` uses it the other way, replacing a land province by `map->provinces[sea_province_id]` until both ends of a pair are sea, which is also what fixes the target as a sea province: the loop terminates only when the province it lands on has `is_land` clear. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-redeploy.md)

fields.name: sea_index
fields.comment: **The province's number in the table of distances by sea, or -1.** Given by CMap::LoadBuildingPositions to a land province whose naval_base position lies on a pixel of a sea province that is not landlocked water - in the order positions.txt names them - and by the end of CMap::LoadPositionsFile to every sea province that is not landlocked water and has none yet, in the order of the ids. The count is CMap +0x2A6C. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

fields.name: name
fields.comment: The province's name, what CProvince::GetName answers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-provincetooltip.md, section 3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-provincetooltip.md)

fields.name: stack_points
fields.comment: five points of three floats, one per stack: where each of the province's stacks stands, **as an offset from the province's label point** (+0x5C/+0x60) - CUnit::MakeArrow adds the label point to one to start its arrow there. **Point 0 (+0xCC) is for a land or sea unit with no path, point 1 (+0xD8) for one with a path, point 4 (+0xFC) for an air unit**; 2 and 3 are the two sides of a battle. CUnit::EnterProvince, CUnit::ShowMoving, CUnit::AdvanceMovement and CUnit::CancelMovement all pick that way. No writer was found. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10. **What writes them is CProvinceTemplate::SetStackPoints (0x4AB310)**: the standing point is the unit point, the stack on the move 2.5 east and 1.0 along y of it, the aircraft on the standing point, and the two battle points on it on land and 2.4 either way along both axes at sea. fields.name: building_positions_begin
fields.comment:
`std::vector<CMapPoint>` _Myfirst - **one 16-byte CMapPoint per building type**, indexed by `CBuilding +0x54`, holding positions.txt's `building_position` block. The constructor reserves and fills exactly `([g_CBuildingDataBase+0x10] - [g_CBuildingDataBase+0xC]) >> 2` elements, which is the number of building types the database holds (59 from the mod's common/buildings.txt plus the built-in `nobuilding` the loader registers at rva 0xB7696, so 60 here). It is a **flat vector, not a list**: the element stride is 0x10 at every one of its six access sites, there is no per-element node, and the exact reserve means no capacity slack. 14,190 templates x 60 elements = 851,400 of the 879,780 live CMapPoints; the other 28,380 are the two embedded at +0x34 and +0x44.

Written by CMap::LoadBuildingPositions (rva 0x90390). Read by CProvinceTemplate::GetNavalBasePosition (rva 0xA9D70, 8 callers), CProvinceTemplate::GetAirBasePosition (rva 0xA9DF0, 1 caller), the land/sea neighbour distance pass at rva 0xA9E70, the building-graphics placement at rva 0x23FB06, rva 0x242230, and three bodies in the rva 0x29Exxx-0x29Fxxx range that also write the nudge float. Freed only in CProvinceTemplate::~CProvinceTemplate (rva 0xA9838). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md)

fields.comment: `std::vector<CMapPoint>` _Mylast for the array at +0x258. The inlined push_back in the constructor advances it by 0x10 (rva 0xA9618); `(+0x25C - +0x258) >> 4` is the element count, taken that way at rva 0x919FC and rva 0xAAA03. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mappoint.md)

fields.name: building_positions_capacity
fields.comment: `std::vector<CMapPoint>` _Myend for the array at +0x258. Because the constructor reserves exactly the building-type count and then pushes exactly that many, it ends equal to +0x25C and the vector never grows: the push_back's `cmp eax, [edi+0x260]` grow arm (rva 0xA9596 / 0xA95DC, calling rva 0xACC40) is taken only on the last push, and CMap::ComputeProvinceGeometry's resize finds the length already correct. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: candidates

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_end

fields.name: deferred_values

fields.name: deferred_values_last

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: value
fields.comment: **The operand, in thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CValueTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D13E0) as `TokenToFixedPoint(text)`, so `war_exhaustion = 7.5` is stored as 7500 - the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `national_unity=81.752`). A leaf's own Evaluate then either compares it straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3 says which does which. **This is the opposite convention from `CIntTrigger::value` at the same offset**, and nothing in the script files distinguishes them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CValueTrigger

CreateRebelsForFaction takes the owner from here when it is not raising for an actor or converting to a government in exile, and passes this pair as both country pairs of the REVOLT message. Tag here, id at +0x50. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: armies_no_unlink

Tested by RunDailyRebelFactionPass (0x4BA13F) and RebelFaction_GrantIndependence (0x4BE6EE); zeroed by the constructor. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: wants_removal
fields.comment: **Asks RunDailyPass to delete the faction.** Set by RunDailyRebelFactionPass on three tests - its country owns nothing and the type's area is `nation`; its independence country owns something; it has no armies and no provinces - and by RebelFaction_GrantIndependence once the provinces are released. RunDailyPass tests it at 0x682E7D and, unless CCurrentGameState +0xC88 is set, unlinks the faction from +0xC7C/+0xC80, frees it and decrements +0xC84. Not saved. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: provinces_count
fields.comment: How many provinces the faction holds - the count of the list at +0x94/+0x98. RebelFaction_TakeProvince increments it; RunDailyRebelFactionPass decrements it on a removal and **ends the faction when it and the armies' count (+0x88) are both zero**. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: provinces_no_unlink

fields.name: key
fields.comment: the rebel type's key. **Read live**: six in this mod - disgruntled_rabble, fascist_rebels, nationalist_rebels, organized_partisans, partisans, patriot_rebels (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRebelFaction.hpp:92)

fields.name: spawn_chance
fields.comment: `spawn_chance`, an embedded CMeanTimeToHappen (0x1C bytes, vftable 0x15F5CB8) that the constructor builds in place at 0x4BEF6B and CRebelType::LoadKey fills through its slot 3 at 0x4BFCA8. **It is read**, at 0x4C0670 - `lea eax, [esi+0x28]; call 0x9C4B90` - by ChooseRebelTypeForProvince (0x4C0430) through CMeanTimeToHappen::GetDays. This comment previously said nothing was found that reads it; what the earlier scan missed is that the workhorse evaluator is GetDays (13 call sites) and not GetChance (one caller, the daily event pass). **The rebel type whose spawn_chance evaluates largest is the one that spawns**, which is what the mod's own comment in common/rebel_types.txt says. Because the accumulator is multiplicative and the comparison starts at 0 with a strict `>`, a modifier with factor 0.0 whose condition holds vetoes the type outright. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-revolt.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: movement_evaluation
fields.comment: the `movement_evaluation` factor block (token 0x63F), an embedded CMeanTimeToHappen. **Read by RebelFaction_ChooseMoveTarget (rva 0xB99D0)** through CMeanTimeToHappen::GetDays, once per candidate province, in a scope with no country, the candidate as its province and one Random() draw as its seed; a candidate that is not a neighbour of the unit's province has its value halved. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: siege_won_trigger

(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

Its text (slot 8, RebelType_GetSiegeEffectText) is the EFFECT of the REVOLTSIEGE message. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

The daily faction pass treats 0 as the value that lets a faction die when its country holds nothing. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-occupation.md)

fields.name: is_triggered_only
fields.comment: The `is_triggered_only` key of rebel_types.txt (token 0x61D), which fieldmap.py could not place. Read out of the loader: CRebelType::LoadKey's jump table (0x4BFD9C, byte index table 0x4BFDD8, base `eax - 0x61D` at 0x4BFB72) sends token 0x61D to 0x4BFD7A, which is `add edi, 0x19C; push edi; call 0xA7B410` - the same bool parser the other byte keys use. Its only runtime reader is ChooseRebelTypeForProvince at 0x4C063B, which skips such a type unless its caller asked for triggered-only types; the only caller that does is SpawnPartisansFromUnderground (0x50B920). So a triggered-only rebel type can be drawn by an underground mobilisation and by nothing else. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-revolt.md, section 2)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the save's `id` pair, written after the id. **Read live**: 41 on what a scenario started with, 4713 on what the game has built since (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:31), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the regiment's id, the first half of the save's `id` pair (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:32), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: strength_ceiling
fields.comment: set to the regiment's strength when it is built and afterwards only raised to it, never lowered; CUnit slot 24 totals it. Not what the regiment has left - that is +0x5C. saved as `highest` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:55), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: builder
fields.comment: who built it, saved as `builder`, and only where the id half of the tag is set (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:59), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: sub_unit_definition_ptr
fields.comment: this regiment's definition, with its country's tech applied. saved as `type`, by writing the definition's own name (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:64), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: strength
fields.comment: what the regiment has left, in the scale of its definition's max_strength; the supply consumption scales by it, CUnit slot 21 averages it. saved as `strength` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:44), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: organisation
fields.comment: organisation x1000, saved as `organisation` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:62), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: home
fields.comment: where it was raised; the save writes that province's id under `home`, and the loader turns the id back into this pointer. **Read live**: a CMapProvince by its own RTTI, and null on a regiment that was never given one (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:68), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: technologies
fields.comment: **the technology levels this regiment was raised with**, one node per entry of its definition's `technologies`, built by CSubUnit::SetType. The save writes a line per node keyed by the technology's own name - `infantry_activation={5 0.000}` - and the loader looks the key up in the technology database, which is what says these are technologies. **Read live**: every node's first word is a CTechnology; none on a CWing, 9 to 52 on a regiment (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:85), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: sunk_by_type
fields.comment: type half of the `sunk_by` object id (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:92), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: sunk_by_id
fields.comment: what sank this ship, saved as `sunk_by`, and only where the pair is not the game's "no object" one. **Read live**: set on 1123 of 3736 ships (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:93), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: is_reserve
fields.comment: saved as `is_reserve`; CRegiment::GetMaxStrength scales the definition's max_strength by RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE where it is set. **Read live**: 1184 of 4000 regiments (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:98), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: pride
fields.comment: the pride of the fleet, saved as `pride`. **Read live**: 31 of 3736 ships (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:102), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: unit_ptr
fields.comment: the CUnit this regiment belongs to; how the per regiment supply and fuel functions reach the unit's order. **Read live**: a CArmy on every regiment (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:108), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: current_distance
fields.comment: how far the regiment is from the enemy in its battle, x1000, saved as `current_distance` - and only where the unit's `combats` list has something in it. **Read live**: zero on all 4000 regiments (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:116), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: extra_consumption
fields.comment: every point is another 1% of supply and fuel: the consumption functions add it x10 to a potency whose base is 1000. A cached total - the levels in `technologies` added up, which CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies recomputes. **Read live**: it is that sum on all 10254 sub units in a running game (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:130), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: historical_model
fields.comment: which historical model it was raised as, saved as `historical_model`; -1 where it is none. **Read live**: -1 on 3940 of 4000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:134), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: experience
fields.comment: The regiment's experience, in thousandths, capped at 0x186A0 (100000 == 100%). GrantCombatExperience (0x1C4200) adds EXP_GAIN_DIV's share to it at 0x1C4671 and clamps at 0x1C467E. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaders.md)

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment:
**The combat modifiers acting on this one ship, wing or brigade** - first here, last at +0x44, count at +0x48, each node holding a 12-byte {id, attack, defence} record exactly like CUnit+0xDC's. Appended to by CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1AC300) from the naval, air, bomber and target slot 19s - 48 call sites - and freed, with all three fields zeroed, by CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590) at the top of every tick. **This, not CUnit+0xDC, is where air and naval combat modifiers live**, which is why a live watch on a ship's parent CUnit never saw the list fill. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit
+0x4 inside it: combat_modifiers_last (LinkedListNode*) - The last node of the CList at +0x40. Written on every push; the head at +0x40 is written only when the count was zero. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit
+0x8 inside it: combat_modifiers_count (int) - How many modifiers are on the list at +0x40. The field to watch for a push, for the same reason as CUnit+0xE4. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every combat modifier's attack side on this ship, wing or brigade**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier multiplies in `max(attack + 1000, 10)` as a 64-bit product divided by 1000; CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers seeds it back to 1000 each tick. **It multiplies the shot count**: CNavalCombatant::Attack computes `shots = sea_attack (or convoy_attack / sub_attack) * this / 1000` at 0x167B3A, the exact counterpart of CUnit+0xEC x +0xF4 on land. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment:
The defence-side counterpart of +0x50, written by the same adder and reset to 1000 by the same slot 19. **Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else**, in CCombatant slot 11's per-sub-unit loop, where it is multiplied by +0x50 and divided by 1000. That read sits past a `ret 4` at 0x566452 and is reached only by `je 0x566455` from inside the loop, which is why it was recorded here as having **no reader** until 2026-10-01 (trap 3). The branch is taken when the sub-unit's slot 9 answers false; the true arm uses the division's CUnit +0xEC/+0xF0/+0xF4/+0xF8 instead, so on a ship or wing the two products are used together.

**What it feeds, corrected 2026-10-01 (second correction, see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat3.md §3).** This entry twice said the product is a 'loss factor' that carries naval, air and bombing modifiers 'into losses'. It does not. That wording was inherited from a wrong owner: the block was first attributed to CCombatant::ApplyLosses (trap 2 - ApplyLosses ends at 0x5662ED and slot 11 begins at 0x5662F0 with no padding), and when the owner was corrected the meaning was not re-asked. **Slot 11 sums strength.** Its only two invocations in the image are 0x57B083 and 0x57B091 inside CCombat slot 17 (0x17B050), which returns the attacker's share of the two sides' total strength in thousandths; that number's only consumer is 0x17BD70, the `combat_status` window's per-tick refresh, called once from the end of CCombat::Tick and only for a combat the player's own country is in, where it picks an icon state at the 66.0%/33.0% thresholds and formats a percentage.

**So the two sides are not symmetrical.** +0x50 multiplies the shot count in CNavalCombatant::Attack and therefore changes the simulation; +0x54's single reader changes a number on screen. On this reading a defence-side naval, air or bombing combat modifier - including the two defence-only ids - is **cosmetic in this build**. The bound: 'slot 11 has exactly two invocations' is confirmed of the entry-set decode, and 6.7% of non-padding .text lies outside that decode, so it is `likely` as a statement about the whole image. One battle in a running game settles it - see FINDINGS-combat3.md's live checks.

**And the one reader only runs for the player's own battles** (2026-10-02): CCombat::Tick gates the combat_status refresh on CountryIdListContains over the attacker's or defender's CCombatant::countries with the player's id from gameState +0xC34. So in an AI-vs-AI combat this field is never read at all. Player-only, not merely display-only.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02.** A hook on the one reader (CCombatant slot 11) in a 1942 war save recorded 39,414 calls with **zero unexplained return addresses**: 39,222 via CLandCombatant's own forwarder and 96 + 96 from CCombat slot 17's two legs. So nothing outside slot 17 reaches this field in practice, the vcall-thunk route the static sweep could not close never fired, and the demotion stands: for naval, air and bombing the defence side of the combat modifier census is cosmetic in this build. Land is unaffected - CUnit +0xF0 has the AI reader.

**"Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else" is wrong, and the conclusion survives (2026-10-05, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md).** There is a second static reader, at 0x160E5B in CBomberCombatant::FireUnit, where this field multiplies the bombing target's `air_defence`; the register is a CSubUnit on independent evidence, being read at +0x58, +0x5C and +0xA8 in the same loop. The 2026-10-02 live check does not contradict it - it hooked CCombatant slot 11's callers, not this field. The demotion stands for a better reason than the old one: **that second reader's result is itself discarded**, so the defence-side product still reaches nothing but a number on screen. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
**The regiment's own name, always present, and the only thing `remove_brigade` can ever match.** Saved as `name` inside a `regiment={}` block, and the loader puts it back. Across the 45-save corpus there are **788,880 regiment blocks and 788,880 of them carry a `name=`, none of it empty**, so an 'unnamed regiment' does not exist at runtime: 290,876 of those instances (7,133 distinct strings) hold an engine-generated name of the shape `<ordinal> <abbrev> Regiment` - `1st HQ Regiment`, `2nd Art Regiment`, `1st Wagon Regiment` - and the rest hold the historical name the order of battle gave them. A wing is a CSubUnit too and carries its name here in the same way.

**So `remove_brigade = <a subunit type>` can never match**, and nothing in the mod tries: of 6,132 distinct `remove_brigade` values none is one of the 1,427 subunit type tokens the mod's `units/*.txt` declare. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: A CCountryTag on the sub unit itself - the three-character tag here, the id at +0x98 - distinct from `builder` at +0x34. CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers resolves a country out of it for the wing's BM_RADAR_STATION technology scaling (0x16D0A6/0x16D0B0) and passes it to CWeather::AirCombatEffect for BM_WEATHER (0x16D109/0x16D100), in both cases in preference to the parent unit's owner. **Read out of the code only**; whether it is the owner or the controller was not established. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: pending_strength_damage
fields.comment: **Strength damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths. CUnit::TakeDamage adds to it per landed shot, CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight reads it to tell whether the unit is already finished, and CSubUnit::SettleDamage subtracts it from `strength` and clears it. **Not clamped** - unlike the organisation half. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: pending_organisation_damage
fields.comment:
**Organisation damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths, spread evenly over the subunits by CUnit::TakeDamage rather than by size.

**It is damage attempted, not damage dealt.** CSubUnit::SettleDamage clamps it to the organisation the subunit actually has (`cmovg` at 0x1ABAE1) before subtracting, so in a one-sided fight most of a tick's total is thrown away. Anything reporting organisation damage has to count the clamped amount at 0x1ABAE7, not this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: target_id_type
fields.comment: The type half of the persistent id of the ship this one last shot at; with +0xBC, the remembered target CSubUnit::PickTarget keeps from hour to hour. Cleared by CCombatant::AddUnit and for a ship that cannot shoot. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: target_id
fields.comment: The id half of the remembered target at +0xB8. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: has_target
fields.comment: Set when CSubUnit::PickTarget found a target this hour and cleared when it did not. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: contributes_to_unit
fields.comment: **A cached `strength >= 0.100 && organisation >= 1.000`**, recomputed by `CUnit::UpdateHourly` (written at 0x1BA2C6) for the zero-combat-width brigades of a land unit only, and left alone on everything else. When it flips, the unit's definition is rebuilt. `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` does not read it - it recomputes the same predicate from +0x5C and +0x60 - and 0x1CD500 asks whether any brigade of a unit satisfies it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: Key
fields.comment: read by CRegion::GetKey

fields.name: useForPeace
fields.comment: read by CRegion::UseForPeace

fields.name: provinces_begin
fields.comment: The begin of the region's vector of province ids. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md)

fields.name: provinces_end
fields.comment: The end of that vector. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airorders.md)

fields.name: ai_front_relevant
fields.comment:
The byte `CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces` tests to add **+100** to an ops-area province's priority, once per region of that province whose byte is set (0x4BD78F region of the body). **The name is a guess from that single reader and is marked `inferred` accordingly** - what sets it is not established. Read live 2026-10-02 as **0 on all 400+ regions** at the scenario start with the game paused at tick 0, so the +100 never fires there; whether that is because the AI has not started (no CAIUnit has a unit pointer at tick 0) or because the byte is set by war is the open question, and running the game on would answer it.

**It does get set - live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save.** Read 1 on **30 of 2,000+** live regions in a May 1942 war save, against **0 of 400** at the scenario start. So ScoreOpsAreaProvinces's +100-per-region really does fire, and the byte is something a war turns on. That is support for the `inferred` name rather than proof of it: what *sets* it is still unread. (Note the region count: an earlier reading of '400 regions' was the scan limit, not the population.) (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-opsarea.md; live 2026-10-02)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect, inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: limit
fields.comment: The `limit` block, an embedded AND trigger (0x40 bytes); every `limit` key appends to it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md), inherited from CMultipleTargetEffect

fields.name: region
fields.comment: The region the key named. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred key. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred keys' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values
fields.comment: First element of the second std::vector<std::string>: the value written beside each deferred key, index for index. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred values' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: region
fields.comment: Null for an unknown name. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent

fields.name: first
fields.comment: **The first party to the agreement** (save key `first`). Resolved from the three letters in the save through CCountryDataBase::GetTag, so the tag characters land at +0x8 and the index at +0xC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: second
fields.comment: **The second party to the agreement** (save key `second`). The same resolution as `first`, into the tag at +0x10 and the index at +0x14. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement began**, as a tick (save key `start_date`). Parsed from `year.month.day.hour` text by Date_SetFromString, which is the same representation every other date in the simulation uses. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement ends**, as a tick (save key `end_date`); **the null date 43,800,000 (`[0x170C2B8]`) where it has none** - every constructor sets it so, not zero. A real date is told by `(end_date - 43,800,000) / 24 / 365.0 > 1`. Read only by CCasusBelli (Activate, which will not attach an expired one, and IsOver) and by CRelation::SaveContents (written only when real). **No other relation's IsOver reads it**: a guarantee ends twenty years after `start_date`, a NAP NAP_EXPIRY_MONTHS after it, and the history files' end dates take effect only while history is replayed before play. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.name: cancel
fields.comment: **Whether the agreement is cancelled** (save key `cancel`), the last of CRelation's own bytes - a subclass's data starts at +0x24. Loaded as a plain comparison against the token `yes`, so any other value, including `no`, leaves it 0. **CDiplomacy::SaveContents skips every relation with it set**, and CRelation::SaveContents, given one, writes `cancel = yes` instead of `start_date`. No writer in play was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. fields.name: Type
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetType, inherited from CDiplomaticAction
BiceLib: type (int) - The action's `CDiplomaticAction::EType`, and the **stage** an offer is at rather than what kind of offer it is: the kind is the C++ subclass, and its name is slot 15's save token. `CDiplomaticAction::GetType` is registered to Lua and resolves to a two-instruction `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret` at 0x416000. The enum has **three** values, all registered in one luabind chain ending at 0x8ED397: ('PROPOSE', ebx) at 0x8ED38D with ebx zeroed at 0x8EAE68 and never rewritten, ('DECLINE', 1) at 0x8ED37F, and **('ACCEPT', 2) at 0x8ED3BB**, appended to the same value vector at 0x8ED3C9 and registered by the loop at 0x8ED3CE. So 0 = PROPOSE, 1 = DECLINE, 2 = ACCEPT. What acts on it: CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute enqueues a PROPOSE on the recipient and anything else on the actor; the hourly AI pass at 0x682BA8 only touches entries still at PROPOSE and writes 2 into the field at 0x682BB3 to accept them. The body at 0x416000 has two references and so is **not** recorded under a class name (trap 4); the field is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: Value
fields.comment:
read by CDiplomaticAction::GetValue, inherited from CDiplomaticAction
BiceLib: value (unsigned char) - A bool, exposed to Lua as GetValue/SetValue: CDiplomaticAction::SetValue (0xA0E980, one reference, no vftable) is `this->+0x24 = [ebp+8]` and the getter is the folded `mov al,[ecx+0x24]` at 0xA0E990. **CTradeAction::IsValid (slot 13, 0xA38770) branches on it at 0xA387DA**: set, and it validates a fresh trade offer; clear, and it instead requires that an identical route already exist on the pair. So `value` is the proposal/cancellation polarity a script controls. **Units: none - it is a bool, not thousandths.** In the save it is written `value=yes` / `value=no`, 39 yes and 6 no over the 45 saves on this machine, which is also how the `value` loader case reads it: ParseBool (rva 0x67B410) at 0xA0E6E6, not a number. Seven of the family also use it as their slot-18 answer, through the folded `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x24], 0; setne al; ret` at 0xA0FE10 and the recorded ReturnByteAt24 at 0xA0E990. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction
