fields.name: persistent_id
fields.comment: Always 0x18D. Written by CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor (0xA0EB30), by each of the eleven Lua `Create` factories (e.g. 0x8E84A9) and copied by every slot-16 clone, so every action in the family carries it. **It is not a per-class discriminator**: CCommand +0x4 is recorded as "a class id" and holds the same 0x18D, and the kind of action is carried by slot 15's save token instead. What reads it was not traced; token 0x18D resolves to `none`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: actor
fields.comment: The country making the offer, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the four-character tag at +0x8 and the country id at +0xC. Loaded from the save key `actor` (token 0x2E9) at 0xA0E7B5/0xA0E7BB, where CCountryDataBase::GetTag's result is copied as two dwords. CNullDiplomaticAction's constructor fills it with "---" and id 0. Every reader that wants the CCountry indexes `g_CCountryDataBase::countries_first` with +0xC: CTradeAction::IsValid, CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute and the base's slot 14 all do. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: recipient
fields.comment: The country being offered to, an 8-byte CCountryTag with the tag at +0x10 and the id at +0x14. Loaded from the save key `recipient` (token 0x2EA) at 0xA0E86A/0xA0E874. The base's slot 14, `IsSelectable` (0xA0EAE0), is three instructions: `return actor_id != recipient_id` - so the family's default selectability test is just "these are two different countries". (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: date
fields.comment: When the offer was made, in **hours** on the same scale as g_CCurrentGameState's tick (+0xBDC), counted from the 43,800,000-hour epoch. Loaded from the save key `date` (token 0x1F8) through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E70A, written by every Lua `Create` factory from the current tick, and set to the epoch itself - the engine's null date, [0x170C2B8] - by the null action's constructor. CDiplomaticActionCommand::Execute's only use of it is `date + 0xA8`, seven days, handed to CDiplomacyStatus::SetNextOfferAllowed. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: last_command_date
fields.comment: When the action was last put on the wire, in hours on the tick scale - the save's own key name (token 0x3EC), loaded through Date_SetFromString at 0xA0E806. **Two independent writers, both setting it to the current tick**: CDiplomaticAction::MakeCommand stamps it just before wrapping the action in a command (0xA0E92D) and CCountry::AddPendingDiplomaticAction stamps it again as the action is enqueued (0x4E62EB). That is what makes it later than `date` for an offer that has travelled: in the save corpus it differs from `date` in 34 of 56 blocks and is never earlier. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CDiplomaticAction

fields.name: unit

**The brigade being lent or reclaimed, held as a 0x28-byte by-value `CRef<CUnit>` spanning +0x2C to +0x53** - cached pointer at +0x2C, persistent type at +0x30, persistent id at +0x34, name at +0x38. Not a pointer at +0x2C, which is what the two-instruction look of GetClaimType next door invites.

**Three writers, and none of them is reachable from script**: LoadKey's `unit` case (token 0x256, 0x63B317), the copy constructor at 0x6394E0, and the two-tag constructor at 0x639260 - which zeroes it, taking +0x30 and +0x34 from the shared null-CRef statics [0x1A8CC94]/[0x1A8CC98] that nothing in `.text` ever writes. Lua registers GetUnit and no setter. The consequence is decided by slot 13: IsValid (0x63AD90) resolves this ref and returns false when it misses, so a script-built action is dropped before Apply runs. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md)

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment:
**The combat modifiers acting on this one ship, wing or brigade** - first here, last at +0x44, count at +0x48, each node holding a 12-byte {id, attack, defence} record exactly like CUnit+0xDC's. Appended to by CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1AC300) from the naval, air, bomber and target slot 19s - 48 call sites - and freed, with all three fields zeroed, by CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590) at the top of every tick. **This, not CUnit+0xDC, is where air and naval combat modifiers live**, which is why a live watch on a ship's parent CUnit never saw the list fill. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit
+0x4 inside it: combat_modifiers_last (LinkedListNode*) - The last node of the CList at +0x40. Written on every push; the head at +0x40 is written only when the count was zero. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit
+0x8 inside it: combat_modifiers_count (int) - How many modifiers are on the list at +0x40. The field to watch for a push, for the same reason as CUnit+0xE4. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every combat modifier's attack side on this ship, wing or brigade**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier multiplies in `max(attack + 1000, 10)` as a 64-bit product divided by 1000; CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers seeds it back to 1000 each tick. **It multiplies the shot count**: CNavalCombatant::Attack computes `shots = sea_attack (or convoy_attack / sub_attack) * this / 1000` at 0x167B3A, the exact counterpart of CUnit+0xEC x +0xF4 on land. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment:
The defence-side counterpart of +0x50, written by the same adder and reset to 1000 by the same slot 19. **Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else**, in CCombatant slot 11's per-sub-unit loop, where it is multiplied by +0x50 and divided by 1000. That read sits past a `ret 4` at 0x566452 and is reached only by `je 0x566455` from inside the loop, which is why it was recorded here as having **no reader** until 2026-10-01 (trap 3). The branch is taken when the sub-unit's slot 9 answers false; the true arm uses the division's CUnit +0xEC/+0xF0/+0xF4/+0xF8 instead, so on a ship or wing the two products are used together.

**What it feeds, corrected 2026-10-01 (second correction, see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat3.md §3).** This entry twice said the product is a 'loss factor' that carries naval, air and bombing modifiers 'into losses'. It does not. That wording was inherited from a wrong owner: the block was first attributed to CCombatant::ApplyLosses (trap 2 - ApplyLosses ends at 0x5662ED and slot 11 begins at 0x5662F0 with no padding), and when the owner was corrected the meaning was not re-asked. **Slot 11 sums strength.** Its only two invocations in the image are 0x57B083 and 0x57B091 inside CCombat slot 17 (0x17B050), which returns the attacker's share of the two sides' total strength in thousandths; that number's only consumer is 0x17BD70, the `combat_status` window's per-tick refresh, called once from the end of CCombat::Tick and only for a combat the player's own country is in, where it picks an icon state at the 66.0%/33.0% thresholds and formats a percentage.

**So the two sides are not symmetrical.** +0x50 multiplies the shot count in CNavalCombatant::Attack and therefore changes the simulation; +0x54's single reader changes a number on screen. On this reading a defence-side naval, air or bombing combat modifier - including the two defence-only ids - is **cosmetic in this build**. The bound: 'slot 11 has exactly two invocations' is confirmed of the entry-set decode, and 6.7% of non-padding .text lies outside that decode, so it is `likely` as a statement about the whole image. One battle in a running game settles it - see FINDINGS-combat3.md's live checks.

**And the one reader only runs for the player's own battles** (2026-10-02): CCombat::Tick gates the combat_status refresh on CountryIdListContains over the attacker's or defender's CCombatant::countries with the player's id from gameState +0xC34. So in an AI-vs-AI combat this field is never read at all. Player-only, not merely display-only.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02.** A hook on the one reader (CCombatant slot 11) in a 1942 war save recorded 39,414 calls with **zero unexplained return addresses**: 39,222 via CLandCombatant's own forwarder and 96 + 96 from CCombat slot 17's two legs. So nothing outside slot 17 reaches this field in practice, the vcall-thunk route the static sweep could not close never fired, and the demotion stands: for naval, air and bombing the defence side of the combat modifier census is cosmetic in this build. Land is unaffected - CUnit +0xF0 has the AI reader.

**"Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else" is wrong, and the conclusion survives (2026-10-05, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md).** There is a second static reader, at 0x160E5B in CBomberCombatant::FireUnit, where this field multiplies the bombing target's `air_defence`; the register is a CSubUnit on independent evidence, being read at +0x58, +0x5C and +0xA8 in the same loop. The 2026-10-02 live check does not contradict it - it hooked CCombatant slot 11's callers, not this field. The demotion stands for a better reason than the old one: **that second reader's result is itself discarded**, so the defence-side product still reaches nothing but a number on screen. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
**The regiment's own name, always present, and the only thing `remove_brigade` can ever match.** Saved as `name` inside a `regiment={}` block, and the loader puts it back. Across the 45-save corpus there are **788,880 regiment blocks and 788,880 of them carry a `name=`, none of it empty**, so an 'unnamed regiment' does not exist at runtime: 290,876 of those instances (7,133 distinct strings) hold an engine-generated name of the shape `<ordinal> <abbrev> Regiment` - `1st HQ Regiment`, `2nd Art Regiment`, `1st Wagon Regiment` - and the rest hold the historical name the order of battle gave them. A wing is a CSubUnit too and carries its name here in the same way.

**So `remove_brigade = <a subunit type>` can never match**, and nothing in the mod tries: of 6,132 distinct `remove_brigade` values none is one of the 1,427 subunit type tokens the mod's `units/*.txt` declare. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: A CCountryTag on the sub unit itself - the three-character tag here, the id at +0x98 - distinct from `builder` at +0x34. CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers resolves a country out of it for the wing's BM_RADAR_STATION technology scaling (0x16D0A6/0x16D0B0) and passes it to CWeather::AirCombatEffect for BM_WEATHER (0x16D109/0x16D100), in both cases in preference to the parent unit's owner. **Read out of the code only**; whether it is the owner or the controller was not established. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: pending_strength_damage
fields.comment: **Strength damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths. CUnit::TakeDamage adds to it per landed shot, CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight reads it to tell whether the unit is already finished, and CSubUnit::SettleDamage subtracts it from `strength` and clears it. **Not clamped** - unlike the organisation half. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: pending_organisation_damage
fields.comment:
**Organisation damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths, spread evenly over the subunits by CUnit::TakeDamage rather than by size.

**It is damage attempted, not damage dealt.** CSubUnit::SettleDamage clamps it to the organisation the subunit actually has (`cmovg` at 0x1ABAE1) before subtracting, so in a one-sided fight most of a tick's total is thrown away. Anything reporting organisation damage has to count the clamped amount at 0x1ABAE7, not this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: children_spare

CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. fields.name: Level
fields.comment:
read by CSpyPresence::GetLevel
BiceLib: level (int) - Spies present, **x1000** and always whole - one spy is 1000 - between 0 and g_MaxSpyLevel (10000). The save key is `spy_allocation`, written through the thousandths vector writer 0x4C8050; Lua's GetLevel. **Every writer** (a displacement sweep of +0x1160 over .text): the constructor and CSpyPresence::Reset (0); SetUpCountryForNewGame's first allocation (0x4D72C6); CCountry::LoadKey through CSpyPresence::SetLevel (0x4CE411, its only caller); CDistributeEspionage::Distribute's whole spies (0x51F0F9); CatchSpies' -1000 (0x52E74F); PerformCoup's 0 (0x4F7D0E); AnnexCountry's 0 for every presence in the annexed (0x4E8AC5); and modify_spies inline (0x9BE185). **It never decays.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: Priority
fields.comment: read by CSpyPresence::GetPriority

fields.name: LastMissionChangeDate
fields.comment:
read by CSpyPresence::GetLastMissionChangeDate
BiceLib: last_mission_change (int) - A game tick, the time of the last CChangeSpyMission executed on this presence; the save key is `spy_date` (a date with the hour, `1.1.1.0` for never) and the Lua accessor GetLastMissionChangeDate. The constructor and CSpyPresence::Reset set the epoch (0x170C2B8, 43800000); **CChangeSpyMission::Execute writes the current tick every time it runs** (0x558F87), even for an out-of-range mission and whether or not the priority changed; the loader reads it back. No C++ code reads it but the save writer: SPY_MISSION_CHANGE_DAYS has no reader, so there is no cooldown on changing a mission. The base game's script/ai_intelligence_minister.lua reads it to hold a mission for 60 days; Their Finest Hour's replaces that file and does not. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: missions
fields.comment: One entry per `SpyMission`, in the order the nine localisation keys sit in .rdata from 0x15EC590 and the order CSpyPresence::RunDailyMissions tests them: 0 counter_espionage, 1 military, 2 tech, 3 boost_ruling_party, 4 boost_our_party, 5 lower_national_unity, 6 increase_threat, 7 raise_national_unity, 8 covert_ops. **Each is the mission's priority, a weight** - the command names it `priority`, Lua reads it with GetMissionPriority, the screen and the AI give 0..3 - and the spies are shared among the missions by mission_share = weight / sum of weights. Written only through CSpyPresence::SetMissionAllocation (and zeroed by Reset). The save writes nine `spy_mission` values per country; a country's own counter-espionage starts at 1. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

Never saved - CCountry::LoadKey goes through the same setter, so a load recomputes it. Every mission effect is scaled by its own entry. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: lower_unity_modifier

fields.name: raise_unity_modifier
fields.comment: The second embedded CStaticModifier, vftable written at 0x52D3F8. Filled from the `spy_raise_national_unity` template for mission 7, with the level and mission_share[7]. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: owner_id

fields.name: covert_ops_points

A leaf's own Evaluate then either compares it straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3 says which does which. **This is the opposite convention from `CIntTrigger::value` at the same offset**, and nothing in the script files distinguishes them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.comment: 0x18D (BiceLib/GameClasses/CModifier.hpp:29), inherited from CModifier

fields.name: values
fields.comment: the values, one entry per ModifierType and indexed by it; CModifier::GetValue reads [this+0x18][type*8]. Typed as a structure of named entries so a read is a field rather than an index. **The index is the definition's registration order, which is CModifier::id only up to 101.** The global initialiser builds 108 definitions in array order but stamps ids that are not in that order at the end: entries 102..107 are LAND_INTEL_BOOST (id 103), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST (id 104), LOCAL_UNDERGROUND (id 102), NAVAL_INTEL_BOOST a second time (id 104 again), STRATEGIC_RESOURCE_EFFICIENCY (id 105) and LOCAL_UNIT_SPEED (id 106). So an index below 102 can be read straight off reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py, and one at or above 102 has to be read off this structure instead - while a comparison against CModifier +0x24 `id` is the other way round. (reversing/CLASSES.md), inherited from CModifier

fields.name: id
fields.comment: Which modifier this is. Typed as the ModifierId enum so those read as names; the enum is built by reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py out of the global initialiser, which is the only place the 107 names exist. (reversing/scripts/modifierIds.py), inherited from CModifier

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

Both descendants read it and mean different things by it: for CLoadOOBEffect it is the order of battle's path under history/units, for CRemoveBrigadeEffect the brigade to take away, which it puts into REMOVE_BRIGADE (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md)

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the save's `id` pair, written after the id. **Read live**: 41 on what a scenario started with, 4713 on what the game has built since (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:31)

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the regiment's id, the first half of the save's `id` pair (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:32)

fields.name: strength_ceiling
fields.comment: set to the regiment's strength when it is built and afterwards only raised to it, never lowered; CUnit slot 24 totals it. Not what the regiment has left - that is +0x5C. saved as `highest` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:55)

fields.name: builder
fields.comment: who built it, saved as `builder`, and only where the id half of the tag is set (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:59)

fields.name: sub_unit_definition_ptr
fields.comment: this regiment's definition, with its country's tech applied. saved as `type`, by writing the definition's own name (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:64)

fields.name: strength
fields.comment: what the regiment has left, in the scale of its definition's max_strength; the supply consumption scales by it, CUnit slot 21 averages it. saved as `strength` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:44)

fields.name: organisation
fields.comment: organisation x1000, saved as `organisation` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:62)

fields.name: home
fields.comment: where it was raised; the save writes that province's id under `home`, and the loader turns the id back into this pointer. **Read live**: a CMapProvince by its own RTTI, and null on a regiment that was never given one (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:68)

fields.name: technologies
fields.comment: **the technology levels this regiment was raised with**, one node per entry of its definition's `technologies`, built by CSubUnit::SetType. The save writes a line per node keyed by the technology's own name - `infantry_activation={5 0.000}` - and the loader looks the key up in the technology database, which is what says these are technologies. **Read live**: every node's first word is a CTechnology; none on a CWing, 9 to 52 on a regiment (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:85)

fields.name: sunk_by_type
fields.comment: type half of the `sunk_by` object id (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:92)

fields.name: sunk_by_id
fields.comment: what sank this ship, saved as `sunk_by`, and only where the pair is not the game's "no object" one. **Read live**: set on 1123 of 3736 ships (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:93)

fields.name: is_reserve
fields.comment: saved as `is_reserve`; CRegiment::GetMaxStrength scales the definition's max_strength by RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE where it is set. **Read live**: 1184 of 4000 regiments (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:98)

fields.name: pride
fields.comment: the pride of the fleet, saved as `pride`. **Read live**: 31 of 3736 ships (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:102)

fields.name: unit_ptr
fields.comment: the CUnit this regiment belongs to; how the per regiment supply and fuel functions reach the unit's order. **Read live**: a CArmy on every regiment (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:108)

fields.name: current_distance
fields.comment: how far the regiment is from the enemy in its battle, x1000, saved as `current_distance` - and only where the unit's `combats` list has something in it. **Read live**: zero on all 4000 regiments (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:116)

fields.name: extra_consumption
fields.comment: every point is another 1% of supply and fuel: the consumption functions add it x10 to a potency whose base is 1000. A cached total - the levels in `technologies` added up, which CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies recomputes. **Read live**: it is that sum on all 10254 sub units in a running game (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:130)

fields.name: historical_model
fields.comment: which historical model it was raised as, saved as `historical_model`; -1 where it is none. **Read live**: -1 on 3940 of 4000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:134)

fields.name: experience
fields.comment: x1000, saved as `experience`. **The constructor writes -1000, 'not given'**, and a new game replaces a negative with the owner's UNIT_START_EXPERIENCE - times (1000 + RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE)/1000 for a reserve, with no mobilisation gate - capped at 100000. A figure from the file is kept as it is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md)

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment:
**The combat modifiers acting on this one ship, wing or brigade** - first here, last at +0x44, count at +0x48, each node holding a 12-byte {id, attack, defence} record exactly like CUnit+0xDC's. Appended to by CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1AC300) from the naval, air, bomber and target slot 19s - 48 call sites - and freed, with all three fields zeroed, by CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590) at the top of every tick. **This, not CUnit+0xDC, is where air and naval combat modifiers live**, which is why a live watch on a ship's parent CUnit never saw the list fill. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)
+0x4 inside it: combat_modifiers_last (LinkedListNode*) - The last node of the CList at +0x40. Written on every push; the head at +0x40 is written only when the count was zero. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)
+0x8 inside it: combat_modifiers_count (int) - How many modifiers are on the list at +0x40. The field to watch for a push, for the same reason as CUnit+0xE4. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every combat modifier's attack side on this ship, wing or brigade**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier multiplies in `max(attack + 1000, 10)` as a 64-bit product divided by 1000; CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers seeds it back to 1000 each tick. **It multiplies the shot count**: CNavalCombatant::Attack computes `shots = sea_attack (or convoy_attack / sub_attack) * this / 1000` at 0x167B3A, the exact counterpart of CUnit+0xEC x +0xF4 on land. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment:
The defence-side counterpart of +0x50, written by the same adder and reset to 1000 by the same slot 19. **Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else**, in CCombatant slot 11's per-sub-unit loop, where it is multiplied by +0x50 and divided by 1000. That read sits past a `ret 4` at 0x566452 and is reached only by `je 0x566455` from inside the loop, which is why it was recorded here as having **no reader** until 2026-10-01 (trap 3). The branch is taken when the sub-unit's slot 9 answers false; the true arm uses the division's CUnit +0xEC/+0xF0/+0xF4/+0xF8 instead, so on a ship or wing the two products are used together.

**What it feeds, corrected 2026-10-01 (second correction, see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat3.md §3).** This entry twice said the product is a 'loss factor' that carries naval, air and bombing modifiers 'into losses'. It does not. That wording was inherited from a wrong owner: the block was first attributed to CCombatant::ApplyLosses (trap 2 - ApplyLosses ends at 0x5662ED and slot 11 begins at 0x5662F0 with no padding), and when the owner was corrected the meaning was not re-asked. **Slot 11 sums strength.** Its only two invocations in the image are 0x57B083 and 0x57B091 inside CCombat slot 17 (0x17B050), which returns the attacker's share of the two sides' total strength in thousandths; that number's only consumer is 0x17BD70, the `combat_status` window's per-tick refresh, called once from the end of CCombat::Tick and only for a combat the player's own country is in, where it picks an icon state at the 66.0%/33.0% thresholds and formats a percentage.

**So the two sides are not symmetrical.** +0x50 multiplies the shot count in CNavalCombatant::Attack and therefore changes the simulation; +0x54's single reader changes a number on screen. On this reading a defence-side naval, air or bombing combat modifier - including the two defence-only ids - is **cosmetic in this build**. The bound: 'slot 11 has exactly two invocations' is confirmed of the entry-set decode, and 6.7% of non-padding .text lies outside that decode, so it is `likely` as a statement about the whole image. One battle in a running game settles it - see FINDINGS-combat3.md's live checks.

**And the one reader only runs for the player's own battles** (2026-10-02): CCombat::Tick gates the combat_status refresh on CountryIdListContains over the attacker's or defender's CCombatant::countries with the player's id from gameState +0xC34. So in an AI-vs-AI combat this field is never read at all. Player-only, not merely display-only.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02.** A hook on the one reader (CCombatant slot 11) in a 1942 war save recorded 39,414 calls with **zero unexplained return addresses**: 39,222 via CLandCombatant's own forwarder and 96 + 96 from CCombat slot 17's two legs. So nothing outside slot 17 reaches this field in practice, the vcall-thunk route the static sweep could not close never fired, and the demotion stands: for naval, air and bombing the defence side of the combat modifier census is cosmetic in this build. Land is unaffected - CUnit +0xF0 has the AI reader.

**"Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else" is wrong, and the conclusion survives (2026-10-05, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md).** There is a second static reader, at 0x160E5B in CBomberCombatant::FireUnit, where this field multiplies the bombing target's `air_defence`; the register is a CSubUnit on independent evidence, being read at +0x58, +0x5C and +0xA8 in the same loop. The 2026-10-02 live check does not contradict it - it hooked CCombatant slot 11's callers, not this field. The demotion stands for a better reason than the old one: **that second reader's result is itself discarded**, so the defence-side product still reaches nothing but a number on screen. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
**The regiment's own name, always present, and the only thing `remove_brigade` can ever match.** Saved as `name` inside a `regiment={}` block, and the loader puts it back. Across the 45-save corpus there are **788,880 regiment blocks and 788,880 of them carry a `name=`, none of it empty**, so an 'unnamed regiment' does not exist at runtime: 290,876 of those instances (7,133 distinct strings) hold an engine-generated name of the shape `<ordinal> <abbrev> Regiment` - `1st HQ Regiment`, `2nd Art Regiment`, `1st Wagon Regiment` - and the rest hold the historical name the order of battle gave them. A wing is a CSubUnit too and carries its name here in the same way.

**So `remove_brigade = <a subunit type>` can never match**, and nothing in the mod tries: of 6,132 distinct `remove_brigade` values none is one of the 1,427 subunit type tokens the mod's `units/*.txt` declare. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: A CCountryTag on the sub unit itself - the three-character tag here, the id at +0x98 - distinct from `builder` at +0x34. CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers resolves a country out of it for the wing's BM_RADAR_STATION technology scaling (0x16D0A6/0x16D0B0) and passes it to CWeather::AirCombatEffect for BM_WEATHER (0x16D109/0x16D100), in both cases in preference to the parent unit's owner. **Read out of the code only**; whether it is the owner or the controller was not established. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)

fields.name: pending_strength_damage
fields.comment: **Strength damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths. CUnit::TakeDamage adds to it per landed shot, CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight reads it to tell whether the unit is already finished, and CSubUnit::SettleDamage subtracts it from `strength` and clears it. **Not clamped** - unlike the organisation half. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: pending_organisation_damage
fields.comment:
**Organisation damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths, spread evenly over the subunits by CUnit::TakeDamage rather than by size.

**It is damage attempted, not damage dealt.** CSubUnit::SettleDamage clamps it to the organisation the subunit actually has (`cmovg` at 0x1ABAE1) before subtracting, so in a one-sided fight most of a tick's total is thrown away. Anything reporting organisation damage has to count the clamped amount at 0x1ABAE7, not this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: target_id_type
fields.comment: The type half of the persistent id of the ship this one last shot at; with +0xBC, the remembered target CSubUnit::PickTarget keeps from hour to hour. Cleared by CCombatant::AddUnit and for a ship that cannot shoot. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md)

fields.name: target_id
fields.comment: The id half of the remembered target at +0xB8. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md)

fields.name: has_target
fields.comment: Set when CSubUnit::PickTarget found a target this hour and cleared when it did not. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md)

fields.name: contributes_to_unit
fields.comment: **A cached `strength >= 0.100 && organisation >= 1.000`**, recomputed by `CUnit::UpdateHourly` (written at 0x1BA2C6) for the zero-combat-width brigades of a land unit only, and left alone on everything else. When it flips, the unit's definition is rebuilt. `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` does not read it - it recomputes the same predicate from +0x5C and +0x60 - and 0x1CD500 asks whether any brigade of a unit satisfies it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md)

fields.name: Defensivness
fields.comment:
read by CSubUnitDefinition::GetDefensivness
BiceLib: defensiveness (int) - **Live, and half of the only defence mechanic in the game.** CLandCombatant::FireUnit reads it off the unit's own definition (CUnit +0xC8 then +0x11C, at 0x16B0A1) when this side is attacking - `toughness` when it is not - and passes it to CUnit::RollToHit (0x1CD250), which **consumes** it: the value divided by 1000 is a number of shots the unit may defend against this tick, counted against CUnit::defences_used (+0x15C), and while slots remain the shot is judged by BASE_CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT plus a technology bonus instead of CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF. RollToHit has exactly one caller in the image, so this is land-only - compare `air_defence` (+0x128), `sea_defence` (+0x160) and `surface_defence` (+0x174), none of which reaches a hit roll. Its other combat-range readers draw rather than simulate: CCombatant::SumSubUnitStrength (slot 11) and two helpers for the combat status window. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md (BiceLib/GameClasses/CSubUnitDefinition.hpp:64)

fields.name: air_defence
fields.comment: **No combat consumer.** The only combat function in the image that reads it is CBomberCombatant::FireUnit (0x160D44), which scales it by the target's combat_defend_product and **discards the result** - five accesses to the frame slot, no esp alias, decode verified by recursive descent over all 829 instructions. CAirCombatant::Attack does not read it at all, and nor does any of the three target-side Attack bodies. Every air and bombing hit roll uses a flat CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF instead; CUnit::RollToHit, where a defence stat buys anything, has exactly one caller and it is CLandCombatant::FireUnit. Still read by the unit stats panel, BuildUnitStatsTooltip, CAir::GetDefenceValue (slot 40) and the AI's power figure, which is why it looks live. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md (BiceLib/GameClasses/CSubUnitDefinition.hpp:56)

fields.name: sea_defence
fields.comment: **No reader in naval combat at all** - a step worse off than `air_defence`, which is at least read and thrown away. A whole-image sweep gives **two** reads with a definition pointer in hand and **neither** in the combat classes: CNavy::GetDefenceValue (slot 40, 0x1D2C5C) and the naval unit stats panel (0x3ABE3A). (Said three until the census filter was corrected to take the nearest write to a register rather than any +0x58 load in the window.) The call closure from the naval combat roots - 654 functions - contains no read of +0x160 inside rva 0x160000-0x180000 either; its 52 `[reg+0x160]` hits are all `CUnit::in_game_idler_ptr`. **The positive control for that negative**: the same filter on the same functions finds `sea_attack` (+0x168) twice and `hull` (+0x178) three times in CNavalCombatant::Attack, and `positioning` (+0x184) in UpdatePositioning and CSubUnit::PickTarget - so it does see naval-combat reads of a definition stat where they exist. CBomberCombatant::FireUnit scales a bombed ship's damage by it too (0x1611EC, 0x1611F5). See findings/FINDINGS-combatmods.md §9 and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md (BiceLib/GameClasses/CSubUnitDefinition.hpp:90)

Zero on all 108 countries at a 1936 scenario start, which is what a nuclear-production bonus should be in 1936 - not evidence that nothing ever sets it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: radar_impact
fields.comment: The file's fraction times 1000. RADAR_IMPACT_TECH at 0x53E5DF from the load at 0x53E5FD. **The record carries this offset on CTechnologyStatus as `radar_combat_bonus`, with the note "The name is ours, off the use"** - it scales BM_RADAR_STATION, `v = radarLevel * RADAR_COMBAT_IMPACT / 1000 * (1000 + this) / 1000`, in CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers at 0x16D0BF. **The game's own name is `radar_impact`**, from the loader key (0x588) and the display label. Not renamed here. **Live**: 2 countries non-zero, 20 and 40; France 20. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: repair_rate
fields.comment: The file's fraction times 1000. REPAIR_RATE_TECH at 0x53E818 from the load at 0x53E836. **Live**: 4 countries non-zero, 85 or 170; France 170. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: bomber_targeting
fields.comment: The file's fraction times 1000. BOMBER_TARGET_TECH at 0x53EA57 from the load at 0x53EA75. **Live**: 7 countries non-zero, -20 to 120; France 80. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: fighter_targeting
fields.comment: The file's fraction times 1000. FIGHTER_TARGET_TECH at 0x53EC96 from the load at 0x53ECB4. **Live**: 7 countries non-zero, -20 to 60; France -20. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: frontline_focus
fields.comment: The file's fraction times 1000. FRONTLINE_FOCUS_TECH at 0x53EED5 from the load at 0x53EEF3. **Live**: 6 countries non-zero, 50 or 100; France 50. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: reserve_focus
fields.comment: The file's fraction times 1000. RESERVE_FOCUS_TECH at 0x53F114 from the load at 0x53F132. **Live**: 12 countries non-zero, 50 or 100; France 50. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: naval_air_target_chance
fields.comment: The file's fraction times 1000. NAVAL_AIR_TARGET_CHANCE_TECH at 0x53F353 from the load at 0x53F371. **Live**: 5 countries non-zero, 100 or 200. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: listening_station
fields.comment: A byte, like allow_escorts: `cmp byte [edi+0xDC], 0` at 0x53C338 then LISTENING_STATION_TECH at 0x53C355 with no number. **Live**: 4 of 108 countries have it set, France among them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: mission_reduction_modifier
fields.comment: **New.** An inline array of 33 ints, the twin of mission_efficiency at +0xE0 and on the same dense index space - the tooltip reaches it as `lea ecx,[edi+0x164]` and then reads `[base]` for this one and `[base-0x84]` for +0xE0, 0x84 being 33 * 4. Labelled ORD_RED at 0x53FE16, which the mod renders "Organisation Penalty". The mod declares it as `<mission_name> = { reduction_modifier = -0.1 }`, stored times 1000. **Its one reader in the whole image is COrder::GetMissionOrgPenalty (0x187A30)** - fieldchain.py --holder 0xDF8 --field 0x164, with the same scan on +0xE0 finding all six known readers as the positive control. **Live confirmation, two-sided**: France reads +0xE0 + 19*4 = 80 and +0x164 + 19*4 = -100, index 19 is `interdiction` in the mission index, and the mod declares `interdiction { efficiency = 0.08 }` and `interdiction { reduction_modifier = -0.1 }`. France's other entries are index 8 (sortie) -15 and 18 (ground_attack) -70. The 33 index names are in OrderMissionIndexToKey (0x1847A0). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: tactic_bonuses
fields.comment: The `tactic_...` keys of a technology, each kept with its number: any key the switch does not know that begins `tactic_` is added here. How they reach the country's table (CTechnologyStatus +0x24) was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 11. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: tech_decay_by_category_end
fields.comment: end of the vector whose begin is +0x1F8, which the record carries on CTechnologyStatus as `tech_decay_by_category` typed `int*` with the note that **its being the technology effect key `decay` (save token 0x52E) is inference**. That inference is now read: the arm at 0x540178..0x5401C6 loads `[edi+0x1F8][i]`, takes the row's label from `GetTechnologyDataBase()->+0x1C[i]` - the category - and emits the key DECAY, which the mod renders "Decay". **Live**: 49 entries for all 108 countries, matching g_CTechnologyDataBase (rva 0x1687B78) +0x1C exactly, whose elements are the theories and practicals in file order (0 nocategory, 1 infantry_theory, ... 26 infantry_practical, ... 48 construction_practical). All 49 are zero for every country, which agrees with CCountryHistory.hpp listing `decay` among the levers the mod never pulls - the mod declares it nowhere. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.name: tech_decay_by_category_capacity
fields.comment: capacity of the vector whose begin is +0x1F8. The record's `int*` on CTechnologyStatus +0x1F8 is the begin pointer of a std::vector<int>, not a bare array. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md)

fields.comment: The technology this entry is for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md)

read by CTechnology::GetKey
BiceLib: key (Hoi3CString) - the technology's key as the files spell it - `art_barrel_ammo`. A sub unit's save keys are technology keys, and its loader looks them up by this (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp:34)

read by CTechnology::GetOnCompletion
BiceLib: on_completion (CTechnologyCategory*) - `on_completion`, save token 0x445 - **the practical or theory this technology feeds**. The ability rebuild at 0x41FEFC calls slot 2 on it and reads its +0x60, so it is a category, not a command (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-research.md)

fields.comment: read by CTechnology::GetFolder

fields.comment:
read by CTechnology::GetResearchBonus
BiceLib: research_bonus_from (void*) - `research_bonus_from`, a linked list: [0] the CTechnologyCategory, [4] the weight in thousandths, [0xC] the next node. Walked at 0x533448..0x53348B, each category's ability term times its weight summed into the research bonus (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-research.md)

fields.comment: read by CTechnology::GetDifficulty

fields.comment: **what this technology does to each unit type**: a list whose nodes hold the effect at +0 and the next node at +8. Each effect is a whole CSubUnitDefinition holding only the changes, and its `Key` is the unit type it is for. **Read live**: 16044 effects across 1175 technologies in this mod (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp:49)

fields.name: start_year
fields.comment: `start_year`; 1173 of 1174 agree across 31 values (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp)

fields.name: first_offset
fields.comment: `first_offset`; 801 of 802 agree across 32 values (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp)

fields.name: stealable
fields.comment: `stealable`; 569 of 569 agree (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp)

fields.name: additional_offset
fields.comment: `additional_offset`; 795 of 795 agree (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp)

fields.name: max_level
fields.comment: `max_level`, and **the loader turns 0 into 1** rather than leaving it; 877 of 877 agree (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp)

fields.name: is_nuclear
fields.comment: `is_nuclear`; 14 declare it and agree, but all 14 say yes, so this rests on the loader (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp)

fields.name: build_cost_ic_modifier
fields.comment: read by 0x45140 into sixteen bytes; what they hold has not been read (BiceLib/GameClasses/CTechnology.hpp)

fields.comment: `activate_unit`, the vector CTechnology.hpp says has no field of its own: begin here, end at +0x304. ApplyTechnologyEffects walks it at 0x532AEE..0x532B1C and marks each definition's index available in CTechnologyStatus +0x27C (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-research.md)

fields.name: is_theory
fields.comment: Set on a theory, clear on a practical. Only a theory can be shared (CShareTechnologyAction::IsValid, CShareTechnologyDialog::BuildCategoryList, CCountry::CheckTechSharing); ApplyTechCategoryDecay picks theories or practicals by it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: Key
fields.comment: read by CTechnologyFolder::GetKey

fields.name: Index
fields.comment: read by CTechnologyFolder::GetIndex

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect, inherited from CIntEffect

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CIntEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CIntEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CIntEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect, inherited from CIntEffect

fields.name: value
fields.comment: The scalar, `atoi(text) * 1000` - whole numbers only, held in thousandths. Written by CIntEffect::TakeScalarValue; CCountryEventEffect::Execute and CRandomEffect::Execute divide it back by 1000. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md), inherited from CIntEffect

fields.name: technology
fields.comment: The technology the key named. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: IcModifier
fields.comment:
read by CTechnologyStatus::GetIcModifier
BiceLib: ic_bonus (int) - thousandths. CCountry::UpdateIC adds it to `1000 + countryValues[MODIFIER_GLOBAL_IC]` to get the multiplier on the province base. Read at 0xF0E3B (cached in a local) and applied at 0xF0FBB. The name is inferred from that one use; nothing else about the 0x29C bytes has been read. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-ic.md)

fields.name: convoy_build_cost_effect
fields.comment: what technology has done to the convoy build cost; the define is scaled by (1000 + this) / 1000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CDefines.hpp:46)

fields.name: convoy_build_time_effect
fields.comment: what technology has done to the convoy build time; the define is scaled by (1000 + this) / 1000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CDefines.hpp:46)

fields.name: escort_build_cost_effect
fields.comment: what technology has done to the escort build cost; the define is scaled by (1000 + this) / 1000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CDefines.hpp:46)

fields.name: escort_build_time_effect
fields.comment: what technology has done to the escort build time; the define is scaled by (1000 + this) / 1000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CDefines.hpp:46)

fields.name: level_by_technology
fields.comment: **the country's researched level of each technology**, ints indexed by a technology's index (`CTechnology +0x244`). `CHistoricalModelSet::MakeSubUnit` copies straight out of it into a new regiment's `CSubUnitTechnology::level` (`mov [ecx+4], esi` at `0x183183`), and **read live** it equals the level 6859 of 7445 regiment entries carry, counting only non-zero ones - the rest being regiments raised before the country researched further. `0x63D40` sums it over a unit type's own technologies and hands the total to GetBuildCostIC, which is what it used to be named for (BiceLib/GameClasses/CHistoricalModel.hpp)

fields.name: build_cost_by_unit_type
fields.comment: ints indexed by CSubUnitDefinition's index: what technology has done to that unit type's build cost (BiceLib/GameClasses/CSubUnitDefinition.hpp:153)

fields.name: build_cost_mp_by_unit_type
fields.comment: the manpower counterpart of +0x24C, read by the total build cost function (BiceLib/GameClasses/CSubUnitDefinition.hpp:156)

fields.name: build_time_by_unit_type
fields.comment: ints indexed by CSubUnitDefinition's index: what technology has done to that unit type's build time (BiceLib/GameClasses/CSubUnitDefinition.hpp:176)

fields.name: division_size
fields.comment: thousandths; what the technology key `division_size` adds up to. The most brigades a division may have is `(BRIGADES_IN_DIVISION + this) / 1000`: CDivisionDesigner::AddBrigade (0x3EA880), CanBuildDivision (0xE1190) and the designer's `allowed_value`. One technology of the base game has the key, `superior_firepower`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-builders.md)

fields.name: fuel_refining_bonus
fields.comment: thousandths. CCountry::ConvertCrudeOilToFuel (0xF19F0) scales the fuel a unit of crude oil makes by (1000 + this) / 1000, and then again by (1000 + MODIFIER_FUEL_CONVERSION) / 1000 - the two multiply. Named from that one reader; which technology key feeds it was not traced, `refinery_efficiency` being the obvious candidate. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-distribute.md)

fields.name: tactic_bonus
fields.comment: A table of fixed-point numbers indexed by a tactic's number: what the country's technologies add to that tactic's weight. Read by CCombatant::PickTactic. What fills it was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 11. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: encryption
fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name. UpdateIntelFunctor_SerialBody takes the province's controller's from the looking country's `decryption` to place its radar rings (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 7). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 11. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: decryption
fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name, set against the holder's `encryption` in the radar part of the intelligence refresh. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 11. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: combined_arms_group_bonus
fields.comment: An array indexed by combined-arms group: CUnit::GetCombinedArmsBonus (0x1B6240) sums this over every group present in the division's group bitmap at CUnit+0x1D0 and adds it to CUnit+0x1CC and the combined_arms_bonus trait to make BM_COMBINED_ARMS. Thousandths. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)

fields.name: free_stacking_allowance
fields.comment: **The technology effect `unit_cooperation`**, thousandths (fieldmap.py 0x537DB0). Subtracted from the stacking penalty before it is pushed as BM_DIVISION_PENALTY, in CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x16A8A9) and in CTargetCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x162DE3) - in both `v = rawPenalty - this`, and the modifier is only added when v is still positive. The field's name is ours and older than the key's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 8. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: naval_positioning_bonus
fields.comment: **The technology effect `targeting_chance`** (CTechStatistics::LoadKey token 0x511, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-fieldmap.md; the tooltip's TARGET_CHANCE_TECH, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md section 4). Scales a ship's positioning score in CSubUnit::PickTarget (0x16764F): `p = p * (1000 + this) / 1000`, where p is the ship definition's `positioning` plus the combatant's accumulated +0x10B4. Thousandths. The record's name is from its use and is kept. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md)

fields.name: naval_targeting_bonus
fields.comment: **The technology effect `targeting_choice`** (CTechStatistics::LoadKey token 0x510, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-fieldmap.md; the tooltip's TARGET_CHOICE_TECH, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-uinumbers2.md section 4). CSubUnit::TargetingSkill adds it for a ship: a tenth of that sum, with ten for each point of the admiral's skill, is the chance in a hundred that a ship takes the best target in reach. Thousandths. The record's name is from its use and is kept. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaairleaders.md)

fields.name: escort_efficiency
fields.comment: The technology effect CConvoy::GetDefence (0xC7C10) applies as (1000 + this) / 1000. Named by elimination from the technology effect keys the image carries - `escort_efficiency` is the only one that could scale escorts - and the function is its only reader found. Inference, not read off a loader. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoys.md)

fields.name: naval_base_efficiency
fields.comment: Added, with 1000 and the country's NAVAL_BASE_EFFICIENCY modifier, to what scales a naval base's capacity: NavalBaseCapacity reads it at 0x4A7652 off the province's controller. **Taken to be what the technology key `naval_base_efficiency` adds up to** (Naval Doctrines.txt gives 0.20 a level), by the same reasoning as +0x94 and `ic_efficiency` and with less behind it: no figure measures it and the key's loader was not read. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-organisation.md)

fields.name: manpower_gain
fields.comment: thousandths; what the technology key `manpower_gain` adds up to. GetMonthlyManpowerGain and UpdateMaxManpower multiply the whole of a country's manpower - what its provinces give and the flat `global_manpower` both - by 1000 + this. It multiplies, where leadership_gain at +0xB8 adds to the laws' bonus. The record carries the same offset on CTechStatistics under the same name, from the loader. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpowergain.md)

fields.name: build_discount_extra
fields.comment: thousandths, added to the technology category discount by CCountry::GetCategoryBuildDiscount (0xE1AC0), its one reader - so it comes off the cost of every unit and off its build time alike. **What the technology key `ic_efficiency` adds up to**: the effect of `industral_efficiency`, 0.025 a level. That is measured, not read off a loader: with Germany's four levels two days of the upgrade share reproduce a savegame on all 1,469 of its technology lines, and without them none of its build times fit. The neighbour of ic_bonus at +0x90, which is `ic_modifier`, and not the same figure. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md)

fields.name: oil_conversion_bonus
fields.comment: thousandths. What technology adds to the crude oil a unit of energy makes: CCountry::GetOilConversionRate (0xF17F0) is 100 - a tenth - plus this, and the energy-to-crude-oil block of CCountry::UpdateIC (UpdateIC_EnergyToCrudeOil, 0xF0FF5) inlines the same sum at 0xF11AC. A savegame's Germany has two levels of the technology whose effect is `energy_to_oil_conversion = 0.1` and converts at 0.3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-distribute.md)

fields.name: supply_production_bonus
fields.comment: thousandths. CDistributeSupply::GetSuppliesMade (0x11ADD0) adds it to MODIFIER_GLOBAL_SUPPLIES and multiplies the day's supplies by one plus the sum. It is what a technology's `ic_to_supplies` key adds up to: a savegame's Germany has four levels of supply_production at 0.05 and its supplies fit a bonus of 0.2 here. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-distribute.md)

fields.name: provincial_aa_efficiency
fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name. StaticAntiAirTerm multiplies the province's anti-aircraft level by one plus the controller's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 7. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: combat_radio_bonus
fields.comment: **The technology effect `combat_efficiency`, which the `radio` technology carries**, thousandths (fieldmap.py 0x537DB0) - and the whole of BM_RADIO (0x09): CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x16CECB), CBomberCombatant's and CTargetCombatant's equivalents read it and push it straight through as both the attack and the defence side, with no define and no further scaling. The field's name is ours and older than the key's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 8. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: research_efficiency
fields.comment: the `research_efficiency` technology effect, thousandths; added to 1000 and the country's MODIFIER_RESEARCH_EFFICIENCY in the research gain (0x532DF0). Named by fieldmap.py 0x537DB0, which places that effect key at +0xA8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-research.md)

fields.name: leadership_gain
fields.comment: thousandths; what the technology key `leadership_gain` adds up to. CCountry::UpdateTotalLeadership adds it to 1000 + GLOBAL_LEADERSHIP_MODIFIER and multiplies the country's leadership by the sum, so it adds to the laws' bonus rather than multiplying it. The record carries the same offset on CTechStatistics under the same name, from the loader. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leadership.md)

fields.name: radar_combat_bonus
fields.comment: **The technology effect `radar_impact`**, thousandths (fieldmap.py 0x537DB0). Scales BM_RADAR_STATION: `v = radarLevel * RADAR_COMBAT_IMPACT / 1000 * (1000 + this) / 1000` in CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x16D0BF) and the bomber's equivalent. The field's name is ours and older than the key's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 8. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: repair_rate
fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name. RunDailyProvincePass multiplies the day's recovery of production and of buildings by one plus the controller's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 11. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: frontline_focus
fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name: the chance, as a share of a hundred, that a ground attack singles out a land unit on the front line of a battle (CCombatant::CollectFightingLandTargets). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: reserve_focus
fields.comment: thousandths; the same chance for a land unit in a battle and not on its front line. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: naval_air_target_chance
fields.comment: thousandths; the technology effect of that name: one plus it scales the chance, ten in a hundred for each point of the bomber's leader's skill, that a ship goes on a bomber's list of targets (CCombatant::CollectBombTargets). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

fields.name: listening_station

fields.name: mission_efficiency
fields.comment:
**The first half of BM_MISSION_EFFICIENCY (0x07)**: indexed by the dense index OrderTypeToMissionIndex (0x184410) makes out of the unit's order's save token, read at 0x16A506 (land), 0x166913 (naval) and 0x16CD3E (air). Read independently by the convoy survey, which adds the indices that matter there: +0xE0 + 9*4 is `convoy_escort` and +0xE0 + 10*4 `convoy_raid`, as MissionIndexToOrderToken (0x184640) numbers them. The two surveys agree on the field and on the name. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_last

fields.name: deferred_keys_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred keys' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values
fields.comment: First element of the second std::vector<std::string>: the value written beside each deferred key, index for index. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred values' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger

fields.name: character
fields.comment: the character this node stands for (mem) (BiceLib/GameClasses/CFlags.hpp:32)

fields.name: element
fields.comment: The CFlag, CVariable or CGuiType whose name ends at this node, or 0 where no name ends here. TernarySearchTreeFind returns `*(*slot)` from here on a match (0xA7E079) and TernarySearchTreeInsert writes it last (0x44DAFB), overwriting it on a key already present. A variable object has its Hoi3CString at offset 0, which is why CVariables::SaveSubtree can hand this pointer straight to `SaveWriteNamedFixed(Hoi3CString* key@EAX, ...)`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

fields.name: low
fields.comment: **The subtree for keys whose current character sorts below this node's.** Taken when `tolower(key[i]) - node->character < 0`: `lea esi,[edi+8]` in TernarySearchTreeFind (0xA7E068) and `lea ebx,[esi+8]` in TernarySearchTreeInsert (0x44DAF3), in both cases without advancing the key position. CVariables::SaveSubtree recurses into it **first**, which is why the savegame's `variables={}` block comes out alphabetically. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

fields.name: high
fields.comment: **The subtree for keys whose current character sorts above this node's.** Taken when `tolower(key[i]) - node->character > 0` (0xA7E061 in the find, 0x44DAEE in the insert), again without advancing the key. CVariables::SaveSubtree iterates it as the loop's continuation rather than recursing, which is the last leg of the in-order walk. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

fields.name: equal
fields.comment: **The next character of a key that matched this node's.** Taken when `tolower(key[i]) == node->character` and the key has more to go, together with `key++` - `inc ebx; lea esi,[edi+0x10]` in the find (0xA7E05B) and `inc edi; lea ebx,[esi+0x10]` in the insert (0x44DAE4). Where the key ends instead, the node's `element` is the answer. **Both ends of the tree fold the key byte through `tolower` (0xB96692) and store the folded form, so every lookup in this structure is case-insensitive** - which is already recorded on TernarySearchTreeFind and is what makes `check_variable = { which = BaseIC }` and `which = baseic` the same variable, in contrast to `remove_brigade`, which memcmps a name. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

fields.comment: x1000, from the terrain's `movement_cost`. **What one pixel of this terrain adds to the distance of an edge whose walk crosses it** - CProvinceTemplate::MeasureEdges sums it into `ProvinceEdge +0xC` when the map cache is built, and nothing reads it afterwards. So it does shape movement, once: a change to it takes effect when the cache is rebuilt, which a changed terrain.txt causes by itself. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: inland_sea
fields.comment: map/terrain.txt's `inland_sea`. Its CTerrain::LoadKey case (save token 0x3C6) hands `this + 0x54` to the bool reader 0x67B410 at 0xADBB2; fieldmap.py reports the key as unplaced because the destination arrives as a register argument. The `is_water` case two cases up does the same thing to +0x48, which is already recorded. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: humidity
fields.comment: terrain.txt's `humidity`, thousandths - the gap the fieldmap already records at +0x60 between `attrition` (+0x5C) and `precipitation` (+0x64). CWeather::Update pulls a province's humidity towards it, and **a positive value is what makes the country's MODIFIER_JUNGLE_EFFECTS apply** to the high-temperature attrition (0xB3F4D) and the high-temperature combat penalty (0xB40E0). In BlackICE the terrains with a positive humidity are jungle (0.8), hills_jungle (1), mountain_jungle (0.9), equator_sea (0.5) and highlands_woods (5); the deserts set -50 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: is_plains
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD8E9 when the terrain's **name** is the literal string `plains` (0x15C06B4). Not a key in map/terrain.txt - that loader has twelve cases and none of them is this. **The AI's armour and mechanised demand is built on it**: the played-country force planner counts the agent's provinces whose terrain has this byte set and asks for armour and mechanised brigades in that proportion (0x4B62E0..0x4B6344, spent at 0x4B63F0). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: is_mountain
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD92B when the terrain's name is the literal string `mountain` (0x15C06BC). **The AI's bergsjaeger demand is built on it**: half of brigadeDemand times the share of the agent's provinces whose terrain carries this byte (0x4B63FB..0x4B6445, spent at 0x4B684D). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: is_urban
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD96A when the terrain's name is the literal string `urban` (0x15C06C8). Nothing in either force planner reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: is_desert
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD981 when the terrain's name is the literal string `desert` (0x15C06D0), through the string compare 0xC3C0 rather than the inline loop the first three use. Nothing in either force planner reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: is_arctic
fields.comment: Set to 1 by CTerrain::CTerrain at 0xAD998 when the terrain's name is the literal string `arctic` (0x15C06D8). Nothing in either force planner reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

Distinct from `fronts_first` (+0x50, CAreaBorder) and `provinces_first` (+0x30). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

Not read directly by anything in this file. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CHistoryEntry, inherited from CCountryHistoryEntry

fields.comment: When the change happens, in hours on g_CCurrentGameState's tick scale (+0xBDC) - the same scale and the same 43,800,000-hour epoch as CDiplomaticAction::date. The constructor (0x1F4550) initialises it from [0x170C2B8], the engine's null date. It is what CHistoryContainer::AddEntry (0x1F4660) sorts the list by and what ApplyRange (0x1F47C0) compares against its two bounds. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CHistoryEntry, inherited from CCountryHistoryEntry

fields.name: country
fields.comment: The country the change applies to, taken from the constructor's one argument (0x1EEA40, the store at 0x1EEA5E). Every derived Apply starts from it: the flag changes hand it to CCountry::GetFlags (0xCCD30) to reach CCountry +0x180. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md), inherited from CCountryHistoryEntry

fields.name: threat

fields.name: previous_threat

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CEffect

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them.
