fields.name: value
fields.comment: **The operand, in thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CValueTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D13E0) as `TokenToFixedPoint(text)`, so `war_exhaustion = 7.5` is stored as 7500 - the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `national_unity=81.752`). fields.name: children_spare

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. fields.name: From
fields.comment:
read by CTradeRoute::GetFrom
+0x4 inside it: from_id (int) - The country id half of `from`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoys.md)

fields.name: To
fields.comment:
read by CTradeRoute::GetTo
+0x4 inside it: to_id (int) - The country id half of `to`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-convoys.md)

fields.name: isInactive
fields.comment:
read by CTradeRoute::IsInactive
BiceLib: inactive (unsigned char) - **Whether the route failed to run today** - the engine's own word, CTradeRoute::IsInactive. Written only by TradeRouteSetInactive, from RunDailyTradeRoutes: set where the route's convoy has no path, no transports or no usable route, or where either stockpile would go below nothing after the day's exchange; cleared on a day it delivers. Not saved. CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingDisabledResource and HasTradeGoneStale read it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: LastInactive
fields.comment:
read by CTradeRoute::GetLastInactive
BiceLib: last_inactive (int) - A CEU3Date in ticks (hours). CTradeRoute::GetLastInactive (0x887F80) is nothing but `*out = this->+0x84`, and that accessor's luabind name is the game's. TradeRouteSetInactive (0xA4D550) is its only writer: it stamps gameState->tick (+0xBDC) when the route goes inactive, but only if the field is still g_NullDate or more than 0x228 = 552 hours = 23 days have passed, so the stamp is deliberately sticky. CEU3AI::HasTradeGoneStale calls a route stale once `last_inactive + 0x150` (336 hours = 14 days) is past. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-trade2.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CRelation

fields.name: first
fields.comment:
**The first party to the agreement** (save key `first`). Resolved from the three letters in the save through CCountryDataBase::GetTag, so the tag characters land at +0x8 and the index at +0xC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation
+0x4 inside it: first_id (int) - Id half of the CRelation base's `first` CCountryTag at +0x8 - the save block's `first="HON"`. FindMatchingTradeRoute (0xA4A750) compares +0xC and +0x14 between two routes before it will compare their goods, which is the pair identity; and the same 8-byte-apart tag/id shape is already recorded at +0x24/+0x28 and +0x2C/+0x30 for `from` and `to`. Placed by shape and by that use, not by a store, hence `likely`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-trade2.md)

fields.name: second
fields.comment:
**The second party to the agreement** (save key `second`). The same resolution as `first`, into the tag at +0x10 and the index at +0x14. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation
+0x4 inside it: second_id (int) - Id half of the CRelation base's `second` CCountryTag at +0x10 - the save block's `second="POL"`. Same evidence as +0xC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-trade2.md)

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement began**, as a tick (save key `start_date`). Parsed from `year.month.day.hour` text by Date_SetFromString, which is the same representation every other date in the simulation uses. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement ends**, as a tick (save key `end_date`); **the null date 43,800,000 (`[0x170C2B8]`) where it has none** - every constructor sets it so, not zero. A real date is told by `(end_date - 43,800,000) / 24 / 365.0 > 1`. Read only by CCasusBelli (Activate, which will not attach an expired one, and IsOver) and by CRelation::SaveContents (written only when real). **No other relation's IsOver reads it**: a guarantee ends twenty years after `start_date`, a NAP NAP_EXPIRY_MONTHS after it, and the history files' end dates take effect only while history is replayed before play. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: cancel
fields.comment: **Whether the agreement is cancelled** (save key `cancel`), the last of CRelation's own bytes - a subclass's data starts at +0x24. Loaded as a plain comparison against the token `yes`, so any other value, including `no`, leaves it 0. **CDiplomacy::SaveContents skips every relation with it set**, and CRelation::SaveContents, given one, writes `cancel = yes` instead of `start_date`. No writer in play was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: trade_to
fields.comment: **What `to` (the recipient) hands over each day**: a vector header (begin at +0x34) over seven values in thousandths a day, one per good in pool order (supplies, fuel, money, crude oil, metal, energy, rare materials). Save key `trade_to` (token 0x6DD), Lua GetTradedToOf. Its money entry (index 2) is the price of `trade_from`'s goods (CTradeRoute::GetCost), recomputed by TradeRouteSetTradedOf; where it is non-zero `to` is the buyer and runs the convoy. RunDailyTradeRoutes moves it from `to`'s stockpile to `from`'s. A positive CTradeAction::SetTrading writes here. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: trade_from
fields.comment: **What `from` (the actor, the route's `first`) hands over each day**: a vector header over seven values in thousandths a day, pool order. Save key `trade_from` (token 0x6DC), Lua GetTradedFromOf, Lua's `voTradedFrom`. Its money entry is the price of `trade_to`'s goods; a negative CTradeAction::SetTrading writes here. CTradeRoute::IsValid refuses a route with goods in both blocks unless both countries have the free_resource_gifts rule. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: convoy_responsible
fields.comment:
A CCountryTag by value, letters here and the id at +0x5C. CCountry::RunDailyTradeRoutes writes it at all three points where it marks the route inactive - 0x4FEFF3/0x4FF006, 0x4FF8C1 and 0x4FFAD1 - and the value it writes is exactly the expression CTradeRoute::GetConvoyResponsible (0xA4D6A0) computes: the `to` tag when the `to` block's money entry is non-zero, otherwise the `from` tag. So it records which side owed the convoy at the moment the route failed. `likely` because no reader was identified; a +0x58 read is a disp8 and the scan used here cannot see one. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-trade2.md)
+0x4 inside it: convoy_responsible_id (int) - Id half of the CCountryTag at +0x58; written in the same instruction pair at each of the three sites (e.g. `mov [ebx+0x5c], ecx; mov [ebx+0x58], eax` at 0x4FEFF3/0x4FF006). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-trade2.md)

fields.name: inactive_reason
fields.comment: Why the route is inactive, as rendered text: TRADE_INACTIVE_CONVOY "§Y$COUNTRY$§W have not assigned enough convoys." (COUNTRY = the convoy's responsible country) or TRADE_INACTIVE_NO_RES "§Y$COUNTRY$§W does not have enough §Y$RES$§Y." (the side whose stockpile would go negative, and the good). Written by RunDailyTradeRoutes when it makes a route inactive and never cleared; shown as the delayed half of the production screen's trade-list `inactive_icon` tooltip (TRADE_IS_INACTIVE). Not saved. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: convoy_id_type
fields.comment: Type half of the CPersistent id of the route's convoy (42 for a convoy), save key `convoy`; with +0x80 it is looked up by FindPersistentByIdPair. The null id ([0x1A8CC94]/[0x1A8CC98]) where the route has no convoy - an overland route, or one whose convoy could not be made. Set by TradeRouteSetConvoy. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: convoy_id
fields.comment: Id half of the route's convoy's CPersistent id; see +0x7C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeaid.md)

fields.name: Route
fields.comment:
read by CTradeAction::GetRoute
BiceLib: trade_route (CTradeRoute) - **The CTradeRoute the action proposes, embedded rather than pointed at.** CTradeAction::GetAIAcceptance passes `this + 0x28` as the `const CTradeRoute&` argument of CEU3AI::AlreadyTradingDisabledResource (0xA38B60-0xA38B64), and reads the route's two goods blocks through the action instead, at this+0x5C and this+0x6C - which are exactly 0x28 + 0x34 and 0x28 + 0x44, the route's two blocks. That double fit is the evidence; it also means CTradeAction's luabind `const CTradeRoute& GetTradeRoute() const` hands out an interior reference. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md)

fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: target
fields.comment: The tag `target` names. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: region
fields.comment: The region `region` names, null (and logged) on a miss. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred key. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred keys' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values
fields.comment: First element of the second std::vector<std::string>: the value written beside each deferred key, index for index. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred values' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: tag
fields.comment: **The country the condition names.** Only the id half at +0x44 is compared - the three characters at +0x40 are loaded into a stack slot that nothing reads again before the exit - so the test is by index and the text is carried for display. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: Children
fields.comment:
read by CUnit::GetChildren. Reached only because the engine hands it in - no constructor and nothing returns one, but scripts use it (scripts/luacensus.py)
+0x8 inside it: children_count (int) - The count of the `children` CList at +0x1E4. Read as `> 0` meaning 'this unit has subordinates' by CAIUnit slot 76 (0x4DC026, 0x4DC5E2), slot 84 (0x4C17FE) and others, which is how those passes tell a leaf unit from an HQ. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: is_selected
fields.comment: the unit is selected - one byte; +0x5 to +0x7 are other fields (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:23)

fields.name: type
fields.comment: type (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:19)

fields.name: id
fields.comment: unit id (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:20)

fields.name: regiments
fields.comment:
the unit's own regiments; a CList<CSubUnit*> base in RTTI (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:26)
+0x4 inside it: regiments_last (LinkedListNode*) - the `last` of the `regiments` CList at +0x38. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md)
+0x8 inside it: regiments_count (int) - how many brigades, ships or wings the unit holds - the `count` of the CList at +0x38, zeroed with it by CUnit's constructor at 0x1B503C. **`CUnit::RebuildDefinition` divides the synthesised definition's organisation, morale, softness and every adjuster by this number**, so it is what turns those sums into averages. Also the guard on reading the first brigade in `AddRegimentToUnit` and `RemoveRegimentFromUnit`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md)

fields.name: disengage
fields.comment: saved as `disengage`. **Read live**: zero on 696 of 750 units and a small number on the rest (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:70)

fields.name: order_ptr
fields.comment: the unit's current order (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:39)

fields.name: CSubUnitDefinitionPtr
fields.comment: sub unit definition (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:28)

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: a date, saved as `end_date`. **Read live**: the epoch value on most units, so unset (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:71)

fields.name: combat_cooldown
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `attack_delay`, which agrees with this name (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:29)

fields.name: supply_received_percentage
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `supplies`, which agrees with this name (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:30)

fields.name: fuel_received_percentage
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `fuel`, which agrees with this name (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:31)

fields.name: combats
fields.comment:
the combats this unit is in. The sub unit writer only writes `current_distance` where this has something in it. **Read live**: 168 of 2000 armies, and what the nodes hold is a CLandCombat (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:116)
+0x8 inside it: combats_count (int) - The count of the CList whose head is the already-recorded +0x114 `combats`; CList is head/tail/count, so +0x118 is the tail. Both AI bodies test it as 'this unit is fighting, leave it alone' - 0x4CE062 and 0x4CE6B7 and 0x4CEEF5 in the air body, 0x4D1A1A in the naval one - and CUnit_IsAtOwnBase tests it on a second object at 0x1CDC74. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorganise.md)

fields.name: owner
fields.comment:
the owner (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:35)
+0x4 inside it: owner_id (int) - The id half of the `owner` CCountryTag whose letters the record already has at +0x124. Compared directly against CCountry +0xCA8 at 0x4B7629 and used to index CCountry::diplomacy_status_array at 0x4B763B, which is the CCountryTag id-half pattern exactly. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

fields.name: leader_ptr
fields.comment: commanding leader (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:34)

fields.name: current_province_ptr
fields.comment: province the unit is in (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:35)

fields.name: movement_order_remaining_provinces_count
fields.comment: (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:39)

fields.name: movement_progress
fields.comment: saved as `movement_progress`, x1000. **Read live**: zero or a part of the way (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:72)

fields.name: retreat
fields.comment: saved as `retreat`. **Read live**: 11 of 750 units retreating (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:73)

fields.name: in_game_idler_ptr
fields.comment: the in game idler (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:40)

fields.name: name
fields.comment: the unit's name (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:43)

fields.name: arrow_state
fields.comment: saved as `arrow_state`. **Read live**: zero on every unit (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:74)

fields.name: dig_in_level
fields.comment: The save writes it under the key `dig_in`, which agrees with this name (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:43)

fields.name: base_ca_bonus
fields.comment: (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:44)

fields.name: higher_oob_unit_ptr
fields.comment: parent unit in the order of battle (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:45)

fields.name: oob_level
fields.comment: 0 theatre .. 4 division, 5 navy (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:49)

fields.name: expeditionary_owner
fields.comment:
who the unit is on loan from, saved as `expeditionary_owner`. **Read live**: `---` on 740 of 750, and ITA, HUN, SLO and POL on the rest (BiceLib/GameClasses/CUnit.hpp:76)
+0x4 inside it: expeditionary_owner_id (int) - The id half of the `expeditionary_owner` CCountryTag whose letters are at +0x28C. CAIUnit slot 79 splits on it at 0x4B335D (non-zero means the unit is on loan and may be returned) and CSendExpeditionCommand::Execute both clears it (0x1E96FC, when it already matches the command's target) and sets it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: has_own_aggression
fields.comment: the unit has an aggression setting of its own: the unit panel's `aggression_checkbox`. A parent's row marks such a unit with a coloured star. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md)

fields.name: aggression
fields.comment: the unit's aggression, fixed-point from -1 to 1: what the unit panel's `aggression_slider` is compared with before a CSetUnitAggressionCommand is posted, and what 0x5D3FE0 colours a parent row's star by (red over 0.1, blue under -0.1). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md)

fields.name: loaded_parent
fields.comment: The id half of the parent a save's `parent` key named (the type half at +0x58), read by CArmy::LoadKey; CUnit::CUnit zeroes both (0x5B5091). CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent (0x1CEDC0) resolves it as the game is entered and attaches the unit. Only a carried unit is saved with `parent`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

fields.name: plan_subunit_difference
fields.comment: Per CSubUnitDefinition::type_index: what the plan wants of that type minus what the unit's OOB actually has. Signed - a negative entry is a surplus. Written wholesale by CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds (0x1BD240) and cleared by CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds for an HQ that has no plan. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: plan_subunit_group_difference
fields.comment: The same differences summed onto one representative subunit type per group (0x1ADF70 does the folding: carrier air, capital ship, transport/submarine, and so on). Zeroed at the top of each pass and accumulated at 0x1BD544. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: plan_subunit_needed
fields.comment: Per subunit type, the part of the deficit that the group as a whole is still short of - min(difference[i], whatever is left of that group's net difference), taken in index order. This is the list the plan machinery asks for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: shadowed_by_patrol
fields.comment: **Set on a fleet a patrol is shadowing**, and cleared when the patrol lets go: CPatrolOrder::UpdateShadow is its only writer in the naval order code (0x59CED5 clears, 0x59D17F sets). ShouldStartNavalCombat doubles the figure of every roll made against a fleet that has it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md)

fields.name: is_reserve
fields.comment: The unit's own `is_reserve` key, token 0x57F, a plain ParseBool. **Its one use in the loader is to be copied onto each brigade read after it**: the `regiment` case of CUnit::LoadKey tests it either side of the brigade's own load and sets CSubUnit +0xA4. Nothing goes back over brigades already read, and the `wing` case does not test it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md)

fields.name: was_paradropped
fields.comment: **Set on a land unit dropped by a paradrop into a province whose controller is at war with the dropper** (CAir::DropCarried, 0x5D0AF6 - the only writer but the constructor's zero), and saved as `was_paradropped` only where set. While it is set: CUnit::StartAttackDelay uses PARATROOP_MISSION_DELAY; CCombat::GetCombatWidth counts no paratrooper after the first; BM_PARATROOP_PENALTY applies (PARADROP_PENALTY + trait paradrop_mission, FINDINGS-combatmods.md); and BM_LACK_OF_SUPPLIES does not. CUnit::UpdateHourly clears it the first hour the unit is in no battle and multiplies every brigade's organisation by PARATROOP_DROP_ORG_MULT (military +0xA4, 0.66) / 1000. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

fields.name: home_base_ptr
fields.comment: The object that knows the unit's base province - for an air unit, its airbase: its **slot 0 returns a `CMapProvince*`**, which `COrder::OrderReturnToBase` and `CAirInterceptOrder`'s slots 13 and 14 all compare against `CUnit + 0x130`. `CAir::UpdateDaily` (rva 0x1D0B60) opens by reading it, and every air order treats a null here as 'no mission possible' - `CAirInterceptOrder` slot 14 returns 'order finished' outright. `COrder::IsTargetInRange` also skips the range test when it is null. Its class has not been identified. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval.md)

fields.name: no_bombing_hours
fields.comment: The twin of +0xA0 for a bombing: CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat writes 2 where the unit is in one (+0x110, at 0x5BA335) and takes one off at its end. Its readers were not looked for; the name is by the likeness. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md)

fields.name: no_battle_hours
fields.comment: **The hours an air unit cannot be drawn into a battle.** CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat writes 2 at its start where the unit is an air unit in a battle (0x5BA350) and takes one off at its end; CCombatManager::StartCombat and JoinCombatInProvince refuse a unit with it above nothing. So an air unit out of a battle has one hour in which it may move and cannot be fought. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md)

fields.name: upgrade_prio
fields.comment: **The unit's priority, for reinforcement as much as for upgrades**, saved as `is_prioritized`. CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute (0x51BC4F) and CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute (0x51CF96, 0x51D087) both read it for the same thing: a unit with it set joins the front of the list the share works through, the rest the back. The constructor clears it. The name is older than the second reader and is left as it is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md)

fields.name: upgrade_active
fields.comment: Whether the unit's brigades are re-equipped, saved as `can_upgrade`. CDistributeUpgrade::Distribute leaves a unit with it clear out of its list (0x51CF82, 0x51D07A). **The constructor sets it**, so a unit upgrades unless told not to. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md)

fields.name: reinforcements_active
fields.comment: Whether the unit's brigades are brought back to strength, saved as `can_reinforce`. CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute leaves a unit with it clear out of its list (0x51BC42, 0x51BD26). **The constructor sets it.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md)

fields.name: disengage_to
fields.comment: The id of the province a fleet in a battle is to go to once it has counted its `disengage` (+0xA8) up: CMoveCommand::RouteUnit puts an ordered move here in place of a path, CUnit::RetreatFromCombat where a fleet beaten in one battle is still in another, and the tail of CNavalCombatant::Attack finds the path once WantsToDisengage. CUnit::ShowFighting zeroes it with the count. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md)

fields.name: move_not_before
fields.comment: An hour before which the unit does not move at all: CUnit::AdvanceMovement returns while the game's hour is under it. Set to the null date by CMoveCommand::RouteUnit and CUnit::CancelMovement together with `end_date`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: hours_attacking
fields.comment: How many hours the unit has been attacking - in a battle, with a path and some progress. Counted up in CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat; once the battle is over and it is at most UNIT_ATTACK_DELAY_PERIOD the attack delay is cut to that share, and it is zeroed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 6. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md)

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment:
**The combat modifiers acting on this unit, on land only**, a CList: first here, last at +0xE0, count at +0xE4, all three cleared together by CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers (0x1C2FE0). One node per modifier; the node's record holds the id at +0 and the attack and defend values at +4 and +8, which the tooltip prints as `x%/y%` when they differ. 0x164060 turns the id into its BM_* key. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)
+0x4 inside it: combat_modifiers_last (LinkedListNode*) - The list's last node - the `last` of the CList at +0xDC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)
+0x8 inside it: combat_modifiers_count (int) - How many modifiers are on the list. **The one to watch** when looking for what adds to it: the head at +0xDC is only written by a push onto an empty list, while every addition has to touch this. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every modifier's attack side**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1C3040) multiplies each one in as it is added - `product = product * (delta + 1000) / 1000` - and CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers seeds it with 1000, an empty product. The battle tooltip prints `+0xEC * +0xF4 / 1000` as its Attack Modifier (0x32AE39). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every modifier's defend side**, the same shape as +0xEC and filled by the same function. The tooltip prints `+0xF0 * +0xF8 / 1000` as its Defend Modifier (0x32AE8A). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: landing_attack_scale
fields.comment: **The landing's attack scale**, thousandths: 1000 but for a land unit landing from the sea on enemy ground, for which CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (slot 19) sets AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_ATTACK_LOW + (HIGH - LOW) * CUnit::MovementProgressShare / 1000 every battle hour after CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers put it back to 1000. CLandCombatant::FireUnit multiplies the unit's shot count by +0xEC * +0xF4 / 1000 (0x16AED2); the battle tooltip prints it as AMPH_INVASION_ATTACK_SCALE where it is not 1000 and folds it into the Attack Modifier. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

fields.name: landing_defend_scale
fields.comment: **The landing's defence scale**, thousandths: 1000 but for a land unit landing from the sea on enemy ground, for which slot 19 sets low + (AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_DEFEND_HIGH - low) * MovementProgressShare / 1000 with low = AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_DEFEND_LOW + the carrying fleet's summed amphibious_invasion_defence. CLandCombatant::FireUnit multiplies the unit's defence as a target by +0xF0 * +0xF8 / 1000 (0x16B0CB); the tooltip prints it as AMPH_INVASION_DEFEND_SCALE where it is not 1000. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

fields.name: heading
fields.comment: Which way the unit faces: the angle from its province's unit point to the next province's, less pi/2, as CUnit::FaceNextProvince works it out. Its avatar's figure and the pointer beside its counter are turned by it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

fields.name: heading_copy
fields.comment: Written with the same angle as `heading` (+0x104) by both of its writers, one instruction apart. What reads this one apart from that was not looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

fields.name: avatar_stale
fields.comment: the avatar is to be made again: set when the intel level changes or the unit crosses between land and sea (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

fields.name: current_combat
fields.comment: The combat the unit is in right now, distinct from the combats list at +0x114. Tested by GrantCombatExperience (0x1C433A, and at the call site 0x1BA54B) and cleared by CCombatant::DetachAllUnits when the combat ends (0x165D11). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaders.md)

fields.name: previous_province_ptr
fields.comment: The province the unit was in before the one it is in. CUnit::AdvanceMovement stores `current_province_ptr` here immediately before CUnit::EnterProvince, and the save key is `previous`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: movement_order_next_province_ptr
fields.comment: **The first node of the unit's path**, a CList of province ids - not a province pointer. The next province is `map->provinces[*node]`. With +0x13C and +0x140 it is the list's first, last and count; +0x144 is its no-unlink byte. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: movement_order_last_current_province_ptr
fields.comment: **The last node of the unit's path** (see +0x138). CMoveCommand::RouteUnit starts an appended route from `map->provinces[*this]`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: path_no_unlink
fields.comment: The `no_unlink` byte of the path's CList at +0x138: where set, a node reached is marked rather than freed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: arrow_percent
fields.comment: How far along the way to the next province the unit is, in whole per cent, capped at 100: `movement_progress * 100 / distance`. Written by CUnit::AdvanceMovement each hour. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: arrow_step_percent
fields.comment: A running sum of each hour's share of the way, in whole per cent, zeroed on arrival and by SetUnitPath and CUnit::CancelMovement. For the arrow; what reads it was not found. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: defences_used
fields.comment: **How many shots this unit has already defended against this tick.** CUnit::RollToHit compares it against the slots its defence value bought and increments it on each one spent; past that the unit falls back to CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF. Reset per tick somewhere not yet found. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

fields.name: avatar
fields.comment: what the unit is on the map (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

fields.name: arrow
fields.comment: The selected unit's movement arrow, made by CUnit::MakeArrow and freed by CUnit::FreeArrow. CUnit::AdvanceMovement writes the share of the path walked into its +0x15C. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: ai_agent
fields.comment:
**The CAIUnit that commands this unit**, or null. Written by CAIUnit::SetUnit (slot 63, at 0x4B9F04) and only when both of the agent's flags +0x3D and +0x3E are clear; CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits skips any unit that already has one, and SetUnit calls the previous agent's slot 64 to detach it. CAIUnit::Tick and slots 76, 78, 83, 84 and 86 all read it.

**Retyped 2026-10-01 from `CAIUnit*`, and this one matters.** `CAIInvasion::AddUnit` (slot 63, at `0x8A16D7`) writes a **`CAIInvasion*`** here under the same two-flag guard, so the field holds either of two `CAIAgent` subclasses. Anything that reads it and assumes a `CAIUnit` can get a `CAIInvasion` and then read `+0x64` - the unit pointer on a `CAIUnit` - out of the middle of the invasion's transport list. Check the vftable, or slot 65/66 (`CAIUnit` has `mov al,1` at 65 and `xor al,al` at 66; `CAIInvasion` is the mirror), before treating it as a `CAIUnit`. See `FINDINGS-aitheatre.md`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

fields.name: trespassing
fields.comment: **The unit stands where its owner may not enter** - CCountry::MayEnterProvince(owner, false, province) answers no (never set for REB). Recomputed every hour by CUnit::UpdateHourly (0x5B9D33-0x5B9D70, both ways) and at once by UnitList_MarkTrespassers on a diplomatic change (CCountry::OnDiplomacyChanged) and on entering a session; cleared by the constructor and by the AI (0x8E35A1, 0x8E3BBB). A trespasser cannot be the attacking unit of CUnit::CanEngage, takes no province in CheckForCombat, moves at full speed whatever its fuel, may stand in land owned by the owner of the province it is in (CArmy::MayStandIn), and is pulled home by the AI (CAIUnit_PullHeadquartersIn). Nothing moves it by itself. A declaration of war makes no trespassers among the belligerents, since war is itself leave to enter. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: subunit_group_present_begin
fields.comment: begin of a vector of one int per entry of `g_CSubUnitDataBase`'s definition vector, ending at +0x1D4. `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` zeroes it (0x1B5F80) and then writes 1 at each brigade definition's `unit_group` (+0x1B4) index (0x1B6123); afterwards it walks the vector from index 1 and totals the +0x28 of each marked definition into `base_ca_bonus` (+0x1CC). So this is **which combined arms groups the unit's composition covers**. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md)

fields.name: subunit_group_present_end
fields.comment: one past the last of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md)

fields.name: intel_level
fields.comment: **How well the screen's country knows this unit**: 9 for its own units and its friends' (the same real faction, or an alliance in the owner's status towards it), else the byte of `intel_by_country` for it in the province the unit is in (0 unseen, 3 partial, 9 own). Written by CUnit::EnterProvince and **every hour for every unit of every country by RunHourlyTick** (0x6822C8..0x6823D7), which sets the avatar's rebuild byte (+0x10C) where it changed. Under 2 its stack is not drawn, under 3 its counter shows the unknown picture, under 5 its name is `???`, under 7 its two figures are `?`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md)

fields.name: plan
fields.comment:
The unit's battle plan, **held by value, not by pointer** - CUnit's constructor builds a CUnitPlan in place here at 0x1B5232 and its destructor destroys it in place at 0x1B5799. 0x90 bytes, so it runs to +0x28B and expeditionary_owner at +0x28C is the next field. Every plan field already recorded on CUnit is this object's offset plus 0x1FC: +0x204 plan_active = plan +0x8, +0x208 plan_stance = +0xC, +0x20C plan_air_stance = +0x10, +0x210 plan_naval_stance = +0x14, +0x26C plan_subunit_wanted = +0x70, +0x27C plan_our_power = +0x80, +0x280 plan_their_power = +0x84. The save writes it under `plan` by calling slot 1 on it, which works because +0x1FC is the embedded object's own vftable pointer. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)
+0x8 inside it: plan_active (unsigned char) - CUnitPlan +0x8. Whether the unit's battle plan is switched on; CUnitPlan::SetActive (0x4DEB10) resets the whole plan when it goes to zero. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)
+0xC inside it: plan_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0xC, the `stance` key. Defaults to 2 when the plan is switched off. The one plan attribute whose change makes CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute call CUnit::RefreshPlanForceNeeds; 5 is the command's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)
+0x10 inside it: plan_air_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0x10, the `air_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it.

**Every writer in the image, and who reaches it:**

| writer | value | path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute, store at 0x1E7907 | the command's `+0x6C`, skipped when it is 3 | the only store by this displacement; everything below goes through it |
| CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan, 0x4DE9EF | 1 | construction, so 1 is every unit's starting value |
| CUnitPlan::SetActive(plan, 0), 0x4DEB78 | 1 | deactivating a plan resets it; reached from CActivateUnitPlanCommand::Execute and CUnitPlan::ApplyToUnit, both interface commands |
| CUnitPlan::LoadKey, 0x4DF93B | whatever the save holds | load |

And the seven places that post that command, by what they pass for air_stance: **2 from CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances (0x4916AD), for every unit agent, every ProcessAI pass**; 0 from CAIUnit::Slot76_BuildPlan (0x4DAD74) when it builds a plan; 3 (leave alone) from CAIUnit::SetPlanStance (0x4C375E) and from the two power-estimate sites 0x4B5152 and 0x4B7E87; and the interface's own control at 0x35244E, which passes the value the player chose (0x351C8E is its naval twin and passes 3 here).

**So the AI drives this field to 2 by itself and the strategic air war is not player-only.** The sentinel-3 AI sites mean the ground-stance machinery never disturbs it.

**Live distribution (live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save)**, unchanged and still worth reading with the above: 1 on 1,125 of 1,126 `CAir` formations and on 737 of 738 `CNavy`, and **2 on all 101 of the armies attached to a CAIUnit agent**. The air formations are not the objects phase 4's gate reads; the 101 armies are. And `+0x20C` and `+0x210` holding the identical value on all 4,864 objects read is explained: the AI's one writer sets both to 2 in the same command, and CUnitPlan's constructor and reset set both to 1. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)
+0x14 inside it: plan_naval_stance (int) - CUnitPlan +0x14, the `naval_stance` key. 3 is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel for it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)
+0x20 inside it: plan_ops_area_count (int) - CUnitPlan +0x18 is the plan's operations-area province CList; this is its count (first at CUnit +0x214, last +0x218). CAIUnit slot 76 tests it twice on its fallback path, at 0x4DBCDA and 0x4DBEB4, to decide whether a CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand is worth posting. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)
+0x38 inside it: plan_objectives (CList) - CUnitPlan +0x38 projected onto the unit (`plan` is held by value at CUnit +0x1FC), so this is the `objectives` block of the unit's battle plan: a list of CObjective, each 0x24 bytes, linked through its own +0x18/+0x1C. CAIUnit::Tick copies it into CArmy +0x2EC once a week through CopyObjectiveList (0x4DD350). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)
+0x40 inside it: plan_objectives_count (int) - Count of the plan's objective CList whose head is `plan_objectives` at +0x234 (CUnitPlan +0x38/+0x3C/+0x40). CAIUnit slot 84 compares it against the objective list it has just computed, and against how many of the two lists' provinces match, to decide whether a CSetPlanObjectivesCommand is needed (0x4C1B08-0x4C1B61). CTogglePlanObjectiveCommand::Execute increments it at 0x1E7036. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)
+0x48 inside it: plan_path_first (void*) - CUnitPlan +0x48 - the plan's `path`, a CList whose nodes carry a province id at +0x0 and chain through +0x8. **This is the list CAIUnit slot 76 walks first**: it follows the drawn path and stops at the last province whose successor the agent may not enter (CCountry::CanOperateIn), which is how the AI turns a drawn arrow into a frontier province to build a front around (0x4DAE8B-0x4DB0C3). read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)
+0x5C inside it: plan_path2_first (void*) - CUnitPlan +0x5C projected onto the unit (`plan` is held by value at CUnit +0x1FC, and 0x1FC + 0x5C = 0x258), so this is the `path2` block of the battle plan: a CList whose nodes carry a province id at +0x0 and chain through +0x8, exactly like plan_path_first at +0x244. CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits walks both at 0x4D5DCA and 0x4D5E9A and adds 90.0 to a front province's attack priority for being on either path and 45.0 for merely touching it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)
+0x70 inside it: plan_subunit_wanted (std::vector<int>) - The composition the plan asks for, per subunit type - the array 0x4E1D00 fills from the plan and the owner's available subunit types. Sits inside CUnit::plan at plan+0x70. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)
+0x74 inside it: plan_subunit_wanted_end (int*) - End of the std::vector<int> whose begin the record already has at +0x26C. 0x4B7D1C/0x4B7D25 takes (+0x270 - +0x26C) and compares it against the subunit database's own count before comparing the vectors element by element; CUnitPlan::SetMinForces replaces the pair. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)
+0x80 inside it: plan_our_power (int) - CUnitPlan +0x80, the `our_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the owner's strength for it. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)
+0x84 inside it: plan_their_power (int) - CUnitPlan +0x84, the `their_power` key - the plan's cached estimate of the opposition's strength. A negative value is CSetPlanAttributesCommand's "not set" sentinel. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: intel_grants
fields.comment: Begin of a vector of 12-byte `{country id, duration, level}` entries: the intel pass gives each listed country at least that level on the province the unit stands in while the duration is above 0 (FINDINGS-airbattle.md). Filled by CUnit_GrantIntel, whose caller is `local_intel_boost` (level 8, SPY_MILITARY_INTEL_LOCAL_TIME_BASE). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectrun.md)

fields.name: intel_grants_end
fields.comment: End of the intel_grants vector. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectrun.md)

fields.name: ai_attack_fitness
fields.comment: **Per-pass scratch, written only by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits (0x4D714A) and read only by its own insertion sort (0x4D716F).** The fitness of this unit as a contributor to an attack on one particular target province: `enemyNeighboursOfItsOwnProvince * 10 - agent->slot89(target, unit, 1) * 10`, plus 100.0 when agent->slot88(unit) exceeds 95.0f, then divided by 10 when the unit answers to another agent and by 5 when UnitHasBlockingOrder accepts it. It is recomputed for every target province of every pass, so a value read out of a live game is only meaningful during that pass. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)

fields.name: ai_uncovered_enemy_neighbours
fields.comment: **Per-pass scratch, written only by CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits (0x4D715A).** The count, as a float, of enemy provinces adjacent to this unit's own province that are garrisoned (or whose owner is reinforcing them) and that nothing of ours is already ordered against. It is the single input to the stay-or-go decision: a unit with a non-zero value, sitting in a province with a supply depot and with no stand-in garrison available, is given a `support_attack` order instead of being marched into the target (0x4D7651, 0x4D7876). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)

fields.name: ai_leader_fit
fields.comment: What AI_ReassignLeaders makes of how well the unit's leader suits it: 0 with no leader, else 0x499500's answer. Read for its shape only. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 8. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md)

fields.name: ai_held_back
fields.comment: **The AI's hysteresis bit on a division.** Slot 78 sets it (0x4B298B) when the division is pushed onto the held-back vector at CAIUnit +0x15C, and clears it (0x4B2CAC) when the division is recalled from it, at 0x4B2714/0x4B2746/0x4B2798 when the division is disqualified for other reasons, and sets it again at 0x4B3243 when a division is taken back out of the committed vector. While set, the strength bar the division has to clear to be committed rises from the commitment factor to halfway between it and 1.0, and the organisation bar from 0.300 to 0.650 (0x4B2835-0x4B2876); it is also worth +0.2 in the detachment score (0x4B30D4). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: unknown_2c9
fields.comment: One reader found, CAIUnit_ManageLandUnits at 0x4D6CE0: a non-zero value disqualifies a land unit from being considered as an attacker for the rest of the pass. No writer was looked for. It sits one byte before the recorded +0x2CA ai_pass_scratch, which slot 78 zeroes at the top of every unit iteration and never reads - worth checking whether the two are the same field and the earlier attribution was off by one. Named unknown deliberately. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)

fields.name: ai_pass_scratch
fields.comment: Zeroed by slot 78 at the top of every unit iteration (0x4B2104) and not read anywhere in slot 78, 79, 0x4B60F0 or 0x4B82F0. Either a flag a later slot consumes or dead. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-power.md)

fields.name: movement_destination_province_id
fields.comment: The id of the province the unit is moving to, resolved against the game state's province array by CUnit::GetMovementDestinationProvince (0x49AF00); zero when it is not moving. read (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_defence
fields.comment: The cached half of AICombatEstimateDefenceValue (rva 0x4D8590), written at 0x4D8A88 with the dirty byte +0x2D8 cleared one instruction earlier and returned unchanged when that byte is zero. It holds a **sum of combat-modifier fractions** - 1.0 means +100% - covering the modifiers that depend on the unit alone: the fort_defence trait, combined arms, experience, the leader bonus, dig-in, the terrain defence adjuster, dissent, lack of supplies, the difficulty modifier and the encirclement penalty. The stacking and envelopment penalties are **not** in it, because they depend on the attackers; the helper subtracts those on every call. 'Defence' is now from the body, not just from which side uses it. CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (slot 31, rva 0x1BA2F0) sets this byte and the attack pair's at 0x1BA313/0x1BA31A and is still the only invalidation found, so how often the value is refreshed is how often slot 31 runs - which that entry records as not established. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aihelpers.md)

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_defence_dirty
fields.comment: The dirty byte for +0x2D4. Non-zero means the AI's defensive combat-value helper (rva 0x4D8590) recomputes; the helper writes zero here at 0x4D8A81 as it stores the new value. Set to 1, together with +0x2E0, at the top of CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (rva 0x1BA313). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attackodds.md)

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_attack
fields.comment: The cached half of AICombatEstimateAttackValue (rva 0x4D8C50), written at 0x4D8FC2 with the dirty byte +0x2E0 cleared at 0x4D8FBB and returned unchanged when that byte is zero. A **sum of combat-modifier fractions** - 1.0 means +100% - over the modifiers that depend on the unit alone: combined arms, experience, the leader bonus, dissent, lack of supplies and the difficulty modifier. The stacking penalty, the weather, the river or amphibious crossing penalty, the terrain attack adjuster and the fort penalty are **not** in it, because they depend on the target province and the two counts, and are recomputed on every call. 'Attack' is now from the body. Set dirty with +0x2D8 at the top of CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (rva 0x1BA31A), still the only invalidation found. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aihelpers.md)

fields.name: ai_combat_estimate_attack_dirty
fields.comment: The dirty byte for +0x2DC, in the same shape as +0x2D8: `cmp byte ptr [esi+0x2E0], 0` gates the recompute at 0x4D8C92, the helper clears it at 0x4D8FBB, and CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat sets it at 0x1BA31A. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attackodds.md)

fields.name: carrying
fields.comment: the units a fleet is carrying: CheckTransportOverload sums their definitions' transport_weight over this list and compares it with the fleet's own transport_capacity (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

fields.name: visible
fields.comment: Whether the object draws. The whole of slot 13 (Show, rva 0x660440) is `mov byte [ecx+0x29], 1`, slot 14 (Hide, rva 0x660450) writes 0, and slot 15 (rva 0x10A0) reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md), inherited from C3dVisibleObject

fields.name: frame
fields.comment: **The frame index into the type's texture strip** - what the combat-status icon state really is. Written by slot 24 (SetFrame, rva 0x660460) and read by slot 25 (rva 0x660470). CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow drives it with 0, 1 or 2 from the attacker's strength share against 66% and 33%, and `interface/mapitems.gfx` gives both combat_status billboardTypes `noOfFrames = 3`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md), inherited from C3dVisibleObject

fields.name: position
fields.comment: The object's world position as a homogeneous vector: slot 90 (SetPosition, rva 0x44AB80) copies three floats into +0x84/+0x88/+0x8C and writes 1.0f into +0x90. CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow sets it to the negated midpoint of the attacker's and defender's first units each tick. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md), inherited from C3dVisibleObject

fields.name: scene
fields.comment: Whatever owns and draws the object: slot 16 (rva 0x10B0) sets it, slot 17 (rva 0x10C0) reads it, and CCombat's destructor path hands slot 17's result to CGraphics::DestroyVisibleObject (rva 0x66FBC0). The owner's class was not identified, so the name is inference from the use. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md), inherited from C3dVisibleObject

fields.name: type
fields.comment: The CObjectType the object was created from, written by the constructor (rva 0x11B0) from its second argument - which is the type, because slot 18 of a CObjectType is `new <size>` followed by this constructor with `this` as the argument. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md), inherited from C3dVisibleObject

fields.name: type
fields.comment: The `arrowType` the arrow was made from, by name out of the object-type registry. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: mesh
fields.comment: The vertex and index buffers CUnitArrow::BuildMesh makes, a 0x24-byte holder; freed and made again on each call. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: points_begin
fields.comment: Begin of the arrow's control points, 12 bytes each - x, height, y - ending at +0x150: the point added before the start, the unit's place, the unit point of each province of the path, and the point added beyond the end. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: points_end
fields.comment: One past the last control point (see +0x14C). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: progress
fields.comment: How much of the arrow is drawn filled, 0 to 1: the unit's movement_progress over CUnit::PathDistance. Written by CUnit::MakeArrow and each hour by CUnit::AdvanceMovement; the shader's CurrentProgress. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: ship
fields.comment: **The carrier this air group is based on.** Read live: all 1851 CUnitBaseCarrier objects point at a CShip here, and that ship's +0xB0 is a CNavy on all 1851. This settles the unidentified third clause of CUnit_IsAtOwnBase (0x5CDC30), which under `if (unit->+0x98->slot1())` reads `base->+0x18->+0xB0` and rejects the unit when that object's CUnit +0x11C combats_count is positive or its +0x110 current_combat is set: the clause means **the fleet carrying this air group is not in combat**. CUnitBase slot 1 is ReturnFalse on CUnitBaseProvince and ReturnTrue on CUnitBaseCarrier, so slot 1 is IsCarrier() rather than the validity test FINDINGS-reorganise.md took it for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)

fields.name: province
fields.comment: **The province this unit base sits in, and what CUnitBase virtual slot 0 returns** - which answers the question FINDINGS-airnaval.md has been asking since 2026-09 about CUnit +0x98's class. Read live: of 542 units whose home_base_ptr (CUnit +0x98) is non-null, 542 point at a CUnitBaseProvince or a CUnitBaseCarrier by their own vftables, and on 400 of 400 sampled CUnitBaseProvince objects this field points at a CMapProvince; on 540 of those 542 units it equals the unit's own current_province (+0x130), the two exceptions being units in transit. Slot 0 is the folded getter 0x4944C0 (`mov eax,[ecx+0x20]; ret`), which the record currently names COrder::GetStance because 36 of its 37 vftable slots are COrder slot 19 - the name does not belong to this class's slot. Note CUnitBaseProvince also carries a CSelectable subobject whose vftable pointer is at +0x18. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiconsumer.md)

fields.name: window
fields.comment: The window made from `division_option`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: unit
fields.comment: The unit, as a reference: the pointer here, its id in the eight bytes after, and CCombatView::FillUnitList looks the pointer up again by the id before it trusts it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: view
fields.comment: The view the entry belongs to. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: is_attacker
fields.comment: Whether the entry's side is the attacker. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 5. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this

Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent

fields.name: name
fields.comment: The block's key in faction_aims.txt, e.g. `operation_sealion`; what the save and the commands name it by. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: trigger
fields.comment: The `trigger = { ... }` block, an embedded CAndTrigger evaluated with an empty scope each day. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: date
fields.comment: The hour the condition last started to hold; the null date (43800000) until then. Saved beside the name. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: met
fields.comment: Whether the trigger held at the last daily check (rewritten every day, not latched); on load, whether a date after the null date was saved. What VictoryConditions_CountMetForFaction counts. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: chosen
fields.comment: Chosen for this game - set by the choice (ChoosePrimaries, ChooseRandomly) and by VictoryConditions_SetChosen; what VictoryConditions_PostChosen collects. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: primary
fields.comment: `primary = yes`: always chosen. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent

fields.name: factions_begin
fields.comment: begin of the vector of factions, in the file's order (+0xC end, +0x10 capacity). Every per-faction vector below is indexed in step with it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: factions_end
fields.comment: end of the factions vector. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: chosen_begin
fields.comment: begin of the per-faction vectors (16 bytes each: begin, end, capacity, and one more) of the conditions **chosen for this game** - what is tested, counted and saved. +0x1C end. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: chosen_end
fields.comment: end of the chosen vectors. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: all_begin
fields.comment: begin of the per-faction vectors of **every** condition the file defines, in the file's order - what the choice is made from. +0x2C end. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: all_end
fields.comment: end of the all-conditions vectors. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: number_of_victory_conditions
fields.comment: How many conditions each faction picks: NUMBER_OF_VICTORY_CONDITIONS / 1000 (15) from the defines when the game state is made and when a scenario is left; a scenario's `number_of_victory_conditions` (CScenario +0x108) where above 0. The denominator of the victory-conditions window, not of winning. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: victory_conditions_to_win
fields.comment: How many met conditions win: VICTORY_CONDITIONS_TO_WIN / 1000 (12) from the defines; a scenario's `victory_conditions_to_win` (CScenario +0x104) where above 0. Read by the daily check, the scenario end screen and the alert (75 per cent of it). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: game_finished
fields.comment: Set by VictoryConditions_DailyCheck when a faction wins; what SaveContents writes as `game_finished`. Cleared by VictoryConditions_SetChosen (each faction's choice), by CSetHistoryDate::Execute and by MarkSimulatedProvinces (with +0x41, one word). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: game_finished_loaded
fields.comment: **Where a save's `game_finished` is loaded** - not into +0x40. Either byte stops VictoryConditions_DailyCheck ending the game again, but only +0x40 is saved, so a save made after loading a finished game writes `game_finished = no`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

fields.name: Attackers
fields.comment:
read by CWar::GetAttackers
BiceLib: attackers (CCountryTag*) - **one side of the war**, a vector of CCountryTag with one `attacker=` line per entry. **Read live**: `ITA` alone against 28 countries in the War of Italian Aggression (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:39)

fields.name: Defenders
fields.comment:
read by CWar::GetDefenders
BiceLib: defenders (CCountryTag*) - the other side, the same shape, one `defender=` line per entry (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:42)

fields.name: isLimited
fields.comment:
read by CWar::IsLimited
BiceLib: is_limited (bool) - **Whether the war is limited** - saved as `limited`, and the game's own Lua `CWar::IsLimited` (rva 0x651FA0) is `mov al,[ecx+0x70]`. Set only by CDeclareWarAction::Apply on a fresh war declared with `value` 0 (Declare Limited War, or `war = { limited = yes }`), and by the loader. What it does: the declarer's bilateral allies are not called (CallAllies on the actor's side is skipped), the attacker side's faction does not join (BringInFactions, and CFaction::AddCountry's war sweep for an attacker-side leader), the messages carry DECLWAR_LIMITED where the declarer is in a real faction, every call to arms CallAllies makes carries it as its `value`, and CCallAllyAction's slot 14 (the screen's Call to Arms row) **requires** it - so a player can call allies by hand only into a limited war. The defenders' side is brought in as in any war. History wars are `limited=no`; every war declared in play in the BlackICE saves is `yes`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: revolutionary_war
fields.comment: saved as `revolutionary_war`, read straight off whether the value token is `yes` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:21)

fields.name: name
fields.comment: saved as `name`. **Read live**: `War of Italian Aggression`, `2nd War of German Aggression`, `Chinese Civil War` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:29)

fields.name: attackers_end
fields.comment: one past the last attacker. **Read the end here, not the capacity at +0x34** - the two differ on some wars and reading the capacity hands back stale tags past the end (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:40)

fields.name: attackers_capacity
fields.comment: the end of the allocation, not of the list (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:41)

fields.name: defenders_end
fields.comment: one past the last defender (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:43)

fields.name: defenders_capacity
fields.comment: the end of the allocation (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:44)

fields.name: original_attacker
fields.comment: saved as `original_attacker`. **Read live**: `---` on every war (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:58)

fields.name: original_defender
fields.comment: saved as `original_defender`. **Read live**: `---` on every war (BiceLib/GameClasses/CWar.hpp:59)

fields.name: action
fields.comment: A tick, saved as `action`. Set to now by CDeclareWarAction::Apply on every declaration, fresh or widening, and by the revolt war's creation (0x4BEA89); the constructor sets the null date. **In the saves it equals the save's own hour on every war with both sides populated in BlackICE games, and stays frozen on a war with an empty side** - so something refreshes it while a war is fought; that writer was not found (a tick-store search over the image finds only the two above). Not read by anything this reading reached. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: history
fields.comment: The war's CWarHistory, held by value (a CHistoryContainer: list head +0x58, +0x6C back to the war). Each membership change made with `recordHistory` appends a dated CAddAttackerChange / CAddDefenderChange / CRemove...Change. CWar::GetStartDate (rva 0x651D20) answers the first entry with a real date and GetCurrentRunningTimeInMonths (rva 0x651D90) counts from it. **SaveContents never writes it** (no `history` key in any of 490 saved wars) although LoadKey reads one - so after a load a war has no history, GetStartDate answers the null date and the running time is 0. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: called_allies
fields.comment: **The war's call map**: a std::map<int,int> held by value (head at +0x78), keyed by country id. CCallAllyAction::Apply writes 1 for the recipient of a PROPOSE and 0 on its ACCEPT or DECLINE; CCallAllyAction::IsValid refuses a PROPOSE to a country whose entry is not 0. Not saved and not loaded, so a reload forgets which calls are pending. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.1. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: target
fields.comment: Saved as `target` by nothing - LoadKey reads the key, SaveContents does not write it. Set to `---` by the constructor and by LoadKey only; no war-making function (Apply, BringInFactions, the four membership functions, CFaction::AddCountry, CCallAllyAction::Apply, the history replay) writes it, nor +0x8C/+0x94 (original_attacker/defender), which are always `---` in the saves. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: war_goals_by_actor
fields.comment: **The war's goals, filed by the country that holds them**: a `std::map<int, std::vector<CWarGoal>>` held by value from here, keyed by the actor's country id, its head (end) node at +0xA0. War_GetGoalsOf (0x652410) answers one country's vector; CWarGoal::AddToWar files a goal here under its actor. Typed void* because the map's own layout is not declared. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggerleaves.md)

fields.name: children
fields.comment: the effects inside this one, where it holds any: RTTI gives CEffect a second base of `PAVCEffect::__CList` at offset 8 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effecttext.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: keyword
fields.comment: **Which keyword built this effect.** Written in exactly one place, the common tail of CEffect::LoadKey at 0x59B630, from LoadKey's own `key` argument, and only when the switch actually made an object. Read by slot 6 (rva 0x16000, `mov eax,[ecx+0x18]; ret`), whose one caller is CEffect::GetBlockText - which uses it to group consecutive siblings built by the same keyword onto one comma-separated tooltip line. Not the same thing as CPersistent::token at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_this
fields.comment: **The value was the word `this`** (SaveToken 0x377) rather than a number or a tag, so the effect's target is the scope's own subject. Set by three unrelated slot-7 handlers at the same offset: CIntEffect's (0x59D4A0), CValueEffect's (0x59CB50) and, per findings/FINDINGS-script.md, the casus belli effects' - which is why the pair belongs to the common base rather than to any one of them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: use_from
fields.comment: **The value was the word `from`** (SaveToken 0x34F), so the effect's target is the scope's FROM. The other half of the pair at +0x1C, cleared with it as one word. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effects.md), inherited from CEffect

fields.name: target
fields.comment: The tag `target` names; Effect_GetTargetCountryTag reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: call_ally
fields.comment: `call_ally = yes|no`, case-insensitive; any other text leaves it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: limited
fields.comment: `limited`, ParseBool. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: window
fields.comment: The dialog's window, made by the constructor; the CAsk* constructors look `AgreeButton`, `DeclineButton`, `Title` and `Description` up in it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CEU3Dialog, inherited from CDiplomacyDialog

fields.name: closed
fields.comment: Set by a button that has done its work; slot 1 then answers false and the idler deletes the dialog. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CEU3Dialog, inherited from CDiplomacyDialog

fields.name: host
fields.comment: The in-game screen the dialog was made for; Accept and Decline post their command through its slot 18. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CDiplomacyDialog

fields.name: action
fields.comment: The dialog's own clone of the offer (slot 16 of the pending action); Accept/Decline set its type and post it, the slot 7 tests read its date. The destructor deletes it while it is still valid. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CDiplomacyDialog

fields.name: idler
fields.comment: The in-game screen the dialog posts through (slot 18) - the same pointer as CDiplomacyDialog's host (+0x68). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.2. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: view
fields.comment: The diplomacy screen that opened it; Decline rebuilds its action list, IsStillOpen tests its action_dialog (+0x518). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.2. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: goal_action
fields.comment: The action whose embedded war goal (+0x28) the dialog fills - the same clone as CDiplomacyDialog's action (+0x6C). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.2. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: cancel_observer
fields.comment: A CButtonObserverGlue<CWarGoalDialog> by value (0x2C bytes to the end of the object), +0x80 the dialog and +0x84 the handler CWarGoalDialog::OnCancelSelect, bound to both cancel_select buttons. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.2. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md)

fields.name: war_goal
fields.comment: The embedded war goal the `war_goal` block loads. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-effectgrammar.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred key. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred keys' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values
fields.comment: First element of the second std::vector<std::string>: the value written beside each deferred key, index for index. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CTagTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_last
