(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: value
fields.comment: **The operand, in thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CValueTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D13E0) as `TokenToFixedPoint(text)`, so `war_exhaustion = 7.5` is stored as 7500 - the same scale the savegame prints for these keys (`neutrality=88.800`, `national_unity=81.752`). A leaf's own Evaluate then either compares it straight against a thousandths field or divides it by 1000 first; findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md section 3 says which does which. **This is the opposite convention from `CIntTrigger::value` at the same offset**, and nothing in the script files distinguishes them. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CValueTrigger

fields.name: token
fields.comment: a SaveToken CPersistent's constructor sets to `none`, and nothing has been found that reads it. Of 714 inlined constructors that write this word and then a vftable, 697 write `none`, and **read live** it is still `none` on every CSubUnitDefinition, CTechnology, CRegiment, CCombat, CAIStrategy, CLeader, CTheatre and CConvoy in a running game - so it is not a class id, whatever a constant at +4 looks like (BiceLib/GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp:57), inherited from CPersistent, inherited from CRelation

fields.name: first
fields.comment: **The first party to the agreement** (save key `first`). Resolved from the three letters in the save through CCountryDataBase::GetTag, so the tag characters land at +0x8 and the index at +0xC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: second
fields.comment: **The second party to the agreement** (save key `second`). The same resolution as `first`, into the tag at +0x10 and the index at +0x14. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: start_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement began**, as a tick (save key `start_date`). Parsed from `year.month.day.hour` text by Date_SetFromString, which is the same representation every other date in the simulation uses. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diploaction.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: end_date
fields.comment: **When the agreement ends**, as a tick (save key `end_date`); **the null date 43,800,000 (`[0x170C2B8]`) where it has none** - every constructor sets it so, not zero. A real date is told by `(end_date - 43,800,000) / 24 / 365.0 > 1`. Read only by CCasusBelli (Activate, which will not attach an expired one, and IsOver) and by CRelation::SaveContents (written only when real). **No other relation's IsOver reads it**: a guarantee ends twenty years after `start_date`, a NAP NAP_EXPIRY_MONTHS after it, and the history files' end dates take effect only while history is replayed before play. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: cancel
fields.comment: **Whether the agreement is cancelled** (save key `cancel`), the last of CRelation's own bytes - a subclass's data starts at +0x24. Loaded as a plain comparison against the token `yes`, so any other value, including `no`, leaves it 0. **CDiplomacy::SaveContents skips every relation with it set**, and CRelation::SaveContents, given one, writes `cancel = yes` instead of `start_date`. No writer in play was looked for. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md), inherited from CRelation

fields.name: vertex_declaration
fields.comment: made by LoadResources, set by BeginBatch, released by CWeatherBillboardType_FreeResources. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: effect
fields.comment: the index of the type's effect in the graphics' effect list (+0x6BD00), from `effectFile` and `effect`, made by LoadResources; DrawQuad takes the effect at [list + 4 x (index - 1)]. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: scale
fields.comment: the billboard type's `scale` (CBillboardType::LoadKey, token 0x5C). For a weather picture: the half-height of each of its two quads, 2.5 in every entry of mapitems.gfx. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: effect_technique
fields.comment: the billboard type's `effect` - for the weather pictures `RainTech` or `SnowTech` of gfx/fx/weather_billboard.fx; DrawQuad sets it as the technique. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: effect_file
fields.comment: the billboard type's `effectFile`, gfx\fx\weather_billboard.fx for every weather picture. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: frames
fields.comment: the billboard type's `noOfFrames` (token 0x1B), 1 where not written; LoadResources divides each texture's u extent by it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: frame_u_extent
fields.comment: the last texture's width over its power-of-two width over `frames`; DrawQuad's vXOffset = this x the column (0 for every weather picture). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: texture_files_first
fields.comment: the `textureFile` list, in the order written: first node (0x28 bytes, the path at +0, the next at +0x20). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: texture_files_last
fields.comment: the `textureFile` list's last node. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: texture_file_count
fields.comment: the number of `textureFile` keys. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: texture_ids_begin
fields.comment: the loaded textures' ids, one per `textureFile` in order; GetFrameCount is their number. Texture 0 is the cloud, 1 the rain or snow, 2 on lightning. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: texture_ids_end
fields.comment: end of texture_ids. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: animation
fields.comment: the `animation` key, 1.0 by default; nothing found reads it (see LoadKey). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: upper_quad
fields.comment: the quad of texture 0, lifted by 0 - drawn last, still, for every weather picture. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: lower_quad
fields.comment: the quad of texture 1, lifted by scale x 2.0 - 0.3, on which the rain or snow and any lightning is drawn. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: simple
fields.comment: the `simple` key, 0 by default; nothing found reads it - the simple pictures are chosen by name (see LoadKey). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: direction
fields.comment: save key `direction`: the front's heading, in thousandths of a full turn. CWeatherFront::Tick adds `rotation` to it on every move and passes it to IsAngleWithinArc (0xB4490) against each candidate neighbour's bearing, which is what decides where the front goes next. Seeded from the home zone's heading cache (CWeatherManager+0x28), which starts at a Random()%1000 and then steps by 1000000/MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE per spawn so a zone's fronts fan out evenly. It is NOT wrapped back into 0..999 after `+= rotation`, but the rotation sum is bounded by about 50 so it stays near the range. Confirmed against autosave.hoi3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

fields.name: provinces
fields.comment:
save key `provinces`: every province the front currently covers. Head +0x0C, tail +0x10, count +0x14, trailing byte +0x18. The constructor puts the home province in it; every move empties it completely and refills it with the neighbours recruited that step, so a front abandons its whole footprint each time it advances. A front whose count reaches zero is deleted by CWeatherManager::Tick. Live fronts in a 1942 savegame hold 1 to 59 provinces. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)
+0x4 inside it: provinces_tail (LinkedListNode*) - tail of the `provinces` CList at +0x0C (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)
+0x8 inside it: provinces_count (int) - count of the `provinces` CList at +0x0C, and the front's liveness test: CWeatherFront::Tick answers `count > 0` and CWeatherManager::Tick deletes the front when it answers false. It is also the front's size class - under 3 provinces widens the spread arc by 0.150, over 30 halves it, over 100 halves it again AND limits each province to recruiting one neighbour, and under 4 provinces lets the front die once it is more than 1000 map pixels from home. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

fields.name: home
fields.comment: the front's home province - the loader's `home` key. CWeatherManager::Tick matches its id (province+0xD0) against the low pressure zone ids on CMap+0x21D8 at 0xB5D38 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: rotation
fields.comment: save key `rotation`: how much the front's `direction` turns per move, in thousandths of a turn. Set to +/-10 at birth ([0x1686FC8], negated where the home province is in the southern half of the map, CProvinceTemplate+0xA2) and multiplied by 800/1000 after every move, so the whole curvature of a front's path is bounded by about 0.050 of a turn (18 degrees) and integer truncation kills it after roughly eleven moves. Confirmed in autosave.hoi3: 38 of 45 fronts read 0.000 and the rest 0.001..0.008 with both signs present. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

fields.name: move_countdown
fields.comment: the loader's `speed` key, used as a countdown: CWeatherFront::Tick decrements it every hour and only moves the front when it reaches zero, then resets it to WEATHERMOVEMENTDELAY/1000 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: fronts
fields.comment: the live weather fronts: head +0x08, tail +0x0C, count +0x10. CWeatherManager::Tick walks it, frees the fronts whose Tick answers false, and tops it up towards (low pressure zones) x MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE/1000 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weather.md)

fields.name: zone_cooldowns_begin
fields.comment: a vector of countdowns in hours, one per low pressure zone (end +0x1C, capacity +0x20). Decremented every hour at 0xB5A65 **with no floor**, filled with zeros by InitialiseWeatherState (0xB54F0) when empty, tested `> 0` by CreateFront (0xB5D80) and set there to 24 + Random()%48 - indexed by the zone's place among the zones its climate mask lets through - and set to 0 by CWeatherManager::Tick for a dying front's home zone, indexed by the zone's place in the whole list. **Not saved**; survives CGameState::ResetSession, so it is emptied only by the manager's destructor and refilled with zeros by the first Tick of a process; zeroed by ResetZoneState only after a multiplayer lobby is reopened. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: zone_cooldowns_end
fields.comment: end of the per-zone cooldown vector at +0x18; +0x20 is its capacity. CWeatherManager::InitialiseWeatherState clears this vector and then pushes one zero per low pressure zone, and CWeatherManager::Tick calls that function whenever the vector is empty. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

fields.name: zone_cooldowns_capacity
fields.comment: capacity of the per-zone cooldown vector at +0x18 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

fields.name: zone_headings_begin
fields.comment: A second per-zone vector (end +0x2C, capacity +0x30), the zone's last front heading in thousandths of a turn, indexed like CreateFront's cooldown slot (the zone's place among the zones its climate mask lets through). Zero means "draw a fresh RandomThousandths"; otherwise CreateFront adds 1000000/MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE and subtracts 1000 above 1000. Pushed full of zeros by InitialiseWeatherState, which does not empty it first. **Not saved**, survives CGameState::ResetSession, and is zeroed only by ResetZoneState after a multiplayer lobby is reopened - so a load in a fresh process starts every zone at a fresh heading, and a second game in the same process inherits the first game's. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: zone_headings_end
fields.comment: end of the per-zone heading vector at +0x28 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

fields.name: zone_headings_capacity
fields.comment: capacity of the per-zone heading vector at +0x28 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

fields.name: parent
fields.comment: `parent = "..."` from the .gui file - the name of the type this one inherits from. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 132 case at 0xAC5721 through ParseString. CWindowType::CreateWindow passes it to the CGui's slot 18 when a child window's own type is not in the tree at +0x150, so it is the fallback type as well as a declared field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: background
fields.comment: `background = "..."` from the .gui file - the sprite name for the window's backdrop. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 153 case at 0xAC5631 through ParseString. The window factory 0xAC4FE0 passes `&type+0x84` to the CFixedWindow constructor as its 23rd argument. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: position
fields.comment: `position = { x = N y = N }` as declared in the `.gui` file, two ints. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey (rva 0x6C55E0) at 0xAC5658: `lea edi, [ebx+0xA0]; call 0xA7B670`, the `{ x = y = }` reader, with ebx the CWindowType itself (LoadKey's `this` is the CPersistent subobject, which sits at offset 0 of a CGuiType). **This offset is per-subclass, not shared by all gui types**: a `positionType`'s coordinates are read at `+0x64`/`+0x68` in CInGameIdler::Enter, and `+0x64` on a CWindowType is its CFactory base's vftable, the RTTI export giving that base at offset 100. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md)

fields.name: size
fields.comment: `size = { x = N y = N }` from the `.gui` file, two ints, written by CWindowType::LoadKey at 0xAC5703 through the same `{ x = y = }` reader as `position`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-gui.md)

fields.name: vertical_scrollbar
fields.comment: `verticalScrollbar = "..."` - the name of the scrollbar child that scrolls this window vertically. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 158 case at 0xAC56B8 through ParseString. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: horizontal_scrollbar
fields.comment: `horizontalScrollbar = "..."` - the name of the scrollbar child that scrolls this window horizontally. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 159 case at 0xAC56DC through ParseString. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: horizontal_border
fields.comment: `horizontalBorder = "..."` - the sprite used along the window's horizontal edges. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 163 case at 0xAC5742 through ParseString. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: vertical_border
fields.comment: `verticalBorder = "..."` - the sprite used along the window's vertical edges. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 164 case at 0xAC5766 through ParseString. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: priority
fields.comment: `priority = N` from the .gui file - the window's draw and hit-test order. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 138 case at 0xAC5676, through 0x67B640, which is a parse helper not yet recorded (it is not ParseInt; it goes through 0xB964D4 with the format string at 0x15FD134). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: moveable
fields.comment: `moveable = N` from the .gui file - whether the player can drag the window. An **int**, not a bool: LoadKey's token 154 case uses ParseInt (0x67B470, already recorded), not ParseBool. The window factory reads only its low word, `movzx edx, word ptr [esi+0x128]` at 0xAC508A, and hands that to the CFixedWindow constructor's 16th argument - so what +0x12A/+0x12B carry, if anything, is not read there. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: gui_button_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `guiButtonType` children - the first of **thirteen** per-kind lists at a 0x10 stride from +0x184 to +0x244, each {head, tail, count, byte} with the tail at +4 and the count at +8.

The nodes are 0x28 bytes: the child's name as an Hoi3CString at +0, prev at +0x1C, next at +0x20, a byte at +0x24. **The list holds names, not objects** - each child type built by LoadKey is inserted into the one gui-type tree at CWindowType +0x150 and only its name is listed here, which is why CFixedWindow::CreateWindow and the six per-kind factories all look a name up in that tree.

The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list, node by node through 0x409D00, into the window's own +0x25C/+0x26C vector pair: so **CFixedWindow +0x25C holds exactly the window's `guiButtonType` children**, which settles what project.json's `child_buttons_begin` is a vector of.

*FINDINGS-guistatic.md said fourteen containers running from +0x174; that is wrong twice. There are thirteen and they start at +0x184. +0x174 is a separate three-pointer std::vector walked at a 4-byte stride, and the fourteenth participant is the all-kinds declaration-order list at +0x25C.* (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: multi_sprite_button_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `multiSpriteButtonType` children. Second of the thirteen; same {head, tail, count, byte} shape as +0x184.

**This settles FINDINGS-guistatic.md's third `likely`.** The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list into the vector pair at window +0x27C / +0x28C, which project.json currently calls `child_vector_unused` - so that vector is the `multiSpriteButtonType` children's, and it is empty on every live window because the keyword occurs in no .gui file the game or the mod ships, not because its purpose was unknown. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: three_d_button_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `3dButtonType` children. Third of the thirteen.

**This settles FINDINGS-guistatic.md's first `likely`.** The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list into the window's name list at +0x434, which project.json already calls `three_d_button_names`, and that list is the source for the registry at window +0x360 - project.json's `registry_unused`. So registry 1 is the `3dButtonType` index, read off the keyword rather than inferred from the widget's base class and its CGraphics objectTypes lookup. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: text_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `textBoxType` children. Fourth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's +0x424 name list, whose registry is window +0x33C. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: instant_text_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `instantTextBoxType` children. Fifth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's vector pair at +0x2BC / +0x2CC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: scrollbar_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `scrollbarType` children. Sixth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's +0x464 name list, whose registry is window +0x3CC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: edit_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `editBoxType` children. Seventh of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's +0x444 name list, whose registry is window +0x384. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: icon_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `iconType` children. Eighth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's vector pair at +0x29C / +0x2AC, project.json's `child_icons_begin`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: checkbox_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `checkboxType` children. Ninth of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's vector pair at +0x31C / +0x32C, project.json's `child_checkboxes_begin`.

Its child type is built with the same 0xB2DA90 constructor as `guiButtonType` and `multiSpriteButtonType` - a checkbox type *is* a button type - which is why FINDINGS-guistatic.md could get as far as 'the third user of the button type class' and no further. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: child_window_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's **`windowType`** children - the tenth of the thirteen, and the one that answers FINDINGS-guistatic.md's open item 5.

Its children are themselves CWindowTypes: LoadKey's `windowType` case does `operator new(0x2A4)` and calls CWindowType::CWindowType, so the type tree is recursive. The CFixedWindow constructor is handed `&this+0x214` as its 11th stack argument and walks it at 0xAC0C33..0xAC0C90, building a full CFixedWindow per name through CWindowType::CreateWindow and adding each one to the window's **subwindow map at +0x414**.

So the chain `windowType` keyword -> CWindowType +0x214 -> CFixedWindow +0x414 is complete, and **CFixedWindow +0x2FC is not on it**. +0x2FC is written only by CFixedWindow::AttachChild (slot 22) and erased only by slot 23, so it holds what game code attaches at run time, which is why a live snapshot found buttons and icons in it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: list_box_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `listBoxType` children. Eleventh of the thirteen. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's +0x454 name list, whose registry is window +0x3A8.

**The token table spells the keyword `listBoxType`, with a capital B.** The data mostly does not: a case-sensitive grep finds `listboxType` in 36 of the game's .gui files and 55 of the mod's against `listBoxType` in 3 and 5, and live windows do hold list boxes, so the .gui key lookup cannot be case-sensitive. The engine's own spelling is the one in the table. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: three_d_gui_names
fields.comment:
Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `threeDguiType` children. Twelfth of the thirteen.

**This settles FINDINGS-guistatic.md's second `likely`.** The CFixedWindow constructor copies this list into the window's +0x474 name list, which project.json already calls `three_d_gui_names`, and that list feeds the registry at window +0x3F0 - project.json's `registry_unused_2`. So registry 5 is the `threeDguiType` index, read off the keyword rather than inferred from its being the only non-button of the three unused kinds.

Its LoadKey case is the odd one of the thirteen: it appends to this list **and** writes the window type's own +0x84/+0x88/+0x90/+0x94 before joining the shared tail, which the other twelve do not. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: overlapping_box_names
fields.comment: Head of the declared-name list for this window type's `OverlappingElementsBoxType` children - the thirteenth and last of the per-kind lists, so the 0x10 stride ends here, with the tail at +0x248, the count at +0x24C and the byte at +0x250. Copied by the CFixedWindow constructor into the window's vector pair at +0x2DC / +0x2EC, project.json's `child_overlapping_boxes_begin`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: full_screen
fields.comment: `fullScreen = yes/no` from the .gui file. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 47 case at 0xAC6487 through ParseBool. Sits immediately after the last per-kind container's byte at +0x250 and immediately before click_to_front, and the CWindowType constructor zeroes the two as one word (`mov word ptr [esi+0x254], bx`). (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: click_to_front
fields.comment: `click_to_front = yes/no` from the .gui file - whether clicking the window raises it. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 420 case at 0xAC6539 through ParseBool. The window factory reads it with `movzx ecx, byte ptr [esi+0x255]` and hands it to the CFixedWindow constructor as its 26th and last stack argument, which the constructor tests at 0xAC01EC. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: orientation
fields.comment: `orientation = "..."` from the .gui file, stored not as a string but as whatever 0xB29CC0 makes of one - CWindowType::LoadKey's token 191 case parses the keyword into a temporary string, hands it to 0xB29CC0 and stores the returned pointer here. The window factory passes it to the CFixedWindow constructor's 8th argument, which the constructor stores and later compares against 1 and 3 while adjusting the window's position. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: declared_children_head
fields.comment:
Head of the list of **every** declared child's name, across all thirteen kinds, in the order the .gui file declares them - the fourteenth container, and the one FINDINGS-guistatic.md was reaching for when it counted fourteen at a 0x10 stride from +0x174. Tail at +0x260, count at +0x264.

Every per-kind case of CWindowType::LoadKey appends to its own list and then jumps to one shared tail at 0xAC58B5, which appends the same name here. The window factory passes `&this+0x25C` as the CFixedWindow constructor's 6th-from-last argument, and the constructor's ordered resolve loop at 0xAC0DF0..0xAC10A3 walks *this* list - which is why the loop can put the window's children into its two intrusive lists in declaration order across kinds. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: up_sound
fields.comment: `upsound = "..."` from the .gui file - the sound played when the window is raised. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 320 case at 0xAC64F8 through ParseString; that case is reached by the `je` on `cmp eax, 0x140` in the dispatch head, not through either byte table. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: down_sound
fields.comment: `downsound = "..."` from the .gui file - the sound played when the window is lowered or closed. Written by CWindowType::LoadKey's token 321 case at 0xAC6A17 through ParseString. Exactly 0x1C above up_sound, so the two strings are adjacent and +0x288 + 0x1C = +0x2A4, which is the whole size of the class. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guicontainers.md)

fields.name: id_type
fields.comment: type half of the save's `id` pair, written after the id. **Read live**: 41 on what a scenario started with, 4713 on what the game has built since (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:31), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: id
fields.comment: the regiment's id, the first half of the save's `id` pair (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:32), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: strength_ceiling
fields.comment: set to the regiment's strength when it is built and afterwards only raised to it, never lowered; CUnit slot 24 totals it. Not what the regiment has left - that is +0x5C. saved as `highest` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:55), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: builder
fields.comment: who built it, saved as `builder`, and only where the id half of the tag is set (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:59), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: sub_unit_definition_ptr
fields.comment: this regiment's definition, with its country's tech applied. saved as `type`, by writing the definition's own name (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:64), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: strength
fields.comment: what the regiment has left, in the scale of its definition's max_strength; the supply consumption scales by it, CUnit slot 21 averages it. saved as `strength` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:44), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: organisation
fields.comment: organisation x1000, saved as `organisation` (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:62), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: home
fields.comment: where it was raised; the save writes that province's id under `home`, and the loader turns the id back into this pointer. **Read live**: a CMapProvince by its own RTTI, and null on a regiment that was never given one (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:68), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: technologies
fields.comment: **the technology levels this regiment was raised with**, one node per entry of its definition's `technologies`, built by CSubUnit::SetType. The save writes a line per node keyed by the technology's own name - `infantry_activation={5 0.000}` - and the loader looks the key up in the technology database, which is what says these are technologies. **Read live**: every node's first word is a CTechnology; none on a CWing, 9 to 52 on a regiment (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:85), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: sunk_by_type
fields.comment: type half of the `sunk_by` object id (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:92), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: sunk_by_id
fields.comment: what sank this ship, saved as `sunk_by`, and only where the pair is not the game's "no object" one. **Read live**: set on 1123 of 3736 ships (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:93), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: is_reserve
fields.comment: saved as `is_reserve`; CRegiment::GetMaxStrength scales the definition's max_strength by RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE where it is set. **Read live**: 1184 of 4000 regiments (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:98), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: pride
fields.comment: the pride of the fleet, saved as `pride`. **Read live**: 31 of 3736 ships (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:102), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: unit_ptr
fields.comment: the CUnit this regiment belongs to; how the per regiment supply and fuel functions reach the unit's order. **Read live**: a CArmy on every regiment (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:108), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: current_distance
fields.comment: how far the regiment is from the enemy in its battle, x1000, saved as `current_distance` - and only where the unit's `combats` list has something in it. **Read live**: zero on all 4000 regiments (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:116), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: extra_consumption
fields.comment: every point is another 1% of supply and fuel: the consumption functions add it x10 to a potency whose base is 1000. A cached total - the levels in `technologies` added up, which CSubUnit::ApplyTechnologies recomputes. **Read live**: it is that sum on all 10254 sub units in a running game (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:130), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: historical_model
fields.comment: which historical model it was raised as, saved as `historical_model`; -1 where it is none. **Read live**: -1 on 3940 of 4000 (BiceLib/GameClasses/CRegiment.hpp:134), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: experience
fields.comment: x1000, saved as `experience`. **The constructor writes -1000, 'not given'**, and a new game replaces a negative with the owner's UNIT_START_EXPERIENCE - times (1000 + RESERVES_PENALTY_SIZE)/1000 for a reserve, with no mobilisation gate - capped at 100000. A figure from the file is kept as it is. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitstart.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: combat_modifiers
fields.comment:
**The combat modifiers acting on this one ship, wing or brigade** - first here, last at +0x44, count at +0x48, each node holding a 12-byte {id, attack, defence} record exactly like CUnit+0xDC's. Appended to by CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier (0x1AC300) from the naval, air, bomber and target slot 19s - 48 call sites - and freed, with all three fields zeroed, by CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590) at the top of every tick. **This, not CUnit+0xDC, is where air and naval combat modifiers live**, which is why a live watch on a ship's parent CUnit never saw the list fill. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit
+0x4 inside it: combat_modifiers_last (LinkedListNode*) - The last node of the CList at +0x40. Written on every push; the head at +0x40 is written only when the count was zero. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit
+0x8 inside it: combat_modifiers_count (int) - How many modifiers are on the list at +0x40. The field to watch for a push, for the same reason as CUnit+0xE4. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: combat_attack_product
fields.comment: **The running product of every combat modifier's attack side on this ship, wing or brigade**, thousandths where 1000 is 100%. CSubUnit::AddCombatModifier multiplies in `max(attack + 1000, 10)` as a 64-bit product divided by 1000; CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers seeds it back to 1000 each tick. **It multiplies the shot count**: CNavalCombatant::Attack computes `shots = sea_attack (or convoy_attack / sub_attack) * this / 1000` at 0x167B3A, the exact counterpart of CUnit+0xEC x +0xF4 on land. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: combat_defend_product
fields.comment:
The defence-side counterpart of +0x50, written by the same adder and reset to 1000 by the same slot 19. **Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else**, in CCombatant slot 11's per-sub-unit loop, where it is multiplied by +0x50 and divided by 1000. That read sits past a `ret 4` at 0x566452 and is reached only by `je 0x566455` from inside the loop, which is why it was recorded here as having **no reader** until 2026-10-01 (trap 3). The branch is taken when the sub-unit's slot 9 answers false; the true arm uses the division's CUnit +0xEC/+0xF0/+0xF4/+0xF8 instead, so on a ship or wing the two products are used together.

**What it feeds, corrected 2026-10-01 (second correction, see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat3.md §3).** This entry twice said the product is a 'loss factor' that carries naval, air and bombing modifiers 'into losses'. It does not. That wording was inherited from a wrong owner: the block was first attributed to CCombatant::ApplyLosses (trap 2 - ApplyLosses ends at 0x5662ED and slot 11 begins at 0x5662F0 with no padding), and when the owner was corrected the meaning was not re-asked. **Slot 11 sums strength.** Its only two invocations in the image are 0x57B083 and 0x57B091 inside CCombat slot 17 (0x17B050), which returns the attacker's share of the two sides' total strength in thousandths; that number's only consumer is 0x17BD70, the `combat_status` window's per-tick refresh, called once from the end of CCombat::Tick and only for a combat the player's own country is in, where it picks an icon state at the 66.0%/33.0% thresholds and formats a percentage.

**So the two sides are not symmetrical.** +0x50 multiplies the shot count in CNavalCombatant::Attack and therefore changes the simulation; +0x54's single reader changes a number on screen. On this reading a defence-side naval, air or bombing combat modifier - including the two defence-only ids - is **cosmetic in this build**. The bound: 'slot 11 has exactly two invocations' is confirmed of the entry-set decode, and 6.7% of non-padding .text lies outside that decode, so it is `likely` as a statement about the whole image. One battle in a running game settles it - see FINDINGS-combat3.md's live checks.

**And the one reader only runs for the player's own battles** (2026-10-02): CCombat::Tick gates the combat_status refresh on CountryIdListContains over the attacker's or defender's CCombatant::countries with the player's id from gameState +0xC34. So in an AI-vs-AI combat this field is never read at all. Player-only, not merely display-only.

**Confirmed live 2026-10-02.** A hook on the one reader (CCombatant slot 11) in a 1942 war save recorded 39,414 calls with **zero unexplained return addresses**: 39,222 via CLandCombatant's own forwarder and 96 + 96 from CCombat slot 17's two legs. So nothing outside slot 17 reaches this field in practice, the vcall-thunk route the static sweep could not close never fired, and the demotion stands: for naval, air and bombing the defence side of the combat modifier census is cosmetic in this build. Land is unaffected - CUnit +0xF0 has the AI reader.

**"Read at 0x56645E and nowhere else" is wrong, and the conclusion survives (2026-10-05, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airdefence.md).** There is a second static reader, at 0x160E5B in CBomberCombatant::FireUnit, where this field multiplies the bombing target's `air_defence`; the register is a CSubUnit on independent evidence, being read at +0x58, +0x5C and +0xA8 in the same loop. The 2026-10-02 live check does not contradict it - it hooked CCombatant slot 11's callers, not this field. The demotion stands for a better reason than the old one: **that second reader's result is itself discarded**, so the defence-side product still reaches nothing but a number on screen. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
**The regiment's own name, always present, and the only thing `remove_brigade` can ever match.** Saved as `name` inside a `regiment={}` block, and the loader puts it back. Across the 45-save corpus there are **788,880 regiment blocks and 788,880 of them carry a `name=`, none of it empty**, so an 'unnamed regiment' does not exist at runtime: 290,876 of those instances (7,133 distinct strings) hold an engine-generated name of the shape `<ordinal> <abbrev> Regiment` - `1st HQ Regiment`, `2nd Art Regiment`, `1st Wagon Regiment` - and the rest hold the historical name the order of battle gave them. A wing is a CSubUnit too and carries its name here in the same way.

**So `remove_brigade = <a subunit type>` can never match**, and nothing in the mod tries: of 6,132 distinct `remove_brigade` values none is one of the 1,427 subunit type tokens the mod's `units/*.txt` declare. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: owner
fields.comment: A CCountryTag on the sub unit itself - the three-character tag here, the id at +0x98 - distinct from `builder` at +0x34. CAirCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers resolves a country out of it for the wing's BM_RADAR_STATION technology scaling (0x16D0A6/0x16D0B0) and passes it to CWeather::AirCombatEffect for BM_WEATHER (0x16D109/0x16D100), in both cases in preference to the parent unit's owner. **Read out of the code only**; whether it is the owner or the controller was not established. (agent findings, combat modifiers wave), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: pending_strength_damage
fields.comment: **Strength damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths. CUnit::TakeDamage adds to it per landed shot, CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight reads it to tell whether the unit is already finished, and CSubUnit::SettleDamage subtracts it from `strength` and clears it. **Not clamped** - unlike the organisation half. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: pending_organisation_damage
fields.comment:
**Organisation damage taken this tick and not yet paid**, thousandths, spread evenly over the subunits by CUnit::TakeDamage rather than by size.

**It is damage attempted, not damage dealt.** CSubUnit::SettleDamage clamps it to the organisation the subunit actually has (`cmovg` at 0x1ABAE1) before subtracting, so in a one-sided fight most of a tick's total is thrown away. Anything reporting organisation damage has to count the clamped amount at 0x1ABAE7, not this field. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: target_id_type
fields.comment: The type half of the persistent id of the ship this one last shot at; with +0xBC, the remembered target CSubUnit::PickTarget keeps from hour to hour. Cleared by CCombatant::AddUnit and for a ship that cannot shoot. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: target_id
fields.comment: The id half of the remembered target at +0xB8. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: has_target
fields.comment: Set when CSubUnit::PickTarget found a target this hour and cleared when it did not. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: contributes_to_unit
fields.comment: **A cached `strength >= 0.100 && organisation >= 1.000`**, recomputed by `CUnit::UpdateHourly` (written at 0x1BA2C6) for the zero-combat-width brigades of a land unit only, and left alone on everything else. When it flips, the unit's definition is rebuilt. `CUnit::RebuildDefinition` does not read it - it recomputes the same predicate from +0x5C and +0x60 - and 0x1CD500 asks whether any brigade of a unit satisfies it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdef.md), inherited from CSubUnit

fields.name: window
fields.comment: The window made from `wing_option`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: sub_unit_id
fields.comment: The id of the sub unit the row stands for, in two dwords; the null id for a row that stands for a building or a good. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: building
fields.comment: The province's building the row stands for, or null. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: good_made
fields.comment: The good whose production the row stands for; 7 for none. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: good_held
fields.comment: The good whose stockpile the row stands for; 7 for none. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: province
fields.comment: The battle's province - for a sub unit of an air battle the dword at its unit's +0x130. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: combat
fields.comment: The battle. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md, section 13. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combatview.md)

fields.name: children_first
fields.comment: First node of the trigger's **child list** - RTTI gives CTrigger a `CList` base at object offset 8, and CAndTrigger's Evaluate walks exactly this: `mov esi, [ecx+8]`, then `[esi]` for the child and `[esi+8]` for the next. A leaf trigger leaves it null. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_last
fields.comment: Last node of the child list. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_count
fields.comment: How many children. CTrigger::LoadKey writes 0x8, 0xC and 0x10 together, which is the CList shape. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: children_spare
fields.comment: The fourth member of the child CList at +0x8. CTrigger's constructor zeroes it in the same run as first, last and count - `mov [edi+8],0; mov [edi+0xC],0; mov [edi+0x10],0; mov byte [edi+0x14],0` at rva 0x1610D-0x16116 - which is the shape the record describes for every other CList here: first, last, count and a spare. No slot body of any of the 168 CTrigger descendants reads it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_this
fields.comment: Set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `THIS` (save token 0x377) instead of a country tag. Written only by the shared slot-7 argument loader at rva 0x5E8F40 (`mov byte [esi+0x18], 1`), and zeroed with `+0x19` as one word by CTrigger's constructor. Every tag-taking leaf then reads it as the first of three branches: CAllianceWithTrigger::Evaluate (0x5EF5A9), CControlledByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DFB6B), COwnedByTrigger::Evaluate (0x5DF30B), CIsCoreTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D67AC) and CNeighbourTrigger::Evaluate (0x5E9009). What it resolves to is **not uniform**: `alliance_with` and `controlled_by` go through EventScope_GetCountryTag (0x5C1A40), which falls back on a province's owner, while `neighbour` reads `this_scope (+0x38) ->country (+0x10/+0x14)` directly and so gets `"---"`/0 on a province-only scope. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: arg_is_from
fields.comment: The twin of `arg_is_this` at +0x18: set to 1 when the key's argument was the keyword `FROM` (save token 0x34F). Written only at rva 0x5E8F84, in the shared slot-7 loader, and read as the second branch by the same five leaves. Every reader resolves it the same way - `scope->this_scope (+0x38) ->from_country_tag (+0x18) / from_country_id (+0x1C)` - so `FROM` is read off the **original** scope, not off whatever context the condition is nested inside. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys
fields.comment: First element of a std::vector<std::string> (`{first, last, end, ?}`, 0x10 bytes; the second vector is at +0x2C): the keys Trigger_LoadDatabaseKey could not resolve while this script-written block was parsed. CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays and clears it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred key. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_keys_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred keys' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values
fields.comment: First element of the second std::vector<std::string>: the value written beside each deferred key, index for index. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_last
fields.comment: One past the last deferred value. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: deferred_values_end
fields.comment: End of the deferred values' storage. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: is_script_block
fields.comment: Set on every block CTrigger::LoadKey builds (`and`, a scope, a region, a context, an ideology block ...) and by CTechnology's constructor on its two embedded triggers; cleared by every constructor. While set, a key in this block that no lookup resolves is queued on +0x1C/+0x2C and dropped without a message, instead of being reported as `Unknown trigger-type`; CTrigger::ResolveDeferredKeys replays the queue only where it is set. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggergrammar.md), inherited from CTrigger, inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: value
fields.comment:
**The operand, as a plain integer - not thousandths.** Written only by slot 7 (`CIntTrigger::LoadArgument`, rva 0x5D1400) as `atoi(text)`, which truncates, so the decimal a mod writes is lost before anything compares it. Zeroed instead when the argument was the keyword `this` (SaveToken 0x377) or `from` (0x34F), which set `CTrigger +0x18`/`+0x19`; only 3 of the 37 leaves read those flags back, so for the other 34 `keyword = this` degenerates to `field >= 0`.

Four leaves multiply this by 1000 inside their own Evaluate because the field they compare it against is thousandths - `revolt_risk`, `pure_revolt_risk`, `nationalism`, `province_temperature` - which is the one place the script number is the natural unit and still cannot carry a fraction. **`CValueTrigger::value` is the same offset with the opposite convention.** (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-numtriggers.md), inherited from CIntTrigger

fields.name: session
fields.comment: The back pointer BindChannel writes. Both posts read [this+0x1C]->[0x54] for the turn stamp, and the loopback pump increments it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md)

fields.name: pending_commands
fields.comment: A {head, tail, count} list of cloned commands waiting to execute. Virtual slot 8 returns it; the loopback pump appends to it and Session::PumpCommands drains it. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md)

fields.name: window
fields.comment: The bar's window, `diplomessageicons_window` (interface/menubar.gui: position (340, 80), size 380 x 48), a copy of CInGameIdler +0x1D34. DiploIconBar_Update puts it at `diplomessageicon_start` every frame; the icons are attached to it as `diploicon_<n>`. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

fields.name: icons_head
fields.comment: Head of the list of the bar's CDiploIcon*, oldest first: nodes {icon, prev, next, byte}, next at +8. DiploIconBar_Add appends at the tail. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

fields.name: icons_tail
fields.comment: Tail of the list at +4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

fields.name: icons_count
fields.comment: Number of icons on the bar. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

fields.name: start_clock
fields.comment: The screen's clock (the in-game screen's +0x192C, its slot 5) when the bar was made; DiploIconBar_Update hands CDiploIcon::Update the clock less this, for the blink. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

fields.name: map_style
fields.comment: style the water shader picks its technique from; 16, 18, 19 colour the sea (BiceLib/GameClasses/GameSettings.hpp:29)

fields.name: debug_saves
fields.comment: 0 rotates three autosave files; N saves a dated file every Nth month (BiceLib/GameClasses/GameSettings.hpp:36)

fields.name: autosave_frequency
fields.comment: 0 never .. 5 five-yearly (BiceLib/GameClasses/GameSettings.hpp:39)

fields.name: show_unit_names
fields.comment: the `show_unit_names` key of the map rendering options: a near counter's second text is the unit's name and not its leader's. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 1. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md)

fields.name: layer_mask_ec
fields.comment: ANDed with +0xF0 by the renderer (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmode.md:370)

fields.name: layer_mask
fields.comment: layer mask written by every map mode setter (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-mapmode.md:368)

fields.name: always_counters

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section C.3. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

fields.name: counter_distance
fields.comment: the `counter_distance` key; 100 from the constructor (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

fields.name: counter_scale
fields.comment: the `counter_scale` key; 1 from the constructor, which also writes it to the global at VA 0x170AF84 that every counter's scale is multiplied through (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

fields.name: entries

fields.name: height

fields.name: gap

fields.name: border

fields.name: scrollbar

fields.name: hidden_entries

fields.name: uses_entry_heights

fields.name: rows

fields.name: max_width
fields.comment: The declaration's maxWidth. Slot 24, the position getter, adds it to x for a box set right. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-textdraw.md)

fields.name: text_object
fields.comment: The CGuiText (0x1D4 bytes, vftable 0x1606C70) that holds the layout and draws the text. Setting the widget's text assigns +0xD0 and then tells this object. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-textdraw.md)

fields.name: text
fields.comment: The text an instantTextBoxType widget is rendering. Struct name deliberately ours: the class (vftable rva 0x11FDB70) has no RTTI and the image has no CInstantTextBox name. **8 bytes lower than the textBoxType class's +0xD8**, and the class keeps no copy of its own name, so +0x54 is its font rather than its name - the two layouts are not interchangeable. Not reachable by name from the parent window: instant text boxes live in the unindexed vector at CGuiObject+0x2A4. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guilive.md)

fields.name: name
fields.comment: The widget's own copy of its name, **in the case the .gui file declared** - 'CountryName', 'DateText' - while the key in the parent window's registry is lowercased, 'countryname', 'datetext'. That is the case-insensitivity of the tree visible from both ends in one object. The offset is class specific: on the instantTextBoxType class (0x11FDB70) +0x54 is the font name, because that class keeps no name copy and everything below shifts by 0x1C. Struct name deliberately ours - see +0xD8. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-guilive.md)

fields.name: text
fields.comment: **The text a textBoxType widget is rendering - a number the UI has already computed.** Struct name deliberately ours: the widget class (vftable rva 0x11FE3B8) has no RTTI and there is no CTextBox name anywhere in the image. Read live out of the topbar's sixteen numbers: ic_number = '\xa7R10/\xa7G21/21', manpower_number = '115', countryname = 'Ireland', datetext = '0:00 1, January 1936'. **Already formatted and already coloured** - \xa7 is the Clausewitz colour escape (\xa7G green, \xa7R red, \xa7Y yellow) - and **Windows-1252**, so it goes through Text::toUtf8. fields.name: kind
fields.comment: What sort of edge this is: **0** plain, **1** a crossing through the province at +8 that can be closed (IsCrossingBlocked), **2** a river, **3** impassable. CMap::LoadAdjacenciesFile sets 1, 2 and 3 from the `Type` column - `sea`, `river`, `impassable` - and CProvinceTemplate::MeasureEdges turns a 0 into 2 where the edge's walk touches the river bitmap. The helper at rva 0x1A2600 refuses the step when that province's controller is hostile to the unit's owner, or when a foreign unit that is not retreating is standing in it - a strait or crossing that can be blocked. fields.name: distance
fields.comment: **Not a geometric distance**: the sum of the terrain `movement_cost` of every pixel on a walk from this province's unit point to the neighbour's, in thousandths - so about a thousand a pixel of plains. Written by CProvinceTemplate::MeasureEdges, cached in adjacencies.bin, and what CUnit::MovementDistance answers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

fields.name: bearing
fields.comment: The compass bearing from this province to the neighbour, in thousandths of a full turn, 0..1000: east 500, north 250, south 750, due west 1000 (776 edges of Their Finest Hour), 0 only just north of west (15). Written by CProvinceTemplate::MeasureEdges as (int)floorf(((float)atan2(sy - ty, tx - sx) / 2pi + 0.5 + 0.0005) x 1000) with a float rounding at every step and no wrap across the map's seam, from the unit points - or, between land and sea, the land province's naval base, which is its bounding-box centre where positions.txt gives none. Reproduces all 83,596 edges of tfh/map/cache/adjacencies.bin. One reader, CWeatherFront::Tick, as the centre of IsAngleWithinArc's window. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section B. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

functions.name: clear
functions.evidence:
**`std::ios_base::clear(iostate, bool)`**, the bottom of every stream error path. `_Mystate` (`+0xC`) = `state & 0x17` (MSVC's `_Statmask`); if nothing in the new state is in `_Except` (`+0x10`) it returns; if `reraise` it rethrows with `_CxxThrowException(0, 0)`; otherwise it throws `std::ios_base::failure` carrying `ios_base::badbit set` (0x15B4E4C), `ios_base::failbit set` (0x15B4E64) or `ios_base::eofbit set` (0x15B4E7C), in that priority order, through `_CxxThrowException` with the `_ThrowInfo` at 0x164B158.

`this` is the `basic_ios` (== the `ios_base` subobject), so callers reach it as `[[os]+4] + os`. The `basic_ios::clear` wrapper is inlined at every call site as the two instructions `cmp dword ptr [ecx+0x38], 0 / or eax, 4` - the 'no rdbuf means badbit' rule - which is why the callee never looks at the buffer itself.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: ScalarDeletingDestructor
functions.evidence:
Confirms the handover in full. MSVC's `??_G` for `ios_base`, and **the virtual-table slot that `std::ios_base::_Ios_base_dtor` (`0x794BAE`) sits behind**:

    mov  [esi], 0x15A7B8C        ; the ios_base vftable
    push esi; call 0x794BAE; add esp,4
    if (flags & 1) free(esi);
    return esi;

`__thiscall`, `ret 4`, the object back in eax. **It has no direct callers at all** - every use is a virtual dispatch, which is what one expects of a slot-0 destructor and is the complement of `_Ios_base_dtor`'s 700 direct calls.

**It is slot 0 of two tables**: `std::ios_base`'s own (`0x15A7B8C`, RTTI `.?AVios_base@std@@`) and `std::basic_ios<char>`'s (`0x15A7B9C`, RTTI `.?AV?$basic_ios@DU?$char_traits@D@std@@@std@@`, which project.json spells `std::anon::anon::std::D::DU__char_traits::__basic_ios`). Both tables have exactly one slot. The body belongs to `ios_base` - it writes `ios_base`'s own vftable, not `basic_ios`'s - and `basic_ios` derives from `ios_base` in project.json's class record, so the derived table holds the inherited body. Both slots are recorded under `vftable_slots`.

The neighbouring vftable `0x15A7B94` is `std::basic_ostream<char>`'s at object offset 8 and its slot 0 is a different body (`0x50E270`), so it is not part of this and is left on the frontier.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: endl
functions.evidence:
**`std::endl`** - MSVC's `basic_ostream<char>::put(widen('\n')); flush(); return os`, out of line. `__cdecl`, one stack argument, bare `ret`, answers the stream in eax so it chains.

The body is two halves. The `put('\n')` half is the call to `0x9B50`, which is `__stdcall` and cleans the argument itself - which is why there is no `add esp,4` after it at any call site. The `flush()` half is inlined here and is instruction for instruction the body of `std::ostream::flush` at `0x65BB20`: `if (!(rdstate() & (failbit|badbit)) && rdbuf()->pubsync() == -1) state = badbit;` then `if (state) clear(rdstate() | state | (rdbuf() ? 0 : badbit), false)` through `std::ios_base::clear` at `0x20B0`.

**681 direct call sites, and they are the game's log.** The idiom is `LogRecord::Make(file, line, channel) << "text" << ... << endl` - `0x2410` builds the record, `0xA64A00`/`0xA64A30` are its own inserters, `0x21D30` writes the C strings and this ends the line. `*::LoadKey` dominates the caller list because that is where the engine complains about a key it did not understand. MSVC inlined the same pair at about 120 further sites (`0x16E92` is one: `push esi; call 0x409B50` followed by a private copy of the flush body), so the real number of `<< endl` in this executable is higher than the call count.

The stream is reached through a virtual base: `[[os]+4] + os` is the `basic_ios`, whose fields this touches are `+0xC` `_Mystate` and `+0x38` `_Mystrbuf`.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: Make
functions.evidence:
**Builds one log record**, and first makes sure there is a sink: if `g_log_sink` (`0x17162A4`) is still null it allocates the four byte do-nothing sink whose vftable is `0x11FCEA0` and installs that, so a message logged before `InstallLogSink` is discarded rather than queued. Then calls the register-convention forwarder `LogRecord::Construct` (`0x6649D0`) with the file, the sink, the line and the channel. There is **no channel test here or anywhere after it** - every record built is flushed to the sink. `this` arrives in ECX and is returned in EAX; the three stack arguments are cleaned by the caller (bare `ret`, `add esp, 0xC` at the call site), so the convention is `__cdecl` with a register `this`, not `__thiscall`.

**`file` is an `Hoi3CString*`, not a `const char*`.** The constructor hands it to `std::string::assignString` (`0x1BD0`), which takes a string, and every call site builds one first: `mov edx, 'battleplan.cpp'; lea esi,[ebp-0x74]; call std::string::fromCString` and then pushes that temporary (0x404743..0x404768).
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: Flush
functions.evidence:
**The complete destructor of the record, and where a log line is decided.** Every message in the game arrives here in a record holding its file, line and channel, and this is what does or does not write it - `[persistent.cpp:39]`, `[countryhistory.cpp:450]` and the 597KB of setup.log all pass through it. Takes the record in eax, pushes `record+0x78` (the `std::basic_ios` virtual base) into `LogRecord::FlushAndDestruct`, then puts the `ios_base` vftable `0x15A7B8C` at `record+0x78` and runs `~ios_base` (`0x794BAE`). functions.name: Destruct
functions.evidence:
Confirms the handover's reading of the body, with one correction to the name's spelling. This is `std::locale::~locale()` with `facet::_Decref()` inlined into it:

    if (_Ptr) {                       // the _Locimp* at locale +0
        _Lockit lock(_LOCK_LOCALE);   // 0x79504A with the literal 0
        if (0 < _Ptr->_Myrefs && _Ptr->_Myrefs != (size_t)-1) --_Ptr->_Myrefs;
        dead = _Ptr->_Myrefs == 0 ? _Ptr : 0;   // the neg/sbb/not/and at 0x42EE69
        ~_Lockit();                   // 0x795072
        if (dead) dead->vftable[0](1);          // scalar deleting destructor
    }

So a `locale` is one pointer wide, which is why `ios_base::_Init` allocates exactly four bytes into `_Ploc`; the refcount is at `_Locimp +4`; and `-1` is the sentinel that keeps the classic locale alive forever.

functions.name: CheckForCombat

functions.name: ShouldStartNavalCombat
functions.evidence:
**Corrected: it returns a bool, not a code.** The function has exactly two exits, `mov al, 1` at 0x431A85 and `xor al, al` at 0x4320B0, both `ret 8`. The `cmp al, 1` at the StartCombat call site that this entry read as a tri-state is how MSVC compares a bool against true; the other three call sites use a plain `test al, al`. It also has **four** callers, not one: 0x430415, 0x430861 (CCombatManager::StartCombat), 0x59A85E and 0x59D12C - the last two in the naval order block, so naval orders ask the question themselves as well. Both manager call sites guard it with CProvinceTemplate.is_land (+0x22), so it only ever runs for a sea zone.

The naval spotting roll, 0x880 bytes, VA 0x00431840..0x004320BD. **Returns a bool, not a code** - exactly two exits, `mov al,1` at 0x431A85 and `xor al,al` at 0x4320B0; the `cmp al,1` at 0x430866 is how MSVC compares a bool, and the other three call sites use `test al,al`. **Argument order**: edi=[ebp+8]=ours, ebx=[ebp+0xC]=theirs, and StartCombat pushes `edi` (theirs) then `eax` (ours). Four callers: 0x430415, 0x430861 (CCombatManager::StartCombat), 0x59A85E, 0x59D12C.

Six gates return false: theirs->regiments.count<1 (0x431862); ours->IsNaval() && ours->AsNavy()->+0x2F8>0, the fleet cooldown (0x431889); ours->order is convoy_raid 0x6E9 (0x4318A3); our owner is AI (gameState->played_countries_array[owner_id]==0) and our order is rebase/invasion/transport/none (0x43194B); both naval and ours.submarines>0 and theirs.screens>ours.submarines/3 (0x431A11); both naval, order==patrol 0x42E, COrder::GetStance()!=0, and 5*(ours.carriers+capitals) < 3*(theirs.carriers+capitals) (0x431A58). The two fleet censuses come from CountShipsByRole (0x1CF640).

Six short-circuits return true: province intel byte >= 9 (0x431A6E); theirs->combats.count>0; theirs->current_combat!=0; g_FogOfWar (0x130AD30) == 0; any unit in theirs->AsNavy()->carrying is moving or fighting (0x431AE0).

Then four scale factors - A = mission efficiency (1000, or 1000 + GetMissionEfficiency(ours->order) - GetMissionEfficiency(theirs->order) when convoy_escort-or-patrol meets convoy_raid); B = 1000, or NAVAL_INTERCEPTION_AFTER_ATTACK_FACTOR (military +0x270) when theirs' province was convoy-raided within one day; C = 1000 + GetTraitEffect(ours, spotting_chance=0xE); D = ours->IsAir() ? 1000 : 10000 - and a double loop over theirs->regiments x ours->regiments:

  V = our->IsAir() ? our.def.surface_detection : (their.def.is_sub ? our.def.sub_detection/2 : our.def.surface_detection)
  S = max(1000, their.def.visibility)
  v = V*S/1000 * C/1000 * A/1000 * B/1000
  v = v*1000 / (theirs->movement_remaining>0 ? 3000 : 2000)
  if (theirs->+0x95) v *= 2
  intel>=2: v = v*1250/1000;  intel>=6,7,8: v *= 2 each
  v = v * (1000 - rain*SPOTTINGRAINMODIFIER/1000 - cloud*SPOTTINGCLOUDMODIFIER/1000) / 1000
  v = max(v, 1000)
  if (rand() % D < v/1000) return true

Everything in thousandths. A moving fleet is HARDER to see (3000 vs 2000). The 1250 is not a define, it is (int)floor(1250.5f) folded at startup into 0x1A88170's family of literals.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval.md)

functions.name: BuildMessagePopupText
functions.evidence:
**Fills a message popup (popup_kind 0: DefaultPopup and CombatStartPopup)**, called once from each 4-byte CMessageDialog<T> constructor - ten callers; the 8-byte templates have their own copy, BuildMessagePopupText_MemberPtr8. The popup's window is +4, its message +0x6C (type +0x8C, variables +0x90). In order:

1. The settings glue (+0x144, right click -> MessageDialog_OpenSettingWindow) is attached to the window's background element (window +0x238) and to AgreeButton, DeclineButton and CenterOK.
2. Texts `<TYPE>_HEADER` and `<TYPE>_1`..`_6`, and for every variable of the message a replacement `$KEY$` -> GetText(value), i.e. **the value is itself looked up as a localisation key** and shows as itself only where no key matches. A variable named ATTDETAIL, DEFDETAIL, ATTTOTAL or DEFTOTAL also sets Line_left_1, Line_right_1, Line_left_2, Line_right_2 (where the window has them) to its raw value, its first §W turned to §b.
3. Header = the rendered _HEADER with its **first** `§W` replaced by `§b`; Line1..Line6 = each rendered line with **every** `§W` replaced by `§b`. A text that renders to exactly `*` renders as empty (CInternationalizedText::Render).
4. Layout: y starts at Header's y plus its drawn height; for i = 1..6, a line whose text is empty is skipped, else it is moved to y + 15 for Line2 (popup_textline_dist_two) or y + 0 (popup_textline_dist, y 0) and y grows by its drawn height. CombatStartPopup's combatstart_divider and the four Line_left/right lines follow. The background is resized to height y + 70 (popup_bottom_button_pos.y) + 50 (popup_textline_dist.**x**), and the three buttons are put at that height less 70.
5. Buttons by the type's `option` (+0x34): **no** -> AgreeButton and DeclineButton hidden, CenterOK shown with `<TYPE>_BTN1` and the dialog's close observer; **yes** -> CenterOK hidden, AgreeButton `<TYPE>_BTN2` (closes), DeclineButton `<TYPE>_BTN3`, which - where the post had a callback - runs it (MessageDialog_PressGoto) instead of closing.
6. Shields: LeftShield the message's first country (+0x34) and RightShield its second (+0x3C); with only one, both shields show it; with neither, they are left as the .gui has them.
7. Placement: the handler's cascade counter (+0x2C) is stepped and wraps from 11 to 0; the dialog goes 10 px x that counter right and down of its base position, clamped (a coordinate whose window would cross the screen's right or bottom edge is set to the screen size less 10), plus 40 px down.
8. Window slot 44 (slot 11 for the four EU3 leftovers WECARDINALBRIBE, WEFCARDINABRIBE, CURIACONTROLLER, CARDINALBRIBE).

See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messageshow.md, section 3.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-messageshow.md)

functions.name: Date_SetFromString
functions.evidence:
Sets a date tick from the text `year.month.day.hour`, in place, joining `Date_Year`, `Date_DayOfYear`, `Date_DayOfMonth` and `Date_DayOfWeek` as the writing half of that family. **782 direct call sites**, the most-called unnamed function in the image after the parse helpers, and the text handed to it is `parse + 0x22C` (`CParseContext::value.text`) at every site inspected.

It is `sscanf(text, "%d.%d.%d.%d", &year, &month, &day, &hour)`, then month and day are decremented to 0 based, then the tick is rebuilt on the epoch `CLASSES.md` records: `tick = 24 * sign(year) * (365*|year| + dayOfYear(old tick)) + 43800000 + hourOfDay(old tick)`, where 0x29C55C0 = 43800000 and 0x538AB8*8 is the same number. The month is then added by 0x4C420 and the day of the month by 0x4C360 - both walk the month length table at rva 0x1313294 - and finally the hour of day is replaced by the parsed one. Callers hand it a date holding exactly the epoch (`mov [esp+0x64],0x29C55C0; lea esi,[esp+0x64]` at 0x4CE4A2), so the old day-of-year and hour-of-day it preserves are both zero and the result is exactly the date in the string.

**The sscanf return is never tested.** A string that is not a date leaves year 0 and, because the decrements are unconditional, month -1 and day -1, so the tick walks backwards off the epoch and nothing is reported - the same silence `FINDINGS-...` records for unknown keys.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

functions.name: Show
Update
functions.evidence:
**Slot 4, every frame the window is shown** (CProductionView::Update at 0x7FEAC4, after the send at 0x7FE444).
1. **Where the list's row count differs from the played country's lend-lease entries**, hide (slot 3) and Show (slot 2) - the rows are rebuilt, and nothing else this frame.
2. Otherwise, pass 1 over the rows: each slider's moved latch (scrollbar +0x252) is read and cleared; `free` = rows less those whose knob is held (slot 44 answering 1, 4 or 5), was moved this frame, or is locked (3); `sum` = the sliders' values (floats).
3. `left = 100.0 - sum`. Where free > 0 and |left| > 0.005: step = left, but at least 0.01 either way (+0.01 / -0.01 where |left| < 0.01); **every slider not held and not locked gets step / free added** (pass 2 re-reads the latch, already cleared, so a slider moved by its arrows is excluded from `free` but still takes its share) - so the sliders are percentages kept summing to 100, by **equal** amounts, not in proportion.
4. L = the lend-lease slider's IC: CCountry +0x5F4's lend-lease setting, base_percentage * factor (48.15) made thousandths, times TotalIC (+0x604) - thousandths of IC, floored at 0.
5. **`actual_IC` of each row = floor((slider / 100 + 0.0005) * 1000) * L / 1000, FormatFixedPoint to 3 places** (truncated) - the receiver's part of the lend-lease IC as the slider shows it, without effectiveness or the resource cap.
Then, where +0x48 is set, hide. Bare `ret`. The name is the builder family's.

functions.name: IntegerSqrt
functions.evidence:
An integer square root by Newton's method, taking its only argument in **edi** and returning it in eax: `x = (v - sign)/2` then iterate `x = (v/x + x)/2` until it stops decreasing, with `v <= 1` short-circuited. Eleven callers and no vftable, so it is a shared utility rather than anyone's method - which is why the name carries no class (trap 11: a register argument is spelled value@EDI and costs no stack). CAlignment::BuildDriftTooltip uses it on the squared compass distance; the same Newton loop is inlined in CAlignment::GetRepulsionTerm at 0x4C4480. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md.

functions.name: GetVariable
functions.evidence:
Lua: CVariables:GetVariable   (script/LUA API.txt, CVariables::GetVariable)
Registered as: luabind::detail::memfun_registration<CVariables,CFixedPoint (__thiscall CVariables::*)(CString const &),luabind::detail::null_type>
luabind signature: CFixedPoint GetVariable(CVariables&,CString const&)
Recovered by emulating SetupAI (0x8EAE30): the registration object luabind builds for this def holds this address.

**The generic read of a script variable, and it creates the variable it fails to find.** 0x476F60 to two `ret 8` at 0x476F81 and 0x476F9F, 21 instructions read end to end, eleven int3 before and fourteen after.

    v = this->slot1(name)                 ; GuiTypeTree_FindByString
    if (v) { *out = v->value (+0x1C); return out }
    CVariables::AddVariable(this@EDI, name, 0)
    *out = 0; return out

**It has no callers in this build** - `findRefs.py --callers` reports zero direct calls - so the create-on-read behaviour reaches the game only through `CVariableTrigger::Evaluate`, which does the same thing inline. It is worth recording anyway, because it is the clearest statement of the intended semantics: in this engine reading a variable is what brings it into existence, and the trigger is not doing anything unusual.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

functions.name: AddVariable
functions.evidence:
**The create half of `check_variable`'s side effect - and of `set_variable`'s and `change_variable`'s. It really does create.** 0x476FB0 to the single `ret 8` at 0x476FFC, 24 instructions read end to end. The registry arrives in EDI, the name and the value on the stack, and the new object comes back in EAX.

It asks `operator new` for **0x20 bytes** and lays out a variable: the Hoi3CString at offset 0 (inline buffer zeroed, length +0x10 = 0, capacity +0x14 = 0xF - the SSO shape), then the value at **+0x1C** from its second argument, then `Hoi3CString::assign` from the name argument, then an insert through the registry's **slot 6** (`[[edi]+0x18]`, pushed the object twice). It never looks the name up first, so on its own it would overwrite an existing payload inside the tree and leak the earlier object - but no caller does that, because all of them look up first and call this only on a miss.

**Six call sites in five functions**, and they are the whole of how a script variable comes into existence:
  - `CVariableTrigger::Evaluate` (0x5F01D0) at 0x5F0237, with `(&this->name, 0)` - this is the `check_variable` side effect, and the trigger then answers `0 >= value`
  - `CSetVariableEffect` slot 11 (0x5AF7A0) at 0x5AF7FE - `set_variable` finds and updates `+0x1C` in place, and creates only when the name is new
  - `CChangeVariableEffect` slot 11 (0x5AF810) at 0x5AF874 and 0x5AF8C6 - `change_variable` reads, adds its own `+0x3C` and writes back, so on a name that does not exist it calls this twice: once to make it zero and once more, which then finds it and updates in place
  - `CSetVariableCommand` slot 6 (0x1532C0) at 0x553313 - the same find-or-create, as a `CCommand`
  - `CVariables::GetValue` (0x76F60) at 0x476F8E - the generic accessor, which **has no callers at all** in this build

`CVariables::LoadKey` (0x77080, slot 4 of the CPersistent vftable 0x11BD724) does not call this; it builds the identical 0x20 bytes inline and inserts them the same way, filling the value through `TokenToFixedPoint`. That is what fixes the layout, because the loader's object is the one a savegame's `name=value` pair becomes.

Slot 6 of CVariables' own vftable (0x11BD700) is `NameTree_Insert` (0x4D8A0), a folded template body in eight tables that therefore stays class-free; it reduces to `TernarySearchTreeInsert` (0x4DA70), whose key comparison runs through `tolower`. **So variable names are case-insensitive** - unlike `remove_brigade`, which memcmps.

**The created variable does not reach the save.** See 0x77000.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

functions.name: SaveSubtree
functions.evidence:
**Why a variable set to zero is not in the savegame.** 0x477000 to the single `ret 8` at 0x477058, 36 instructions read end to end. An in-order walk of the variable tree: recurse into `node->low (+8)`, write this node's payload, recurse into `node->equal (+0x10)`, then iterate `node->high (+0xC)` as a loop. That order is why the `variables={}` block comes out alphabetically.

The payload step is the point:

    v = node->element (+0)
    if (v != 0 && v->value (+0x1C) != 0)
        SaveWriteNamedFixed(v, writer, v->value)

The `test eax,eax; je` at 0x47702B is a **zero test on the value**, so a variable whose value is exactly zero is skipped. There is no 'absent means zero' distinction to lose, because `CVariableTrigger::Evaluate` treats a missing name as zero anyway - but it does mean the variable `check_variable` creates on a miss **is session-scoped and erases itself at the next save**, so the side effect cannot accumulate across a save/load and cannot be seen from outside the process.

Reached only from `CVariables::SaveContents` (0x77060), which is slot 2 of CVariables' CPersistent vftable 0x11BD724 and is the whole of `add ecx,-0x24; if (this->root) 0x77000(writer, root)`. The -0x24 is the second-base adjustment: CCountry holds the tree part at +0x1AC and the CPersistent part at +0x1D0, and CCountry::SaveContents does the matching `lea esi,[edi+0x1d0]` before writing key 0x411 `variables` at 0x4CFE2D.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)
