A potency starts at 1000; unless withoutLeaders, it takes the owner's SUPPLY_CONSUMPTION modifier (49), loses the army group leader's skill x 50 scaled by CommandReach - only where the unit stands in a province (+0x130) - and gains CommandEffect(unit, 2), floored at 0. Then per brigade: (potency + extra_consumption (+0xCC) x 10) x the definition's supply_consumption / 1000, and **unless the unit is naval** (slot 16) x strength x 1000 / the definition's max_strength / 1000. extra_consumption is the sum of every technology level the brigade holds, so each level is 1% more. Last, a land unit whose order answers 0x5A4 - a strategic redeployment - has the total x STRAT_REDEP_SUPPLY_MOD (military +0x1E8) / 1000, twice in Their Finest Hour. Both callers that move goods pass withoutLeaders = 0. **Measured**: with no leaders, the formula gives a capital's garrison to the thousandth in 38 of 65 savegame capitals. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md, section 2.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitdaily.md)

functions.name: FuelConsumption
functions.evidence:
Unit fuel consumption in thousandths, written through out and answered in eax; unit in eax, ret 8. A land unit on a strategic redeployment (order slot 16 answering 0x5A4) gives 0. Otherwise a potency of 1000 plus the country's SUPPLY_CONSUMPTION modifier, less the army group leader's skill x 50 scaled by how far that HQ's command reaches, plus the chain of command's own effect of type 2; then per regiment (potency + regiment[+0xCC] x 10) x the definition's fuel_consumption / 1000. Unlike supply it does not scale by the regiments' strength.
(reversing/CLASSES.md:267)

functions.name: ConsumeSuppliesAndFuel
functions.evidence:
**One unit's day at the supplies.** It asks CUnit::SupplyConsumption and CUnit::FuelConsumption what the unit uses. In arcade mode it takes that straight out of its country's stockpile. Otherwise it draws on **a province**: the one the unit is in - its owner's acting capital where it is in none - or, where it has a home base (+0x98), the base's, wherever the unit is; an air unit based on a carrier takes the carrier's own base's. `need` is that province's (+0x244) and depot the province its supply_depot_id names. Where the depot's controller is not the payer (the expeditionary owner, else the owner) but is its friend, the payer **pays**: price = (1000 - full) x 250 / 1000 + 1000 with full = pool x 1000 / (SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS x need), 1000 where there is no need, for supplies and fuel apart; price x asked is added to the payer's TradedAway, moved from its stockpile to the depot holder's as far as it has it, and added to the holder's TradedFor and unit_demand. A fleet under a rebase order (0x6DE) has province and depot replaced by its owner's capital after that. Where there is a depot and its controller is no friend of the unit's owner both received figures are 0 and nothing more happens. Then: have = the province's pool, and where that is under `need`, have x (asked x 1000 / need) / 1000 - the unit's share of what there is; received = 1000 and all taken where that covers what was asked, else have x 1000 / asked and `have` taken. Without a friend's payment what was asked is the unit_demand of **whoever controls the province drawn on**. The take is that country's `usage` only where the unit stands in its acting capital. **Fuel is worked out the same but only taken, and only counted as usage, for a unit that is moving or a fleet away from its base.** Last, the red mark on the counters of the player's own units. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md, section 4.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md)

functions.name: CUnit_SetOwner
functions.evidence:
**Sets a unit's owner, and its regiments'.** 0x5BC460 to the single `ret 8` at 0x5BC53E; the unit in ESI. Clears ai_agent (+0x198) without detaching it; writes the tag and id into every regiment's owner (CSubUnit +0x94/+0x98, the list at +0x38) and into the unit's owner (+0x124/+0x128); where the owner changed and the unit has its in-game idler (+0x160), intel_level (+0x1F8) = 0 and CUnit::RebuildAvatar. Not recursive: children keep their owner. It also looks up `REB` and does not use the answer. 19 callers. The name is ours.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

functions.name: CreateAvatar
functions.evidence:
Finds the figure for a unit - `<tag>_<type>_<model>_actor`, falling back through earlier models, then `Generic<kind>`, then `GenericInfantry` with the log line 'Missing avatar graphics for type' - and makes its CHoiAvatar with CUnit::GetCounterSize. Only the counter side was read; the figure's naming is from the literals. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

functions.name: GetCounterSize
functions.evidence:
**The frame of the size strip a unit's counter shows, 0 to 5**, by `oob_level` (+0x1F4): 0 -> 5, 1 -> 4, 2 -> 3, 3 -> 2, 4 -> 1 with more than one brigade else 0, 5 -> 1, anything else 0. The strip's frames are X, XX, XXX and on. CUnit::CreateAvatar, CDeploymentEntry and CDeploymentTargetEntry each carry the same jump inline. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

functions.name: UpdatePlanForceNeeds
functions.evidence:
Recomputes, per subunit type, what this unit's order of battle is short of against its plan. The three vector<int> arguments are always &unit->+0x5C, &unit->+0x6C and &unit->+0x7C at both call sites; all three are indexed by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index and sized to the subunit definition database's count ((db+0x20 - db+0x1C)/4), grown and zero-filled on the first call and, on later calls, with the second and third zeroed at 0x1BD40C while the first is overwritten wholesale. It then walks up higher_oob_unit_ptr to the top of the OOB and, unless that top unit has plan+0x8 (CUnit +0x204) set with oob_level 0, calls ComputePlanWantedSubUnits (0x4E1D00) to build the wanted composition out of the unit's plan (CUnit +0x1FC) and the owner's available subunit types; with the fifth argument null it fills the plan's own buffers at plan+0x18/+0x70/+0x80/+0x84, with it non-null it fills locals instead. The wanted list is the local one where 0x4E1D00 produced one and unit->+0x26C (which is plan+0x70) otherwise. CUnit::CountSubUnitsByType (0x1BD7E0) then counts what the unit actually has, and: difference[i] = wanted[i] - have[i]; groupDifference[GenericType(i)] += difference[i] for every non-zero entry, where GenericType is 0x1ADF70 folding a subunit type onto a representative one; then, over a copy of groupDifference, needed[i] = min(difference[i], groupNet) for each positive deficit, drawing that group's remaining net down as it goes - so a surplus of one type inside a group cancels a deficit of another. Returns true if any entry of needed was set. Runs once a day from CUnit::UpdateDaily for units at oob_level 0 and for HQs at level 1..3 whose +0x198 is set; the level 1..3 units with +0x198 clear have the three vectors cleared instead, and level >=4 is skipped entirely.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: RefreshPlanForceNeeds
functions.evidence:
The out-of-line copy of the gate CUnit::UpdateDaily inlines at 0x1BB273. On a unit with oob_level >= 4 it does nothing; with oob_level 0, or with +0x198 set, it calls CUnit::UpdatePlanForceNeeds(unit, &unit->+0x5C, &unit->+0x6C, &unit->+0x7C, 0); otherwise it clears all three vectors. Called from CSetPlanForcesCommand slot 6 (twice) and CSetPlanAttributesCommand slot 6.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: CUnit_CountSubUnitsByTypeIndex
functions.evidence:
0x1BD740-0x1BD7D7 (`ret 4`), 52 instructions, read end to end, 12 callers. Lazily builds the CSubUnitDataBase singleton (0x1A886F0), memsets (definitions_end - definitions_begin) ints at the ESI array, then walks unit->+0x38 doing `counts[subunit->+0x58->type_index]++`. Both AI bodies _alloca the array first (0x4CDA79, 0x4CE698) and then index it with the cached role type_indices, which is how a wing's or a fleet's composition is tested.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorganise.md)

functions.name: CountSubUnitsByType
functions.evidence:
Counts this unit's subunits by CSubUnitDefinition::type_index into a vector<int>, recursing through the OOB. Where the vector is empty it is first grown to the subunit definition database's count and zero-filled; then counts[regiment->sub_unit_definition_ptr->type_index]++ over CUnit::regiments (+0x38), then the same call on every entry of CUnit::children (+0x1E4). The second argument is pushed as 0 at both call sites and never read.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: CollectSubtree
functions.evidence:
0x1BDA90 to the `ret 4` at 0x1BDAF4 - 101 bytes, read end to end. Appends `this` to the CList it is handed (a fresh 0x10-byte node: payload, prev at +4, next at +8, byte at +0xC; head/tail/count written at list +0/+4/+8) and then recurses into every child on CUnit +0x1E4, so the list comes back holding the unit and every unit below it in the OOB. Called by CUnit::MeanDistanceToProvince (0x4C1FC0).
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-subdivide.md)

functions.name: CountDivisions
functions.evidence:
`ret 0x10`, 5 callers, recursive. Counts this unit and everything under it whose `oob_level` (CUnit +0x1F4) is **>= 4** - i.e. divisions and below - skipping a non-land unit when the first argument is set. Every call site in the image passes (1, 0, 0, 1) and the recursion passes the first argument down unchanged; the other three are never read. This is the strength figure CAIUnit slot 76 divides a front's length by.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiplans.md)

functions.name: CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey
functions.evidence:
**Which unit type a counter shows**: the key of the unit's FIRST brigade's type (`regiments.first->data->definition + 8`) where its intel level (+0x1F8) is above 2 and it has a brigade; otherwise the static string at VA 0x170D858, which is empty in the file and whose run-time value was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

functions.name: RebuildAvatar
functions.evidence:
**Throws a unit's avatar away and makes it again** (CUnit::CreateAvatar), then gives each of its two counters the owner's colour (CCountry +0xC34), CUnit::GetCounterSize, and the texture of the sprite `GFX_small_counter_<key>` for `unit_counter` or `GFX_map_counter_<key>` for `unit_counter_close`, `<key>` from CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey; then the two figures and the name. Does nothing without an in-game screen. Called from 23 places, whenever the unit's `avatar_stale` (+0x10C) is found set. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

functions.name: CUnit_RefreshCounterName
functions.evidence:
Chooses the name a unit's near counter shows and hands it to CHoiAvatar_SetCounterName: `???` where the intel level (+0x1F8) is under 5; else, with the setting at CSettings +0xE9 clear, the unit's leader's name (CLeader +0x4C) where its slot 8 says it is a real one and an empty string where not; with the setting set, the unit's own name (slot 7). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

functions.name: GetRegimentList
functions.evidence:
Six instructions: `return unit ? &unit->regiments (+0x38) : nullptr`. Bare ret, no stack arguments, `this` in EAX. Used by ShouldStartNavalCombat to get the inner loop's list.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navaldetection.md)

functions.name: AddRegimentToUnit
functions.evidence:
The counterpart of `RemoveRegimentFromUnit` (0x1BE9A0), which abuts its `ret 4` at 0x1BE995: it pushes the regiment onto the unit's `regiments` list (+0x38), writes the regiment's `unit_ptr` (+0xB0) at 0x1BE6CD, and - where the unit is on the map - gives its two counters their size again and, if the key CUnit_GetCounterTypeKey answers has changed with the new brigade, their colour and the picture `GFX_small_counter_<key>` or `GFX_map_counter_<key>` again; it ends by calling `CUnit::RebuildDefinition(unit, false)` at 0x1BE937. The unit arrives in **edi** and is never loaded from the frame.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

functions.name: RemoveRegimentFromUnit
functions.evidence:
**Takes a regiment out of its unit.** It walks the unit's `regiments` for the node holding this one and unlinks it, then sets the regiment's `unit_ptr` (`+0xB0`) to zero - which is what says so rather than any guess. The caller deletes the regiment afterwards.\n\n**No signature recorded**: the compiler passed the unit in `edi` and the regiment on the stack.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: CarrySupplies
functions.evidence:
**What a unit brings with it into a province**: SUPPLYPOOL_DAYS - PARASUPPLYPOOL_DAYS where `parachuted` - of what it uses in supplies and in fuel, as far as the source has them, moved into the province's pool. The source is its owner's stockpile; but the pool of the unit's previous province (+0x134) where it has one and that is land; and for a unit with none, where `fromStockpile` is clear, the game is under way and the province's controller is not the owner, the pool of the province's depot - or nothing at all where the province is not the owner's own or has no depot. Five callers: CUnit::EnterProvince (0x5BF313) for a land unit aboard nothing entering a land province other than its own, before current_province_ptr is changed; RemoveFromTransport (0x5CF1B8) and CNavy::UnloadCarried (0x5CFEC2) for units put ashore; CAir::ReleaseCarried (0x5D09F8) with the parachute byte; and RunSupplyAndConvoyIterations (0x6790D7) for every unit the filling left with nothing. So a marching army takes its days of supplies out of the province it leaves. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md, section 5.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supplypass.md)

functions.name: EnterProvince
functions.evidence:
**Puts a unit into a province**: it writes `current_province_ptr` (+0x130) at 0x1BF4D3, after taking the unit's counter out of the old province's stack and before putting it in the new one's. It refreshes the unit's intel level (+0x1F8) and marks the avatar stale where that or land-and-sea changed, and then places the avatar: at the province's point +0xCC for a land or sea unit with no path, +0xD8 for one with a path, +0xFC for an air unit, and for a fleet in a land province or a wing at its own base at the port or the unit point less the label point. A fleet entering takes what it carries with it, and puts ashore and checks for combat what it carries into a land province at the end of its path. For a selected unit with a path the arrow is made again. Logs 'is located in illegal province 0!' (unit.cpp). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md; reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: CanCommand
functions.evidence:
No for a leader of rank 0, for a land unit and a leader whose type (+0x68) is not 0, a naval one and type not 1, an air one and type not 2; with the flag, no where he has a unit (+0x40) that is not this one. Otherwise yes. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 6.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md)

functions.name: MayTakeLeader
functions.evidence:
CLeader::CanCommand, and for a land unit an exact rank by oob_level (+0x1F4): a division 1 and CUnit::GetCounterSize not 0 - more than one brigade - a corps 2, an army 3, an army group and a theatre 4. A fleet or an air unit takes any rank. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 6.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md)

functions.name: SetLeader
functions.evidence:
**Puts a leader on a unit, or takes one off by being given `CLeader::null()`.** `this` in ECX, three stack arguments, `ret 0xc`. Where the new leader differs: the old one's unit is set to null and his unit cleared; whatever the new one commanded is set to null and his unit becomes this; **resetTraitHours** zeroes his CTraitGainTracker's duration and sets current to -1, throwing away banked battle hours; **organisationHit** multiplies every brigade's organisation by NEW_LEADER_ORG_HIT / 1000 (not below 0) unless a custom game setting's first byte is set. Then the counter's name is redone - `???` under intelligence 5, else the leader's name, else empty - unless the game setting at +0xE9. The start and CUnit::AssignBestLeader pass (0, 0); CAssignLeaderCommand::Execute (1, 1). 23 callers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 9.

functions.evidence:

CCombat::UnitLeaves(unit, false) for each combat on the unit's list and for its bombing (+0x110), and both emptied. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 7.

functions.name: MayLeaveCombats
functions.evidence:

functions.name: HasEnemyLandUnitIn

CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat asks it of the next province of a land unit's path before it starts a battle there, and of the province a retreating unit stands in. The name is ours. functions.name: IsHoldingGround
functions.evidence:
True where the unit is on the defender's list of some combat whose attacker still has a country, or on the attacker's list of one whose defender has. SetUnitPath marks a unit that leaves such a combat as retreating. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 7.

functions.name: CanEngage
functions.evidence:
**`this` is in EDI**, `ret 0xC`. The filter CCombatManager::StartCombat and StartBombing apply to a unit standing in the province. After a war between the owners (or an undeclared one covering the province), different units and owners and neither retreating: **for a battle that is not a bombing**, the same arm, and for two air units the orders count only at a base - where this unit is at its own base its order's slot 34 and slot 25, where the other is, **this** unit's slot 34 and the **other's** slot 25. **With the bombing flag**: of two air units, the other at its own base and this unit's order's slot 29 and slot 17 of this unit's province; a fleet or a land unit as `this` only against an air unit. functions.name: CUnit_SetRingBelow
functions.evidence:
**Gives every unit of a list, and every unit under any of them, one ring.** For each unit of the list that is not itself selected (the byte at +4), the two counters of its avatar (+0x164, then +0x140 and +0x13C) get CCounterObject::SetSelection(state); then the same for its own list of units (+0x1E4) where that has any (+0x1EC). functions.name: OnSelected
functions.evidence:
Slot 4, one body for CUnit, CArmy, CNavy and CAir: what a unit does when it becomes selected. Among it: **its own two counters get ring 1, white, and CUnit_SetRingBelow(3, its units) gives every unit under it the counter type's color2.** CInGameIdler::ShowSelection afterwards makes the selected unit's own ring 2, color1, where an AI commands it. functions.name: OnDeselected
functions.evidence:
Slot 5, one body for CUnit, CArmy, CNavy and CAir: what a unit does when it is selected no longer. Frees its arrow (keeping its counter at +0x18C), destroys the object at +0x168, **sets its own two counters' ring to 0 and CUnit_SetRingBelow(0, its units)**, and clears the province's +0x2E8. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 6.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md)

functions.name: AnnounceArrival
functions.evidence:
Posts the message that a unit has arrived - UNITARRIVED_LAND, UNITARRIVED_NAVAL or UNITARRIVED_AIR, with NAME, PROV and TYPE - to the player, only for the player's own units and not under orders of type 0x42E, 0x6E8 or 0x6E9. (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: OrderToProvince
functions.evidence:
**CUnit slot 6: a right click on a province with this unit selected.** A unit in a battle is never appended to. Nothing happens for a unit with no brigades, a retreating one, or one with an AI agent on a unit above it. For a land unit outside the battle plan branch: the province it stands in, with `append` clear or no path, posts a CCancelMovementCommand; a province CUnit::CanMoveTo refuses gets the `illegal_selection_projection` effect and the `error` sound; otherwise `legal_selection_projection`, the sound `army_move`, and `CMoveCommand(unit, province id, !append, 0, 0)`. functions.name: MayStandIn
functions.evidence:
**CUnit slot 34: whether this unit may stand in that province.** No where the province's template flag +0x13D is clear. functions.name: CanMoveTo
functions.evidence:
**Whether this unit may enter that province**, virtual slot 35.

Among its tests: a land unit whose strength fraction is below CUnit::ShatterThreshold **may not enter an enemy controlled province at all**. CPathFind::MayStep applies the same test, and the interface shows it as `UTM_MAY_SHATTER` and `UTM_NOT_LEGAL_RETREAT`.

So the shatter threshold does two jobs: below it a unit shatters when hurt, and below it a unit cannot push into enemy ground.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-shatter.md)

functions.name: IsLandingFromSea
functions.evidence:
Whether a land unit with a path stands in a sea province with a land province next: with `onAnyGround` that is the answer, without it the land has also to be controlled by an enemy of the unit's owner. CUnit::MovementSpeed and CUnit::MovementDistance inline the same test for the amphibious figures. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: OtherFighterBoundFor
functions.evidence:
Whether **another** land unit of the unit's country (CCountry +0xBAC, its list of units) has a path, can fight (slot 33) and has the province as the **last** province of its path (CUnit +0x13C). Asked by CUnit::AdvanceMovement of a land unit landing on enemy ground that cannot fight itself - yes, it waits the hour; no, its move is cancelled - and by CNavalInvasionOrder::IsActive for the passengers that cannot fight. The other unit need not be landing at all. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: ResetCombatModifiers
functions.evidence:
**Empties a unit's combat modifiers and puts the four multipliers back to neutral.** Frees every node of the CList at +0xDC, zeroes its three fields, and writes 1000 into +0xEC, +0xF0, +0xF4 and +0xF8 - which is what settles that all four are multipliers rather than two values and two multipliers.

Two callers: CCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers (0x165590), which clears before it rebuilds, and CUnit::~CUnit (0x1B5560). Found with a hardware write watchpoint on a live unit - see BiceLib/Reversing/WriteWatch.hpp - after a byte search for stores to +0xDC had turned it up and a range filter had thrown it away for sitting in CUnit's code rather than the combatant's.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

functions.name: AddCombatModifier
functions.evidence:
**Adds one modifier to a unit's list and folds it into the running product.** `ret 0xC` for the three stack arguments; the unit arrives in **ESI** and is never loaded from the frame, which is why a byte search for stores to +0xDC through a named pointer never found this.

It allocates twice: a 12 byte record holding the id at +0, the attack delta at +4 and the defend delta at +8 - which is what the battle tooltip reads and prints as `x%/y%` when the two differ - and a 16 byte CListNode for it. Then `last = node`, `++count`, and `first = node` only when the count was zero, which is why watching +0xDC caught resets and no additions: the head is written on the empty-list branch alone.

**Then it multiplies.** `unit->+0xEC = unit->+0xEC * max(attack + 1000, floor) / 1000` and the same for the defend side into +0xF0, with `floor` read from the global at 0x1A8873C (zero in the image, so presumably set at load). So a modifier's value is a **delta** - +22.5% is 225 - turned into a factor by the `add eax, 0x3e8`, and the two fields hold the running product of everything on the list. That is what the tooltip prints as its Attack and Defend Modifier, and why CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers seeds both with 1000.

Found with a hardware write watchpoint on a live unit's +0xE4, the list's count - see BiceLib/Reversing/WriteWatch.hpp. Nothing static had reached it.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

functions.name: ShatterThreshold
functions.evidence:
**How weak a unit has to get before it shatters**, in per mille of full strength: `t = min(1000 - 500 * officerRatio / 1000, 500)` - the owner's officer ratio (CCountry +0xD4), or the expeditionary owner's where there is one - less the leader's skill times 10, less the unit's average experience (slot 22) times 3 over 1000. The 500, 3 and 10 are g_ShatterBase, g_ShatterStatWeight and g_ShatterSkillWeight, filled by static initialisers. It dereferences `leader_ptr` with no null check. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 3.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md)

functions.name: SettleCombatDamage
functions.evidence:
**Where a combat tick's damage lands on a unit, and where shattering is decided.**

Walks the regiments through CSubUnit::SettleDamage, totalling the strength lost into the out parameter, then adds the casualty trickleback and charges the owner's officer pool. After that:

    strength = sum(regiment->strength)
    fraction = strength * 1000 / GetTotalStrengthCeiling()
    if (fraction < CUnit::ShatterThreshold(unit))
        CCountry::ShatterUnit(owner, unit)

**Nothing here looks at where the unit is** - not the province, not its controller, not whether anything has it surrounded. Shattering is a strength check and only that, which is why a surrounded unit is not reliably destroyed: it shatters here, before ever reaching the retreat that would have removed it.

The third argument is untouched on the paths read.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-shatter.md)

functions.name: AddCasualtyTrickleback
functions.evidence:
**What comes back to the manpower pool from casualties.** The only reader of the `casualty_trickleback` modifier in the executable, at `0x1C3FB6`.

    manpower = casualties x build_cost_manpower / max_strength
             x (trickleback + a technology bonus) / 100000

The first half is the same pricing the reinforcement pass uses, so a casualty is valued at what replacing it costs, and the modifier decides how much of that returns. It credits the **expeditionary owner** where there is one (`+0x28C`) and the owner otherwise.

**No signature recorded**: the compiler gave it a register convention, taking the unit in `eax` and the casualties on the stack, so it cannot be written as an ordinary function - the same reason `CCountry::IsEnemy`'s second overload has none.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

functions.name: GrantCombatExperience
functions.evidence:
The only source of leader experience in the build. Builds one value from the enemy side's size (0x1D6710/0x1D6670), scales it by the double 328.18 at 0x120A7B8 (0.01 in 48.15), clamps it to 6, divides by 3 and adds a 1..6 die, then multiplies by EXP_GAIN_LAND/NAVAL/AIR (vslot 15/16/17 pick), by 1 + the leader's xp_gain trait effect, by EXP_GAIN_CONVOY_MODIFIER when convoyRaid, and by 0.01 a second time. Then EXP_GAIN_DIV x 1000 goes to every regiment (+0x3C, capped at 100000) and EXP_GAIN_LEADER goes to the unit's leader and to every HQ leader above it, divided at each level by that HQ's child count clamped to 2..5. Called from 0x1BA555 (in combat) and 0x1D243C (convoy, flag 1). **The enemy term, read 2026-10-11**: for each combat, the side whose country list (+0x54, the countries still in the fight) does not hold the unit's owner (+0x128) - neither: nothing - contributes (its units' sub unit counts summed << 15) x CUnitList::AverageOrganisation(side) in 15 places >> 15; the current combat (+0x110) the same where the unit is not land. The constant is 328 (0.01 in 15 places, a hair over). **A ship (sub unit slot 10) gains nothing without a target (+0xC0)**. The chain divides at each headquarters whether or not it has a leader. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-battlegains.md, section 1.

functions.name: FindRetreatProvince
functions.evidence:
**Where a unit falls back to**, or null when there is nowhere - which is what has CUnit::RetreatFromCombat remove it from the game instead.

Walks the provinces adjacent to the unit's own, over the path node's edge array (stride 0x14), and keeps the **best scoring** one. A candidate has to be passable and to pass the unit's virtual slot 13; its score is then built from *its* own neighbours:

- one under the unit owner's control, or passing the test at `0x0EFA00`, adds **1000**;
- one under nobody's enemy control adds **500** (g_RetreatNeutralNeighbourScore);
- **an enemy controlled neighbour halves the total** rather than adding to it.

The province is only taken if it scores above a floor, and the highest score wins. **Nothing qualifying means null**, and the unit is destroyed.

Rebels come first and separately: an owner tag of `REB` takes a path of its own which returns null outright unless `0x286C10` finds them somewhere with a flag at `+0x30`'s `+0x198` set.

**For an air unit** the neighbours are scored otherwise: a sea province 1000, and 2000 more for each land province beside it with a naval base that the unit may stand in; a land province nothing, which is never above the floor. And where no neighbour qualifies an air unit with a base goes to its base's province. So a beaten air unit beside the sea falls back out to sea. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md, section 6.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airbattle.md)

functions.name: RegainOrganisation
functions.evidence:
**The hourly return of a unit's organisation, as far as the unit decides it.** Bare `ret`, one caller: CUnit::UpdateHourly at 0x5B9C8A, for a unit with no combat that is not moving onto enemy ground. Returns at once for a unit in combat (+0x11C > 0), and for a land unit aboard a fleet (slot 9's object has +0x300 set) whose province is not land.

It builds one factor in thousandths, each step an imul and an __alldiv by 1000: supply_received_percentage (+0xFC); on land, times the province's infrastructure - `modifiers[12] * (modifiers[13] + modifiers[14] + 1000) / 1000`, held between 10 (floor(10.5f), cached at 0x1BEA400) and 1000; times the owner's OfficerRatio (+0xD4), or the lender's for a unit with an expeditionary owner (in a scenario only if the scenario lists the lender); for a fleet or an air unit with a home base, times the base's crowding - what the base has room for over the brigades of every unit based there, held between 250 and 1000, the same term CDistributeReinforcement::Distribute computes; times `1000 + ORG_REGAIN` of the owner's modifier (id 67). **A unit whose supply_received_percentage is 0 gets -1000 instead**, and loses organisation.

Then the bonus GetMaxOrganisation would work out - the leader's skill of the unit of oob_level 2 above, times CUnit::CommandReach - and CSubUnit::RegainOrganisation for each brigade with the factor and the bonus. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-organisation.md, section 3.

functions.name: ShowMoving
functions.evidence:
What SetUnitPath calls once a unit has a path: moves the avatar (+0x164) to the province's **moving** point (CProvinceTemplate +0xD8, or +0xFC for an air unit), plays `move`, makes the selected unit's arrow (0x5CC230 into +0x188) and moves the counter to the moving stack with CProvinceTemplate::MoveUnitCounter. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: NextArrivalHour
functions.evidence:
**The hour a unit reaches the next province of its path**: now + attack_delay / 1000 + ceil((CUnit::MovementDistance - movement_progress) / CUnit::MovementSpeed), or `end_date` (+0xD0) where that is later. What an arrival date is shown from. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: MovementProgressShare
functions.evidence:
**How far a unit is along the step it is taking, in thousandths**: 0 with no path, -1 where CUnit::MovementDistance is 0, otherwise movement_progress (+0x14C) * 1000 / MovementDistance, truncated (a 64-bit division where the product would overflow). For a unit landing from the sea that is the **invasion's progress** - progress over AMPHIBIOUS_INVADE_MOVEMENT_COST - which CLandCombatant::ApplyCombatModifiers interpolates the two landing scales by, the battle tooltip prints as AMPH_INVASION_PROGRESS and the battle entry's `combat_unit_bg` bar shows. CUnit::RetreatFromCombat takes the largest of it over the defender's units. The sibling of CUnit::SetMovementProgressShare. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section B.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: SetMovementProgressShare
functions.evidence:
Sets `movement_progress` to `share` thousandths of CUnit::MovementDistance, or to zero for a unit with no path. One caller, 0x565AF0 in the combat code, not read. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: AdvanceMovement
functions.evidence:
**One pass of a moving unit's hour.** CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat (slot 31) calls it for a unit with a path, once with `addSpeed` set and then again with it clear for as long as it answers true, so one hour can carry a unit through several short provinces. Nothing for a unit with no sub unit, with an attack delay and no progress, before `move_not_before`, or whose next province is the one it is in. **An air unit in a bombing (+0x110) that is not retreating does not move at all.** With `addSpeed` it adds CUnit::MovementSpeed to `movement_progress` (+0x14C); in a battle the progress is held at the distance and nothing more happens. **Otherwise - on every pass of a unit that is in no battle - `no_bombing_hours` (+0x9C) and `no_battle_hours` (+0xA0) are set to nothing**, so the hours in which an air unit starts no battle and no bombing end with its first move. When the progress reaches CUnit::MovementDistance it drops the first province of the path, takes the distance off the progress (zeroing it under an attack delay), **takes the unit out of the bombing it is in** (CCombat::UnitLeaves on +0x110), clears `retreat`, stores the current province at +0x134, and calls CUnit::EnterProvince and CCombatManager::CheckForCombat. It cancels the move where the province the unit is in has no edge to the next, where the crossing is blocked (not for an air unit), where the unit may no longer stand there, and for a land unit with no supplies headed onto enemy ground. Answers true when a path is left, the unit is in no battle and its progress already covers the next distance. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 3. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md, section 12.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-bombing.md)

functions.name: SetHeading
functions.evidence:
Stores an angle at CUnit +0x108 and +0x104 and hands it to the avatar's slot 37, CHoiAvatar::SetRotation, where the unit has an avatar. CUnit::AdvanceMovement and CUnit::CancelMovement call it when a unit comes to a stop. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

functions.name: FaceNextProvince
functions.evidence:
**Turns a moving unit towards the next province of its path.** Takes the unit point of the province it is in and of the path's first province (slot 30), asks 0xC0BDBA for the angle between them with the map's width, takes pi/2 off, stores the result at +0x104 and +0x108 and hands it to the avatar's slot 37, CHoiAvatar::SetRotation - which turns the figure and the `counter_arrow` pointer of both counters. Does nothing for a unit with no province or no path. Called by CUnit::ShowMoving and by CUnit::AdvanceMovement after an arrival that leaves a path. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md)

functions.name: FreeArrow
functions.evidence:
Hides an arrow, takes it out of the scene of the unit's graphics owner (+0x160) and destroys it through CGraphics::DestroyVisibleObject, then stores null where it was held. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: RemakeArrow
functions.evidence:
Frees the unit's arrow (+0x188) where it has one, through CUnit::FreeArrow, and stores a new one from CUnit::MakeArrow. CUnit::AdvanceMovement calls it on an arrival. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: MakeArrow
functions.evidence:
**Makes the arrow drawn along a selected unit's way.** Null for a unit with no graphics owner or no path. Its points are the unit's own place - its stack's point plus the province's label point - and the unit point of every province of the path, x moved by the map's width where that is the short way round, each with a height of 0.02 over land and 0 over sea; a fleet starts and ends at a naval base position where it is in a land province, a wing at an air base. A point is added 5 beyond each end in line with the end's leg. The type is looked up by name: `unitInvasionArrow`, `retreatArrow`, `attackArrow`, `stratArrow` under order type 0x5A4, else `moveArrow`. Then `new 0x160` and the CUnitArrow constructor, and the arrow's +0x15C is set to movement_progress over CUnit::PathDistance. Callers: CUnit::ShowMoving and CUnit::EnterProvince, both only for a selected unit, and CUnit::RemakeArrow. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md, section 10.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: PathDistance
functions.evidence:
The length of the whole path, for the arrow: CUnit::AdvanceMovement divides the progress by it into the arrow's +0x15C. It walks the path's nodes looking each province up among the edges of the province the unit is in; the decompilation loses the sum, so what exactly is added was not established. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: GetPosition
functions.evidence:
CUnit slot 30, the base: the province's unit point (CProvinceTemplate +0x64, +0x68). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 6.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

functions.name: StrengthDamageFactor
functions.evidence:
**How hard a unit hits for the men it still has.** Totals its subunits' strength, divides by GetMaxStrength (slot 23), and returns roughly that percentage over a hundred - floored at 1, so even a shattered division still throws something - times the global at rva 0x1A8874C. Added to the combat's doctrine figure by CLandCombatant::FireUnit to scale a landed shot.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

functions.name: RollToHit
functions.evidence:
**Whether one shot lands, and it spends the target's defence.** `defence` is thousandths; its whole part is how many shots the target can still defend against this tick and the remainder is a chance at one more.

    if (slots <= target->defences_used)  avoid = CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT_AT_NO_DEF
    else { avoid = BASE_CHANCE_TO_AVOID_HIT
           if (target->IsLand()) avoid += the owner's TechnologyStatus +0x8
           ++target->defences_used }
    avoid = min(avoid, 99000)
    return avoid / 1000 <= rand() % 100

**So a unit does not dodge by chance alone - it runs out.** Once `defences_used` reaches what its defence value bought, every further shot that tick is judged by the much worse no-defence figure, which is what makes being outnumbered compound.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

functions.name: TakeDamage
functions.evidence:
**Spreads one landed shot over every subunit of the unit hit.** The unit is in EAX. Strength damage is shared in proportion to each subunit's own maximum - `share = subunit.GetMaxStrength * 1000 / unit.GetMaxStrength` - while organisation damage is split evenly, one part per subunit.

Nothing is subtracted here. It accumulates into CSubUnit +0xA8, which CCombatant::ApplyLosses spends against `strength` at the end of the tick, and into +0xAC, **whose consumer has not been found** - see that field. That is what lets CUnit::IsOutOfTheFight tell a unit already killed this tick from one still worth shooting at, before any of it has been applied.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

functions.name: IsOutOfTheFight
functions.evidence:
**True when every subunit is already dead on this tick's arithmetic**, which is what stops a unit being shot at twice over. For each subunit it takes `strength - pending_strength_damage` - or `strength - global(0x1A8868C) * pending / 1000` where the subunit answers either of slots 9 or 11 - and returns 0 the moment one of them is still above zero. The unit is in EAX.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-combat.md)

functions.name: CanFight
functions.evidence:
CUnit slot 33, the base CArmy::CanFight overrides: true where some sub unit has at least g_IneffectiveStrength and at least g_IneffectiveOrganisation. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 2.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md)

functions.name: GetCombatWidth
functions.evidence:
**How much of the front a unit takes**: the sum of its brigades' definition width (CSubUnitDefinition +0xE8), times 1000 + the owner's COMBAT_WIDTH modifier over 1000 - the expeditionary owner's where there is one - and at least 1000. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md, section 2.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-landbattle.md)

functions.name: AssignBestLeader
functions.evidence:
**The choice of a leader for a unit.** Over the unit's country's active_leaders: skips one with a unit (+0x40) or that CUnit::MayTakeLeader(unit, him, 1) refuses; scores (skill + 1) * 1000, a hundredth of that for a fleet or an air unit with more brigades (+0x40) than CLeader::CommandSize, plus for every effect of every trait a set amount where its kind suits the unit's own definition (byte table 0x1CD8FC over kind - 3, arms at 0x1CD8C4): defence_modifier 10000 under max_speed 3.000; offence_modifier and combat_move_speed 10000 over 4.000 or with base_ca_bonus over 50; river, fort and amphibious attack 20000 for a positive adjuster; combined_arms_bonus 50000 for any base_ca_bonus; submarine_attack 20000 where the first brigade is a submarine; defender_softness 5000 for soft over hard attack; strategic_attack and naval_attack 10000 over air attack; tactical_attack 10000 for soft plus hard over air; paradrop_mission 50000 off the definition's can_paradrop byte, which nothing sets. The effect's figure is never read. Strictly greater wins, from 0, so the first of equals keeps it; then CUnit::SetLeader(unit, him, 0, 0). Nine callers: CInGameIdler::Enter for every leaderless unit of a new game (not gated), and DeployAt, JoinUnit, CCreateHigherCommand::Execute and others gated by CCountry +0x74B. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 5.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md)

functions.name: LeaderCommandsEnough
functions.evidence:
The fleet and air arm of CUnit::LeaderHasRankForCommand: yes for a land unit, else yes where CLeader::CommandSize(leader, unit) is at least the unit's brigade count (+0x40). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 7.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md)

functions.name: LeaderHasRankForCommand
functions.evidence:
**The gate on BM_LEADER_BONUS**, and what the unit panel writes a leader's name in red for. `this` in EAX, a jump table on oob_level (+0x1F4) against the leader's **rank** (+0x6C): 0 and 1 rank above 2, 2 above 1, 3 above 0, 4 and 7 yes, 5 and 6 - fleet and air - CUnit::LeaderCommandsEnough (0x1CD920). Looser than the exact rank CUnit::MayTakeLeader asks when a leader is chosen. Called at 0x16AA22 and inlined in the naval, air and target slot 19s. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md, section 7.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaderassign.md)

functions.name: SetOrder
functions.evidence:
**`this` is in EAX**, the new order on the stack, `ret 4`, 14 call sites. Parks a fresh `CreateOrder(0x18D, 0)` in `this->+0xB0`, deletes the old order through its slot 0 with the delete flag, deletes that temporary `CNullOrder` too, then installs the real order. So `CUnit + 0xB0` is briefly a throwaway `CNullOrder` in the middle of this function - a hook that reads the order here can see it.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval.md)

functions.name: ReinforceChance
functions.evidence:
A reserve's chance of coming up, thousandths: 0 where it cannot fight; else `(10 + the owner's technology +0x58 + its ATTACK_ or DEFEND_REINFORCE_CHANCE modifier + where the unit is a corps, or a division under one, and that corps stands in the unit's province or its province has an edge to the unit's (CProvinceTemplate::HasEdgeTo): the corps commander's skill * 1000 * 10 / 1000 * CUnit::CommandReach(unit, 3) / 1000) * (average organisation * 1000 / 100000) / 1000`. The 10 is the global Define10. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-battleleaders.md, section 8.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-battleleaders.md)

functions.name: SetBase
functions.evidence:
Takes the unit out of its old base's list of units, stores the new base object at CUnit +0x98 and adds the unit to the new one's list (CUnitBase::AddUnit). The two rebase orders call it the first hour they are looked at, and CAir's hourly base check for a unit with none. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 3.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

functions.name: CUnit_IsAtOwnBase
functions.evidence:
**Whether a unit is at its own base, ready.** False with no base (+0x98) or where the base's slot 0 - its province - is not the province the unit is in (+0x130). For a carrier base (slot 1, IsCarrier), whose slot 0 answers the province the carrier's fleet is in, false again while that fleet (CUnitBaseCarrier +0x18 -> CShip +0xB0) is in a battle (+0x11C) or a bombing (+0x110). So an air group aboard a carrier is 'at base' where the fleet is and only while the fleet is not fighting. 58 callers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section D.1.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: CUnit_MergeInto
functions.evidence:
**Merges one unit into another**: every brigade of `from` moved to `into`; where both are fleets, every land unit `from` carries moved onto `into`'s list with carried_by = `into` (dig_in_level and staging_province zeroed, as CNavy::AddCarried does) - **where `into` is not a fleet they stay on `from`'s list**; where both are air units, what `from` carries likewise (+0x304, +0x2E8 zeroed); the better leader kept; `into` rebuilt (RebuildDefinition, RebuildAvatar) and put back into its province. Nothing here checks `into`'s capacity - the next CheckTransportOverload does. Callers: CMergeCommand::Execute (0x5DBCF6), CJoinFleetOrder's slot 14 (0x59BCB1) and CJoinAirOrder's (0x597C4D), each queueing `from` for removal after. The name is ours.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: DefenderAcceptsBattle
functions.evidence:
**Whether a unit found in a province may be made the defender of a battle**, by the found unit's order. Under a patrol (0x42E): yes with stance 0 (aggressive), no with stance 2 (passive), otherwise only where the asking unit's GetPower is under its own. Under convoy_raid (0x6E9) or transport (0x3A8): no. Anything else: yes. CCombatManager::StartCombat asks it of each unit CUnit::CanEngage passes, so a fleet on a defensive patrol is only brought to battle by a weaker one and a raider or a transport never is. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md, section 1.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seabattle.md)

functions.name: IsTargetInRange
functions.evidence:
**`this` is in EAX**, `ret 8`, 12 call sites. Short-circuits to true for the three rebase orders - GetTypeId `0x574` `rebase_air`, `0x573` `rebase_to_carrier`, `0x6DE` `rebase` - and for any unit with no base at `+0x98`; otherwise takes the range from `unit->+0xC8->+0x148` (the CSubUnitDefinition) and the origin from the base province, and compares. `CAirInterceptOrder` slot 14 calls it with the unit's *current* province and, on failure, orders a return to base and clears `CAirOrder + 0x68`.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval.md)

functions.name: MayStandIn
functions.evidence:
**CArmy slot 34.** A sea province only where a fleet of the same owner is there that is in no battle, not moving, not retreating and can still carry the unit's weight (0x5CEFB0). A land province only where its owner area's slot 0 (province +0x2B4) says yes - then yes outright where the byte at CArmy +0x1A8 is set and the province's owner is the owner of the province the unit is in, and CUnit::MayStandIn otherwise. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-movement.md)

functions.name: StrengthText
functions.evidence:
**An army's strength as men**, the header's `unitstrength`: the sum over its brigades of strength * CRegiment::MenPerStrength / 1000, each cut to a whole number; written whole under 1000 and as thousands, a comma and three digits above; with the colour R in front where its strength over its strength ceilings is under CUnit::ShatterThreshold. Slot 37. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md, section 4.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-unitpanel.md)

functions.name: ClassifyRole
functions.evidence:
0x5CE8A0-0x5CEC31, bare `ret`, `this` in ecx. **CArmy virtual slot 41, and the writer of `CArmy +0x2FC`.** CUnit's slot 41 is `_purecall` (0xB961D5) and CAir's and CNavy's are the folded empty stub 0xABF890, so only an army has a role. It writes **ten** distinct values; the full enum is 0..9 and the order of the tests is the order below. First it sets 9, then returns at once with 9 if `this->+0x40` (brigade count) is zero. Otherwise it walks the brigade list at `+0x38` (the `PAVCSubUnit::__CList` base RTTI puts at offset 56) and for each brigade reads its `CSubUnitDefinition` at `CSubUnit +0x58`, taking the definition's `type_index (+0x24)` and comparing it against the cached definitions on g_CSubUnitDataBase: `+0x78 hq_brigade` sets role **0** and returns immediately; `+0x4C police_brigade`, `+0x50 garrison_brigade`, `+0x54 militia_brigade` count towards role **5**; `+0x40 bergsjaeger_brigade` towards **6**; `+0x44 marine_brigade` towards **7**; `+0x48 paratrooper_brigade` towards **8**. It also accumulates `softness (+0x124)`, `max_speed (+0x108)` and the number of brigades whose `combat_width (+0xE8)` is under 1000. After the loop: average softness below g_FixedPoint0_500 gives role **3** and wins over 5/6/7/8; then 5, 6, 7, 8 in that order; then, only if nothing matched, average max_speed at or above 6000 gives **4**, at least half the brigades having combat_width under 1.000 gives **1**, and the fall-through is **2**. Reading the stock `units/` folder, combat_width 0 is exactly the support brigades, 1 the infantry family and 2 the armour family, so role 1 is a mostly-support formation and role 3, by softness, is armour. Dispatched virtually only; `AddRegimentToUnit` (0x5BE96A) and `RemoveRegimentFromUnit` (0x5BED3F) both call slot 41 on the unit, so the role is recomputed whenever the order of battle changes. The name is from the body.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aifields.md)

functions.name: LoadKey
functions.evidence:
`this` is the CPersistent subobject, CArmy + 8. `target` (0x6A) into CArmy +0x2E8, `staging_province` (0x3A4) into +0x2E4 - both as integers - and `parent` (0x84) as an id pair into CUnit +0x54/+0x58, which CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent resolves as the game is entered. Anything else to CUnit::LoadKey. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.7.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

Slot 4 of CPersistent, this class's own: the RTTI export says CArmy introduced the implementation at this address. See GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp for what the five do. **`this` is the CPersistent subobject, CArmy + 8**, because that is where CPersistent sits in this class; add 8 to any offset here to get a CArmy one.

functions.name: SaveContents
functions.evidence:
CArmy's slot 2 of its CPersistent table (at +8): CUnit's contents, then `target` (+0x2E8) where above 0, `staging_province` (+0x2E4) where above 0, and **`parent` - the parent's id pair - only where the unit has a parent and is carried, by a fleet (+0x300) or by air (+0x304)**. So `parent` is the key a carried unit, saved outside its land hierarchy, finds its way back with. `ret 4`.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

Slot 2 of CPersistent, this class's own: the RTTI export says CArmy introduced the implementation at this address. See GameClasses/CPersistent.hpp for what the five do. **`this` is the CPersistent subobject, CArmy + 8**, because that is where CPersistent sits in this class; add 8 to any offset here to get a CArmy one.

functions.name: CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent
functions.evidence:
**Puts a unit loaded out of its carrier's block back under its parent.** Where the id pair a save's `parent` key left at CUnit +0x54/+0x58 is not the null id, it resolves it and attaches the unit to it (0x5B9760(unit, parent)). One caller, CInGameIdler::Enter (0x65B803), for every unit of every country's list as the game is entered. The name is ours.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: CNavy
functions.evidence:
Calls the CUnit base constructor (0x1B5010), writes CNavy's two vftables (0x15C869C at +0, 0x15C8750 at +8), then initialises **CNavy's own fields**: +0x2E4/+0x2E8/+0x2EC a CList (the `carrying` list), byte +0x2F0 (`at_sea`), float +0x2F4, int +0x2F8 (the combat cooldown), and oob_level (+0x1F4) = 5. So CNavy is 0x2FC bytes and everything from +0x2E4 up belongs to CNavy, not CUnit - project.json currently records `carrying` on CUnit. Returns this in eax. It is the only writer of CNavy's vftable in the image.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navaldetection.md)

functions.name: MayStandIn
functions.evidence:
**CNavy slot 34: whether a fleet may be in a province.** A land province must have an owner, a CPort (+0x354) and a naval base (level above 0), its controller must be no enemy of the fleet's country (CCountry::IsEnemy) and be counted a friend by it (CCountry::IsFriend), and its owner area's slot 0 must agree. Then WaterIsClosed must be false, and last the base rule, CUnit::MayStandIn. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 5.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

functions.name: GetPosition
functions.evidence:
**CNavy slot 30: where a fleet is in a province** - in a land province the naval base position (CProvinceTemplate::GetNavalBasePosition), in a sea province the unit point (+0x64, +0x68). CUnit::EnterProvince and the arrow use it. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 6.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md)

functions.name: CanCarry
functions.evidence:
**Whether a fleet can take a land unit aboard.** False unless: the two have one owner (+0x128); the fleet is in no battle (+0x11C <= 0), not moving (+0x140 <= 0) and not retreating (+0x158); and `unit.definition.transport_weight / 1000 + SumTransportWeight(fleet.carrying) <= fleet.definition.transport_capability / 1000`, each /1000 cut toward zero. Both figures are the units' own rebuilt definitions (CUnit +0xC8): the passenger's sum over its brigades (an ineffective support brigade adds nothing, FINDINGS-unitdef.md), the fleet's sum over every ship - only transport ships declare a capability in Their Finest Hour (transport_ship 40, invasion_transport_ship 60; an infantry_brigade weighs 10). Eight callers: CUnit::AdvanceMovement (0x5CAD03, boarding by marching onto a fleet), CArmy::MayStandIn (0x5CE2E0), CLoadArmyCommand::IsValid (0x5E4135), the unit panel's fleet chooser 0x75E510 (0x75E585), 0x653990 and 0x669AA0 (interface), and the AI at 0x8A0BD3 and 0x8D4070. The name is ours.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: AddCarried
functions.evidence:
**Puts a land unit on a fleet's carrying list.** Through the unit's slot 9 (AsArmy): carried_by (+0x300) = the fleet, dig_in_level (+0x1C8) = 0, staging_province (+0x2E4) = 0, and target (+0x2E8) = 0 only where the fleet is null. Returns where the unit is already listed; otherwise appends a node at the tail of the fleet's +0x2E4 list. Last, the first AI agent up the fleet's hierarchy (CUnit +0x198, then the parent's at +0x1E0) is told through its slot 69 with the CArmy. It does not touch the unit's province, path, order, movement_progress or hierarchy. Four callers: CLoadArmyCommand::Execute (0x5E3B96); CUnit::AdvanceMovement twice - a land unit marching into a sea province boards the first own fleet there that CanCarry it (0x5CAD69), and a landing that may not stand on the land after all goes back aboard (0x5CAF5F); and CNavy::LoadKey for each `division` (and the other land keys) inside a navy block (0x5CF79E). The name is ours.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: RemoveFromTransport
functions.evidence:
**Takes one land unit off a fleet.** In order: the first AI agent up the fleet's hierarchy (+0x198, then +0x1E0's) is told through its slot 70 with (the CArmy, `province`) - the only use of `province`; carried_by (+0x300), dig_in_level (+0x1C8), staging_province (+0x2E4) and target (+0x2E8) of the CArmy zeroed; where `carrySupplies` is set, CUnit::CarrySupplies(unit, **the province the unit is in now**, false, true); the node unlinked from the fleet's list (CList_RemoveNode, which only marks it while the list is locked); CCombatManager::CheckForCombat(unit, the province it is in). It does not move the unit - every caller follows with CUnit::EnterProvince. Four callers: CUnit::EnterProvince for each passenger of a fleet ending its path in a land province (0x5BF965, carrySupplies set); CUnit::AdvanceMovement for a passenger stepping ashore (0x5CACA6, set, after clearing previous_province); CheckTransportOverload in port (0x5CFC75, clear); CUnloadArmyCommand::Execute (0x5E3666, clear). **Because the unit has not moved yet, CarrySupplies fills the pool of the province it is leaving** - for the first two callers the sea zone it was carried through.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: CountShipsByRole
functions.evidence:
Zeroes five ints at `out` and walks unit->regiments (+0x38), classifying each ship by its CSubUnitDefinition (CSubUnit +0x58) in this exclusive order: def->is_capital (+0x2F) -> out[4] (+0x10); def->is_transport (+0x30) -> out[1] (+0x04); def->is_sub (+0x31) -> out[0] (+0x00); def->carrier_size (+0x190) > 0 -> out[3] (+0x0C); otherwise -> out[2] (+0x08), the screens. Bare ret, 0x60 bytes. Its only caller is ShouldStartNavalCombat, which uses out[0] against out[2] for the submarine gate and out[3]+out[4] for the patrol gate. The name is ours; nothing in the image names it.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navaldetection.md)

functions.name: LoadKey
functions.evidence:
What a `navy` block adds over CUnit::LoadKey; **`this` is the CPersistent subobject, CNavy + 8**. `at_sea` (0x3FC) is read into this+0x2F0, which is **CNavy +0x2F8, the post-battle wait** - not +0x2F0, so it never touches the carrying list's lock byte. `base` sets the home base through CUnit::SetBase where the province has a naval base (else logs 'can not find NAVAL base'). **`army`, `theatre`, `armygroup`, `corps` and `division`** each build a CArmy (new 0x308, ctor 0x4828C0): byte +0x48 set, oob_level from the key (0x5B8C70), slot 28 with the fleet's +0x160, the fleet's owner (0x5BC460), the block read by the unit's Load; where it then has a location it goes aboard - CNavy::AddCarried(the fleet, it), which **zeroes the dig_in and staging_province just read** and keeps `target` - and into its owner's unit list (CCountry::AddUnit); without a location it is deleted. Its `parent` is restored later, by CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent as the game is entered. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-oob.md and FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.7.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: CheckTransportOverload
functions.evidence:
**Whether a fleet carries more than it can, and what it does about it.** Overloaded where SumTransportWeight(fleet.carrying) > fleet.definition.transport_capability (+0x144) / 1000. Then, until it is not: walk the passengers in list order; one standing in a **land** province (the fleet is in port) is put ashore - RemoveFromTransport(fleet, carrySupplies = false, its province) and EnterProvince(it, its province) - and the walk goes on; at the first passenger at **sea** that still has a brigade, its first brigade is taken off (RemoveRegimentFromUnit, which rebuilds its definition) and deleted, and where that was its last brigade the unit is queued for removal (the inline CGameState::QueueUnitRemoval, CCurrentGameState +0xBF4) - then the load is measured again. Nothing tells the player. **Five callers**: CUnit::UpdateHourly for every fleet every hour (0x5BA003), CUnit::UpdateDaily behind in_game (0x5BB413), CUnitList::RemoveSpentSubUnits after each round of a battle (0x5D6653), the source fleet of a sub-unit transfer (CTransferSubUnitCommand::Execute, 0x5DCDC1) and of a split (0x5EB737, in the split helper 0x5EB620). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.2.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md)

functions.name: CheckOrderAndCombat
functions.evidence:
`CNavy`'s slot 31 override: 0x34 bytes, and no `ret` of its own. It decrements the countdown at `CNavy +0x2F8` when positive, calls `0x5C7C70(this)` when the fleet has combats (`+0x11C > 0`) or `+0x110` is set, and then **tail-jumps to `CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat`** (`jmp 0x5BA2F0` at `0x5CFDFF`). That tail jump is why the navy path needs no separate call site.

Slot 31 holds `CUnit::CheckOrderAndCombat` in `CUnit`, `CArmy` and `CAir` (vftables `0x15C85CC`, `0x15BDE0C`, `0x15C8774`) and this override in `CNavy` (`0x15C869C`), and nowhere else in any of the image's 2707 vftables - read out of the image at each vftable address, since the RTTI export records only slot counts.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-schedule.md)

functions.name: UnloadCarried

The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.6.

functions.name: CanMoveTo
functions.evidence:
**The one place weather gates air.** CAir's override of CUnit::CanMoveTo (vftable slot 35, CAir's vftable VA 0x15C8774 slot at 0x15C8800): `bool CanMoveTo(CProvince* p)`, `this` in ECX untouched, `ret 4`. functions.name: ResolveConvoyRaid
functions.evidence:
**The convoy raid, end to end.** One body from 0x5D1250 with an early `ret 4` at 0x5D201C and the success path continuing at 0x5D201F in the same frame (trap 3). Three callers: 0x1998EF (CAirConvoyRaid), **0x19C66B (CPatrolOrder::IsActive)** and 0x1A02CD (CConvoyRaid::IsActive). **1. The raider's attack**, over its ships or wings: `convoy_attack` for a fleet, `sea_attack` for an air unit, times strength/100 and organisation/100; `detect` is the best `surface_detection`. **2. A convoy**, over those registered in the raider's province (CMapProvince +0x38): not its own, at war (or REB, or an undeclared war covering the province), with a transport, and `Random() % 50 < detect / 1000`; one whose CConvoy::GetDefence is no more than the attack is preferred, else the first. **3. The test**: an air raid's attack is multiplied by 5; a defence above it fails with CONVOY_TOO_STRONG and a tenth of STRAT_CONVOY_DAMAGE / the victim's convoys off its series. **4. The battle.** A throwaway CNavy (byte +0x48 set) of the convoy's owner is filled with `(escorts + transports) / scale` ships, scale = a fifth of the path's length and 1 at least, each count raised to 1 where it was above nothing: the first escorts/scale of them `destroyer`s (CSubUnitDataBase +0xA8), the rest `transport_ship`s (+0x88); the destroyers get the owner's technology levels and the transports none, the loop's bounds being the destroyer's list for both. It enters the raider's province; a CNavalCombat (a CNavalBombing for an air raider) is made with **byte +0x2B set**, the raider attacking; every ship of both is put at distance 1.000; and **five rounds are fought at once** (slot 15 five times, GrantCombatExperience before the first three). **5. The count**: strength lost by the destroyers and by the transports, each `* 2 / 100`, the transports' raised to one ship where above 0.3 of one (the fixed point at 0x1A88748, which a startup initialiser fills with the float 300.5 at 0x160AAB4, floored); with either at one or more, CConvoy::LoseShips with both rounded, and the victim's series. **6.** The province's last_convoy_attack is the hour, the battle goes to the history, and the throwaway fleet is removed. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-navalmissions.md, section 9. **The battle is never ended**: after the rounds it is taken off the raider's combats by hand (CList_RemoveNode, 0x5D2476), recorded (CCombatHistory::RecordCombat, 0x5D2904) and destroyed through its slot 0 with a zero flag (0x5D2910) - no CCombat::End and no CCombatant::DetachAllUnits - so CTraitGainTracker::Update does not run for the raider against it (inferred: the destructor's virtual calls were not followed). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-battlegains.md, section 4.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-battlegains.md)

functions.name: CAssignLeaderCommand
functions.evidence:
**The game's own way to assign - or unassign - one unit's leader**, and so the command to post when the choice of units has to survive the trip to another client. `ret 0x10`, four stack arguments, the object back in EAX. Five callers, all of which `push 0x90` before `operator new`, so **`sizeof(CAssignLeaderCommand)` is 0x90**.

It writes the `CPersistent` token 0x18D at +0x4, its own save token 0x3A3 at +0x2C and +0x30 (which slot 7 returns), then turns `unit` into the persistent reference at +0x3C/+0x40/+0x44 through 0x42DD70 and `leader` into the one at +0x64/+0x68/+0x6C through 0x7C9530, and puts `flag` on the byte at +0x8C. **Holding both ends as persistent ids rather than pointers is what lets the command resolve on every client**, which is the difference between it and anything read out of the local selection.

`Execute` (slot 6, 0x1D7570) resolves both back, detaches the leader from whatever unit it was on, and calls `CUnit::SetLeader`. **Unassigning is `leader = CLeader::null()`**: the site at rva 0x36955C builds exactly that, and `Execute`'s own fallback for a leader id that does not resolve is the same call.

The two swap sites in one function at rva 0x33ACAC and 0x33ADA2 pass `flag` 0 and the two single-assignment sites pass 1; **what the flag does is not established.**
(BiceLib/Hooks/UnassignSelected.cpp)

functions.name: Execute
functions.evidence:
**Virtual slot 6: how one unit's leader is actually changed, and the model for any command that names its targets.** Bare `ret` at 0x5D7729, `this` in ECX, no stack arguments.

It resolves **both** of its persistent references back to pointers with `FindPersistentById` (0xA9DA00), choosing the registry `[0x1A857F0]` or `[0x1A857F4]` on whether the id exceeds 0x1268: the unit from the pair at `+0x40`/`+0x44` into `+0x3C`, and the leader from `+0x68`/`+0x6C` into `+0x64`. **An unresolvable leader becomes `CLeader::null()`** (0x57F510), which is what makes "assign nobody" the same operation as "assign somebody".

Then, gated on the unit's owner matching `played_country_id`, it builds the player message; and unconditionally: if the leader is already on another unit, `CUnit::SetLeader(thatUnit, CLeader::null(), 0, 0)` to detach it, then `CUnit::SetLeader(targetUnit, leader, 1, 1)` to attach.

**Why it matters beyond leaders**: it holds its ends as `CPersistent` id pairs rather than pointers, which is exactly what lets the command mean the same thing on every peer - and that is the property any custom command has to copy.

functions.name: Execute
functions.evidence:
**What the "unassign all leaders" button does**, and the command the `CONFIRM_REMOVEAll` dialog queues when it is confirmed. Virtual **slot 6** of `CRemoveAllLeadersCommand`; `this` in ECX, no stack arguments, one bare `ret` at 0x5D8655 with nine `int3` after it and slot 7 (`mov eax, 0x5d8; ret`, the command's save token) at 0x5D8660.

It resolves its own country - `this->+0x40` is a country id, indexed into `g_CCountryDataBase (0x1A855A4) ->+0x16C` - and walks that country's `units` (`CCountry +0xBAC`), `edi` holding each unit and `[esp+0x14]` the next node. Per unit:

- **0x5D84A1: `cmp [edi+0x290], ebx` / `jne 0x5D863A`** - skip a unit whose `expeditionary_owner`'s id is set, i.e. one on loan to another country. This is the loop's only skip.
- 0x5D856C: `cmp [edi+0x128], ecx` against the game state's `player_tag`'s id (+0xC34). This gates **only the two message strings** built at 0x5D8590-0x5D8617, not the work: both arms fall into the call below.
- **0x5D8635: `call 0x5BFC10`** with the unit in ECX and `(eax, 1, 0)` on the stack - the per-unit strip - **`CUnit::SetLeader`**, now recorded at rva 0x1BFC10. It opens `mov edi, ecx; mov ecx, [edi+0x12c]`, reading `CUnit::leader_ptr`, which is what says this is the leader detach. `ret 0xc`, in no virtual table, 23 callers. Virtual slot 6 - the command's own Execute, the same shape as CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute next door. It resolves its unit reference (`this->+0x40`/`+0x44` through FindPersistentById against [0x1A857F0] or [0x1A857F4] by whether the type half exceeds 0x1268, then `-8` to reach the CUnit), takes the byte at `this->+0x64` and calls `CUnitPlan::SetActive(&unit->plan (+0x1FC), active)` at 0x1E5451, then goes on to the rest of the command.

functions.name: ParseObjectReference
functions.evidence:
**Reads the `{ type = N id = N }` block a save writes for an object reference into the 0x28-byte reference a command keeps.** It calls `ParseObjectId` (0x67B250) for the pair and then fills the reference: `+0` the cached object pointer, set to 0 because the block names no object yet; `+4` type; `+8` id; `+0xC` an `Hoi3CString` assigned from the parse context's own name at `+0x32C`. It takes no stack argument - the parse context arrives in ECX and the reference in ESI (`mov ecx,[ebp+8]` and `lea esi,[this+0x3C]` at the call site, a bare `ret` here), the same register-argument style as the rest of the loader primitives. 61 call sites, every one of them a command's `LoadKey` case for a key whose value is an object: `unit` is token 0x256 and `parent` 0x84, and a command keeps one such reference per key at `+0x3C`, `+0x64` and so on, 0x28 apart. **It stores nothing when the parse context's error handler at `+0x35C` has latched** - handler non-null and both its bytes at `+4` and `+5` set jumps straight to the epilogue and leaves the reference as it was, although `ParseObjectId` has already consumed the tokens. The mirror image is the command's `SaveContents`, e.g. `CMoveCommand`'s at 0x1D9160: `SaveWriteKey(0x256)` then the pair out of `+0x40` and `+0x44` - the string at `+0x4C` is never written to the save. functions.name: CCountryHistoryEntry
functions.evidence:
The base of all twenty-odd `C*Change` classes that hang off a country's history. 0x1EEA40 to the `ret 4` at 0x1EEA67, `this` in ECX and the country on the stack. Calls `CHistoryEntry::CHistoryEntry` (0x1F4550), writes its own vftable 0x15C96EC, and stores the country at **`this+0xC`** (0x1EEA5E) - the field every derived Apply reads to find the object it changes. functions.name: Apply
functions.evidence:
**`capital = N` in a country's history moves both capitals.** Slot 7 of the history entry, one holder (table 0x15C973C). 0x5EEAD0 to the `ret 4` at 0x5EEB65. Forward: the country's current declared capital (CCountry_GetCapitalProvinceId, `+0xE20`) is kept at `this+0x14`, then CCountry_SetCapital(country, this+0x10, logHistory 0) and CCountry_SetActingCapital(country@EDI, this+0x10). Backward: both set back to the kept `+0x14`. `this+0xC` is the CCountry. So a game started from the history files has `acting_capital == capital` for every country whose history names one; the declared and acting capitals part only in play (UpdateActingCapital, EnsureCapital, SetGovernmentInExile). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-capitalreaders.md, section 2.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-capitalreaders.md)

functions.name: CAddCountryFlagChange
functions.evidence:
0x1EF220 to the `ret 4` at 0x1EF24D. `this` in ECX, the country on the stack, `this` back in EAX. Calls the base `CCountryHistoryEntry::CCountryHistoryEntry` (0x1EEA40) with the country, writes its own vftable 0x15C9880, then constructs the Hoi3CString at `this+0x10` through 0x65A700 (0x1EF23F). **Two callers**: `CSetFlagCommand::Execute` at 0x152C87, and 0x1ED218 inside the country history's own entry factory (`CCountryHistory` slot 9, 0x1ECA90) - so the class exists both to be loaded out of a history block and to be filed by the command. In no virtual table; recorded under the class because it writes that class's table.

functions.name: Apply
functions.evidence:
**Slot 7, one holder, and this is where a country flag actually gets set** - the write `CSetFlagCommand::Execute` does not do. 0x1EF250 to the one `ret 4` at 0x1EF2BC, no interior `ret`. The bool is the direction `CHistoryContainer::ApplyRange` (0x1F47C0) and `ApplyAll` (0x1F4830) pass: 1 to apply, 0 to undo.

Both arms resolve the country the same way - `CCountry::GetFlags` (0xCCD30, `lea eax,[ecx+0x180]; ret`) on the `CCountry*` at `this+0xC` (0x1EF273) - and take the flag name from the Hoi3CString at `this+0x10` through its `c_str` (0xC3B0, at 0x1EF265). Forward calls `CFlags_SetFlag` (0x4D6A0) at 0x1EF288, which creates the flag if it is not in the tree; backward calls `CFlags_ClearFlag` (0x4D6C0) at 0x1EF2B3, which does not. `CRemoveCountryFlagChange::Apply` (0x1EF380) is the same body with the two arms swapped.

functions.name: CFactionJoin
functions.evidence:
The 0x18-byte object `CFaction::AddCountry` allocates when `recordInHistory` is set (0x4F5FD5/0x4F5FE6). Calls the base constructor 0x5EEA40(country), writes its own vftable 0x15C997C - which the RTTI export names `CFactionJoin` - and returns `this`. `ret 4`. This closes FINDINGS-faction's open item: the faction-change history entry is `CFactionJoin` for a join and `CFactionLeave` for a leave, both derived from `CCountryHistoryEntry` at offset 0.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-faction.md)

functions.name: Apply
functions.evidence:
`CFactionJoin` slot 7, which the RTTI export says the class introduces; one holder, `ret 4`, read end to end, 0x7E bytes. The argument is a direction flag.

    forward: this->+0x14 = this->country->faction     // remember what to undo
             if (this->+0x10 && this->+0x10->IsValid())
                 CFaction::AddCountry(this->+0x10, this->country, 0, 0)
    reverse: CFaction::AddCountry(this->+0x14, this->country, 0, 0)

So `+0x10` is the faction the entry records and `+0x14` the one to put the country back into - which settles the roles of the two faction pointers FINDINGS-faction could only count. The reverse arm is **unguarded**, so `+0x14` may be the null faction, and that is the one call site in the image that deliberately uses AddCountry's step 3 as a leave. The name `Apply` is ours; `CCountryHistoryEntry`'s slot 7 is unnamed.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-faction.md)

functions.name: AppendStatisticsSample
functions.evidence:
**The whole of what a year change records.** 0x1F3B90 to the `ret 0x28` at 0x1F3E37, and 0x28 = 4 + 0x1C + 4 + 4 fixes the argument list exactly, with the string passed by value. It walks the collection's records - begin `collection[+8]`, end `collection[+0xC]`, stride 0x44, each holding a name at +0x18 compared with 0x15F70 - and appends `value` to that record's vector at +0x24/+0x28 and `year` to the one at +0x34/+0x38; if no record matches it builds one (name plus the two vectors) and pushes it in.
