labels.name: WindspeedDecayNoFront
labels.evidence:
`imul dword ptr [0x1686F3C]` in CWeather::Update, bytes f7 2d 3c 6f a8 01, then /1000: windspeed = windspeed * 750/1000 an hour wherever no front is over the province. [0x1686F3C] is floor(750.5) = 750. CORRECTION: project.json's CWeather+0x10 comment and the weather survey both say 0.980 here; 0.980 is [0x168703C], a different global, which is the humidity and pressure transfer factor in CWeatherFront::SpreadWeather. The hourly windspeed decay is 0.750.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: PrecipitationFromCloud
labels.evidence:
`movss xmm0,[0x120A5F4]` (2000.5) feeding floor+__ftol2 and then `imul esi` on (cloud_coverage - threshold): precipitation = 2.000 x (cloud_coverage - threshold), clamped to [0, 1.000] by CWeather::Clamp, where threshold is 0.500 at sea, 0.250 on land under a front and 0 on land with no front. The 2.000 is an inline floor of a float literal, not a define and not even a cached static, so nothing in defines.lua moves it. Verified against autosave.hoi3 on 2092 of 2092 provinces.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: RainConsumesHumidity
labels.evidence:
`sub dword ptr [edi+8], eax` in CWeather::Update, with eax = precipitation * floor(10000.5)/1000 = 10 x precipitation. Together with the cloud burn-off four instructions earlier it runs ONLY where the province has no weather front (guarded at 0xB27B8), which is why a front means persistent rain: under a front neither the cloud nor the humidity that feed the rain are consumed.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: TemperatureClimateMultiplierSignGate
labels.evidence:
`cmp dword ptr [ebp-8], 0; jle` in CWeather::Update, where [ebp-8] holds TEMPERATURECHANGESPEED. It gates the climate-3 x10 multiplier on the define being POSITIVE, and the twin test at 0xB2A56 gates a climate-5 x2 multiplier on it being NEGATIVE. Since TEMPERATURECHANGESPEED is 0.075 in BlackICE and positive in vanilla, the climate-5 branch is unreachable dead code. The direction of the temperature step is decided separately at 0xB2A92, so the sign is not doing double duty.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: NewFrontPressureDropDivide
labels.evidence:
`idiv edi` in CWeatherFront::CWeatherFront with edi = LOWPRESSUREOFFSET/1000, taking `Random() % (LOWPRESSUREOFFSET/1000)`. There is no zero check anywhere on the path, so a defines.lua `LOWPRESSUREOFFSET` below 1.0 divides by zero the first time a weather front is created - inside the first game hour. The flagged limit for the mod.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: FrontPressureThresholdTest
labels.evidence:
`sub eax,[g_PRESSURETHRESHOLD]; cmp eax,edx` in CWeatherFront::Tick - the ONLY reader of PRESSURETHRESHOLD in the whole image. It refuses to spread into a neighbour whose pressure exceeds the current province's by more than the define. CWeather::Clamp holds every pressure inside [PRESSUREMIN, PRESSUREMAX], a span of 220 at BlackICE's 870/1090, so at PRESSURETHRESHOLD = 300 the test can never fire and the define is effectively dead; it would start to bite below 220.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: WeatherFrontMarkInsteadOfUnlink
labels.evidence:
`cmp byte ptr [edi+0x14], 0` in CWeatherManager::Tick: while that byte is set, a spent front's list node is marked (node+0xC = 1) instead of being unlinked, although the front object is deleted either way. The manager is embedded at CGameState+0xAEC, so the byte is CGameState+0xB00; of the eight instructions in the image that touch [reg+0xB00] the only write to a CGameState is `mov byte ptr [ebx+0xb00], 0` at 0x27D1D9 inside CGameState::CGameState. NOTHING EVER SETS IT, so this path is dead - and would be a use-after-free if it ran, because the walker at 0xB5CA4 dereferences node->data without testing node+0xC.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: LowPressureZoneClimateMask
labels.evidence:
`mov eax,1; shl eax,cl; test ebx,eax` in CWeatherManager::CreateFront, with cl = CProvince+0x30 (the climate zone, 1..5) and ebx the second dword of the CMap+0x21D8 record - i.e. the number after the `=` in default.map's `low_pressure_zones`. So that number is a BITMASK OVER CLIMATE ZONES, and because the zones are numbered from 1 its bit 0 is wasted while bit 5 (value 32) is needed for climate 5: the ubiquitous `31` covers climates 1-4 only, and 62 or 63 would cover all five. Vanilla uses the same values, so this is an engine/vanilla trait rather than a BlackICE mistake. Note this branch skips the zone WITHOUT advancing the index into the manager's per-zone cooldown and heading vectors.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: FrontHeadingStep
labels.evidence:
`add edi, eax` in CWeatherManager::CreateFront, with eax = 1000000 / MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE and edi the zone's cached heading, then wrapped by `if (edi > 1000) edi -= 1000`. So MAXFROMEACHPRESSURE does two jobs: /1000 it caps the fronts one zone may have alive, and here it sets the angle between successive fronts from that zone - at BlackICE's 8 that is a step of 125, one eighth of the compass. Confirmed in autosave.hoi3: zone 13833's eight live fronts read 0.060, 0.185, 0.310, 0.435, 0.560 and the same 0.125 lattice appears in every multi-front zone.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: LowPressureZoneCooldown
labels.evidence:
`call Random; idiv 0x30; add edx,0x18; mov [esi+ebx],edx` in CWeatherManager::CreateFront: after a zone spawns a front its cooldown is set to 24 + Random() % 48 hours. Hardcoded - no define touches it - so one low pressure zone produces a front every 24 to 71 hours at best.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: FrontRotationHemisphereFlip
labels.evidence:
`cmp byte ptr [eax+0xa2], 0 ... neg ebx` in CWeatherManager::CreateFront: a new front's rotation is +[0x1686FC8] (= 10) in one hemisphere and -10 in the other, chosen by CProvinceTemplate+0xA2. Confirmed in autosave.hoi3, where the surviving non-zero rotations include -0.003 and -0.008 alongside +0.001..+0.008.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: HighPressureScratchReset
labels.evidence:
`mov edi, 0x1869f` and the loop that follows: PropagateHighPressure begins by writing 99999 into CProvince+0x10 on EVERY province. It runs once per high_pressure_zones entry per hour, so BlackICE's nineteen highs cost about 95,000 stores an hour before any pressure is propagated - the one place in this subsystem where a long list in default.map has a measurable cost.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: HighPressureTargetReduction
labels.evidence:
`imul eax,eax,0x3e8; imul dword ptr [g_PRESSUREREDUCTION]; ... /1000` in CWeatherManager::PropagateHighPressure. The x1000 and the /1000 cancel, so the target pressure for a province at accumulated cost d is PRESSUREMAX - d * PRESSUREREDUCTION with both already in thousandths - NOT `- d * PRESSUREREDUCTION/1000` as the earlier outline had it. At BlackICE's PRESSUREREDUCTION = 2 the target reaches zero, and the walk stops, at an accumulated cost of 545. The cost is the sum of CProvinceTemplate+0x24 along the path, the same per-province traversal cost CSupply::SpreadFromDepot uses, not a hop count.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weatherfront.md)

labels.name: CBuildingDataBase_RoleByModifierId
labels.evidence:
The building-role ladder in the building-database loader. eax = building->+0xC, the CModifier the building's one modifier key mapped to, then five compares of the modifier id at CModifier +0x24: 0x2E MODIFIER_AIR_CAPACITY -> db +0x1C, 0x2D MODIFIER_NAVAL_CAPACITY -> db +0x20, 0x4B MODIFIER_LOCAL_AA -> db +0x24, 0x0F MODIFIER_IC -> db +0x2C, 0x66 MODIFIER_LOCAL_UNDERGROUND -> db +0x28. In vanilla and in BlackICE that is air_base, naval_base, anti_air, industry and underground. It is an if/else ladder with no break, so where two buildings carry the same modifier the last one parsed takes the slot. The defaults are set at rva 0xB769B, which points all five slots at the built-in 'nobuilding'.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-definitions.md)

labels.name: rebeltype_is_triggered_only_case
labels.evidence:
CRebelType::LoadKey's handler for `is_triggered_only` (token 0x61D). The loader's jump table is at 0x4BFD9C with a byte index table at 0x4BFDD8 and a base of `eax - 0x61D` (0x4BFB72), so token 0x61D is index 0 and lands here: `add edi, 0x19C; push edi; call 0xA7B410`. This is what places the key fieldmap.py could not see.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-revolt.md, section 2)

labels.name: read_rebeltype_spawn_chance
labels.evidence:
`lea eax, [esi + 0x28]` immediately before `call CMeanTimeToHappen::GetDays` at 0x4C0676, with esi a CRebelType*. **The only reader of CRebelType::spawn_chance in the image**, and the evidence that the key is not dead: the type with the largest value is the one chosen for the province.

labels.name: revolt_roll_ai_halves_the_chance
labels.evidence:
`mov dword [ebp-0x1c], 0x4E20` - reached when gameState->+0xBCC[country id] is zero, i.e. when nobody is playing the country. It doubles the revolt roll's denominator from 10000 to 20000, so **an AI country gets exactly half a human player's revolt chance**, on top of whatever the difficulty static modifiers do.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-revolt.md, section 1)

labels.name: revolt_roll_risk_gate
labels.evidence:
`call Random; cdq; idiv [ebp-0x1c]; cmp edx, edi; jge` - the first of RunDailyRevoltRoll's two gates. edi is round(effective_revolt_risk / 50) and [ebp-0x1c] is 10000 for a human-played country or 20000 for an AI one. Bytes: e8 85 24 5e 00 99 f7 7d e4 3b d7 7d 25.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-revolt.md, section 1)

labels.name: revolt_roll_annual_gate
labels.evidence:
`call Random; cdq; mov ecx, 0x16D; idiv ecx; test edx, edx; jne` - RunDailyRevoltRoll's **second** gate, a flat 1-in-365 every day on top of the risk gate, and the reason revolts are almost never seen: the two together give threshold/denom per year rather than per day. Bytes: e8 78 24 5e 00 99 b9 6d 01 00 00 f7 f9 85 d2 75 14. Hooking here, or patching the `jne` to a `nop`, is the cheapest way for a mod to make revolt risk matter.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-revolt.md, section 1)

labels.name: RunCountryHourlyPass_TheatrePass
labels.evidence:
`cmp byte [edi+0x580], 0` inside RunCountryHourlyPass - the fork that decides which theatre pass a country gets this hour, and **the proof that the whole theatre-building layer is tick-thread code**: `retsBefore(0x4D8EB0, 0x4D9093)` is empty and 0x4D8EB0 is a fresh prologue with its own SEH push after a single int3 at 0x4D8EAF, so this is inside the confirmed tick-thread hourly pass. Set: `BuildTheatres(&country->Strategy, 0)` at 0x4D9093, the full rebuild. Clear: `MaintainTheatres(&country->Strategy, hour == country->id % 24)` at 0x4D90C6 - the same per-country stagger the ministers use.
(agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion)

labels.name: ExileHourly_FollowFactionLeaderCapital
labels.evidence:
**Every hour, a government in exile whose acting capital an enemy holds moves into its faction leader's.** In exile, CCountry::IsEnemyTag(country, the controller of its acting capital), faction slot 7 true and the first member not the country: CCountry_SetActingCapital(country, the first member's acting_capital_province_id).

labels.name: ExileDaily_PuppetSwapGate
labels.evidence:
**The daily test that can turn a government in exile into the puppet of whoever holds its capital.** Runs only where CCurrentGameState +0xD0C is null; the country in exile; its capital's controller C not an enemy (CCountry::IsEnemyTag); C's faction pointer not the exile's; no truce between them (the exile's status towards C, HasTruce). Then CCountry_ReplaceExileWithPuppet (0x50C0B0) at 0x4DA722, which acts where C controls at least half of what the exile owns.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

labels.name: RunCountryDailyPass_NationalUnityDrift
labels.evidence:
**National unity's daily change**, 0xDA727-0xDA895 in RunCountryDailyPass, for every country the pass runs for, unconditionally (REB and provinceless countries included), after RebuildStaticModifiers and before the manpower gain. (1) StrategicWarfare_PruneList on the three lists of the embedded CStrategicWarfare (+0x1184): convoy (+0x119C), alliance (+0x11AC), ground bombing (+0x11BC), dropping entries dated more than 168 hours before now; (2) CStrategicWarfare::RecomputeImpacts: each impact = the sum of its list, held to -2.000..2.000; (3) `month = fp15(convoy + allies + bombing) + max(fp15(values[MODIFIER_NATIONAL_UNITY, id 44, +0x160]), -1.0)`, where fp15(x) = trunc(x * 32768 / 1000); `day = trunc(month / 30)`; (4) **only away from 50**: where unity < 49000 and day < 0, `day = trunc(day / IntegerSqrt(50 - trunc(unity / 1000)))`; where unity > 51000 and day > 0, `day = trunc(day / IntegerSqrt(trunc(unity / 1000) - 50))`; (5) `delta = floor(day * 1000 / 32768)` (an arithmetic shift, so any negative fraction is at least -0.001 and a positive one under 0.001 is nothing) and CCountry::ChangeNationalUnity(country, delta), which scales by national_unity_effect and clamps. So the figures every source of the `national_unity` modifier and the three strategic-warfare impacts carry are **per month**, which is what the top bar's tooltip calls them (STRMONTHLY_CHANGE). Measured: between the maintainer's saves of 4 and 8 January 1936 all 21 countries whose cabinet holds no party of another ideology group than the ruling one stood still (and 2 rose), and every country that fell has such a party - static `fractured_government` (national_unity -0.05), -2 a day before scaling; propaganda_press (-0.1) or state_press (-0.05) turns it into -1, free_press (+0.2) leaves -2.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-government.md)

labels.name: RunCountryDailyPass_AddManpower
labels.evidence:
**Where a country's manpower grows.** `add [ebx+0xbcc], eax`, the country in ebx, taken only when eax is above nothing. eax = GetMonthlyManpowerGain(country) * 1000 / (days * 1000), where days is the length of the current month: the day of the year, off the tick at [ebp-0x28] less 43800000 hours over 24 and reduced by whole 365-day years, is walked down MonthLengthTable (0x4DA8F0, with the out-of-line `inc edx; jmp` at 0x4DC3FF). So **a day adds the month's figure over the days that month has**, February more than January. Unconditional for every country the pass runs for, and nothing compares the result with max_manpower. It comes after RebuildStaticModifiers (0x4DA5E3) and the strategic-warfare change to national unity (0x4DA890), and before UpdateTotalLeadership (0x4DAEA7).
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpowergain.md)

labels.name: DailyPass_ActivateLeaders
labels.evidence:
The only place RunCountryDailyPass (0xDA530) touches CCountry's leaders list (+0xE10). The block runs to 0xDAB2A and does leader activation only - no experience, no skill: for each leader it finds the date of the first history entry whose save token is 0x10A (rank), falling back to the global at rva 0x130C2B8, and when that date equals CCurrentGameState->tick and the leader is not yet in active_leaders (+0xE00), sets rank (+0x6C) to 1 and appends him.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leaders.md)

labels.name: RunCountryDailyPass_ExpirePendingActions
labels.evidence:
`xor edi, edi` - the start of the block in RunCountryDailyPass (0x4DB042-0x4DB179) that **deletes, unanswered, every pending action (CCountry +0xF24) whose last_command_date + 0x60 (96 hours, four days) is before today's tick**. It runs for a country with a CEU3AI that nobody plays, and for the local player's own country only while his first delegation flag is 1 (foreign policy left to the AI) - so never for an undelegated player. In practice what it catches are the trade offers AnswerPendingOffers keeps back (only one trade is accepted per pass); they are dropped four days after they arrived. Removal honours the list's no_unlink byte (+0xF30), marking the node instead of unlinking it while that is set.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-agreements.md)

labels.name: ExileDaily_SuppliesAndFuelToHost
labels.evidence:
**A government in exile hands its supplies and fuel over every day.** Right after its CollectDailyProduction, RunDailyTradeRoutes, UpdateIC and ConvertCrudeOilToFuel (which run for a country that owns a province or is in exile): pool_in_exile's supplies (+0xA00) and fuel (+0xA04) are added to the received_from_exiles ledger (+0xA64: +0xA6C, +0xA70) of the controller of the exile's acting capital province, and to that province's pool (+0x164, +0x168), and both are set to 0.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

labels.name: RunCountryDailyPass_DistributeProductionShares
labels.evidence:
**Where the six IC shares are run, and with what.** The loop at rva 0xDB4F3..0xDB54B walks ProductionDistribution (CCountry +0x5F4) in index order - lend-lease, consumer goods, production, supply, reinforcement, upgrade - calling slot 0 of each with (&out, (__int64)TotalIC << 15, flag = 0). So `available` is the whole-number TotalIC after the day's resource cap and with lend-lease added, and each share's resource charge comes off the stockpile before the next one's check. The loop at rva 0xDB610 does the same for the four leadership shares with TotalLeadership (+0xBD8), turned from thousandths into fixed 15. **Its gate is not the economy block's.** The calls before it - rva 0xF1F50, RunDailyTradeRoutes, UpdateIC(country, 1) and CCountry::ConvertCrudeOilToFuel - run only when CCountry +0xCF8 > 0 or government_in_exile is set; this loop runs for every country whose id (+0xCA8) is non-zero and whose tag is not REB (the three byte compares at rva 0xDB4D4). So a country that holds no province still earns money, makes supplies and is charged resources every day, in the pool of whoever holds its capital - 23 such countries in a vanilla 1936 savegame show `usage`, each exactly its consumer goods share plus its supply share times its IC.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-distribute.md)

labels.name: RunCountryDailyPass_DistributeLeadershipShares
labels.evidence:
**Where the four leadership shares are run.** In RunCountryDailyPass, the country in ebx, inside the same gate as the six IC shares: a tag, and not REB. First, if gamestate->scenario (+0xD0C) is set, LeadershipDistribution[0] - officers - has its base_percentage zeroed and, when it was not zero already, its slot 4 called, which is the shared empty stub for every class but CDistributeResearch. Then the loop at 0x4DB610 calls slot 0 of each of the four in index order - officers, diplomacy, espionage, research - with (&out, available, flag = 0), where available is the whole of TotalLeadership turned from thousandths into fixed 15 by a truncating divide: `(x << 30) / (1000 << 15)`. `out` is not read afterwards. So in a stand-alone scenario no officers are trained, the same pointer that skips the dissent change in CDistributeConsumerGoods::Distribute.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-leadership.md)

labels.name: ExileDaily_ReturnWhenFactionLeader
labels.evidence:
**A government in exile that leads its faction leaves it and comes back from exile.** Reached every day the country does not surrender (it owns nothing, or GetSurrenderProgress < 1000, or it is not at war - an exile always). In exile, faction slot 7 true, 1 or more members and the first member the country itself: CCountry::LeaveFaction(country, 0) then SetGovernmentInExile(country, 0). Next, at 0x4DBE73, a country **not** in exile has unknown_a1c's supplies (+0xA24) held to SupplyCapacity of its acting capital; an exile skips that.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-surrender.md)

labels.name: RebuildStaticModifiers_AddBaseValues
labels.evidence:
**The first thing CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers adds is `base_values`, whole.** The country is the stack argument; its modifier is the CModifier at +0xD90 (global_modifier), cleared at 0x4DDDFE. From here the loop adds statics->base_values (+0x64)->values[id] into it for every modifier id and appends the static to the modifier's contributor list. At 0x4DDEDE the same is done for the CModifier at faction (+0xD8) +0x7C when the faction's slot 7 says it is a real one. That is how `global_leadership = 3.5` and the two consumer goods demands reach every country. The rest of the function was not read.

labels.name: RebuildStaticModifiers_AddControlledProvinceModifiers
labels.evidence:
**A country's modifier takes in the whole modifier of every province it controls.** In CCountry::RebuildStaticModifiers, the loop 0x4DEA50..0x4DEB98 walks ControlledProvinces (+0xD00) and, for each, adds the province's CProvinceModifier (+0xFC) into the country's one modifier id at a time - `values[id] += provinceValues[id]` over all ([0x1A86198] - [0x1A86194]) / 4 ids - and records the province modifier in the contributor vector. So anything a province's modifier holds reaches its controller's, once for each province, the country-wide kinds included; the local kinds come along too and are read by nothing at country level. **This is not how a strategic resource reaches a country**: that is step 9 of the rebuild, from the levels UpdateStrategicResources keeps. The same loop then tests, for a country at war, whether a province flagged at +0x36C that it owns is in its capital's area; what that is for was not read.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countrymodifier.md)

labels.name: RebuildNeighbours_CountRebelHeldProvince

labels.name: UpdateIC_EnergyToCrudeOil
labels.evidence:
**Energy into crude oil, read through.** rva 0xF0FF5..0xF13E2 of CCountry::UpdateIC, the country in ebx, run only with applyDailyEffects. All thousandths. need = TotalIC * 2000; spare = pool.energy - need; most = max(TotalIC * 1000 * 1000 / 20000, 1000), so 0.05 an IC and at least 1. Skipped when spare <= 0. energyNet and crudeNet are yesterday's income less expense for each good, summed off the same fifteen CGoodsPools one slot apart (income: home, convoyed_in, traded_for, +0x848, conversion_made, +0x8FC, back, +0xA64; expense: to, usage, conversion_used, convoyed_out, traded_away, less +0x824 and +0x920). rate = CCountry::GetOilConversionRate = 100 + technology_status->oil_conversion_bonus, so 0.1 plus technology. wanted = (pool.energy + energyNet - 2 * (pool.crude_oil + crudeNet)) * 1000 / (1000 + rate * 2000 / 1000) - the energy that, converted, leaves the country holding exactly twice as much energy as crude oil; `1 + 2 x rate` is this divisor and nothing else. per = max(round(1000000 / rate), 1000), the energy one unit of crude oil costs. energy = min(most * per / 1000, wanted, spare); crude = energy * rate / 1000. Then pool.crude_oil += crude, pool.energy -= energy, conversion_used.energy (+0x8F4) += energy and conversion_made.crude_oil (+0x8C8) += crude. **So a country makes at most max(0.05 x TotalIC, 1) crude oil a day, at 1 / rate energy each** - the cap is on the oil made, not the energy spent, and the rate is not `1 + 2 x technology`, both of which FINDINGS-ic.md had. The min and the final rounding go through single-precision floats: (x / 1000.0 + 0.0005) * 1000.0, then 0x401FD0 / 0xC08870.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-distribute.md)

labels.name: UpdateIC_ResourceCapAndLendLease
labels.evidence:
**The resource cap and the receiver's lend-lease, read instruction by instruction 2026-10-13.** rva 0xF146E..0xF15A5 of CCountry::UpdateIC, the country in ebx, run only with applyDailyEffects (the test at 0xF145E jumps to the epilogue otherwise, so +0x608 stays at the 0 written at entry). All thousandths unless said:

    limit = CCountry::GetResourceLimitedIC(country) / 1000          ; whole IC, truncated
    if (TotalIC > limit) { ic_lost_to_shortage (+0x614) = (limit - TotalIC) * 1000 ; TotalIC = limit }
    ll = lend_lease_income (+0x6E8) / 1000                          ; whole IC, truncated toward zero
    TotalIC += ll ;  lend_lease_ic (+0x608) = ll
    LendLeaseReceipts_Clear(&lend_lease_from_yesterday_values (+0x6D8))
    if (lend_lease_from_values (+0x6C8) has entries):
        LendLeaseReceipts_AppendAll(+0x6D8, +0x6C8)                  ; yesterday = the receipts as they stand
        lend_lease_income_yesterday (+0x6EC) = ll * 1000
    else:
        lend_lease_income = 0 ;  lend_lease_income_yesterday = 0
    left = ll * 1000
    for each receipt in list order, while left > 0:
        left -= receipt.amount
        if (left < 0) { receipt.amount = -left ; stop }            ; this giver keeps the remainder
        receipt.amount = 0
    lend_lease_income -= ll * 1000

So the receiver turns the whole IC of what it holds into IC that needs no resources, **after** the cap - lend-lease IC is extra IC above what its own stockpile supports - and the fraction stays for tomorrow, credited to the givers last in its list. The cap has no floor: TotalIC may be cut to 0 here, where the province sum gave at least 1. The no-giver branch zeroes the income before subtracting, which is only consistent because CCountry::RemoveLendLeaseSource takes a giver's entry off the income when it removes it.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-tradeui.md)

labels.name: FactionLeaderPromotion
labels.evidence:
**The one place in the image that changes a faction's leader.** Leadership is positional - `CFaction::GetFactionLeader` returns `Members (+0x28)`'s first node - and `CFaction::AddMember`'s only caller always appends at the tail, so a join can never promote. This block can.

It sits in the unnamed function at rva 0x102BC0, which sets `country->government_in_exile (+0x95) = 1` and scales `Manpower (+0xBCC)` and `officers (+0xC4)` by the float at 0x160A684 - a country losing its homeland. The block runs only when `faction->IsValid()`, the country's own id equals the leader's (0x502E5F), and `NumberOfMembers > 1`; it then walks the member list skipping any country with `government_in_exile` set and skipping itself, keeps the one with the greatest `max_ic (CCountry +0x60C)`, and promotes it by `CFaction::RemoveMember` (0x502F07) followed by the push-front helper 0x523770 (0x502F34), finishing `faction->+0x38 = 1`.

So: **when a faction leader goes into exile, the surviving member with the highest max IC takes the lead, and the rest of the order is untouched.** The 45 savegames on this machine agree: 44 of them have GER, ENG and SOV first in `axis`, `allies` and `comintern`, and in the only exception - Ireland1945_01_22_02 - `axis` reads JAP, GER, SLO, ... with Germany simply displaced one place, which is what removing JAP and pushing it to the front produces.

**The enclosing function is now bounded (wave 15 agent C): rva 0x102BC0, 0x502BC0 to the `ret 8` at 0x5033AD, 0x7F0 bytes.** Two stack arguments and nothing in ECX - `[ebp+8]` and a bool at `[ebp+0xC]`, tested against 1 at 0x502BE6 - so it is `ret 8` with both on the stack. The four `ret 8` at 0x50315F, 0x503376, 0x503393 and 0x5033AD are arms of one frame; `retsBefore(0x502BC0, 0x5033AD)` lists the first three and nothing in the body branches past the last.

**And 0x5033AD/0x5033B0 is a new trap 2 pair, with zero padding**: the byte after the `ret 8` is the `mov ecx, [0x1A87818]` that opens a *different* function, which (a) ends in a **bare** `ret` at 0x503650 where every exit of this one cleans eight bytes, and (b) has a caller of its own at 0x68F05F. That is wave 12's independent rule for an unpaddded boundary, and it is what settles the extent - an int3 scan runs 0x2A3 bytes past the end, and a scan stopping at the first `ret` stops 0x24E bytes short of it. The seven callers the entry already claims check out: 0x47ADAF, 0x4DBE6E, 0x50C228, 0x54D8FE, 0x5F1EDD, 0x5F1EF9 and 0x9BB1AB. The body outside the promotion block is still unread, so the function is still unnamed and still in the frontier.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-faction.md)

labels.name: BombFire_AirDefenceDeadStore

labels.name: FireUnit_ArmorOnSoftTest

This is the counterpart of the deflection halving the record already notes on this function, which runs the other way round (attacker piercing below target armor). Note it is the **summed** definition on both sides, so a division's armour is the sum of its brigades'.

labels.name: CCombat_Conclude_RecordLastBattleLosses
labels.evidence:
**Where the six `last_*_battle_*_losses` figures are written** - the only writes of CGameState +0x30..+0x44 in the image, all inside CCombat::Conclude (0x174580), before its relation change, counters, on-actions and messages. Then `attackerLost` picks the sides: loser = attacker's figure when the attacker lost, else the defender's. Land (GetKind 1) writes +0x34 loser at 0x174879 and +0x30 winner at 0x17491C; naval (2) +0x44/+0x40; air (3) +0x3C/+0x38; other kinds write nothing. labels.name: MapEdgeScrollTests
labels.evidence:
**Where the map starts scrolling because the mouse is against the edge of the screen**, and where BiceLib stops it.

Four tests in a row, one per edge, each the same shape: ask EDI for the mouse position, compare one coordinate against one of the camera's edges give or take six pixels, and move the camera if it is past it.

    mov  edx, [edi]              ; the mouse object's vftable
    mov  edx, [edx + 0x4C]       ; its "where is the mouse"
    lea  eax, [esp + 0x24]
    push eax
    mov  ecx, edi
    call edx
    mov  ecx, [esi + 0x328]      ; edge_top, then bottom, left, right
    add  ecx, 6
    cmp  [eax + 4], ecx
    jge  <past it>

They run from here to **0x23CFB5**, where the camera is clamped, with nothing else in between - so a five byte jump from the first to the last removes all four and leaves the keyboard and the drag alone. The two instructions it replaces are exactly five bytes.

**Every branch that enters the range lands on this first byte** - five of them, with the only others being each test skipping itself - which is what makes jumping over the whole run safe. Checked with `reversing/scripts/cfg.py --lands-in 0x63ce97 0x63cfb5`.

labels.name: PlayerEliminatedSetsGameOver
labels.evidence:
`mov byte ptr [ebx+0x1CD9], 1` - the elimination detector at the head of ProcessSessionEndRequests, so it is evaluated every frame. Reached only when the played tag's CCountry has NumberOfOwnedProvinces (+0xCF8) below 1 (tested at 0x254306) and the tag is not "REB" (0x25431D..0x25432C), and only when CInGameIdler +5 is clear. The flag is acted on 7 bytes later, in the same call. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

labels.name: ExitToMenuRequestGate
labels.evidence:
`cmp byte ptr [ebx+0x1CDA], 0` followed by `je 0x2547D2` - the predicate FINDINGS-session.md section 4 said "was not read". It is the gate on the only reachable path from CInGameIdler::Update to CGameState::ResetSession. Its one writer of a one is 0x24FF10, inside UpdateTutorialAndAuxWindows, under `if (state->tutorial_active)`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

labels.name: SessionExitCallsReset
labels.evidence:
`push 1; call 0x23A460` inside ProcessSessionEndRequests - **the only path from CInGameIdler::Update to the full game-state reset.** It is reached only when exit_to_menu_requested (+0x1CDA) is set, which in this build happens only when a tutorial's lesson runner reports itself finished.

**It does not leave a frame in which in_game is 1 over a wiped state.** 0x49 bytes later in THIS function - not inside 0x23A460, which has only dead clears - CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd is called at 0x254775 and clears in_game at 0x2ED9AF. The only branch in between is the `operator new` failure arm at 0x254760, and even on that arm CInGameIdler::Leave clears the byte at 0x262337: the run loop's swap calls the OUTGOING screen's slot 4 at 0x2913BC, four instructions after Update's slot-1 call returns and before it ever reads the incoming pointer. The only other call in the window is an indirect one at 0x254743 that resolves to 0x20CD50, a bare `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md sections 3 and 4.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

labels.name: InertSuspendCallInResetWindow
labels.evidence:
`call eax` reached through `[[idler+0x1790]+0xE4]` with `[vft+0x10]` - slot 4, index 4 - sitting **between** the game-state reset at 0x25472C and the in_game clear inside CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd. It is the one call in that window that could have touched the wiped state, and **it does nothing**: CEU3Application +0xE4 is a 0xC0-byte object installed once by the base CApplication constructor at 0x690B1C, its primary vftable is 0x15FDDC0 for the object's whole life (findValue finds that constant written only by the constructor, by its own slot 0 at 0x6802C8 and by one other method of the same class - the standard MSVC pattern), and slot 4 of that table is **0x20CD50, a bare `ret 4`** - TRAPS.md trap 4's 1420-holder shared stub. So it reads nothing, raises nothing and cannot reach a DLL; the hazard does not exist inside the frame either.

The same stub call appears with argument 1 at 0x254726, just before the reset, and again in CInGameIdler::AutosaveWrite at 0x25000C before the `save games/` path is built, so the idiom is a suspend/resume bracket that is inert in this build. Beware the off-by-one: reading `[vft+0x10]` as index 3 gives 0x680BA0, a plausible-looking global getter, and the wrong answer. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 3(a).
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

labels.name: ExitToMenuAllocationFailureArm
labels.evidence:
`cmp eax, esi; je 0x25477E` - **the only branch between the game-state reset and the in_game clear**, and it is taken only when `new(0x8B0)` at 0x25474A returns null. On that arm CFrontEnd::CFrontEnd never runs, so in_game is NOT cleared inside ProcessSessionEndRequests; the function instead installs a **null** pending screen (app->+0x88 = 1 at 0x254797, app->+0xE0 = 0 at 0x2547B8) and returns.

It is discounted twice over. First, in_game is still cleared: the run loop's swap calls the OUTGOING screen's slot 4 - CInGameIdler::Leave, clearing the byte at 0x262337 - at 0x2913BC, *before* it reads app->+0xE0 at 0x2913BE. Second, the arm is self-terminating: with app->+0x84 set to 0 at 0x2913E4, the swap dereferences it with no null test at 0x291404 (`mov edx,[ecx]`) and faults 0x48 bytes later. Same class of arm as the dead "release the old one" branch in FINDINGS-session.md section 5 - reachable only if operator new returns 0. Recorded because it is the one branch in the window and the block should not be described as straight-line. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 3(b).
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

labels.name: InGameIdler_EndDateCheck

labels.name: CInGameIdler_Enter_SeedTemperature
labels.evidence:
**A new game starts every province's temperature at its target.** In CInGameIdler::Enter's per-province loop (0x25BD12-0x25C01C, logged 'provinces initialised<'), after UpdateProvinceNightFlag and only where loaded_from_save (+0xD9C) is clear: `temperature (+0x7C, CWeather +0x14) = CWeather::BaseTemperature(&province->weather)` - with the night flag just set, the climate set by the earlier latitude and climate loop (0x25AFAD/0x25AFB3), and cloud, rain, frozen and wind at nought from CProvince_ResetState, so the cloud, cold-rain and wind-chill terms add nothing. Then RebuildProvinceModifierValues and 0x4A6C30. Happens before the 96-hour pre-roll. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section A.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md)

labels.name: CInGameIdler_Enter_WeatherPreRoll
labels.evidence:
**The new game's weather pre-roll**, inside CInGameIdler::Enter after the supply network is built (0x25C611) and after RebuildStrategicResourceProvinces (0x25C803); skipped for a session loaded from a save (`loaded_from_save` +0xD9C tested at 0x25C7FA) and in a tutorial (+0xD9D, 0x25C808). `hours = trunc(INITIAL_SIMULATION_HOURS_AHEAD / 1000)` read straight off the defines (GetDefines +0xEC +0xDC; 96 in Their Finest Hour), the province count taken once, then `hours` times: CWeatherManager::Tick, and CWeather::Update on every province of the vector in index order - **no simulated-flag test, no IsNight, no GraphicName, and the date never moves**, so all 96 hours see the night flag and climate of hour 0 of the start date. The first day's RunDailyPass (0x25CB2E) follows, and the two days' block ends with one RunHourlyPass, so a new game has run 97 weather hours before its first tick. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-weathersim.md, section A.

labels.name: EnterGame_SetInGame
labels.evidence:
**The only instruction in the executable that writes `CCurrentGameState +0xDA4` a nonzero value**: `mov byte ptr [ecx + 0xDA4], 1`, with `ecx` loaded from `g_CCurrentGameState` two instructions earlier.

It sits near the end of `CInGameIdler::Enter` (`0x25A2B0`), after the session has been built - the log lines above it are `Countries initialized<`, `provinces initialised<`, `information caches setup<`, `supply logic defined<`, ` processed weather <`, ` processed intel setup <` - and before the in-game GUI is built (`menubar`, `chat_list`, `mapmode_1`..`mapmode_10`).

Unconditional on its path: the block at `0x25D120` is the join of the inlined get-or-create of the game state, entered from `0x25D082(taken)`, `0x25D114(taken)` and `0x25D11E(flow)`, and the block above it at `0x25D075` is reached from all three arms of the camera setup. **So the attrition gate opens in every game**, which is what the live tooltip measurement already showed.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-manpower.md)

labels.name: RunHourlyPass_ResetFactionProgress
labels.evidence:
`mov dword ptr [eax+0xac], 0` inside RunHourlyPass: **every hour, before the province pass adds to it, each ideology group's faction has its Progress set to 0.** The loop at 0x68274F..0x6827BD walks the ideology database's groups ([0x1A878BC] +0x1C..+0x20) and takes each group's faction (+0x54) - or, for a group with none, the null faction (lazily built) - and zeroes it. **The null faction is zeroed only for a group with no faction**: Their Finest Hour's three groups all have one, so - inferred, no other store resetting it having been found - the null faction's Progress is never reset and grows each hour by the victory points of every province controlled by a country in no faction (see FINDINGS-factionplay.md section C). Between this store and the province pass at 0x682A75 the per-country hourly pass and the unit functors run, so anything reading Progress there would see a partial sum; nothing in Their Finest Hour's or BlackICE's script does.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

labels.name: MarkSimulatedProvinces_StoreScenario
labels.evidence:
`mov dword ptr [eax + 0xD0C], ecx` at the tail of MarkSimulatedProvinces (0x285FB0) - `eax` the game state from [ebp+8], `ecx` the scenario from [ebp+0xC]. **The only instruction in the image that writes CCurrentGameState +0xD0C scenario** (the other two hits on that displacement are CGameState::CGameState zeroing it at 0x27D535 and 0x4C964D, which is another class). So the field is a pure function of who calls MarkSimulatedProvinces and with what: the session reset passes 0, CGameState::LoadKey passes 0, the savegame loader passes whatever 0x45E690 resolved from the save's `scenario` name, and of the six lobby callers five pass 0 and only 0x30FBDE passes a value. This extends the existing comment on 0x285FB0, which describes only its effect on CProvinceTemplate +0x13D. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-session.md section 8.

labels.name: RunLoopCallsScreenUpdateSlot
labels.evidence:
`call eax` with eax = `[[app->+0x84]] + 4` - **slot 1 of the current screen**, loaded at 0x291397/0x291399. While the in-game screen is current this is CInGameIdler::Update (0x2559D0).

This is the only way Update is reached: image.findValue(0x6559D0) returns ZERO hits in .text - it has no direct callers anywhere in the image - and exactly one in .rdata, at 0x15CEB58, which is CInGameIdler's vftable 0x15CEB54 + 4. One holder, so trap 4 is discharged too. Slot 1 differs per class (CFrontEnd 0x2EDD60, CBackEndIdler 0x208AF0), so the slot identifies which Update runs. project.json's comment on CEU3Application::Run gives 0x29138D, which is where the screen pointer is loaded; the call is here. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 4.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

labels.name: RunLoopCallsOutgoingScreenLeave
labels.evidence:
`call eax` with eax = `[[app->+0x84]] + 0x10` - **slot 4 of the OUTGOING screen**, and the first thing the pending-screen swap at 0x2913A0 does. For the in-game screen that is CInGameIdler::Leave (slot 4 = 0x262060; padding ends at 0x26205F and retsBefore(0x662060, 0x662340) is empty, so its in_game clear at 0x262337 is inside it); for the frontend it is 0x2F0140.

**This is the control that settles whether a reset game state can ever be seen with in_game set.** Between Update's slot-1 call returning at 0x2913A0 and this call there are four instructions and no call at all, so no frame can be presented in between - whatever the screen's Update did to the game state, and whichever arm of 0x254760 it took. It also runs *before* the swap reads app->+0xE0 at 0x2913BE, which is why a null pending screen still gets the byte cleared. CEU3Application::Run's existing comment lists the swap's calls to the INCOMING screen's slots 2, 3 and 5 but not this one. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 4.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

labels.name: RemoveAllLeaders_PostCommand
labels.evidence:
`mov ecx,[eax+0x38]; mov eax,[ecx]; mov edx,[eax+0x18]; push edi; call edx` - eleven bytes, the post of the command `CConfirmRemoveAll::OnConfirm` has just built. `eax` is the dispatcher off `CCurrentGameState +0xBE8`, its `+0x38` is the command queue, queue slot 6 is the post, and `edi` is the command.

**Hooked by BiceLib.** With Ctrl held it posts one `CAssignLeaderCommand(unit, CLeader::null(), 1)` per selected unit instead of the country-wide command, and destroys the unused one through its own slot 0. This is the right place for that choice **because this handler only runs on the machine whose player clicked**, so what leaves it is an explicit list of units that every client resolves the same way. **Tested in multiplayer on 2026-10-04 and it holds** - which is the observation the design rests on, not an argument from the code. The first attempt filtered inside `CRemoveAllLeadersCommand::Execute` instead and desynced, because that body runs on every client while the key and the selection do not; see rva 0x1D84A1. The bytes are `8B 48 38 8B 01 8B 50 18 57 FF D2` and the hook verifies them before writing.
(BiceLib/Hooks/UnassignSelected.cpp)

labels.name: ProcessAI_TheatreReadinessGate
labels.evidence:
`cmp byte [edi+0xa6], al` with al == 0 - the top of a block in ProcessAI (0x8897E8-0x889852) that runs only while CEU3AI +0xA6 is set. It walks `GetCountry(ai->tag)->+0x570` (read at 0x8897F7), resolves each theatre's `unit` id pair (CTheatre +0x74/+0x78) through 0xA9D390, and **bails back to the agent loops the moment one does not resolve**, leaving +0xA6 set to retry next hour. When every theatre has a live HQ unit it calls AnnounceLoadedUnitsToScreen(ai, ai->id == gamestate->+0xC34) at 0x88984D and clears +0xA6 at 0x889852. Worker thread - which means AnnounceLoadedUnitsToScreen reaches CCurrentGameState::in_game_screen off the tick thread.
(agent report: the AI's theatre layer and CAIInvasion)

labels.name: ProcessAI_UpdateUnitAgents
labels.evidence:
`mov edi, [edx+0x40]` inside ProcessAI (0x4894E0): the head of the CEU3AI's **unit-agent** list, walked through node `+8` calling each agent's slot 9 (`[vftable+0x24]`, CAIAgent::Update) at 0x489881. **This is the only recurring path that ticks a CAIUnit**, and it runs where ProcessAI runs - on a TBB worker thread, once per game hour. Unlike the minister loop at 0x4896C8 it does not test the agent's `+0x3C` byte itself; slot 9 does that through slot 8.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

labels.name: ProcessAI_UpdateInvasionAgents
labels.evidence:
`mov edi, [eax+0x50]` inside ProcessAI, immediately after the unit-agent loop: the head of the CEU3AI's **CAIInvasion** list, walked the same way through node `+8` calling slot 9 at 0x48989B. So ProcessAI ticks three agent families per country per hour: the ministers (+0x74), the unit agents (+0x40) and the invasion agents (+0x50).
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-aiunit.md)

labels.name: AiDrivesAirAndNavalStanceToTwo
labels.evidence:
**This is the answer to 'does the AI ever set plan_air_stance to 2'. It does, unconditionally, for every one of its unit agents, on every ProcessAI pass.**

CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances runs two loops over `ai->unit_agents (+0x40)`. The second one starts at 0x49161E (head reloaded at 0x491621) and its body is:

    unit = agent->slot74()                       ; ReturnDwordAt0x64, = agent->unit (+0x64)
    if (!unit) continue                                                   0x491655
    if (unit->plan_air_stance (+0x20C) == 2 &&
        unit->plan_naval_stance (+0x210) == 2) continue                   0x491660-0x49166E
    cmd = new CSetPlanAttributesCommand(unit, 5, 2, 2, &-1000, &-1000)    0x4916AD
    post cmd                                                              0x491751

The stance argument 5 and the two -1000s are that command's "leave alone" sentinels; **air_stance 2 and naval_stance 2 are real writes**, landing at CSetPlanAttributesCommand::Execute's 0x1E7907 and 0x1E7950. The `== 2 && == 2` test is an idempotence check, not a condition: the arm exists only to avoid re-posting a command that would change nothing, so the steady state of every agent unit is air_stance 2.

The two pushes of 2 are read off the stack arithmetic, not guessed: `push ecx` at 0x49168B reserves a slot, `mov [ecx],0xFFFFFC18` at 0x491697 and 0x4916A7 fill the two power slots with -1000, and the ctor (0x1E7710, `ret 0x1C`) stores `[ebp+0x10]`->+0x68 stance, `[ebp+0x14]`->+0x6C air_stance, `[ebp+0x18]`->+0x70 naval_stance. It also sets `+0x64 active = 1` from `ebx` at 0x1E77AD, so Execute's SetActive call cannot take the reset arm.

**Consequence: AirPhase4_StrategicArmRequiresAirStanceTwo's gate passes for the AI, and logistical_strike, strategic_bomb, nuke_mission, naval_strike and port_strike are live.** CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances has exactly one caller, ProcessAI at 0x489B8F, so this is AI worker-thread code and nothing a player does is needed.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

labels.name: AIForeignMinister_LimitedWarByFactionRule
labels.evidence:
**The AI's war plans declare a limited war where its faction rule allows one.** In CAIForeignMinister::DoWork's walk of prepared war targets (country +0x5D4), a target **without** a decision (rva 0x49D967) gets a CDeclareWarAction built in place (constructor 0xA11DF0, which sets `value (+0x24)` = 1, a full war) with the war goal 'conquer'; then, **where the target entry's byte +0x14 is clear and the AI's own country has the faction rule limited_war (`CCountry +0xDDC`)**, `value` is set to 0 - a limited war (FINDINGS-war.md: value 0 sets CWar +0x70, and the declarer's allies are not called). In Their Finest Hour that is every member of the Axis. What the target's +0x14 means was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md, B.3.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-factionplay.md)

labels.name: AirTargetTransportListGate
labels.evidence:
The gate on the fourth list, and **it is the opposite of the gate the reader uses.**

Here (0x4B4D1F-0x4B4DAC): `n = (agent->+0x170 - agent->+0x16C) / 4`; if `n <= 0` nothing is appended to `air_target_provinces_transport (+0x22C)` at all. Otherwise, for each CUnit in that vector, the unit's `current_province_ptr (+0x130)`'s area (`+0x2B4`) must answer true to its own virtual slot 0, and then the candidate is accepted if that area **is** the candidate's area or appears in the area's `+0x34` list. One acceptance is enough; the record is then built and appended at 0x4B4E00.

In CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 2 the same vector is tested at 0x4CE28E-0x4CE29F and the sense is reversed: for a wing carrying a transport plane, `(+0x170 - +0x16C) & ~3 > 0` makes the body **jump out** (`jg 0x4CE63B`) and skip the wing entirely, and `+0x22C` is selected only when the vector is empty.

**So the transport list is filled only when the vector is non-empty and read only when it is empty.** Within one pass the two can never both hold, so anything read out of `+0x22C` was built on an earlier pass: the lists are built once and then only on a replan (`+0x83`), while `+0x16C` is erased and refilled by slot 78 every pass (0x4B1E14). Reported as read, not explained - it looks like a sense error in one of the two places, but nothing in the code says which.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

labels.name: ComputePlanForces_LandTypeFallbackChain
labels.evidence:
0x4B65DD..0x4B683E, the substitution ladder: eight `unit_available[type] && SubUnitDefinitionIsUsableBy(tag, type)` tests, each falling back to a cheaper type when it fails. battleship -> heavy_cruiser -> light_cruiser; heavy_cruiser -> light_cruiser; mechanized -> motorized -> infantry; armor -> light_armor -> whatever the mechanised chain settled on; bergsjaeger -> infantry; garrison -> infantry. labels.name: ComputePlanForces_LandWants
labels.evidence:
The five stores that put the whole land order of battle into the want vector, 0x4B684D..0x4B6879: want[bergsjaeger-or-infantry] += the mountain share, want[armour chain] += the armour share, want[mech chain] += the same share again, want[garrison-or-infantry] += min(round(theatre->areas_count * shortage * 3), brigadeDemand), want[infantry] += whatever is left of brigadeDemand after the other four, floored at zero (0x4B65D9). The mountain share is brigadeDemand * (mountain provinces / all provinces) * 0.5; the armour share is brigadeDemand * (plains provinces / all provinces) * CCountry +0x594 / 1000, which is zero unless something writes +0x594.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

labels.name: ComputePlanForces_AirborneAndMarineWant
labels.evidence:
w = max(invasion weight, base_ic / 40); then want[paratrooper] += ceil(w/2) and want[marine] = max(floor(w/2), theatre->areas_count), each only when the type passes the availability gate - paratroopers additionally need transport_plane to pass. The invasion weight is counted at 0x4B69A0..0x4B6AFB: one per plan objective province that an enemy holds and whose area is not adjacent to our capital's area, plus one more if that area has over 5 provinces and one more over 10. The whole block is skipped unless the country's base_ic (+0x604) is at least 50 and the agent's theatre is the capital's theatre.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

The five libdivide sequences at 0x4B7B11..0x4B7B6A are T/20, T/35, T/50, T/100 and T/200, applied as **floors** (a max, not a sum) on want[destroyer], want[light_cruiser], want[heavy_cruiser], want[capital ship] and want[carrier] respectively. labels.name: ComputePlanForces_PostIfChanged

The stack at that call is (this, unit, 5, 3, 3, our_power = fp+0x4C, their_power = fp+0x18) - `ret 0x1C` over seven dwords, which settles the argument order FINDINGS-power.md gives.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-forceneeds.md)

labels.name: DistributeOpsAreaToSubordinates_Apportion
labels.evidence:
The largest-remainder apportionment inside CAIUnit slot 83, 0x4C0D47-0x4C0DE8. Per subordinate, with `weight` = the CIDValue's +0x10 divided by 1000 (its division count), `total` = the summed division count and `n` = the number of the parent's ops-area provinces lying in that subordinate's own owner area:

    exact = n * (weight / total)
    quota = (int)exact
    carry += exact - quota
    if (carry >= 1.0f) { carry -= 1.0; quota++; }
    cidValue->+0x10 = quota * 1000

`carry` lives in [esp+0x60], is zeroed once before the loop at 0x4C0BEA and is carried across subordinates, so the fractions are not lost - the classic Hare/largest-remainder split. The 1.0f is the float at 0x171DBAC and the 1.0 the double at 0x160A248. Note that the CIDValue's value field is **reused**: it holds divisions*1000 going in and quota*1000 coming out.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-subdivide.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_SortWingsIntoMissionPools
labels.evidence:
Phase 4's entry. Four CLists are zeroed here - P at [ebp-0x114], Q at [ebp-0xBC], R at [ebp-0x38], S at [ebp-0xF0], each {head, tail, count, byte} - and `[ebp+0xC]`, which held the caller's `force` argument, is reused as a budget `agent->+0x1E4 * 4`.

The loop at 0x8CEEF0 walks listB (the phase-1 candidate list, head at [ebp-0xD0]) and sorts each wing into one pool by role, after repeating the gates `combats_count (+0x11C) <= 0`, CUnit_IsAtOwnBase, !UnitHasBlockingOrder and not-already-in-listA:

- any tactical_bomber, cas or cag in the group -> 0x8CF047: if the budget is positive and the wing's definition has `sea_attack (+0x168) > 0`, into **R** (naval/port strike) and the budget drops by one; otherwise 0x8CF0A2.
- any strategic_bomber, or `strategic_attack (+0x17C) > 50000` -> **Q** (logistical strike, then strategic bomb or nuke).
- else any naval_bomber -> **R**.
- else any interceptor -> **S** (air intercept).
- else dropped.
- 0x8CF0A2, the overflow from the first arm: into **Q** when the agent's ops area (+0x90/+0x94) is empty, the country is at war or in an undeclared war, `strategic_attack >= 1000` and the group holds no cag; into **P** (ground attack) otherwise.

**So P is the ground-attack pool and R the naval-strike pool, and `agent->+0x1E4 * 4` caps the naval-strike pool, not the ground-attack one.** findings/FINDINGS-reorganise.md had the budget on the tactical pool and left CSubUnitDefinition +0x168 unidentified; it is `sea_attack`, already named in project.json, which is what makes the arm read correctly.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_CollectBattleProvinces
labels.evidence:
The ground-attack target survey, 0x8CF18A-0x8CF31F, which also lazily builds the CCurrentGameState singleton and loads `[ebp+0xC] = state->tick (+0xBDC)` - the absolute hour that every mission window in phase 4 is written from.

It walks the agent's front provinces (+0xC0/+0xC4) and keeps a province in the CList at [ebp-0x94] when: `p->intel_country_count (+0x374) > ourCountry->id (+0xCA8)`; `p->intel_by_country_ptr (+0x370)[ourId] >= 2` (we can see it); and some unit in `p->units (+0x2B8)` passes slot 15, has `combats_count (+0x11C) > 0` and `current_combat (+0x110) == 0`.

**So the ground-attack target set is the provinces on our own front where a battle is in progress** - which is what makes the block the close-air-support arm.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_IssueGroundAttack
labels.evidence:
0x8CF330-0x8CF63C, over pool P. Per wing: not in listA; `home_base_ptr (+0x98)` set and its slot 0 answering a province; then the daylight window - `hour = state->tick % 24`, the dead guard at 0x8CF3AA (see CProvince::GetSunriseHour), and `hoursLeft = GetSunsetHour(baseProvince) - hour >= 3`.

Two target arms, each ending in the same issue:
1. 0x8CF403-0x8CF489 over `agent->+0x1AC` (recorded as invasion_target_provinces): the province must hold at least one enemy land unit (CountEnemyLandUnitsInList), `CWeather::AirCombatEffect` on it must be at or below **[0x1B151C0] = 400**, and the wing's `range (+0x148)` must be at least 1000x CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces.
2. 0x8CF4A3-0x8CF55D over the battle provinces from 0x8CF18A: weather at or below **[0x1B15240] = 330**, at most one of the agent's own wings already on `ground_attack (0x6FB)` against that province (counted through `order->+0xC` at 0x8CF50F), and the same range test.

The order: `CEU3AI::CreateUnitOrder(ai, 0x6FB, wing, p->id, &{p->id}, &now, &now + hoursLeft, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8CF5F5, then the province is removed from the battle list so two wings are not sent to the same battle in one pass. **So the mission window runs from now until local sunset at the airbase.**
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_IssueAirIntercept
labels.evidence:
0x8CF643-0x8CF902, over pool S (interceptors). Gated on `country->at_war (+0xACC) || country->in_undeclared_war (+0xACD)`.

Per wing it scans **the whole province table** - `state->provinces_begin (+0xB8C)` to `+0xB90`, the loop index doubling as the province id - and collects every province where 0x4EFA50(province@EDI, ourCountry, 0) holds, intel is at least 2, the province is not an enemy-controlled one carrying a building (`+0x304->+0x20 > 0` and CCountry::IsEnemy on `controller (+0x334)`), and the wing's `range (+0x148)` reaches it.

The order: `CreateUnitOrder(ai, 0x718 air_intercept, wing, firstCollectedId, &list, &now, &now + 0x78, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8CF8BF. **0x78 = 120 hours, five days** - the longest window phase 4 writes, and the only one not tied to sunset. No weather test anywhere in this block.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_StrategicArmRequiresAirStanceTwo
labels.evidence:
`cmp dword ptr [agent->unit + 0x20C], 2; je 0x4CF9FB` - and the fall-through is the full teardown and return.

**So `plan_air_stance == 2` is a hard precondition for every one of logistical_strike, strategic_bomb, nuke_mission, naval_strike and port_strike.** At any other non-zero stance phase 4 issues `ground_attack` and `air_intercept` and nothing else; at stance 0 it does not run at all (0x4CEE6E).

**The object it reads is the agent's own unit, not the wing** - `mov edx,[ebp+8]; mov eax,[edx+0x64]` - so the stance that matters is the one on the army or theatre HQ, and the AI drives that to 2 itself. `CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances`'s second loop posts `CSetPlanAttributesCommand(agent->unit, 5, 2, 2, -1000, -1000)` for every agent in `ai->unit_agents` whose unit is not already at 2, once per ProcessAI pass (see AiDrivesAirAndNavalStanceToTwo, 0x4916AD). **The gate therefore passes for the AI in the ordinary case, and the five strategic and naval missions are live, not dead.** The 1s the live sample found are on the air formations themselves, which this instruction never reads.

What is still one instruction, and still worth knowing for a mod, is the shape of the gate: anything that puts an agent's unit at stance 1 - a player deactivating that unit's plan, which resets air_stance to 1 through CUnitPlan::SetActive - silences the strategic air war for that agent until the next ProcessAI pass restores it.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_CollectInterdictionProvinces
labels.evidence:
The logistical-strike target survey, 0x8CF9FB-0x8CFC1A, reached only at air stance 2 and only when pool Q is non-empty.

It opens with `CUnitPlan::GetPowerRatio(&agent->unit->plan (+0x1FC))`, and **when the ratio is at or above [0x1B15210] = 750 the whole logistical-strike arm is skipped** (0x8CFA1C jumps past it) - so the AI interdicts when it is losing, not when it is winning.

Otherwise it rebuilds the list at [ebp-0x94] from the agent's front provinces: the front province must be enemy-controlled, then for each of its template's edges (`+0xD4 -> +0x90/+0x94`, stride 0x14) that is not edge kind 3, the neighbour must have `template +0x22 is_land` and `+0x13D` set, be enemy-controlled, have `ai_front_value (+0x5C)` at least **[0x1B151E4] = 200**, and **not** pass CProvince::HasHostileLandNeighbour. That last clause is what makes it a rear-area set: a province one step behind the enemy's front line.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_IssueLogisticalStrike
labels.evidence:
0x8CFC37-0x8CFD85, over pool Q. Per wing not in listA it collects the interdiction provinces whose weather is at or below [0x1B15240] = 330 and that the wing's `range (+0x148)` reaches, and then issues `CreateUnitOrder(ai, 0x6FD logistical_strike, wing, firstId, &list, &now, &now + 0x18, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8CFD5A. **0x18 = 24 hours.** No sunrise or sunset test - unlike ground attack and naval strike, interdiction is flown round the clock.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_IssueStrategicBombOrNuke
labels.evidence:
0x8CFDA5-0x8CFFF8, over pool Q again, with its own survey first.

The survey (0x8CFDA5-0x8CFE87) walks `agent->strategic_target_provinces (+0x18C/+0x190)` and keeps each enemy-controlled province. **When `ourCountry->nukes (+0x90) >= 1000` - that is, at least one bomb - an extra filter applies**: the province's `cores (+0x344)` list must hold an entry whose `+4` equals the province's own `controller_id (+0x338)`, so a nuke is only ever aimed at territory the controller also cores, never at land it merely occupies.

The issue (0x8CFE8D-0x8CFFF8) is per wing over Q, collecting targets by weather at or below 330 and by range, and then `CreateUnitOrder(ai, token, wing, firstId, &list, &now, &now + 0x18, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8CFFD6, where the token is chosen once at 0x8CFF8E - `0x579 nuke_mission` when `nukes >= 1000`, `0x6F9 strategic_bomb` otherwise. **The choice is per country, not per target or per wing**: a country with one bomb in stock sends every strategic bomber it has on a nuke mission.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: AirPhase4_IssueNavalOrPortStrike
labels.evidence:
0x8CFFFB-0x8D03E8, over pool R, gated on R's count.

The survey (0x8D0031-0x8D01CB) walks `agent->enemy_units_sighted (+0x25C)`, resolves each id pair through 0xA9D390 and backs up eight bytes to the CUnit, requires CCountry::IsEnemy on `owner (+0x124)` and weather at or below 330 over `current_province_ptr (+0x130)`, and then **splits by the target province's `template +0x22 is_land`**: a land province's id goes into list X at [ebp-0xE0], a sea zone's into list Y at [ebp-0x4C], and for a sea target that is moving (`+0x140 > 0`) the first waypoint `+0x138[0]` goes into Y as well.

The issue (0x8D01E0-0x8D03E8) repeats the sunset window - `GetSunsetHour(base) - hour >= 3`, the same dead guard at 0x8D0241 - and then tries **Y first with token `0x700 naval_strike`**; only when nothing in Y is within `range (+0x148)` does it fall to **X with `0x701 port_strike`** (the token is rewritten at 0x8D030C). `CreateUnitOrder(ai, token, wing, firstId, &list, &now, &now + hoursLeft, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8D03CE.

**So port strike is the fallback, not a separate decision**, and it works because a ship in harbour sits in the coastal land province.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: NavalConvoyRaid_ScoreConvoyRoutes
labels.evidence:
What fills the two vectors the convoy-raid draw runs on, 0x8D2526-0x8D28B3, and the reason the draw is weighted at all.

The arm is reached only for a fleet that is **a wolfpack**: `CountShipsByRole` must report the fleet all submarines when the AI runs its own units (`owner_ai->+0x2C` or `unit->+0x205`), or no transports and more than half submarines otherwise; plus `at_war || in_undeclared_war` and `plan_naval_stance (+0x210) != 0`.

It then walks `agent->+0x24C`, a CList of convoy object id pairs, resolving each through FindPersistentById against [0x1A857F0] or [0x1A857F4] by whether the id type is above 0x1268. A convoy counts when CCountry::IsEnemyTag accepts its `+0x30/+0x34` tag, or failing that when that tag is on our `undeclared_war_opponents (+0x1018)` list. For each province of the convoy's `path (CConvoy +0xB0)`, skipping the route's two endpoints (`*(+0xB0)` and `*(+0xB4)`), skipping province ids **0x2927..0x292A**, and skipping what 0x8D0520 refuses, and requiring `COrder::IsTargetInRange(fleet, id)`:

    weight = CConvoy::GetDesiredTransports(convoy) * abs(i + 1 - path_count / 2)

where `i` is the province's index along the route. **The weight is zero at the route's midpoint and largest at its ends**, so the AI's submarines are drawn to the waters near the convoy terminals rather than to mid-ocean - and a province exactly at the midpoint can never be picked.

A second pass per candidate (0x8D2830-0x8D2894) accumulates the same `GetDesiredTransports` into an ordered map keyed by each province of the agent's area (`area->+0x94`) that lies within the fleet's `range (+0x148)` of the candidate - the raidable-tonnage-per-port figure the rebase block then has available.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: NavalConvoyRaid_WeightedRandomTarget
labels.evidence:
**The only MT19937Next draw in either air or naval AI body, and it picks the province a submarine wolfpack is sent to raid.** 0x8D2B59-0x8D2CB6.

Two preconditions: the candidate vector must be non-empty (`[esp+0xFC] > 0`) and the total weight positive (`[esp+0x38] > 0`). Then:

    r = MT19937Next(&gameState->+0x124) % totalWeight          ; 0x8D2BBF, then cdq/idiv edi
    chosen = 0
    for (c = candidates, w = weights; c < candidatesEnd && r > 0; c++, w++) {
        chosen = *c
        r -= *w
    }

which is plain roulette-wheel selection over two parallel `std::vector<int>` - province ids at [esp+0xC4]/[esp+0xC8], weights at [esp+0xE8], the running total at [esp+0x38] - built by the loop at 0x8D2526. **One quirk worth knowing: `r` can come out 0** (one draw in `totalWeight`), and then the loop exits before it reads a candidate, `chosen` stays 0, and the order is issued against province id 0 all the same - nothing tests it.

The order is `CreateUnitOrder(ai, 0x6E9 convoy_raid, fleet, chosen, &emptyList, &now, &now + 0x1F8, 0x1A8CC94)` at 0x8D2CA5, with **0x1F8 = 504 hours, 21 days** - much the longest-lived order either body writes - and an empty province list, so the single chosen province is the whole of the mission.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: NavalRebase_ChooseHomePort
labels.evidence:
The rebase half of the same per-fleet loop, 0x8D2D8B-0x8D3141. It runs when the fleet's order is not blocking, and it is skipped entirely for a fleet holding any submarine (0x8D2E3A) and for one whose current port is not overcrowded - `shipsAtBase + pendingArrivals <= port->naval_base (+0x300)->level_max (+0x20)/1000 + 2` (0x8D2EDC-0x8D2EFA).

The scoring, over `area->+0x94` (the theatre's provinces), lowest wins, starting from 1e6f:

    if (candidate->area (+0x2B4) != fleetParentProvince->area) skip
    score = DistanceBetweenProvinces(candidate, fleetParentProvince) + 10.0
    load  = shipsBasedAt(candidate->+0x58) + pendingArrivals[candidate->id]
            + (we are not already there ? fleet->regiments_count (+0x40) : 0)
    over  = load - candidate->naval_base->level_max/1000
    if (over > 0) score += over * 2000
    if (we are already there) score *= 0.75
    if (score < best && CMapProvince::CanUnitReach(candidate, fleet, 0, 0)) best = score

and then `CEU3AI::IssueUnitOrder(ai, 0x6DE rebase, fleet, best->id)` at 0x8D313C, with the pending-arrivals map moved over. **So the AI's fleets spread themselves across the theatre's ports in proportion to berth capacity, pay 2000 per berth of overcrowding, get a 25% discount for staying put, and never cross out of their own COwnerArea** - and the `+ 10.0` floor means distance never scores zero.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airnaval4.md)

labels.name: AILandAttackOdds_ReadDefendProduct
labels.evidence:
`mov eax,[esi+0xF8]` at 0x4D981F then `imul dword ptr [esi+0xF0]` here, then __alldiv by 1000 - the **CUnit defend-product pair** on one of *our* candidate attackers, inside CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds (rva 0x4D93B0). The product is divided by 1000 again in floats and multiplied by `def->toughness/1000` into the mean D, which ends up as the factor `(1 - D/100)` on the **enemy's** estimated damage output. Repeated at 0x4D9C3A on one of *their* defenders, where it multiplies `def->defensiveness (+0x11C)` instead.

**Promoted from `likely` to `confirmed` 2026-10-02 when the body was read.** `esi` is a CUnit by a chain, not by trap 12's neighbour fallback: scripts/fieldchain.py --holder 0xC8 --field 0x134 (window 0x200) puts both of this function's soft_attack reads behind a `[esi + 0xC8]` load, which is CUnit::CSubUnitDefinitionPtr; the same holder reaches +0x11C, +0x120, +0x124 and +0x138; `esi` is the receiver of `[[esi]+0x50]` and `[[esi]+0x54]`, which vtable.py --holding shows are CUnit/CArmy/CNavy/CAir slots 20 and 21, CUnit::GetAverageOrganisation and CUnit::GetAverageStrength; and esi is written only at 0x4D94CC and 0x4D994D in the whole function, each time from a unit-list node's payload, so the register that reads +0xF0 is the register that reaches all of those.

**The products are not always neutral, and not always 1000 either.** CUnit::CUnit (rva 0x1B5010) zeroes +0xDC..+0xF8 at 0x1B513C-0x1B514E, and the only writers of +0xF0 in the image are CUnit::ResetCombatModifiers (rva 0x1C3029, the 1000) and CUnit::AddCombatModifier (rva 0x1C3108, the multiply) - both reached only from CCombatant slot 19, i.e. only for a unit in a combat. So a unit that has never fought reads +0xF0 == 0 here and gets **no** toughness or defensiveness term at all; a unit fighting now reads its real land defend product; a unit that has stopped fighting keeps the last combat tick's value, because nothing clears it on exit.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attackodds.md)

labels.name: AILandAttackOdds_Recurse
labels.evidence:
`call 0x4D93B0` - CAIUnit::EstimateAttackOdds calling itself, its own third caller. It runs once per enemy defender, for the first combat in which that defender appears in `combat->attacker->units`, and asks how that unit's own attack elsewhere is going: arg1 = `&combat->attacker->units`, the cache's list = `&combat->defender->units`, target = that combat's province (+0x18), excludeProvince = the province we are estimating, and **followCombats = 0**, which is what bounds the recursion at one level - the combat walks that reach this call are inside `if (followCombats)`. The answer is clamped to 4.0 [0x171DF34], has 0 replaced by 0.01 [0x160A378], is scaled by 0.25 [0x160A258] and replaces that defender's engagement seed of 1.0, so the factor lies in (0.0025, 1.0].
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attackodds.md)

labels.name: AILandAttackOdds_ReadDefendProduct2
labels.evidence:
The second `imul dword ptr [esi+0xF0]`, preceded by `mov eax,[esi+0xF8]` at 0x4D9C34 - the same CUnit defend-product pair as rva 0x4D9825, but in the **defending** side's loop, where it multiplies `def->defensiveness (+0x11C)` rather than `toughness (+0x120)` and ends up as the factor `(1 - D/100)` on **our** estimated damage output. See 0x4D9825 for the chain that makes `esi` a CUnit and for the writer census; same confidence and the same reason for it.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-attackodds.md)

labels.name: AiSlot76PostsAirStanceZero
labels.evidence:
`CSetPlanAttributesCommand(agent->unit (+0x64), 1, 0, 0, &-1000, &-1000)` - the plan builder posts **stance 1, air_stance 0, naval_stance 0**. The two zeroes come from `esi`, zeroed at 0x4DAD44; the two -1000s are written into their stack slots at 0x4DAD5D and 0x4DAD67.

air_stance 0 is the value at which CAIUnit_ManageAirUnits phase 4 does not run at all (0x4CEE6E). So the AI's own two writers pull in opposite directions: slot 76 zeroes the stances when it builds a plan, and CEU3AI::UpdateUnitStances drives them back to 2 on the next pass (0x4916AD). Slot 76 is reached from CEU3AI::CreateAgentsForPlannedUnits, which ProcessAI runs only while `ai->unit_agents_count (+0x48)` is zero, and from CObjectivesEntry slot 22 - so the zero is the rare event and the 2 is the steady state.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-airstance.md)

labels.name: FallbackOpsArea_FirstPostFallsThrough
labels.evidence:
The join of CAIUnit slot 76's fallback epilogue, and the instruction that settles whether the fallback's two CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand posts are on one path. cfg.py gives it exactly two predecessors - 0x4DBCF5 (taken, the 'nothing to post' arm) and **0x4DBE39 (fall-through, straight out of CAIUnit::ReplanSubtree after the first post)** - so after the first command is posted control reaches here, not a return. Read off the edge list, not off one jump (trap 13).
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

labels.name: FallbackOpsArea_EmptyListBeforeSecondPost
labels.evidence:
`xor esi, esi` then three stores zeroing head, tail and count of the province CList at [esp+0x7C] (0x4DBE74/0x4DBE78/0x4DBE7F) and its trailing byte at 0x4DBE86, after the free loops at 0x4DBE3E-0x4DBE56 and 0x4DBE58-0x4DBE70. Between here and the second CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand construction at 0x4DBEE8 nothing writes those three slots, so the second command's payload is necessarily **empty**.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

labels.name: FallbackOpsArea_SecondCommandWithEmptyList
labels.evidence:
`call 0x1E60B0` - CSetPlanOpsAreaCommand's constructor, taking `lea edx, [esp+0x7C]` from 0x4DBEE1: the same stack CList the fallback filled and 0x4DBE72 has just emptied. Guarded at 0x4DBEB4 by `unit->plan.ops_area_count (+0x21C) > 0` alone, which is a strict subset of the first post's guard at 0x4DBCE2/0x4DBCF5 (`count > 0 || the agent's own ops-area vector is non-empty`), so **this post never happens without the first and can only undo it**. Posted through the same channel in the shared epilogue at 0x4DC96F, so it executes second. Net behaviour of the fallback path: a unit the AI could not find a front for ends the hour with an empty ops area, whichever way the author's intent is read.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-negatives.md)

labels.name: CUnitPlan_Ctor_ZeroesUnnamed58
labels.evidence:
`mov [eax+0x58], ecx` in CUnitPlan::CUnitPlan, with ecx zero - and, with the `mov [eax+0x6c], ecx` at 0x4DEA34, **the only write to either field in any CUnitPlan method**. The constructor lays the object out as: vftable, 0x18D at +4, the two bytes at +8, stances 2/1/1 at +0xC/+0x10/+0x14, four CLists (+0x18, +0x28, +0x38, +0x48), **an unnamed dword at +0x58**, a fifth CList at +0x5C, **an unnamed dword at +0x6C**, the `min` vector's three pointers (+0x70, +0x74, +0x78), then +0x80..+0x8C. It never touches +0x7C at all.

What is known about the three: the destructor frees nothing at any of them, so none is a pointer the plan owns; CUnitPlan::SetActive (the reset, 0x4DEB10) clears every list, the vector and +0x80..+0x8C and leaves all three alone; the applier at 0x1D0F00 copies active, stance, ops_area, objectives, path, path2, min, our_power and their_power from one plan to another and copies none of them; and LoadKey (0x4DF720) and SaveContents (0x4DF160) never mention them, so nothing about them reaches a savegame or the network. They are runtime-only, unread by the class itself, and cannot be named from the executable alone.
(reversing/CLASSES.md)
