labels.name: EventScopeUnknownKey
labels.evidence:
The default arm of CEventScope::MakeScope's token switch, and the **only** writer of `CEventScope::unknown_context (+0x3D)`: `mov byte ptr [esp+0x75], cl` with `cl == 1`. It then falls into the empty-candidate arm at 0x5C1F34, which also clears `resolved (+0x3C)`. Reached for every key the switch does not recognise and the spec could not turn into a literal country tag.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

labels.name: EventScopeNoCandidate
labels.evidence:
`mov byte ptr [esp+0x74], 0` - the **only** writer that clears `CEventScope::resolved (+0x3C)`, reached when the candidate vector CEventScope::MakeScope built is empty. That happens for `ally` on a country with an empty list, for `local_enemy` in a province with no qualifying unit, and for every unrecognised key, which arrives here through the default arm at 0x5C1F01. It is the byte CContextTrigger::Evaluate (0x5D154D) and CContextTrigger::WalkChildren (0x5D248D) test before doing anything, and that two of the three effect-side callers of MakeScope test as well (0x59E2CD, 0x59E33C). CContextTrigger::CountEvaluation, CContextTrigger::GetBlockText and the caller at 0x59E635 do not.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

labels.name: LoadKeyRegionScopeArm
labels.evidence:
`call CRegionScopeTrigger::CRegionScopeTrigger` inside CTrigger::LoadKey (0x5C8D10), and the instruction that makes **every region name in `map/region.txt` a trigger scope keyword**. The arm runs 0x5CAE1C-0x5CAE5D: it calls 0x52A710 with `g_CMap (0x1A8557C) + 0x2A50` - CMap's by-name string hash table - and the key's text; on a hit it takes a 0x44-byte `operator new` and constructs a CRegionScopeTrigger over the region, and on a miss it falls through to 0x5CAE62, which is the CContextTrigger arm FINDINGS-triggereval.md section 3 describes.

So the loader's order for a key that is not in the compiled trigger table is: **region name, then speculative scope resolution, then `Unknown trigger-type` through trigger.cpp.** FINDINGS-triggereval.md section 3 had the second and third steps and not the first.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

labels.name: TriggerKeyScopeAcceptance
labels.evidence:
**Where the trigger loader decides that a key it does not recognise is a scope, and the test it uses.** 0x5CAE62 is the arm CTrigger::LoadKey (0x5C8D10) falls into when the key is neither one of its 153 keywords nor a region name - the region lookup is immediately above it, at 0x5CAE1C, and jumps here when `StringHashFind(g_CMap + 0x2A50, text)` answers null.

    EventScopeSpec_Construct(&spec, parse + 0x20)          ; 0x5C1B30, at 0x5CAE72
    CEventScope trial(seed = 0, arg = 0)                    ; 0x5C1610, at 0x5CAE82
    CEventScope::MakeScope(&trial, &spec, &out)             ; 0x5C1C10, at 0x5CAE96
    if (out.unknown_context (+0x3D) == 0) {
        t = operator new(0x150)                             ; 0x5CAEA6
        new CContextTrigger(t, <spec by value, 0x104 bytes>) ; 0x5D14A0, at 0x5CAED7
    } else
        "Unknown trigger-type " <key> " in " <file>          ; trigger.cpp line 0x10B

So **a key becomes a scope by being rebound successfully against an empty scope at parse time.** The test is `unknown_context`, **not** `resolved`: the trial scope is freshly constructed with seed 0, country `"---"`/0 and province 0, so `owner`, `controller`, `ally`, `capital_scope`, `sea_zone` and `local_enemy` all resolve to nothing on it and every one of them would fail a `resolved` test. That is why the parse-time check cannot be the same check CContextTrigger::Evaluate makes at run time.

The accepted set is therefore exactly eleven forms: a country tag `CCountryDataBase` knows (MakeScope's pre-switch arm), a number (lexer token 0xC), and the nine keyword tokens `owner` 0x1EC, `controller` 0x1ED, `from` 0x34F, `ally` 0x359, `this` 0x377, `capital_scope` 0x3B4, `sea_zone` 0x3E8, `local_enemy` 0x621, `overlord` 0x631. **None of those nine is among CTrigger::LoadKey's own 153 cases** (checked with `scripts/switchmap.py 0x9C8D10`: no case for 492, 493, 847, 857, 887, 948, 1000, 1569 or 1585), so a condition keyword and a scope keyword can never shadow each other in either direction.

The tail at 0x5CADC1 is shared with the region arm and with all 153 keyword cases: it `operator new`s a 0x10-byte list node `{payload@+0, prev@+4, next@+8, byte@+0xC}`, appends it to the parent's child list (`children_last +0xC`, `children_count +0x10`, `children_first +8` when the count was 0), sets the **new child's** `+0x3C` to 1 (0x5CAE09), and calls the child's **slot 3** (`[vftable+0xC]`, CPersistent::Load) with the parse context to read its `{ ... }` block. So `CTrigger +0x3C` is a byte the base constructor zeroes and this loader sets on every trigger it builds; nothing that reads it was looked for.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-scopetriggers.md)

labels.name: TriggerLoadKeyScopeTest
labels.evidence:
**The seam between the grammar and the evaluator**, inside CTrigger::LoadKey's default arm: `cmp byte ptr [eax+0x3d], 0; sete al`. A key that is none of the 152 trigger keywords is turned into a scope specification (EventScopeSpec_Construct at 0x5CAE72), tried against a throwaway CEventScope built at 0x5CAE82, and **only if `unknown_context (+0x3D)` is still zero** does the loader `operator new(0x150)` a CContextTrigger for it (0x5CAEA6) rather than reporting a parse error through `trigger.cpp` at 0x5CAEEE.

This is why `CContextTrigger` has 10,974 live instances while `findings/FINDINGS-script.md` could place only 2 of its 153 keys: its keys are not in CTrigger::LoadKey's table at all - they are whatever CEventScope::MakeScope recognises, which is ten tokens plus any country tag plus any number. It is also the only reader of `+0x3D` in the image.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-triggereval.md)

labels.name: BaseBlockChildBranch
labels.evidence:
`je` past the leaf line to the block path, inside `CTrigger::GetBlockText`. The block path draws **neither indent nor icon** - it goes straight to the child's own slot 9 - which is why a nested `and` or `or` inside a scope used to come out with no asterisk at all.

**BiceLib retargets this branch** (the condition is kept, only the destination changes) to a stub that draws the indent and the asterisk for a block child and then rejoins at `0x5D05DA`.
(BiceLib/Hooks/TriggerText/TriggerIndentText.hpp)

labels.name: AndBlockNoHeaderAtTop
labels.evidence:
**An `and` at depth 0 draws no header.** `jne` past this and it renders `AND_TRIGGER_STARTS` and its children; fall through and it hands the whole call to `CTrigger::GetBlockText` instead. That is why a technology's `allow`, which is an implicit `and` at the top, lists its conditions without an `All of the below:` above them.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

labels.name: AndHeaderIndentLoop
labels.evidence:
The `jle` past an `and` header's own indent loop. **A BiceLib patch site**: one byte to `jmp`, because the parent has already indented this line and the header indenting itself again is what pushed the text right of its icon.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

labels.name: AndBlockChildDepth
labels.evidence:
What an `and` passes as the depth when a child is itself a block. The game sends a constant, so a block inside a block restarted at the same level; BiceLib sends the `and`'s own depth plus one.
(BiceLib/Hooks/TriggerText/TriggerIndentText.hpp)

labels.name: AndPerChildIndent
labels.evidence:
Where an `and` reads its depth as the number of indents to put before each child's line. **A BiceLib patch site**: it wants `depth + 1`, since the children sit *inside* the block, and using the block's own depth left every condition level with its header.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

labels.name: AndTriggerExit
labels.evidence:
`mov ecx, [esp + 0xE4]`, the last instruction of `CAndTrigger::GetBlockText` before its epilogue, and the point every path through the function converges on - two branches inside it land exactly here.

**BiceLib stands here to scroll a requirement tooltip too tall for the screen**: the finished text is in `esi` and the frame is still up, so lines can be taken off the front before the tooltip sees it. One instruction before the epilogue rather than over it, because the epilogue writes `fs:[0]` and reproducing that from inline assembly is a warning and a SAFESEH question nobody needs.
(BiceLib/Hooks/TriggerText/TriggerScrollText.hpp)

labels.name: OrBlockOwnIconAtTop
labels.evidence:
**An `or` draws an icon for its own header only at depth 0**, where nothing above it has drawn one; `jne` skips it at any other depth. The test reads the same register the header's indent loop counts down, which is why BiceLib's indent patch has to disable that loop rather than zero the register - zeroing it made every nested `or` draw a second asterisk.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-script.md)

labels.name: NotTriggerEpilogue
labels.evidence:
The epilogue of `CNotTrigger::GetBlockText`, which BiceLib replaces whole.

A `not` flips `redWhen` and forwards to the base **with the depth unchanged**, so the base indents the condition inside it a second time - into the middle of a line the parent has already placed. No depth fixes that: the base draws the icon when the depth is 0 or arrived negative and the indent whenever it is above 0, so "neither" is not a value it can be given. The stub takes the leading indent off the finished text instead.
(BiceLib/Hooks/TriggerText/TriggerIndentText.hpp)

labels.name: ContextTriggerHeaderIndent
labels.evidence:
Its own indent loop, at the top of the renderer and before a word of its own text - so it indents a line its parent has already placed, and the text ends up adrift of its own asterisk. **BiceLib turns the `jle` that guards it into an unconditional `jmp`**, which skips the loop and leaves the depth register for the icon test that reads it next.
(BiceLib/Hooks/TriggerText/TriggerIndentText.hpp)

labels.name: ContextTriggerChildDepth
labels.evidence:

The sign is read at the top of `CTrigger::GetBlockText`, which negates it back and remembers that it did.

labels.name: CombatModifierTrigger_ReadFlagArray
labels.evidence:

labels.name: CGraphics_CreateDevice
labels.evidence:
**The device the game draws with is created without `D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE`.** CGraphics::CGraphics calls `IDirect3D9::CreateDevice` (vtable +0x40 on the object at CGraphics +0x60) at four places, VAs: 0xA6E960 (adapter 1, HAL, flags 0x40), 0xA6EA1F (the `PerfHUD` adapter, REF, 0x40), **0xA6EAE9 (the ordinary path: HAL, flags = settings +0x1C)** and 0xA6ECE8 (the retry at default refresh after Sleep(100), flags = settings +0x1C). The settings flags are 0x40 or 0x20 as GraphicsSettings_DetectDevice wrote them. So Direct3D 9 puts the creating thread's x87 unit into **24-bit precision, round to nearest**.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-luahost.md)

labels.name: CommandExecute_CallSite
labels.evidence:

(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-commands.md)

labels.name: ApplicationInstallsObservable
labels.evidence:
`mov dword ptr [esi+0xE4], edi` inside the base CApplication constructor 0x6909A0, which CEU3Application::CEU3Application (0x22F080) calls at 0x22F0F3 - **the only write to CEU3Application +0xE4 in the image.** edi is a 0xC0-byte object allocated at 0x690AD2, constructed by 0x732CB0, and given five vftables: 0x15FDDC0 at +0 and 0x15FDE20/0x15FDE30/0x15FDE40/0x15FDE50 at +0x18/+0x30/+0x48/+0x60. None has RTTI, so the class is unidentified; only slot 4 was resolved, and it is the shared empty stub 0x20CD50.

That `esi` is the application is self-evident from the same function zeroing +0x88 at 0x690AAA and +0xE0 at 0x690ACC - the pair CEU3Application::SetNextScreen writes and CEU3Application::Run reads - which independently confirms that CInGameIdler +0x1790 is the CEU3Application.

**Trap 12 warning attached to this offset:** 0x2913F0 writes +0xE0, +0xE4, +0xF4 and +0xF8 in the same shape and is NOT the application - it constructs a CIngameLobby (vftable 0x15CFBA4, base CReferenceObject 0x15C3AE4, CSessionInfoObserver sub-object at +0x30). Four matching displacements in the same address band is not an identification. And +0xE4 is not +0x124, the still-unidentified field CInGameIdler slot 15 (0x24D7C0) returns. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md section 3(a).
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-resetpath.md)

labels.name: g_Float800Point5
labels.evidence:
The float 800.5, read once in code, at 0x52E4D3 in CSpyPresence::CatchSpies, where it goes through floorf (0x401FD0) and a float-to-int (0xC08870) to give **800**, i.e. 0.800 in thousandths. Its role there: the home counter-espionage chance is scaled by `1 - 800*(1000 - mission_share[0])/1000`, so a country with no spies on counter-espionage keeps a fifth of the detection chance.

labels.name: g_FogOfWarEnabled
labels.evidence:
**The fog-of-war switch, set by default and toggled by the `fow` console command.** One byte, 1 in .data. ClearIntelFunctor_SerialBody fills every province's intel bytes with 0 while it is set and 9 while it is clear (0x6881C5: `cmp byte [0x170AD30], cl; setne cl; dec ecx; and ecx, 9`); RunIntelRefresh, after the UpdateIntel fan-out, gives the screen's country 9 on every simulated province while it is clear (0x689280); ShouldStartNavalCombat starts a sea battle without a spotting roll while it is clear. The console handler (0x4418C4, the literal 'fow' at 0x15B84E0) prints 'Fog of war turned OFF' when it was set, 'Fog of war turned ON' when it was clear, and stores the opposite (`sete cl; mov byte [0x170ad30], cl` at 0x441908..0x44191B). 17 code references in all; the others (province graphics, the map's colour textures, messages, the scenario end dialog) were not read.

labels.name: g_NullDate
labels.evidence:
**At run time 43808760 - 1 January of year 1, hour 0 - not the 43800000 the file holds.** A CRT initialiser, NullDate_Init (rva 0x8A8210, in the `.CRT$XCU` table at VA 0xD2BD78), runs `Date_SetFromString(&g_NullDate, "1.1.1")` at startup; the 43800000 in the image (= 0x29C55C0, the game's hour epoch) is only the value that call starts from, and it keeps its day of the year and hour (both 0). That is why a save prints every unset date as `1.1.1.0`. Used as the **'never' value for a date field**: TradeRouteSetInactive compares CTradeRoute +0x84 against it before stamping a tick (0xA4D585) and CEU3AI::HasTradeGoneStale refuses to call a route stale while +0x84 still equals it (0x89B672). **The history subsystem is the second independent confirmation**: it is the default date of every CHistoryEntry (the base constructor writes the immediate 0x29C55C0 at +8 and then this static over it, at 0x200AA9/0x200AB0 and in every inlined copy), the default date of every CHistoryContainer (0x1F45BA) and what CHistoryContainer::Reset puts back (0x1F4768); CHistoryEntry::DateIsUnset (0x1EC6E0) is `year(date) < 2`, which is true of it; and it is the fallback the leader part of RunCountryDailyPass uses when a leader's history has no `rank` entry - a date no live tick can equal, so such a leader is never activated. It is also the start and death date of a CMinister whose block gives none (0x52C3DA, 0x52C3E6). Of its 234 references in .text, the initialiser's `mov esi, 0x170C2B8` (VA 0xCA8216) is the one write; every other reads it. The next global, 0x130C2BC, is set the same way to `9999.1.1` (rva 0x8A8230) and is read nowhere else.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-history.md)

labels.name: g_DayLengthByMonth
labels.evidence:
Twelve int32 thousandths {-6, -3, 0, +3, +6, +12, +6, +3, 0, -3, -6, -12}, read by IsNight at 0xA73E4 as monthTable[month] x CProvince +0x388 / 1000 - the seasonal swing in day length, scaled by latitude. Since +0x388 is zero across the southern hemisphere the term vanishes there, so southern provinces get twelve-hour days all year. IsNight shifts the month by six where CProvinceTemplate +0xA2 is clear, which is the southern hemisphere.

labels.name: g_RadarNearScale
labels.evidence:

labels.name: g_random_object
labels.evidence:

labels.name: g_SpyCheat

labels.name: g_AiYesmen
labels.evidence:
**The `yesmen` console cheat.** One byte. The command handler tests it at 0x4419CA, toggles it with `sete al; mov byte [0x1A8562F], al` at 0x4419D8, and prints 'AI now always responds favorably' (0x15B8598) or the off message - the `yesmen` literal it matches on is at 0x15B8590. That matters because it is the second half of the `return 100` short-circuit in GetDiploScoreFromLua and in all five of its clones (0xA0DD14, 0xA0DE94, 0xA348AF, 0xA44734, 0xA448B4, 0xA44A34, 0xA44C04): `if (actor == player && g_AiYesmen) return 100`. FINDINGS-diplomacy.md read the condition right but concluded that a script's opinion of a human offer is never consulted; with the byte identified, the short-circuit **never fires in normal play** and the mod's Lua is asked about the player's offers like anyone else's. Its neighbours in the same handler are the other cheat flags - 0x1A8554F `nopopup`, 0x1A855F4 `spy`, and 0x170AD30, which project.json already names g_FogOfWarEnabled. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-survivors.md)

labels.name: g_CBuildingDataBase
labels.evidence:
The one `CBuildingDataBase`, 0x30 bytes, built lazily exactly as `g_CSubUnitDataBase` is: every user does `if (!g) g = new 0x30 bytes, init`. The init at rva `0x5BD30` is shared with 198 other databases and lays out the first 0x18 bytes - `+0x00`..`+0x0B` a name -> `CBuilding*` hash map (count at `+0x00`, `0x1FF` buckets at `+0x04`, the bucket array allocated and zeroed at `+0x08`) and `+0x0C`/`+0x10`/`+0x14` a `vector<CBuilding*>`. Everything from `+0x18` on is this class's own and the init does not touch it.

**Five of those six slots are cached `CBuilding*` for well-known roles**, filled by the loader at rva `0xB769B` (the defaults, all five pointed at the built-in 'nobuilding') and rva `0xB78AB` (the modifier ladder): `+0x1C` air_base, `+0x20` naval_base, `+0x24` anti_air, `+0x28` underground, `+0x2C` industry. The setup at `0x968B8`..`0x96A50` turns four of them into a province's building shortcuts,

    province->+0x308 = province->buildings[ db->+0x24->index ]
    province->+0x304 = province->buildings[ db->+0x1C->index ]
    province->+0x300 = province->buildings[ db->+0x20->index ]
    province->+0x30C = province->buildings[ db->+0x28->index ]

where `index` is `CBuilding +0x54` and `buildings` is `CProvince +0x310`.

**`+0x18` is the sixth slot and is dead.** It is the first dword the class adds on top of the shared 0x18-byte base, so it is a member rather than padding, but no instruction in the image writes or reads it: the init stops at `+0x14`, the loader's defaults set exactly the five role slots, and the ladder has exactly five branches. The object is `malloc`ed and never zeroed, so whatever stands at `+0x18` is heap garbage, not a building.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-supply.md)

labels.name: g_CSubUnitDataBase
labels.evidence:

labels.name: g_decision_database
labels.evidence:
**The decision database**, a 0x38-byte CDecisionDatabase: diplomatic decisions by name at +0x00 and in file order at +0x0C, political decisions by name at +0x1C and in file order at +0x28. Created by GetDecisionDatabase (0x598BD0), replaced by SetDecisionDatabase (0x599B50), filled once by LoadDecisions (0x598E30). Addresses here are rvas.

**Who uses which half** (every code chunk that addresses this global or calls the getter, 14 of them, read 2026-10-12): the three walks over a vector - CDiplomacyView::RebuildDecisionList (0x38C560, the decisions list box), CAIForeignMinister::ExecuteDiploDecisions (0x49DD50, the AI) and CAlertManager_Update (the walk at 0x206D41, the national decisions alert) - all walk **the diplomatic vector at +0x0C**, and each asks `potential` and then `allow`. The name lookups: CExecuteDecisionCommand::Execute and ::IsValid (0x608610, 0x609A30) try the diplomatic table and then the political; SetUpCountryForNewGame (0xD6230) the political and then the diplomatic; CCountryWarTargetValue::LoadKey (0x76701) the diplomatic alone. **So a `political_decisions` decision loads, can be executed and replayed by name, and is never offered to anybody.** The rest are its life: LoadDecisions' stage (the chunk at 0x2348F0), SetDecisionDatabase, the teardown at 0x22F832, CDecisionEntry::OnClicked, PostExecuteDecisionCommand, CAIForeignMinister::DoWork and a static destructor. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfiles.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfire.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfiles.md)

labels.name: g_event_list
labels.evidence:
**The event list: a 0x20-byte CEventList holding two CLists - every `country_event` at +0x00 and every `province_event` at +0x10.** LoadEventFile (0x5BF7B0) appends each event to one or the other by the key it was written under; nothing else distinguishes the two kinds, which are the same CEvent class. RebuildCountryEventCandidates (0x5C0050) walks only +0x00, so only country events become monthly candidates. RunMonthlyPass creates the list if it is null (0x283C72, a zeroed 0x20 bytes) and then rebuilds every country's candidate list from it; a null value therefore means the scenario has not finished loading. BiceLib's EventCandidates module reads it and calls the rebuild once per session rather than waiting for the month to turn - see reversing/findings/FINDINGS-events.md; the two halves are in reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfiles.md.
(reversing/findings/FINDINGS-eventfiles.md)
